title: CI red: flagged-claim reap test still expects in_progress after kehw release-to-open
description:
## Objective

Restore green test workflow hermetic pytest on who/ortus main after ortus-kehw (ebd0b48) started releasing human-flagged heads to open, while test_flagged_claim_is_reaped_within_a_poll_not_timed_out still asserts parked in_progress.

## Behavioral context

Before: last green main run was https://github.com/who/ortus/actions/runs/35973719012 on 85b03fc (ortus-5yjr, completed about 01:10 PT on 2026-09-24). After ebd0b48 (ortus-kehw: Release a parked claim and count the whole queue at exit), every subsequent completed main test run fails all six pytest matrix legs at step "Run comprehensive hermetic pytest gate". Latest red: https://github.com/who/ortus/actions/runs/36010560043 on 2d31399 (started 07:08 PT). Single failure on ubuntu-latest/py3.12 junit: tests/test_grind_reap.py::test_flagged_claim_is_reaped_within_a_poll_not_timed_out with AssertionError: assert 'open' == 'in_progress' at the post-reap shown["status"] check. Same failure on the first post-green run https://github.com/who/ortus/actions/runs/36006192935 (ebd0b48). Locally on [redacted]2 WSL the same command fails identically in about 29s. After this fix: that integration test matches the kehw release-to-open contract (or production stops over-releasing if product reverses), and the hermetic gate is green again on main.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Align the flagged-claim reap integration contract with _release_parked_head introduced in ebd0b48 / ortus-kehw, so CI stops failing on a stale in_progress assertion. Prefer updating tests/test_grind_reap.py::test_flagged_claim_is_reaped_within_a_poll_not_timed_out (and any sibling assertions that still expect parked in_progress after a mid-window human flag) to expect open with the human label kept and the reap log line still present, matching kehw's own After/AC that a human-flagged head leaves non-in_progress. Only change production in src/ortus/commands/grind.py if a recorded product reversal says mid-window flagged reaps must remain in_progress; do not silently undo kehw's exit-count / release behavior.

## Non-goals

Do not revert ortus-kehw _exit_counts or the operator-facing exit summary. Do not start/stop the main grind seat. Do not patch unrelated red history before 85b03fc. Do not expand into a full local six-leg matrix as the worker default. Do not paste secrets from CI logs.

## Concrete locations

- src/ortus/commands/grind.py - _release_parked_head, _parked_head_comment, and the post-window not-resuming excluded-label call site that now reverts the claim to open (added in ebd0b48).
- tests/test_grind_reap.py - test_flagged_claim_is_reaped_within_a_poll_not_timed_out (assert near line 506: shown["status"] == "in_progress"); nearby kehw unit tests test_human_flagged_head_hand_back_reverts_the_parked_claim already expect open.
- CodeGraph evidence: explore/query on test_flagged_claim_is_reaped_within_a_poll_not_timed_out, _release_parked_head, _reap_worker / _flagged_claims (call path _reap_worker -> _reap_reason -> _flagged_claims).

## Resolved decisions

1. Authoritative signal: Actions run 36010560043 / job pytest ubuntu-latest py3.12 and matching local repro; introducing commit is ebd0b48 (first red after green 85b03fc).
2. Product intent from closed ortus-kehw: mid-window human-flagged heads must not stay stuck in_progress; _release_parked_head reverts to open with label kept. The failing test still encodes the pre-kehw parked-in_progress contract - that is test/contract drift, not a flaky runner or env issue.
3. Default fix path: update the stale integration assertion(s) to expect open + human label + reap log; keep production release behavior unless a PLAN-GAP records an explicit reverse of kehw.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux and macOS; Python 3.10-3.12 hermetic gate. Flagged-claim reap must still log claim flagged human (...); reaping worker and must not fire TIMEOUT. Human label must remain on the issue. Misclaim hand-back (test_misclaim_is_handed_back_after_the_reap) stays open-with-label as today.

## Ordered steps

1. Confirm still red: uv run pytest tests/test_grind_reap.py::test_flagged_claim_is_reaped_within_a_poll_not_timed_out -q --tb=short.
2. Read _release_parked_head call site and the failing assert; confirm status is opened on the not-resuming excluded-label path after the flagged reap.
3. Update the integration test to assert open (and keep human label + reap log + no TIMEOUT), matching kehw unit coverage; scan the same file for other post-flag status==in_progress asserts that conflict.
4. If product instead requires parked in_progress after mid-window flagged reap, stop calling _release_parked_head on that path only and document the contradiction with ortus-kehw as PLAN-GAP - do not half-apply both contracts.
5. Re-run the targeted pytest command; land on main and confirm the test workflow goes green.

## Dependencies

None - standalone CI blocker. Related closed context: ortus-kehw (introduced release-to-open), ortus-lf02 (EXCLUDED_LABELS resume trap; closed). Callers: grind outer loop post-mortem / not-resuming path.

## Edge cases

Worker reaped for human flag but tracker update_status fails - claim may stay in_progress; test should not require open if release logged failure. Distinct from misclaim hand-back of a second operator-labelled issue. Exit summary _exit_counts must keep counting human-labelled issues even when loop snapshots exclude them.

## Plan-gap guidance

If operators decide mid-window flagged reaps must remain in_progress (pre-kehw park) while kehw still requires release-to-open for not-resuming heads, stop and record PLAN-GAP: those two contracts conflict on the same post-reap status. Do not invent a third status or drop the human label.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1: uv run pytest tests/test_grind_reap.py::test_flagged_claim_is_reaped_within_a_poll_not_timed_out -q --tb=short exits 0 and no longer asserts pre-kehw parked in_progress against a release-to-open outcome.
- AC-2: uv run pytest tests/test_grind_reap.py -k "flagged_claim or human_flagged_head_hand_back" -q --tb=short exits 0 so the integration reap contract and kehw unit release tests agree on open-with-human-label.
- AC-3: After push, GitHub Actions workflow test on main for the fix commit concludes success (or the worker records the run URL and remaining unrelated failures if any).

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_reap.py::test_flagged_claim_is_reaped_within_a_poll_not_timed_out -q --tb=short`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_reap.py -k "flagged_claim or human_flagged_head_hand_back" -q --tb=short`
- AC-3: `gh run list --repo who/ortus --branch main --workflow test --limit 3`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_grind_reap.py::test_flagged_claim_is_reaped_within_a_poll_not_timed_out tests/test_grind_reap.py::test_human_flagged_head_hand_back_reverts_the_parked_claim -q --tb=short`
close_reason: Flagged-claim reap integration case now expects release-to-open with the human label kept, matching the harness contract that turned the hermetic gate red

comments.author: who
comments.text:
Test/contract drift, fixed on the test side as the work spec's default path directs. The flagged-claim reap integration case still asserted the pre-release parked in_progress status, while production now reverts a head that ends its window carrying an excluded label back to open with the label kept. No recorded product reversal, so the release behavior and the exit counts are untouched.

The integration case now asserts open plus the kept human label, and additionally asserts the release log line so the revert is proven rather than inferred from a status that open could also reach by other means. The flagged-claim reap log line and the no-TIMEOUT assertion stay as they were. Scanned the rest of the file for sibling post-flag status assertions: the only other in_progress assertion is the mis-claim hand-back unit test for a worker's own flag, which exercises a different helper that genuinely does not revert, so it was left alone.

AC-1 and AC-2 criterion checks pass locally. AC-3 (the main workflow run for this commit) is checked after push.

comments.author: who
comments.text:
AC-3 record: the test workflow run for the fix commit 8d2b36a is https://github.com/who/ortus/actions/runs/36041738556, queued at the time of session-close. It was not yet concluded when this window ended, so this is the recorded-URL branch of AC-3 rather than an observed success.

Evidence that the gate is fixed, short of that conclusion: the local repro was byte-identical to the CI failure (AssertionError: assert 'open' == 'in_progress' at the post-reap status check in the flagged-claim reap case), and that same command now exits 0 locally. The prior red run 36010560043 reported exactly one failing test across all six matrix legs, so no other failure is known to be outstanding on main. If the run concludes red on something else, that is new and unrelated and wants its own bead.

title: Repair the grind start-line assertions after the prompt-variant field
description:
## Objective
Restore the three verification-mode start-line assertions in `tests/test_grind.py`.

## Behavioral context
`ortus-xfw1` added a `prompt=<variant>` field to the `=== ortus grind started ...` marker line. The three `test_grind_start_line_records_verification_mode_*` tests still assert the old suffix `backend=claude; verification=full) ===`, so they fail against a start line that now reads `...; verification=full; prompt=...) ===`. The start line itself is correct; only the assertions are stale. Observed while landing ortus-jlxt, whose diff does not touch that line.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Update the three assertions in tests/test_grind.py to match the current start-line shape, asserting the verification field without pinning the end of the line, so the next additive field does not break them again.

## Non-goals

Do not change the start line's shape or the prompt-variant field. Do not touch the worker-failure marker.

## Concrete locations

tests/test_grind.py — test_grind_start_line_records_verification_mode_default_full, test_grind_start_line_records_verification_mode_flag_wins, test_grind_start_line_records_verification_mode_from_ortusrc.
src/ortus/commands/grind.py — the start-line emitter around the `=== ortus grind started` marker that appends `verification={verification_note}; prompt={prompt_variant_note}) ===`.
src/ortus/core/prompt_audit.py — audit_note(), which supplies the prompt= value.

## Resolved decisions

1. The production line is right; the tests are stale.
2. Assert the field, not the line terminator.

## Compatibility constraints

Keep the `prompt=<variant>` field that ortus-xfw1 added to the grind start line. Update the three verification-mode assertions to accept that additive field (assert `verification=<mode>` without requiring `) ===` immediately after) rather than removing or rewriting the production start-line emitter. Do not break start-line parsers in cost/tail/dashboard that already tolerate trailing `; key=value` fields before the closing `) ===`.

## Ordered steps

1. Run the three tests and capture the current start line.
2. Re-assert on verification=<mode> alone.
3. Re-run them.

## Dependencies

None — ortus-xfw1 (Worker prompt audit behind a flag) is closed and already shipped the `prompt=` field on the start line; this bug only repairs the stale test expectations.

## Edge cases

The flag-wins and ortusrc variants assert different modes; keep each one's mode distinct.

## Plan-gap guidance

If the expected start-line suffix is ambiguous after the change (for example, whether to pin `prompt=` or only `verification=`), match the current start-line format emitted by grind at src/ortus/commands/grind.py (`verification=...; prompt=...) ===`) and update the assertions accordingly. Do not park the issue for human review over that ambiguity.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1 (guards-existing): the three verification-mode start-line tests pass.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind.py -k verification_mode -q`

## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_grind.py -k verification_mode -q`
close_reason: Start-line checks match the verification field through its separator, so the prompt-variant field no longer breaks them

The claim is reverted to open, the label is kept, and the packet is untouched. An issue labelled human is the operator's: repair or unlabel it before a worker can take it.

comments.text: The three verification-mode start-line checks now match each mode's value up to the semicolon that ends that field, instead of pinning the closing parenthesis. The start line is an open-ended list of semicolon-separated fields, so an appended field no longer falsifies a correct line, and matching through the separator keeps the pinned-full and flag-override modes distinct. The shared recording helper's docstring records the convention. Criterion check AC-1 passed: uv run pytest tests/test_grind.py -k verification_mode -q (3 passed).

title: Route the worker phase in cost.py through the lifecycle declaration
description:
## Objective

Make `tests/test_core_lifecycle.py::test_no_bare_phase_literals` pass again by having `src/ortus/core/cost.py` name the implement phase through the shared lifecycle/profile declaration instead of a bare string literal.

## Behavioral context

Before: the bare-phase-literal gate fails on HEAD. `src/ortus/core/cost.py:70` declares `_WORKER_PHASE = "implement"` and line 551 reads the profile table with it, so the fast gate reports one failure (`journal phases must not be written; live grind does not persist them: src/ortus/core/cost.py:70`) on a clean tree, independent of any working-tree change. After: cost telemetry resolves the same phase from the declared phase enum, the gate passes, and the cost rollup keeps attributing worker usage to the implement profile exactly as it does now.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

- Replace the bare `"implement"` literal in `src/ortus/core/cost.py` with the declared phase value the rest of the codebase uses.
- Keep the profile lookup at `src/ortus/core/cost.py:551` resolving the same table entry.
- Leave the lifecycle gate itself unchanged; it is the contract, not the defect.

## Non-goals

- Changing what the cost rollup measures or which buckets it writes.
- Loosening or re-scoping `test_no_bare_phase_literals`.
- Touching the prompt-audit flag or any other worker-prompt surface.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/core/cost.py` — `_WORKER_PHASE` (line 70) and its single reader near line 551 (`profiles.get(_WORKER_PHASE, (None, None))`).
- `src/ortus/core/profiles.py` — `Phase` enum, whose `Phase.IMPLEMENT.value` is the declared spelling.
- `src/ortus/core/lifecycle.py` — the declaration side the gate protects.
- `tests/test_core_lifecycle.py` — `test_no_bare_phase_literals`, the failing gate.
- `tests/test_cost_telemetry.py` — the rollup contract that must stay green.

## Resolved decisions

- The gate is right and the literal is the defect: phases are declared once and read from the declaration.
- The profile table is keyed by the phase value, so `Phase.IMPLEMENT.value` is a drop-in replacement rather than a schema change.

## Compatibility constraints

- Cost log parsing and the buckets in `src/ortus/core/cost.py` keep their current shape; a grind log written before this change still parses.
- Linux and macOS only, as elsewhere in the project.

## Ordered steps

1. Read the phase declaration in `src/ortus/core/profiles.py` and confirm the value the profile table is keyed by.
2. Replace the bare literal in `src/ortus/core/cost.py` with that declared value, keeping the module-level name and its docstring.
3. Run the gate and the cost rollup tests.

## Dependencies

None — the literal arrived with the token-bucket work in commit 36a7089 and nothing else blocks the fix.

## Edge cases

- An import of `profiles` into `cost` that creates a cycle: resolve it with a local import inside the reader rather than reintroducing the literal.
- A second bare phase literal elsewhere in the module: the gate names every offender, so fix each one it lists.

## Plan-gap guidance

If the profile table turns out not to be keyed by the declared phase value — so the substitution would change which profile the rollup reads — record PLAN-GAP naming the table and its key type, and stop rather than guessing at a mapping.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1: the bare-phase-literal gate passes. `uv run pytest tests/test_core_lifecycle.py -k bare_phase_literals -q`
- AC-2: the cost rollup still attributes worker usage to the implement profile. `uv run pytest tests/test_cost_telemetry.py -q`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_core_lifecycle.py tests/test_cost_telemetry.py -q`
close_reason: Cost telemetry resolves the implement phase from the Phase enum; the bare-phase-literal gate passes and the rollup still attributes worker usage to the implement profile.

comments.author: who
comments.text:
Done. `src/ortus/core/cost.py` now resolves `_WORKER_PHASE` from `Phase.IMPLEMENT.value` instead of a bare string, so the phase is read from the declaration the gate protects. The profile table stays keyed by the same spelling: the marker line grind writes renders `Profile.display_name`, which interpolates `self.phase.value`, so the lookup near the window opener resolves the identical entry and the rollup attributes worker usage to the implement profile exactly as before. No cycle — `profiles.py` imports nothing from ortus.

AC-1 passes: uv run pytest tests/test_core_lifecycle.py -k bare_phase_literals -q (1 passed). AC-2 passes: uv run pytest tests/test_cost_telemetry.py -q (13 passed). Targeted set: uv run pytest tests/test_core_lifecycle.py tests/test_cost_telemetry.py -q (20 passed). The gate named cost.py as its only offender before the change and names none after.

title: Load ~/.config/ortus/.env for TYPESAFE_API_KEY across projects
description:
## Objective
Ortus loads a user-level environment file at `~/.config/ortus/.env` into the process environment (without logging values) so secrets such as `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` are available to the Jev/TypeSafe judge across reboots and all projects without per-job shell sourcing.

## Behavioral context
Before: Ortus docs tell operators to inject `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` via the process environment or an existing user environment file, but Ortus has no dotenv loader. After a host reboot, herdr-started `ortus grind --judge` processes often lack the key even when `~/.config/ortus/.env` already contains a nonempty `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, producing `judge proceed reason=service_failure failure=key_missing` while `failure_mode=open` continues without Jev.
After: On grind/plan/validate/check (and any other entry that constructs the TypeSafe judge or reads judge env), Ortus loads `~/.config/ortus/.env` if present into `os.environ` for missing keys only (or documented merge rules), never prints secret values, and never requires the key inside `.ortusrc` or repo-checked-in files. Existing process env values still win over the file.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Add a small user-env loader used before TypeSafe/Jev needs `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, documented in `docs/judge.md`, with unit tests. Likely modules: `src/ortus/core/judge_typesafe.py` and/or a shared helper near config startup; call sites that currently read `os.environ` for the judge.

## Non-goals
Do not put secrets in `.ortusrc`, project `.env` checked into git, beads, or CLI argv. Do not add a mandatory dependency on python-dotenv if a tiny parser for `KEY=VALUE` lines is enough. Do not change Claude/Codex sandbox bypass behavior. Do not require Windows User env vars.

## Concrete locations
- File `src/ortus/core/judge_typesafe.py`, symbols `API_KEY_ENV`, `TypeSafeJudge` key check (`key_missing` when env empty) — CodeGraph.
- File `docs/judge.md` — current text claims no dotenv loader / inject via host runner.
- New or existing helper under `src/ortus/core/` for loading `~/.config/ortus/.env` (CodeGraph for config home path patterns in `src/ortus/core/config.py`).
- Tests under `tests/test_core_judge_typesafe.py` (and related judge env tests).

## Resolved decisions
1. Canonical file path: `~/.config/ortus/.env` (already used on [redacted]2; mode 600 expected).
2. Process environment wins: if `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is already set and nonempty, do not overwrite from the file.
3. Load only when the file exists; missing file is not an error.
4. Never log key values or file contents; tests assert presence/absence behavior only.
5. Prefer a minimal KEY=VALUE parser over adding python-dotenv unless the repo already depends on it.

## Compatibility constraints
Linux/WSL2 and macOS local hosts. Must not break hermetic tests that unset the key. Must not read project-directory `.env` by default (avoids leaking repo-local secrets into Ortus unexpectedly); user-level path only unless a follow-up bead expands that.

## Ordered steps
1. Use CodeGraph to find every path that raises or returns `key_missing` for `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`.
2. Add `load_user_ortus_env(home=...)` (name as fits repo style) that parses `~/.config/ortus/.env` and sets missing keys into `os.environ`.
3. Invoke it before TypeSafe judge construction / key check on grind (and other judge entry points that need the key).
4. Update `docs/judge.md` to say Ortus loads that user file when present; process env still overrides; still never put the key in `.ortusrc`.
5. Add bounded unit tests for missing file, empty key, nonempty file filling env, and non-overwrite of existing env.
6. Stop with PLAN-GAP if product owners decide project-local `.env` must also load — do not invent that scope here.

## Dependencies
None blocking. Motivated by ochw3-judge post-reboot `key_missing` while `~/.config/ortus/.env` already held the key.

## Edge cases
- Quoted values, blank lines, `#` comments in the env file.
- Empty `TYPESAFE_API_KEY=` in file must not clobber a good process env value; if process env is unset, empty file value still yields key_missing.
- Concurrent tests mutating `os.environ` — isolate with monkeypatch.
- File unreadable (permissions) — treat as load failure with a safe diagnostic, never dump contents.

## Plan-gap guidance
If loading user `.env` would violate an existing security invariant documented in AGENTS/judge contracts, stop, record PLAN-GAP with the conflicting text, and route to human rather than logging secrets or reading repo `.env` silently.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1 With process env lacking `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` and a user `~/.config/ortus/.env` containing a nonempty key, the TypeSafe/judge key check no longer reports key_missing solely due to unloaded file: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_judge_typesafe.py -k "env or key or dotenv or user_env" -q`
- AC-2 An already-set nonempty process `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is not overwritten by the file: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_judge_typesafe.py -k "env or key or overwrite or precedence" -q`
- AC-3 Docs state that `~/.config/ortus/.env` is loaded when present and that `.ortusrc` must not hold the secret: `rg -n "config/ortus/\\.env|TYPESAFE_API_KEY|dotenv" docs/judge.md`

## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_core_judge_typesafe.py -q`
close_reason: Implemented user environment defaults for all judge key checks, preserving process precedence and secret-safe diagnostics; criterion checks passed.

comments.author: who
comments.text: Implemented user-only environment loading before pre-turn, semantic, pre-tool and post-turn judge key checks. Nonempty process values win; missing and unreadable files are handled without exposing contents. Hermetic tests isolate the user file. Criterion checks passed: uv run pytest tests/test_core_judge_typesafe.py -k "env or key or dotenv or user_env" -q -n auto --test-timeout=30 (13 passed); uv run pytest tests/test_core_judge_typesafe.py -k "env or key or overwrite or precedence" -q -n auto --test-timeout=30 (13 passed); documentation rg check for config/ortus/.env, TYPESAFE_API_KEY and dotenv exited 0. git diff --check passed.

title: CI: fix hermetic timing gate on grind verification_mode start-line test
description:
## Objective
Make `tests/test_grind.py::test_grind_start_line_records_verification_mode_from_ortusrc` pass the hermetic CI timing gate on ubuntu-latest/py3.11 so main stays green after ortus-1yn0.

## Behavioral context
Before: CI run https://github.com/who/ortus/actions/runs/35670767505 failed only on `pytest (ubuntu-latest / py3.11)` because that hermetic test took 15.33s and the suite fails hermetic tests over 15s unless marked slow. Five other matrix jobs passed; local `uv run pytest tests/test_core_agent.py tests/test_check.py -q` for the sandbox leftovers is green.
After: the test either runs under 15s hermetically or is marked `pytest.mark.slow` (or otherwise excluded from the hermetic gate) in line with repository policy, and the ubuntu/py3.11 hermetic job can pass.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Inspect and fix `tests/test_grind.py::test_grind_start_line_records_verification_mode_from_ortusrc` and any shared hermetic timing enforcement it trips. Prefer a bounded speed fix if cheap; otherwise apply the repository's established `slow` marking pattern used by other grind tests.

## Non-goals
Do not revert ortus-u8zn or ortus-1yn0 sandbox bypass / writable-roots changes. Do not broaden the hermetic suite. Do not change Codex launch argv.

## Concrete locations
- File `tests/test_grind.py`, symbol `test_grind_start_line_records_verification_mode_from_ortusrc` (CI JUnit failure on ubuntu-latest/py3.11, 15.33s).
- Hermetic timing gate that emits `hermetic tests over 15s must be optimized or marked slow` (locate via CodeGraph / repo search from that exact message).
- Nearby grind tests already marked `slow` in `tests/test_grind.py` as the pattern to copy if marking is the chosen fix.

## Resolved decisions
1. Root cause is timing-gate failure, not a functional regression from ortus-1yn0 (JUnit message is explicit; other matrix cells green).
2. Prefer optimizing if a clear wait/sleep/subprocess waste exists; otherwise mark the test `slow` consistently with sibling grind tests.
3. Ship with Claude backend on the ortus seat.

## Compatibility constraints
GitHub Actions hermetic pytest matrix for ubuntu/macOS and py3.10–3.12. Marking `slow` must match how CI selects hermetic vs slow jobs so the test is not silently dropped from all coverage.

## Ordered steps
1. Use CodeGraph to open the failing test and the hermetic >15s enforcement helper.
2. Decide optimize vs `pytest.mark.slow` based on whether the test is inherently multi-second by design.
3. Apply the minimal change; update marks/imports if required.
4. Run a bounded local pytest for that test and the timing-gate unit if one exists.
5. Stop with PLAN-GAP if CI selection rules for `slow` are unclear and marking would remove all coverage.

## Dependencies
None blocking. Triggered by red CI on HEAD `6b24df3` after ortus-1yn0.

## Edge cases
- Flaky timing near 15s on slower runners: prefer mark-slow over brittle micro-optimizations if the test is integration-shaped.
- Do not mark an entire module slow if only this test trips the gate.

## Plan-gap guidance
If the hermetic gate lives only in CI configuration and marking `slow` would exclude the test from every job with no alternate coverage job, stop, record PLAN-GAP with the workflow selectors, and route to human.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

title: Retire inert Codex workspace-write leftovers after sandbox bypass
description:
## Objective
Retire or re-justify the inert Codex workspace-write leftovers that ortus-u8zn made obsolete: the writable-roots carveout on bypassed write launches, and the ortus check expectation that `.codex/config.toml` pins `sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"`.

## Behavioral context
Before: After ortus-u8zn, non-readonly `CodexRunner.build_argv` launches with `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, so `CodexRunner._write_argv` still appending `-c sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots=[...]` is inert config on every write launch. Separately, `ortus check` still requires `sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"` in the repo `.codex/config.toml` and can fail hosts that no longer need that pin.
After: write launches do not carry an inert workspace-write writable-roots override unless a comment documents a retained posture that still uses it, and `ortus check` accepts Codex repos configured for the bypassed launch without demanding a workspace-write pin that argv no longer uses.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Update `CodexRunner._write_argv` in `src/ortus/core/agent.py` and its Codex argv tests in `tests/test_core_agent.py`. Update the Codex `.codex/config.toml` / `sandbox_mode` assertion in `src/ortus/commands/check.py` and matching tests in `tests/test_check.py`.

## Non-goals
Do not reintroduce `--sandbox` on non-readonly Codex argv. Do not change the readonly verifier posture (`--sandbox read-only`). Do not change Claude, Grok, or opencode argv. Do not remove Ortus bwrap/docker precondition checks in `src/ortus/core/sandbox.py`.

## Concrete locations
- File `src/ortus/core/agent.py`, symbol `CodexRunner._write_argv` (CodeGraph: still emits `sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots` after ortus-u8zn bypass).
- File `src/ortus/core/agent.py`, symbol `CodexRunner.build_argv` (posture branch already uses bypass vs read-only; do not regress).
- File `src/ortus/commands/check.py`, symbol that asserts Codex `sandbox_mode` / workspace-write in `.codex/config.toml` (CodeGraph via check Codex path).
- File `tests/test_core_agent.py`, tests asserting writable-roots / write-session git carveout for CodexRunner.
- File `tests/test_check.py`, tests asserting Codex config workspace-write requirement.

## Resolved decisions
1. Product bypass on non-readonly Codex launches is settled by closed ortus-u8zn; this issue only cleans leftovers.
2. Prefer deleting the inert writable-roots override on bypassed write launches over leaving dead `-c` config, unless a concrete remaining Codex posture still requires it — then document that posture in a code comment and keep the override only for that posture.
3. `ortus check` must align with actual launch argv: do not require `sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"` solely because historical write workers used it.
4. A runner constructed with `sandbox_mode="read-only"` still takes the read-only branch and keeps Codex sandbox protection.

## Compatibility constraints
Linux/WSL2 and macOS local grind hosts. After this change, `ortus check` must not fail correctly configured bypass hosts. Existing repos with `workspace-write` in `.codex/config.toml` may keep that file content; check must not require it when Ortus argv bypasses.

## Ordered steps
1. Use CodeGraph on `CodexRunner._write_argv` and the Codex branch of `ortus check` to list every workspace-write assumption.
2. Decide per symbol: delete inert override, or keep with a comment naming the posture that still needs it.
3. Align `check.py` Codex config expectations with bypassed write argv; update `tests/test_check.py`.
4. Update `tests/test_core_agent.py` writable-roots / write-session assertions to match the chosen behavior.
5. Run the bounded targeted tests; fix failures.
6. Stop with PLAN-GAP if removing the override breaks a documented Codex config-only posture that argv cannot express, rather than inventing a new sandbox mode.

## Dependencies
Depends on closed ortus-u8zn (bypass already on main). Code consumers: grind/plan write workers via `CodexRunner`, and `ortus check` for Codex backends.

## Edge cases
- Readonly verifier and `sandbox_mode="read-only"` constructors must keep `--sandbox read-only` and must not gain the bypass flag.
- Repos that still have `sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"` in `.codex/config.toml` must not be forced to delete it if check becomes permissive.
- Live Codex integration tests outside the targeted unit files are out of scope unless a unit assertion cannot cover the check contract.

## Plan-gap guidance
If CodeGraph or tests show a write posture that still requires `sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots` despite the bypass flag, stop, record PLAN-GAP with the exact argv and Codex version, preserve candidate edits, and route to human — do not silently keep inert config without stating why, and do not reintroduce `--sandbox workspace-write` on non-readonly argv.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1 Bypassed Codex write argv does not include an inert sandbox_workspace_write writable-roots override, or the retained override has an adjacent comment naming the posture that still needs it: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_agent.py -k "write_session or writable_roots or codex" -q`
- AC-2 Codex check tests pass without requiring a workspace-write pin that bypassed argv no longer uses: `uv run pytest tests/test_check.py -k codex -q`
- AC-3 Readonly Codex argv still uses sandbox read-only and never the bypass flag: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_agent.py -k readonly -q`

## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_core_agent.py -k "codex or readonly or writable_roots or write_session" -q`
`uv run pytest tests/test_check.py -k codex -q`

title: Codex: pass --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox on worker launch
description:
## Objective
Ortus Codex write workers launch with `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` so nested child processes used by acceptance checks are not killed with EPERM inside the Codex Linux sandbox.

## Behavioral context
Before: `CodexRunner.build_argv` launches `codex exec` with `--sandbox workspace-write` (or configured `sandbox_mode`). Nested `spawnSync` / npm / shell AC checks often fail with EPERM under that sandbox; hello-world Codex grinds (ochw/ochw2) implemented the CLI then labeled PLAN-GAP/human on AC failure.
After: non-readonly Codex argv includes `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` instead of `--sandbox <mode>`, so the same nested AC checks can run. Readonly verifier argv stays `--sandbox read-only`. Claude/Grok backends are unchanged.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Change `CodexRunner.build_argv` in `src/ortus/core/agent.py` so non-readonly launches pass `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`. Update argv snapshot tests under `tests/test_core_agent.py` (and any sibling Codex argv assertions) to expect the new flag. Document the reason in a short comment at the launch site.

## Non-goals
Do not change ClaudeRunner or Grok argv. Do not rewrite hello-world PRD acceptance criteria as the primary fix. Do not require interactive approval prompts. Do not remove Ortus's own bwrap/docker precondition checks in `src/ortus/core/sandbox.py`.

## Concrete locations
- File `src/ortus/core/agent.py`, symbol `CodexRunner.build_argv` (CodeGraph: class `CodexRunner` at line ~118; `build_argv` currently emits `--sandbox` + `read-only` or `self.sandbox_mode`).
- File `tests/test_core_agent.py`, symbols `test_codex_exec_gets_plain_prompt_not_slash_goal`, `test_codex_profile_routes_model_and_reasoning_effort`, `test_codex_unset_profile_preserves_old_argv` (and any other Codex argv assertions CodeGraph lists under callers of `CodexRunner`).
- Related: `CodexRunner.__init__` `sandbox_mode` default `"workspace-write"` — keep the attribute for compatibility but non-readonly `build_argv` must not pass `--sandbox` when using the bypass flag.

## Resolved decisions
1. Product (Andy 2026-09-21): use Codex CLI `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` for Ortus Codex grind/plan write workers. Rationale: trusted local seats; Codex sandbox EPERM blocks nested AC spawn even with `workspace-write` / approval never.
2. Readonly sessions keep `--sandbox read-only` via the existing `readonly=True` branch; do not apply the bypass to readonly verifier argv.
3. When bypass is used, do not also pass `--sandbox <mode>` on the same argv (flags conflict / are redundant).
4. Prefer extending existing argv unit tests over live Codex integration as the default gate for this change.

## Compatibility constraints
- Linux/WSL2 local grind hosts where Codex CLI is already required (`ortus check` / Codex backend). Flag name must match current Codex CLI (`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`).
- Public CLI of Ortus itself is unchanged (`ortus grind --backend codex` still works); only subprocess argv to `codex` changes.
- Stored beads / `.ortusrc` schema unchanged.

## Ordered steps
1. Read `CodexRunner.build_argv` and existing Codex argv tests in `tests/test_core_agent.py`.
2. Change non-readonly argv construction to include `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` and omit `--sandbox` + mode; keep readonly branch as `--sandbox read-only`.
3. Add a one-line comment citing Codex sandbox EPERM on nested spawn/AC and that bypass is intentional for Ortus local write workers.
4. Update argv snapshot assertions to require the bypass flag on non-readonly Codex argv and still require `--sandbox read-only` when `readonly=True`.
5. Run the bounded targeted tests listed in acceptance; fix failures.
6. Stop with PLAN-GAP if Codex CLI rejects combining bypass with other required flags after a smoke argv dry-run, rather than inventing alternate flag spellings.

## Dependencies
None — no blocking bd issues. Code consumers: `make_runner` and grind/plan worker launch paths that call `CodexRunner.build_argv` (CodeGraph callers include grind/plan via `make_runner`).

## Edge cases
- `readonly=True`: must still get `--sandbox read-only`, not the bypass flag.
- `sandbox_mode` constructor override: ignored for non-readonly argv once bypass is always on (document in comment); do not leave stale `--sandbox workspace-write` on argv.
- Codegraph MCP `-c` overrides and `-m` / reasoning effort flags must still append after the bypass flag.
- Missing `codex` binary remains a preflight/`ortus check` concern, not this task.

## Plan-gap guidance
If the installed Codex CLI does not recognize `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, or if readonly verifier behavior regresses when write workers bypass, stop, record PLAN-GAP with the CLI version and exact argv, preserve candidate edits, and route to human — do not invent a different flag spelling or silently keep `--sandbox workspace-write`.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1 Non-readonly `CodexRunner.build_argv` includes `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` and does not include a `--sandbox` pair: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_agent.py -k codex -q`
- AC-2 Readonly `CodexRunner.build_argv` still includes `--sandbox` then `read-only` and does not include `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`: `uv run pytest tests/test_agent.py -k readonly -q`
- AC-3 Comment at `CodexRunner.build_argv` mentions sandbox EPERM / nested spawn and that bypass is intentional: `rg -n "dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox|EPERM" src/ortus/core/agent.py`
- AC-4 Claude/Grok `build_argv` paths are untouched by this change: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_agent.py -k "claude or grok" -q`

## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_core_agent.py -k codex -q`
`uv run pytest tests/test_agent.py -k readonly -q`

comments.author: who
comments.text: Non-readonly Codex launches now carry --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox instead of a --sandbox pair, so the nested processes an acceptance check spawns are no longer killed with EPERM. Readonly verifier argv, and a runner constructed with sandbox_mode=read-only, still get --sandbox read-only and never the bypass; Claude and Grok argv are untouched. The installed Codex CLI lists the flag in codex exec --help, so the plan-gap branch on flag spelling did not apply. Corrected the Codex worker-prompt sandbox note, which asserted the workspace-write premise this change removes. Filed ortus-v2xb for the now-inert sandbox_workspace_write writable-roots override and the ortus check .codex/config.toml workspace-write expectation.

title: Fix CI regressions from ortus-86ui continue-on-leftover on who/ortus main
description:
## Objective

Restore green main `test` workflow hermetic pytest on who/ortus HEAD `f134344` after ortus-86ui (Resume a stalled claim in the running loop) changed the grind outer loop to continue in-process on leftover in_progress claims.

## Behavioral context

Before: Actions run https://github.com/who/ortus/actions/runs/35544851932 (ortus-h6l7) succeeded on prior HEAD. After push `f134344`, Actions run https://github.com/who/ortus/actions/runs/35547971118 fails pytest (ubuntu-latest / py3.12) with 7 failed, 2324 passed: bare journal phase literal in `_escalate_wedged_claim`, and several grind/judge hermetic tests that expect a single worker window now loop or hang (Expected run called once, Called 4 times; TimeoutError exceeded 180s on post_service_failure_keeps_claim). After this fix: those seven tests pass under the hermetic gate and the continue-on-leftover product behavior remains intact for real leftover claims.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Repair the ortus-86ui continue path so hermetic CI is green again without reverting the product rule that one grind process keeps chewing leftover in_progress claims. Two concrete breakages on HEAD f134344: (1) `_escalate_wedged_claim` writes journal phase='startup' which violates the no-bare-phase-literals contract in tests/test_core_lifecycle.py; (2) outer-loop continue causes extra `run` invocations / infinite-looking windows in mocked hermetic tests that previously ended after one no-close window. Prefer fixing production control flow and phase tagging so tests and product agree; update tests only when they assert the old one-window death behavior that ortus-86ui intentionally removed.

## Non-goals
Do not revert ortus-86ui continue-on-leftover. Do not paste secrets from CI logs. Do not expand into full multi-hour local matrix as the default worker loop. Do not change diamond/Jev policy.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` ? leftover resume / outer loop continue (~1896+), `_escalate_wedged_claim` (~1979 phase='startup'), `_WEDGED_WINDOW_THRESHOLD`
- `tests/test_core_lifecycle.py::test_no_bare_phase_literals`
- `tests/test_grind_judge.py` ? timeout/attribution cases failing after continue
- `tests/test_judge_post.py` ? leaves_claim_and_counter, watchdog/handshake, shadow baseline, post_service_failure_keeps_claim
CodeGraph/Read fallback: `rg -n "_escalate_wedged_claim|_WEDGED_WINDOW_THRESHOLD|for the next window|resume_no_close" src/ortus/commands/grind.py tests`

## Resolved decisions
1. Actions run https://github.com/who/ortus/actions/runs/35547971118 job pytest (ubuntu-latest / py3.12) on HEAD `f134344dea9b78486955d19e6a89501f7f82516e` is the authoritative bug signal.
2. Keep product rule: one `ortus grind` owns the backlog and continues in-process on leftover claims (ortus-86ui).
3. Fix production so no live grind path writes bare journal phase literals; make hermetic mocks terminate under the new continue semantics without requiring the old process-exit-on-leftover behavior.

## Compatibility constraints
Linux and macOS; Python 3.10-3.12 hermetic gate. Continue-on-leftover must still resume the same claim for the next window in live grinds. Escalation, caps, and human halts remain honored.

## Ordered steps
1. Reproduce the seven failures: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_lifecycle.py::test_no_bare_phase_literals tests/test_grind_judge.py::test_timeout_preserves_consumed_claim_and_records_outcome tests/test_grind_judge.py::test_attribution_ignores_unrelated_close tests/test_judge_post.py::test_grind_leaves_claim_and_counter_for_next_window tests/test_judge_post.py::test_grind_watchdog_is_a_fact_and_handshake_failure_wins tests/test_judge_post.py::test_grind_shadow_preserves_baseline tests/test_judge_post.py::test_grind_post_service_failure_keeps_claim -q --test-timeout=180`.
2. Remove or retarget the bare `phase='startup'` write inside `_escalate_wedged_claim` so test_no_bare_phase_literals passes.
3. Adjust outer-loop continue / mock harness so hermetic tests that leave a claim for the next window do not spin unbounded `run` calls; preserve live resume behavior.
4. Re-run the seven named tests (and a narrow leftover-related grind suite if touched) and push the fix.

## Dependencies
None ? standalone CI regression from ortus-86ui landing; queue was otherwise drained.

## Edge cases
1. A true leftover in_progress after a worker window must still become the next iteration resume target without exiting the process.
2. Wedged-claim escalation after threshold must not introduce forbidden journal phase literals.
3. Service-failure / watchdog / shadow post_turn paths must keep the claim when required without hanging past hermetic timeouts.

## Plan-gap guidance
If fixing CI requires reverting the locked one-grind-owns-backlog continue rule or inventing a new human-only policy for leftover claims, stop: comment PLAN-GAP with conflicting commit/bead evidence, label human, and leave the issue in_progress for operator/planning instead of improvising a contract change.

- AC-2: the six grind/judge CI failures pass ? `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_judge.py::test_timeout_preserves_consumed_claim_and_records_outcome tests/test_grind_judge.py::test_attribution_ignores_unrelated_close tests/test_judge_post.py::test_grind_leaves_claim_and_counter_for_next_window tests/test_judge_post.py::test_grind_watchdog_is_a_fact_and_handshake_failure_wins tests/test_judge_post.py::test_grind_shadow_preserves_baseline tests/test_judge_post.py::test_grind_post_service_failure_keeps_claim -q --test-timeout=180`

title: Grind must continue in-process through leftover claims (Codex one-window death)
description:
## Objective
Make one `ortus grind` process continue through leftover `in_progress` claims so it chews an entire backlog without exiting after a single no-close Codex (or any backend) worker window.

## Behavioral context
Before: a worker that leaves a claim `in_progress` causes grind to log "left <id> in_progress for the next window" and `break` the outer loop. The process exits with iters_run=1. Operators must re-invoke grind (or wrap Herdr in a restart loop). Codex often ends a window in ~60s with no close and no new commits on main, so long Codex runs die repeatedly even when git remotes exist and branch-guard reports in sync with origin/main (Daymark A/B repro 2026-09-20). After: the same grind process continues to the next iteration, resumes the leftover claim, and keeps going until the queue drains, wedged-claim human escalation, or a legitimate halt/cap.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Change the outer-loop control flow in `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` so leftover `in_progress` after a worker window continues the loop instead of breaking. Update comments and leftover happy-path user messaging that currently tell operators to run `ortus grind` again. Add or adjust automated tests for continue-vs-break. Preserve wedged-claim escalation and all legitimate exit paths.

## Non-goals
None ? not changing Codex provider prompts, not changing `_WEDGED_WINDOW_THRESHOLD` value, not adding Herdr restart responsibility, not fixing false PLAN-GAP-on-no-remote (already separate), not changing judge diamond-model policy.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` ? outer loop after `left {judged_id} in_progress for the next window` (approx lines 2674?2680): replace `break` with `continue`; rewrite the "One context window per leftover claim / next grind invocation" comment; update the final leftover progress message that says `next: run ortus grind again`.
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` ? `_WEDGED_WINDOW_THRESHOLD` and `_record_no_close_window` / resume no-close counter path must remain the escalation mechanism.
- Tests under `tests/` that cover grind outer-loop leftover behavior (grep/Read for existing leftover / no-close tests; extend or add `test_grind` coverage for continue-not-break). Fallback if CodeGraph empty: `rg -n "for the next window|no-close window|_WEDGED_WINDOW" tests src/ortus/commands/grind.py`.

## Resolved decisions
- Product lock (Andy 2026-09-20): one `ortus grind` process owns and chews the whole backlog; Herdr is only the seat and must not restart/reinvoke grind.
- "Next window" means the next iteration inside the same process, not a new process.
- Temporary Daymark bash restart loops are operator bandage only and are not the product fix.

## Compatibility constraints
CLI surface of `ortus grind` stays the same. Exit codes for real failures unchanged. Behavior change: leftover in_progress no longer ends the process. Scripts that assumed one-window-then-exit will see longer-lived grind processes (intended).

## Ordered steps
1. Locate the `break` after the leftover in_progress log in `grind.py` and change it to `continue`.
2. Rewrite comments so they describe in-process continuation; remove language that the next invocation is the next window.
3. Update leftover happy-path `output.progress` messaging so it does not instruct re-invocation as the normal backlog path.
4. Find or add a unit/integration test that asserts the outer loop continues on leftover in_progress and still exits on queue drain / wedged escalate.
5. Run the bounded targeted tests for the changed grind path.
6. Confirm Daymark-style scenario (remote present) is addressed by continue, not by Herdr.

## Dependencies
None ? self-contained grind outer-loop control flow. Callers: `ortus grind` CLI only. No bead dependency required.

## Edge cases
- Fresh claim left in_progress (first window): must continue, not exit.
- Resumed leftover with commits on integration branch: reset no-close counter and continue.
- Resumed leftover with no commits: increment no-close counter; at threshold escalate to human and stop resuming that claim per existing policy.
- Queue empty after continue: drain exit still works.
- `--iterations` / `--tasks` caps: still exit when reached.
- HALT / judge human / BackendError / multi-leftover PLAN-GAP: still abort.
- Multiple leftover claims at startup: existing multi-leftover human path unchanged.

## Plan-gap guidance
If tests reveal that changing `break` to `continue` interacts with flock, journal discard, or bind_worker in a way not covered above, stop, comment `PLAN-GAP` on the issue, preserve candidate state, and route to planning ? do not invent a Herdr restart contract.

title: macOS CI red: ingest packet-gap assertion breaks on rich's 80-column wrap
description:
## Objective

Make `tests/test_ingest_cli.py::test_ingest_missing_packet_section_errors_before_validation` pass on every CI matrix cell by asserting the packet-gap wording against flattened stderr, so the length of the runner's tmp path can no longer split the phrase across rich's wrap.

## Behavioral context

Before: run 34059163435 on main (HEAD 48427b1) is red on all three macOS cells — py3.10, py3.11, and py3.12 — with this single failure each while 1331 tests pass. `assert "acceptance.md or acceptance_criteria.md" in result.stderr` is false because the captured stderr reads `packet /private/var/folders/.../packet has no acceptance.md or \nacceptance_criteria.md`: rich wraps `output.error` at the 80-column default of a non-TTY console, and the long macOS `/private/var/folders/<hash>/T/pytest-of-runner/...` path pushes the phrase across the break. The three ubuntu cells pass only because `/tmp/pytest-of-runner/...` is short enough to keep the phrase on one line — the same test is one path-length change away from red there too. Reproduced locally at `COLUMNS=80` with a macOS-length `--basetemp`: identical AssertionError.

After: the test asserts the same contract — exit code 1, both acceptance file names reported, empty stdout, no bead written — against wrap-independent text, and main is green on macOS.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

- Route the packet-gap assertion in `test_ingest_missing_packet_section_errors_before_validation` through the file's existing `_flat()` helper, which already strips CSI sequences and collapses wrapping for the stdout help tests.
- Give the sibling stderr assertions in the same file the same treatment, so the next long-path message does not reopen this bug on a different line.
- Keep every assertion's contract identical: same exit codes, same required wording, same "no bead was written" checks.

## Non-goals

- No change to `src/ortus/commands/ingest.py` or the `PacketError` wording; the CLI behaviour under test is correct.
- No change to `src/ortus/core/output.py` console width or wrapping. Wrapping to terminal width is intended for human stderr; if this class of breakage shows up outside the ingest tests, a repo-wide fix belongs in its own bead.
- No global pytest/conftest terminal-width override.

## Concrete locations

CodeGraph (`codegraph explore "output.error rich Console stderr wrapping ingest PacketError read_packet_dir"`) traces the failing path as `ingest` (src/ortus/commands/ingest.py:155) -> `load_packet` (:92) -> `read_packet_dir` (:53), with `output.error` (src/ortus/core/output.py:38) carrying 27 callers across the command surface.

- `tests/test_ingest_cli.py:203` `test_ingest_missing_packet_section_errors_before_validation`; the failing assertion is line 215. Sibling raw-stderr assertions: lines 127, 242, 254, 277, 290.
- `tests/test_ingest_cli.py:64` `_strip_ansi` and `:71` `_flat` — the helpers added by ortus-w9mw for the stdout help tests; both apply unchanged to stderr.
- `src/ortus/commands/ingest.py:74` raises `PacketError(f"packet {directory} has no {wanted}")` — the message that embeds the tmp path — and `:210` renders it through `output.error`.
- `src/ortus/core/output.py:23` `_err = Console(stderr=True)` — no width override, so a captured (non-TTY) console wraps at 80 columns. This is the wrap source, and it stays as it is.

## Resolved decisions

- Fix the assertion, not the CLI. `ortus ingest` already does the right thing: exit 1, the gap named, nothing written. Only the raw-substring check is terminal-width dependent. This is the same call ortus-w9mw (48427b1) made for the help tests.
- Reuse `_flat`/`_strip_ansi` rather than adding a second helper; that commit already proved the pattern on this file.
- Do not pin a wide `CliRunner` terminal width. It hides the wrap instead of making the assertion wrap-independent, and it does not cover output captured from a subprocess.

## Compatibility constraints

- Must pass on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest across py3.10, py3.11, and py3.12, and locally where tmp paths are short.
- ortus stderr stays human-formatted rich output. Nothing in the suite may start treating unwrapped stderr as a machine-readable contract.

## Ordered steps

1. Reproduce with a wrap-forcing path: `env COLUMNS=80 uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q -k missing_packet_section --basetemp=/tmp/private/var/folders/d8/hvxvltxn0fl4rmnd52sncbth0000gn/T/pytest-of-runner/pt` and confirm the AssertionError names the split phrase.
2. Assert against `_flat(result.stderr)`; leave the exit-code, empty-stdout, and `_open_ids` checks as they are.
3. Apply the same flattening to the sibling stderr assertions in the file.
4. Re-run bounded: `uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q` plus the step-1 reproduction; both green.

## Dependencies

None blocking. Same failure class as closed ortus-w9mw (48427b1), which flattened the stdout help assertions and left this stderr assertion raw. Builds on shipped `ortus ingest` (ortus-82bn / 2599c18).

## Edge cases

- A path long enough to wrap twice, or to break inside a token (`acceptance_criteri` / `a.md`). Whitespace flattening cannot repair an intra-token break; if CI ever shows one, assert the two file names separately rather than shortening the substring.
- A runner that sets `COLUMNS` to something other than 80, including a very narrow value.
- The stdout assertion in the same test must keep proving stdout is empty; flattening must not be applied in a way that turns whitespace-only stdout into a pass for non-empty output.

## Plan-gap guidance

If the flattened assertion still fails on CI, stop, record `PLAN-GAP`, preserve candidate state, and investigate whether the ingest error wording changed or whether `output.error` is truncating rather than wrapping. Do not weaken the assertion to a shorter substring to get green.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1: `test_ingest_missing_packet_section_errors_before_validation` checks the packet-gap wording against flattened stderr rather than raw `result.stderr` — `rg -n "_flat\(result\.stderr\)" tests/test_ingest_cli.py`
- AC-2: the test passes when the tmp path is long enough to force a wrap — `env COLUMNS=80 uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q -k missing_packet_section --basetemp=/tmp/private/var/folders/d8/hvxvltxn0fl4rmnd52sncbth0000gn/T/pytest-of-runner/pt`
- AC-3: the contract is unchanged — exit code 1, both `acceptance.md` and `acceptance_criteria.md` named, stdout empty, and the repo's open bead ids identical before and after — `uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q -k missing_packet_section`
- AC-4: no sibling stderr assertion in the file still reads raw wrapped text — `uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q`
- AC-5: `src/ortus/commands/ingest.py` and `src/ortus/core/output.py` are unchanged by this bead — `git diff --stat -- src/ortus/commands/ingest.py src/ortus/core/output.py`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q`
close_reason: Ingest CLI stderr substring checks go through _flat so wrap no longer splits the packet-gap phrase

title: Harden ingest help CI assertion against rich/ANSI wrapping
description:
## Objective
Make `tests/test_ingest_cli.py::test_ingest_help_describes_one_command_without_subcommands` pass on GitHub Actions by asserting ingest help flags against flattened, ANSI-stripped help text instead of raw CliRunner stdout.

## Behavioral context
Before: main `test` workflow fails every matrix cell on that one test — `'--packet' in result.stdout` is false on CI while ~1328 other tests pass; locally the flag is present.
After: the help discovery test is CI-stable (same contract: flags present, no create/fill/ready subcommands) and main goes green for this failure mode.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
- Fix `test_ingest_help_describes_one_command_without_subcommands` in `tests/test_ingest_cli.py` to reuse the existing `_flat()` helper (and strip ANSI escapes) before checking `--packet`, `--stdin`, `--title`, `--type`, `--priority`.
- Keep AC intent: single `ortus ingest` verb, those flags advertised, no `ingest create|fill|ready` subcommands.
- Optionally set a wide `CliRunner(terminal_width=...)` if needed for stability; prefer strip+flat over depending on width alone.
- Do not change `ortus ingest` runtime behavior unless a real help registration bug is proven; this bead targets the brittle assertion first.

## Non-goals
- No redesign of ingest UX.
- No changes to release/TestPyPI workflow (`ortus-m5bb`).
- No broad pytest config rewrite.

## Concrete locations

- Optionally a tiny shared `strip_ansi` helper in the same file if not already present

## Resolved decisions
- Root cause treated as CI help-rendering / assertion fragility (rich/typer + raw stdout), not missing `--packet` registration (local help and functional ingest tests show the flag works).
- Match the pattern already used by sibling help tests in the same file.

## Compatibility constraints
- Must keep passing locally and on ubuntu/macOS py3.10–3.12 CI matrix.

## Ordered steps
1. Reproduce assertion style; add ANSI strip + `_flat` (or equivalent) for flag checks.
2. Run `uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q -k help`.
3. Confirm no ingest command code change required; if help truly omits `--packet` on CI after strip/flat, PLAN-GAP and investigate registration.

## Dependencies
- None. Builds on shipped `ortus ingest` (`ortus-82bn` / `2599c18`).

## Edge cases
- ANSI codes inserted inside option tokens on CI.
- Soft wrapping splitting `--packet` across lines.

## Plan-gap guidance
If after strip+flat the flags are still absent from `ingest --help` on CI, stop and investigate Typer option registration / rich rendering rather than weakening the assertion further.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: `test_ingest_help_describes_one_command_without_subcommands` asserts flags on flattened ANSI-stripped help (not raw rich stdout alone).

## Targeted tests

title: opencode Q1: prove headless opencode drives the local model with tool use, JSON stream, MCP, and a sandbox posture
description:
## Objective

Record verified findings, before any runner leaf, on whether headless `opencode run` can serve as a grind worker driver against a local OpenAI-compatible server: it drives the model to a tool call, emits a machine-parseable event stream, registers and calls a CodeGraph MCP tool client-side, exposes a non-interactive read-only posture, and can (or cannot) run git/bd session-close — each as a recorded token, consumed by later leaves that must not guess.

## Behavioral context

Before. opencode 1.18.27 is installed at ~/.opencode/bin/opencode; it writes to ~/.opencode and ~/.local/share/opencode so it cannot run inside the Ortus dev sandbox and must be probed on the host. Its surface is known from --help: `opencode run [message] --format json` emits raw JSON events; `-m provider/model` selects a model; a custom provider is an opencode.json block (`provider.<id>.npm = "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible"`, `options.baseURL`); `opencode mcp` manages MCP servers; `--auto` auto-approves non-denied permissions; `opencode serve`/`acp` are server modes. What is NOT verified: that a custom provider actually drives llama-server on [redacted]2:8080, that the model produces a real tool call opencode executes, the exact JSON event schema (event/type field names) a decoder must read, that a CodeGraph MCP server registers and is called client-side (no namespace shim needed), what non-interactive permission posture yields a read-only verify, and whether a worker can git-commit/bd-close non-interactively.

After. bd memories opencode-q1 (driver + stream), opencode-q1-mcp (MCP client-side call), and opencode-q1-sandbox (permission/read-only posture) exist, each starting with a verdict token, capturing the exact opencode version, provider config, event-type names, MCP registration method, and the permission-config shape — enough that OpenCodeRunner and the decoder are written from findings, not guesses.

## Design

See design field.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

An operator-run, host-side probe (opencode cannot run in the dev sandbox). Stand up a scratch repo with an opencode.json custom provider pointing at http://[redacted]2:8080/v1 and the served model id, then run headless `opencode run --format json` across five checks: (1) plain reply, (2) a tool-use task (list files / read a file) confirming opencode executes a model-issued tool call, (3) capture the JSON event stream and enumerate the event-type field names and the assistant/tool/finish shapes a decoder must classify, (4) register the CodeGraph MCP server (opencode mcp add or opencode.json mcp block) and confirm the model calls a codegraph tool with opencode executing it client-side (no namespace drop), (5) determine the non-interactive permission posture that yields tool use for implement and a read-only posture for verify (permission config keys, --auto behavior, and whether an outer bwrap wrap is still wanted). Record findings via bd remember. No Ortus code changes.

## Non-goals

Do not write OpenCodeRunner or any src/ change — findings only. Do not modify the codex-local machinery yet (retirement is a later leaf). Do not decide the final backend NAME here beyond recording a recommendation (keep `local` vs rename `opencode`). Do not benchmark model quality (that is the audition leaf). Do not solve multi-provider or per-phase mixing. Do not probe Windows.

## Concrete locations

Findings consumed by future leaves in src/ortus/core/agent.py (OpenCodeRunner beside LocalRunner), src/ortus/core/runstate.py (event decoder, cf. is_grok_event/_describe_codex_item), src/ortus/commands/check.py and src/ortus/core/codegraph.py (MCP registration, cf. _grok_mcp_registered). Reference adapters: ClaudeRunner/CodexRunner/GrokRunner/LocalRunner in src/ortus/core/agent.py. Probe scratch: a temp git repo on the host with opencode.json. bd memories to write: opencode-q1, opencode-q1-mcp, opencode-q1-sandbox.

## Resolved decisions

1. Server under test is the operator's running llama-server ([redacted]2:8080, model 0bserverx/Qwen3.8-27B-Heretic-Abliterated-Uncensored-GGUF:Q4_K_M) — proven 2026-09-02 to serve /v1/chat/completions and make clean tool calls, so a chat-completions harness should compose without the Responses-wire failures codex hit.
2. Provider config candidate: opencode.json `provider.ortuslocal = { npm: "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", options: { baseURL: "http://[redacted]2:8080/v1" }, models: { "<id>": {} } }`; the probe confirms this exact shape or records the correction.
3. The JSON stream is captured with `--format json` and its event-type vocabulary written down verbatim — the decoder leaf depends on the real field names, not assumed ones.
4. MCP is expected client-side (opencode runs the server and presents flat tools), so the namespace shim must NOT be needed; the probe proves a codegraph call reaches turn completion and records HOW the server is registered (CLI vs config).
5. Sandbox is the load-bearing unknown: record the permission-config keys that (a) allow bash/edit/read for implement and (b) deny writes for verify, and whether grind should additionally wrap opencode in the Claude-style bwrap read-only root. A gap here is a recorded PLAN-GAP, not an assumption.
6. Non-interactive session close: probe whether an opencode worker can run `git commit` and `bd` non-interactively under the chosen posture; if not, that is the same PLAN-GAP shape the codex/grok notes already carry.

## Compatibility constraints

Findings-only: this spike changes no shipped behavior, so every existing backend (claude, codex, grok, local) keeps its current argv, decoder, and tests. The recorded provider config and event-type names become the contract the later runner and decoder leaves must match; if a future opencode version changes --format json, the finding pins the tested version (1.18.27). The probe runs only on the host and writes only to a scratch repo and bd memory — it must not modify the real project, ~/.ortusrc, or any shipped config. bd memory keys are additive and do not collide with the local-backend-* codex findings they supersede.

## Ordered steps

1. On the host, create a scratch git repo with the opencode.json provider block; redirect opencode data dirs if needed so nothing leaks into the real project.
2. `opencode run --format json -m ortuslocal/<id> "Reply with exactly OK"` — confirm the provider drives the model; capture the event stream.
3. Run a tool-use task ("list the files here, then read README.md") and confirm opencode executes a model-issued tool call; save the JSONL.
4. Register CodeGraph MCP; run a codegraph-orientation task; confirm a client-side MCP tool call completes.
5. Exercise permission posture: find the config for auto tool-use (implement) and for read-only (verify); test whether git/bd run non-interactively.
6. Write bd memories opencode-q1, opencode-q1-mcp, opencode-q1-sandbox, each starting with a verdict token (OK / BROKEN / PLAN-GAP) plus the exact config and event-type names.

## Dependencies

Parent ortus-t2kn. Predecessor evidence: bd memories local-backend-q1, local-backend-mcp, local-backend-mcp-decision (the codex-side findings this pivot supersedes). Blocks every build leaf under ortus-t2kn (runner, decoder, check, preflight) — they consume these findings.

## Edge cases

opencode requires network to fetch the @ai-sdk/openai-compatible provider package on first run (npm) — if the host is offline that is a recorded precondition, not a failure. opencode may need an API key env even for a keyless local provider — record the exact keyless config. If the served model id contains characters opencode rejects in `-m provider/model`, record the alias needed. If --format json changes shape between opencode versions, pin the tested version (1.18.27) in the finding.

## Plan-gap guidance

If opencode cannot yield a non-interactive read-only verify posture at all (permissions are TUI-approval-only in headless mode), stop and record PLAN-GAP in opencode-q1-sandbox: grind verification requires a posture that cannot write, and if opencode cannot provide one the pivot needs an outer OS sandbox wrap decided before the runner leaf, not improvised.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1 (proves-new): bd memory opencode-q1 exists, starts with a verdict token, and records the working provider config plus the observed --format json event-type names.
- AC-2 (proves-new): bd memory opencode-q1-mcp exists and records whether a CodeGraph MCP tool call completes client-side and how the server is registered.
- AC-3 (proves-new): bd memory opencode-q1-sandbox exists and records the permission posture for implement (tool use) and verify (read-only), plus the git/bd non-interactive finding.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `bd memories opencode-q1`
- AC-2: `bd memories opencode-q1-mcp`
- AC-3: `bd memories opencode-q1-sandbox`

## Targeted tests

None — spike findings are recorded in bd memory; no repository code changes.
close_reason: All three findings recorded and complete: opencode-q1 (OK: keyless @ai-sdk/openai-compatible provider drives the 27B; -m ortuslocal/<id>; full step_start/step_finish/tool_use/text event schema captured for the decoder), opencode-q1-mcp (OK: client-side MCP, flat tool name codegraph_codegraph_explore, NO shim — the pivot thesis, proven), opencode-q1-sandbox (OK: implement free via headless auto-approve; git/bd non-interactive proven; read-only verify = permission bash:deny for a no-bash verify OR a Claude-style bwrap wrap if bash is needed). Verified 2026-09-03 on the host against llama-server [redacted]2:8080 + the reference 27B. Build leaves t2kn.2-.6 unblocked.

title: local backend Q1/Q2: verify codex exec drives an unauthenticated local provider with an unchanged stream
description:
## Objective
Produce an evidence-backed finding, stored under two bd memory keys, that codex-cli 0.147.0 honours `-c model_provider=ortus_local` against a local OpenAI-compatible server without ChatGPT login, keeps the `--json` event stream shape, and composes the provider `-c` overrides with the CodeGraph MCP `-c` overrides.

## Behavioral context
Before. Nothing records whether `codex exec` will talk to a local server through a custom provider, whether it demands login first, or whether the JSONL stream is unchanged. The runner leaf must not guess. After. `bd memories local-backend-q1` holds `PROVIDER_OK codex=<version> wire_api=responses server=<name> model=<id>` or `PROVIDER_BROKEN <reason>`, and `bd memories local-backend-q2` holds exactly one of `NO_AUTH_NEEDED`, `NEEDS_EXPLICIT_FLAG`, or `LOGIN_REQUIRED`. This issue carries a comment with the exact argv, the isolated `CODEX_HOME`, and the artifact path.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Run one bounded, isolated `codex exec --json` probe against a local server through a custom provider, inspect the JSONL stream and the rollout, classify the two findings, and record them with `bd remember`. Repeat the probe once with the CodeGraph MCP `-c` block added to confirm the overrides compose.

## Non-goals
Do not implement `LocalRunner`. Do not edit `BACKENDS`, config, check, or grind. Do not audition the reference 27B model (that is the Q3 spike). Do not use `--oss` or `oss_provider`; the finding is about the explicit `model_providers` table because `--oss` cannot target an arbitrary base URL.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/core/agent.py` — `CodexRunner.build_argv()` is the consumer of this finding; do not edit it here. It already emits `-c mcp_servers.codegraph.command=...`, `-c mcp_servers.codegraph.args=...`, `-c mcp_servers.codegraph.enabled_tools=...` with `json.dumps` values.
- `src/ortus/core/codegraph.py` — `CodeGraphAdapter.probe()` codex branch builds the `CodeGraphCapability` whose command/args/tools you copy into the second probe.
- `tests/fixtures/codex-exec-events.jsonl` — the stream shape (`thread.started`, `turn.started`, `item.*`, `turn.completed`) the decoders expect.
- bd memory `codex-backend-q1-finding-verified-against-codex-cli` — the isolated-CODEX_HOME method to mirror.

## Resolved decisions
1. Server for this spike: Ollama, already installed (0.23.0, serves `/v1/responses`), with the small tool-capable model `qwen3:4b` pulled by the operator (`ollama serve` then `ollama pull qwen3:4b`). llama-server is audited in Q3; Q1 is about codex, not the server brand.
2. Provider id is `ortus_local`. Argv under test: `codex exec "<one-line no-op task>" --json --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check --color never -c model_providers.ortus_local.name="ortus_local" -c model_providers.ortus_local.base_url="http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1" -c model_providers.ortus_local.wire_api="responses" -c model_provider="ortus_local" -m qwen3:4b`, with `CODEX_HOME` pointing at an empty temp dir (no `auth.json`) and stdin from `/dev/null`.

title: grok backend Q1: verify whether grok -p expands /goal
description:
## Objective

Produce a written, evidence-backed finding that says whether Grok Build
headless mode expands a `/goal` slash command or forwards the string
verbatim, so the runner leaf can pick exactly one termination shape.

## Behavioral context

Before. Ortus has two backends. Claude workers are launched as
`claude -p '/goal …'` and rely on Claude's managed `/goal` Stop hook.
Codex workers are launched as `codex exec '<plain task>'` because
`codex exec` does not expand slash commands (verified 2026-07-18 against
codex-cli 0.144.6). Grok Build documents `/goal` in the TUI
(`~/.grok/docs/user-guide/04-slash-commands.md`) and documents headless
as `grok -p` (`14-headless-mode.md`). Nobody has recorded what
`grok -p '/goal …'` does.

After. A keyed bd memory `grok-backend-q1` holds exactly `EXPANDS` or
`VERBATIM`, and the spike issue carries a comment with the argv used, the
artifact path, and the observation that decided the value. The runner leaf
reads that memory and does not invent a third path.

## Findings

Unrun. The spike worker overwrites this section with EXPANDS or VERBATIM,
the exact argv, and the isolated artifact path. Until that probe lands, do
not treat this paragraph as a finding.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Run a bounded, isolated `grok -p` (or `--single`) probe with a `/goal`
string, inspect the session/init advertisement and the first user-visible
prompt the model received, and record EXPANDS or VERBATIM. Update this
issue and `bd remember --key grok-backend-q1`.

## Non-goals

Do not implement `GrokRunner`. Do not change `BACKENDS`. Do not pass a
literal `/goal` into grind. Do not spend a full implementation worker —
the probe is query-only, no repo edits, no `bd close`. Do not treat
interactive TUI `/goal` as evidence for headless.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/core/agent.py` — `compose_worker_prompt()` is the consumer of
  this finding; do not edit it here.
- `src/ortus/core/claude.py` — `ClaudeRunner.build_argv()` is the Claude
  comparison (`claude -p <prompt>`).
- `~/.grok/docs/user-guide/04-slash-commands.md` — `/goal` contract.
- `~/.grok/docs/user-guide/14-headless-mode.md` — `grok -p` / `--single`,
  `--output-format`, `--verbatim`.

## Resolved decisions

1. Two legal findings only: EXPANDS (headless expands `/goal` the way
   Claude's `-p` does) or VERBATIM (the model sees the literal `/goal …`
   string, like `codex exec`).
2. Evidence must include the exact argv and either (a) a `system/init`
   `slash_commands` list plus proof the host ran the goal driver, or (b)
   the recorded user_message / prompt payload containing the literal
   `/goal` string before any model call.
3. `--verbatim` is a confounder: a probe that passes `--verbatim` cannot
   claim EXPANDS failed. The primary probe omits `--verbatim`.
4. Isolated `GROK_HOME` / temp cwd, matching the Codex Q1 method, so a
   personal `~/.grok` config cannot fake the result.
5. The finding is written to `bd remember --key grok-backend-q1` so later
   leaves do not re-litigate it from a comment.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux + macOS only. The probe must not write into this repository's tree
except the bd comment/memory. No Windows path. Requires a working `grok`
binary and operator auth (`XAI_API_KEY` or an existing Grok login); if
auth is missing, stop and report rather than guessing VERBATIM.

## Ordered steps

1. Read `04-slash-commands.md` and `14-headless-mode.md` and record the
   argv you will run.
2. Create an isolated temp dir and `GROK_HOME`.

   prose about what it thinks `/goal` means.
5. `bd remember --key grok-backend-q1` with exactly that token plus a
   one-line reason, and comment this issue with argv + artifact path.

Blocks the runner leaf. No code callers yet. Comparison surfaces:
`compose_worker_prompt()` and the Codex Q1 memory
`codex-backend-q1-finding-verified-against-codex-cli`.

TUI_ONLY — TUI-only is VERBATIM for Ortus's headless worker.
