comments.author: who
comments.text:
Fixed by giving the whole test session a console wide enough that no ortus
message wraps mid-token, so an assertion on a substring of CLI output no longer
depends on the length of the temporary path it names.

What was actually broken. Rich wraps at 80 columns whenever stdout is not a
terminal, and the parallel runner inserts a popen-gwN segment into every
temporary path. On the Ubuntu legs that moved the break inside the log filename
the plan test matches on, so the rendered pointer read `.../logs/plan` newline
`-20260925-101038.log` and "plan-" was genuinely absent; the macOS legs lost
"goal-prompt.md" the same way. Rendering the zero-issue message at width 80
with a parallel-runner-length path reproduced the split exactly.

The fix. A session-scoped autouse fixture, wide_test_console in
tests/conftest.py, sets COLUMNS for every console built from that point on and
also widens the two module-level consoles in ortus.core.output, which are
constructed when that module is first imported — before any fixture runs — and
which the installed Rich pins at construction when COLUMNS is already set. Both
are handed back when the session ends, so the production width is untouched and
an operator's terminal still wraps to its own width. Neither failing test lost
an assertion and neither was skipped, xfailed or deselected.

The guard. test_zero_issue_message_survives_a_wrapped_log_path renders the
zero-issue message with a parallel-runner-length path through the real emitter
and asserts the whole path survives, then renders the same message through an
80-column console of its own and asserts the token is split there. The second
half means the guard fails rather than passes vacuously if the session width is
ever removed.

No PLAN-GAP. The design's edge case — a test that asserts on wrapping or
truncation on purpose, which a global width would change — does not exist here:
every test that touches wrapped output collapses whitespace to tolerate it, and
tests/test_output.py builds its own wide consoles.

Verification: AC-1 `uv run pytest tests/test_plan.py::test_plan_zero_issues_exits_one
tests/test_grind_completion_contract.py::test_stale_leave_open_prompt_override_rejected_before_spawn -n 4 -q`
(2 passed). AC-2 `uv run pytest tests/test_plan.py tests/test_grind_completion_contract.py -q`
(32 passed). AC-3 `uv run pytest tests/test_plan.py -k wrapped_log_path -q` (1 passed).
Targeted set at -n 4: 47 passed. Because the fixture is session-wide, the
hermetic gate shape `uv run pytest -m "fast or integration" -n auto
--test-timeout=30` also ran: 2761 passed, 29 skipped, all pre-existing skips.

title: Shorten the worker-timeout close test's real wait
description:
## Objective

Cut the real wall-clock wait in tests/test_grind_worker_timeout.py::test_worker_timeout_counts_close_when_worker_hangs_after_closing from its 30-second --worker-timeout to 10 seconds or less, while it still proves that a close landed before a hang survives the watchdog kill. CI goal checked afterwards: that test under 8s on Ubuntu CI (33.9s median today, 36.9s on macOS; 62.9s on Aug 15).

## Behavioral context

Before: the close-then-hang shim runs bd ready, bd update and bd close, then sleeps 120s; the test passes --worker-timeout 30 to leave room for those three Dolt calls, so the test always waits the full 30 seconds for the watchdog. It is the slowest test in the suite on every leg.

After: the shim closes its issue with fewer bd calls (for example claiming and closing the known issue id the test passes to it through an environment variable, instead of listing ready work first), and the timeout is a named module constant _CLOSE_HANG_TIMEOUT_S of 10 or less. The test still asserts the watchdog logged worker TIMEOUT after N seconds, the issue is closed, and grind logged worker closed <id>.

Audit evidence (2026-09-24, read-only test audit): green main runs went from a 9.3m wall / 8.2-8.7m Ubuntu pytest step with 907 tests (run 31893074541, Aug 15) to 18.2m wall / 13.0-14.0m Ubuntu and 15.5-17.6m macOS with 2677 tests (run 36094936392, Sep 24). JUnit shows 195 of about 2700 tests take 1s or more and hold 729s of the 784s Ubuntu per-leg total; the gate runs serially; almost all of that time is spent inside real bd subprocesses (about 1s each on a runner).
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

- tests/test_grind_worker_timeout.py: _CLOSE_THEN_HANG shim and test_worker_timeout_counts_close_when_worker_hangs_after_closing; add module constant _CLOSE_HANG_TIMEOUT_S used for both the flag and the TIMEOUT log assertion.

## Non-goals

- No change to grind's watchdog, SIGTERM/SIGKILL grace or logging.
- The other three worker-timeout tests are not required to change.
- No test is deleted, skipped, xfailed, loosened or re-marked to hit a time target (test-audit skill rule: slow is not a deletion reason); a test that must change keeps every assertion it had, and a merge carries every assertion into the keeper.
- Do not modify, stage or commit the untracked .feature-inbox/ directory or prd/PRD-jev-loop-middleware.md; do not run scripts/reinstall-cli.sh; do not touch ortus-nudo, ortus-2637 or any other agent's seat.
- No machine names, user names or host paths in code, docs, tests or fixtures.

## Concrete locations

- tests/test_grind_worker_timeout.py: _CLOSE_THEN_HANG (~125), _seed_repo(), test_worker_timeout_counts_close_when_worker_hangs_after_closing (~222), make_inline_python_shim from tests/_shims.py.
- src/ortus/commands/grind.py --worker-timeout handling in grind() (unchanged, read for the log text).
- Evidence: audit JUnit medians and --durations output (33.60s call on Ubuntu in run 36094936392).

## Resolved decisions

1. The contract is unchanged: a close that lands before a hang must count after the watchdog kill.
2. Speed comes from fewer bd calls in the shim and a smaller timeout, not from faking the watchdog.
3. The timeout must stay comfortably above the shim's bd latency on a slow macOS runner; 10s is the ceiling, lower only if measured headroom allows.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux and macOS runners, Python 3.10-3.12, parallel-safe under -n auto (contention slows bd, so keep headroom).

## Ordered steps

1. Record this test's current call duration on this machine in the bead notes.
2. Pass the issue id to the shim and cut its bd calls to the minimum that still claims and closes.
3. Introduce _CLOSE_HANG_TIMEOUT_S (10 or less) for the flag and the log assertion.
4. Run the file serially and under -n 4 several times for stability; record the new duration.

## Dependencies

No issue dependency. Consumers: none outside this test file.

## Edge cases

- Under xdist contention the shim's bd close must still finish before the watchdog fires; a flake means the timeout is too tight.
- The shim must still leave the worker hung (sleeping) so the watchdog path, not a clean exit, is exercised.

## Plan-gap guidance

If no timeout of 10s or less is stable under -n 4 on this machine, record PLAN-GAP with the measured bd latency instead of raising the constant or weakening assertions.

title: Cut the bd calls grind makes per loop
description:
## Objective

Reduce how many bd subprocesses one ortus grind loop spawns, in product code, so real grinds and the grind-family tests both get faster: at least halve the bd invocations of a one-iteration grind that leaves a claim in progress, and of the flagged-claim reap path, measured with a PATH bd logger. CI goal checked afterwards: the grind-family JUnit total (tests/test_grind*.py plus tests/regression/test_grind_no_stream_leak.py) drops at least 30% per Ubuntu leg from the audit's baseline (test_grind.py 136s, test_grind_completion_contract.py 33s, test_grind_reap.py 19s, test_grind_orphan_policy.py 25s on Ubuntu).

## Behavioral context

Before: every BdClient method is a fresh bd process opening the embedded Dolt database (about 1s on a runner). A PATH logger around bd on the audit machine counted 37 bd calls for tests/test_grind.py::test_grind_leaves_unfinished_claim_in_progress (13 list, 7 count, 6 show, 3 ready, 2 comments, 2 hooks run, 1 update, plus the session's one template init and create), 82 for test_no_close_counter_resets_on_head_advance (30 list, 16 count, 13 show, 9 comments) and 51 for tests/test_grind_reap.py::test_flagged_claim_is_reaped_within_a_poll_not_timed_out; 99% of each test's wall time was inside bd. The same grind tests grew from about 3.7s to 4.6-5.3s each on Ubuntu CI between Aug 15 and Sep 24 as features added bd reads per loop.

After: within one loop step grind reads each bd view it needs once (for example one bd list --json snapshot answering count_by_status, in_progress_ids, open_ids and closed_ids, and no repeated bd show of the same issue between two points where the worker could have changed it), while every decision that must observe worker changes (done bar, reap reasons, post-window judging) still reads fresh state. Grind's observable behavior, logs and bd writes are unchanged.

Audit evidence (2026-09-24, read-only test audit): green main runs went from a 9.3m wall / 8.2-8.7m Ubuntu pytest step with 907 tests (run 31893074541, Aug 15) to 18.2m wall / 13.0-14.0m Ubuntu and 15.5-17.6m macOS with 2677 tests (run 36094936392, Sep 24). JUnit shows 195 of about 2700 tests take 1s or more and hold 729s of the 784s Ubuntu per-leg total; the gate runs serially; almost all of that time is spent inside real bd subprocesses (about 1s each on a runner).
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

- src/ortus/core/bd.py BdClient: add a snapshot/read path so several derived queries are answered from one bd list --json (and one bd show per issue per step), with explicit invalidation.
- src/ortus/commands/grind.py and src/ortus/core/grind_loop.py: use the snapshot inside one loop step and each reap/done-bar poll; drop duplicate reads of the same view; keep fresh reads where the worker may have mutated state.
- tests/test_grind_bd_budget.py (new): a PATH-prepended bd logger shim (a script that appends one line per invocation, then execs the real bd) wrapped around (a) the one-iteration leave-claim-in-progress scenario from test_grind_leaves_unfinished_claim_in_progress and (b) the flagged-claim reap scenario from test_flagged_claim_is_reaped_within_a_poll_not_timed_out; templates are built before counting starts. Each test asserts its count is at most a hard ceiling equal to half the count the same test measures on the unchanged code; record both counts in the test's comment and the bead notes.

## Non-goals

- No change to what grind decides, logs, writes to bd or commits; no caching across a worker window or across loop iterations.
- No change to bd itself or to the worker prompt.
- No test is deleted, skipped, xfailed, loosened or re-marked to hit a time target (test-audit skill rule: slow is not a deletion reason); a test that must change keeps every assertion it had, and a merge carries every assertion into the keeper.
- Do not modify, stage or commit the untracked .feature-inbox/ directory or prd/PRD-jev-loop-middleware.md; do not run scripts/reinstall-cli.sh; do not touch ortus-nudo, ortus-2637 or any other agent's seat.
- No machine names, user names or host paths in code, docs, tests or fixtures.

## Concrete locations

- src/ortus/core/bd.py: BeadsTracker.run(), BdClient._run(), BdClient.show(), comments(), count_by_status(), in_progress_ids(), open_ids(), closed_ids().
- src/ortus/commands/grind.py: grind(), _done_bar_met(), _reap_reason(), the on_poll reap/handshake callbacks (~3171).
- src/ortus/core/grind_loop.py and src/ortus/core/judge_claim.py: callers of BdClient during a loop step.
- tests/test_grind.py (test_grind_leaves_unfinished_claim_in_progress), tests/test_grind_reap.py (test_flagged_claim_is_reaped_within_a_poll_not_timed_out), tests/conftest.py copy_bd_workspace().
- Evidence: codegraph explore on grind test harness fake worker subprocess poll found the BdClient callers; rg found 34 BdClient read calls in grind.py and grind_loop.py; audit PATH logger counts above.

## Resolved decisions

1. Product change, not only a test change: real grinds pay the same per-call cost.
2. A snapshot lives for one loop step or one poll tick and is invalidated by any grind-side bd write and by the start/end of a worker window.
3. The measure is invocations counted by a PATH logger, the same method the audit used, with a ceiling of half the pre-change count per scenario.

## Compatibility constraints

bd 1.2.1 JSON output (bd list --json, bd show --json); Python 3.10-3.12 on Linux and macOS. The reap poll cadence and every log line stay as they are.

## Ordered steps

1. Write tests/test_grind_bd_budget.py with the logger and run it on unchanged code to record both baseline counts.
2. Add the BdClient snapshot path with invalidation.
3. Route grind's per-step and per-poll reads through it, removing duplicate reads.
4. Set each ceiling to half its baseline and run the budget tests.
5. Run the grind-family suites, then the acceptance checks.

## Dependencies

No issue dependency. The fake-bd/test_core_bd bead depends on this one because it fakes the BdClient surface this bead changes. Consumers: every grind loop path, judge_claim, the done bar, the reap poll, grind-family tests.

## Edge cases

- The worker closes or claims an issue mid-window: the next done-bar or reap check must see it.
- A failed bd read must still surface as today (BdError, tracker-error reap behavior), not as a stale snapshot.
- Excluded labels (human) must still be honored in counts and id sets.
- The logger must count bd calls from grind only after templates exist, so template builds are not in the count.

## Plan-gap guidance

If halving a scenario's count needs grind to observe bd state less often than a decision requires (for example skipping a fresh read the done bar depends on), record PLAN-GAP with the counts reached and the read that cannot be removed, instead of relaxing the ceiling or the decision.

- AC-4: The whole hermetic gate selection stays green under xdist on WSL, with no test failing, erroring or newly skipped. `uv run pytest -m "fast or integration" -n auto --test-timeout=180 -q`

- AC-6: No test was deleted: the gate selection still collects at least 2770 tests (2770 at the starting sha 01ecee3c). `bash -c 'test "$(uv run pytest --collect-only -q -m "fast or integration" | grep -c ::)" -ge 2770'`

## Targeted tests

uv run pytest tests/test_grind_bd_budget.py tests/test_grind.py tests/test_grind_reap.py -n auto -q
close_reason: One tracker reading per decision: the leftover-claim window spends 14 bd invocations against 31, the flagged-claim reap 21 against 44, each under a ceiling of half its pre-change count

comments.author: who
comments.text:
**Changes**:
- BdClient gained a snapshot read path: one `bd list --all --limit 0 --json --brief` reading answers count_by_status, in_progress_ids, open_ids and closed_ids, and memoizes show/comments per issue. Any write through the client invalidates it; `no_snapshot()` suspends it across a turn another process runs.
- grind groups its repeated reads into one reading per decision: startup claims + initial counts, the step's before-counts + closed ids, the three pre-window baselines, each reap poll tick, the post-mortem read-back through the stuck decision, and the exit summary. `_flagged_claims` confirms a candidate via `labels_of` rather than a second `bd show`, and the duplicate show between selecting a work spec and pinning it is removed.
- New `tests/test_grind_bd_budget.py` counts invocations with a PATH bd logger around both scenarios.

**Verification**: AC-1 `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_bd_budget.py -k leftover -q` (1 passed); AC-2 `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_bd_budget.py -k reap -q` (1 passed); AC-3 the seven grind/judge suites under `-n auto` (130 passed, 26 skipped, all pre-existing); AC-4 `uv run pytest -m "fast or integration" -n auto --test-timeout=180 -q` (2743 passed, 29 skipped, 0 failed); AC-5 the tests/ diff adds no skip/xfail/importorskip marker beyond the bd-not-on-PATH guard; AC-6 the gate collects 2772 tests (>= 2770).

Measured budgets: leftover claim 31 -> 14 invocations (ceiling 15, half of 31); flagged-claim reap 44 -> 21 (ceiling 22, half of 44). No decision reads less often than it needs: readings never span a worker window or a triage re-spec turn, and a write drops the reading it invalidates.

Follow-up filed: ortus-6c86 reads the grind-family CI wall clock on a green main Ubuntu leg against the audit baseline, which is the part of the objective a local invocation count cannot answer.

title: Stop running a real bd init in every init test
description:
## Objective

Make tests/test_init.py and tests/test_init_flags.py stop spawning a real bd init per test, keeping about five tests (four to six) that deliberately run the real bd as the init contract owners, marked with a registered real_bd marker. CI goal checked afterwards: test_init.py plus test_init_flags.py under 40s per Ubuntu leg (182s today).

## Behavioral context

Before: test_init.py (66 tests) and test_init_flags.py (25 tests) run ortus init through CliRunner against the real bd, so 64 of them cost 1.5-3s each on CI (182s per Ubuntu leg, 207s per macOS leg); test_init.py had 19 tests on Aug 15 and is the single biggest growth file (+94s Ubuntu, +117s macOS). Locally one init test spent 8.3s in two real bd init calls. Most of these tests assert rendered files, .ortusrc facts, managed blocks and gitignore splicing, not bd behavior.

After: an autouse fixture in those modules replaces init's bd init step with a copy of the session's bare bd template (tests/conftest.py copy_bd_workspace) re-prefixed as init would, for every test not marked real_bd. Four to six real_bd tests keep the real contract: --non-interactive is passed, the prefix is respected, init completes with closed stdin, and a bd failure is surfaced clearly (plus at most two more if needed). Every assertion is kept.

Audit evidence (2026-09-24, read-only test audit): green main runs went from a 9.3m wall / 8.2-8.7m Ubuntu pytest step with 907 tests (run 31893074541, Aug 15) to 18.2m wall / 13.0-14.0m Ubuntu and 15.5-17.6m macOS with 2677 tests (run 36094936392, Sep 24). JUnit shows 195 of about 2700 tests take 1s or more and hold 729s of the 784s Ubuntu per-leg total; the gate runs serially; almost all of that time is spent inside real bd subprocesses (about 1s each on a runner).

v1

- Keep test_init_under_five_seconds meaningful (it already excludes bd time; it may be one of the real_bd tests).

## Non-goals

- No change to ortus init product behavior and no new production seam; patch existing module attributes only.
- tests/test_cli_verbs.py progress-line tests are out of scope (the merge bead owns them).
- No test is deleted, skipped, xfailed, loosened or re-marked to hit a time target (test-audit skill rule: slow is not a deletion reason); a test that must change keeps every assertion it had, and a merge carries every assertion into the keeper.
- Do not modify, stage or commit the untracked .feature-inbox/ directory or prd/PRD-jev-loop-middleware.md; do not run scripts/reinstall-cli.sh; do not touch ortus-nudo, ortus-2637 or any other agent's seat.
- No machine names, user names or host paths in code, docs, tests or fixtures.

## Concrete locations

- src/ortus/commands/init.py: _bd_init() (line 70), _codegraph_index() (259), _backend_cli, probe_models (already faked by autouse fixtures).
- tests/test_init.py: autouse fixtures _require_bd, _fake_codegraph, _fake_backend_clis, _fake_local_probe; test_prefix_is_respected, test_default_prefix_is_dir_basename, test_init_passes_non_interactive_to_bd, test_init_completes_with_closed_stdin, test_init_surfaces_bd_failure_clearly, test_init_under_five_seconds.
- tests/test_init_flags.py; tests/conftest.py copy_bd_workspace(), BD_TEMPLATE_PREFIX; pyproject.toml markers.

## Resolved decisions

1. Fake at the _bd_init boundary with a real bd workspace copied from the session template, so downstream init steps see a genuine .beads directory.
2. Four to six real_bd tests own the bd contract; everything else is about rendering.

## Compatibility constraints

2. Register the real_bd marker.
3. Add the autouse fake for unmarked tests; mark the contract tests real_bd.
4. Fix any test that relied on real-bd side effects, keeping its assertions.
5. Run both files and the acceptance checks.

- --force re-init over an existing .beads must still take the same code path.
- Tests that re-patch _bd_init themselves (failure surfacing) must win over the autouse fake.

## Plan-gap guidance

If more than six tests genuinely assert real bd behavior, record PLAN-GAP listing them rather than faking a bd contract.

title: Run the CI pytest gate in parallel with an honest duration budget
description:
## Objective

Run the comprehensive hermetic pytest gate in .github/workflows/test.yml with pytest-xdist (-n auto) on every matrix leg while keeping --enforce-duration-budget on, scaled for contention, so the suite's subprocess-bound tests run concurrently. Any test that fails under xdist is made parallel-safe, never skipped. CI goal checked afterwards: Ubuntu pytest step under 7 minutes and macOS under 9 minutes on three consecutive green main runs (today about 13.2 and 17.4 minutes median).

## Behavioral context

Before: the gate runs serially (uv run pytest -m "fast or integration" --test-timeout=180 --enforce-duration-budget ...). pytest-xdist 3.8.0 is already a dev dependency but deliberately left out of the gate because contention inflates per-test durations against the 5s budget (x3 in CI via ORTUS_TEST_BUDGET_SCALE). Worker and verifier sweeps already run -n auto, and the bd template harness in tests/conftest.py is per-process by design. A local measurement on the audit machine: tests/test_core_bd.py plus tests/test_init_flags.py (46 tests) took 192.7s serially and 61.3s with -n 4.

After: the gate command carries -n auto (4 workers on ubuntu-latest, 3 on macos-latest), --enforce-duration-budget stays, and ORTUS_TEST_BUDGET_SCALE for the gate is raised to 5 (a 25s cap) so contention does not manufacture breaches while a pathological test still fails. The --test-timeout per-test guard still works on xdist workers. Every test in the selection passes under xdist.

Audit evidence (2026-09-24, read-only test audit): green main runs went from a 9.3m wall / 8.2-8.7m Ubuntu pytest step with 907 tests (run 31893074541, Aug 15) to 18.2m wall / 13.0-14.0m Ubuntu and 15.5-17.6m macOS with 2677 tests (run 36094936392, Sep 24). JUnit shows 195 of about 2700 tests take 1s or more and hold 729s of the 784s Ubuntu per-leg total; the gate runs serially; almost all of that time is spent inside real bd subprocesses (about 1s each on a runner).

## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

- .github/workflows/test.yml gate step: add -n auto to the uv run pytest command and set ORTUS_TEST_BUDGET_SCALE to '5'; keep --test-timeout=180, --enforce-duration-budget, --durations=20, --junitxml and the coverage flags as they are (the coverage bead moves coverage later).
- Update the explanatory comments in test.yml and the ORTUS_TEST_BUDGET_SCALE comment in tests/conftest.py, the pyproject.toml pytest-xdist comment, and the Verification-to-CI flag parity section of docs/testing.md so they describe the parallel gate.
- Make any test that fails, flakes or collides under -n auto parallel-safe (unique tmp paths, no shared cwd or global env mutation, no fixed ports, per-worker templates), keeping its assertions.
- Confirm the SIGALRM-based pytest_runtest_call timeout in tests/conftest.py still fires on an xdist worker; if it cannot, replace it with an equivalent per-test bound that works under xdist, keeping the node-id message.

## Non-goals

- No serial budget leg (it would keep wall time at the serial 13+ minutes, since run wall time is the slowest leg).
- No change to markers, selection, matrix entries or coverage placement.
- No test is deleted, skipped, xfailed, loosened or re-marked to hit a time target (test-audit skill rule: slow is not a deletion reason); a test that must change keeps every assertion it had, and a merge carries every assertion into the keeper.
- Do not modify, stage or commit the untracked .feature-inbox/ directory or prd/PRD-jev-loop-middleware.md; do not run scripts/reinstall-cli.sh; do not touch ortus-nudo, ortus-2637 or any other agent's seat.
- No machine names, user names or host paths in code, docs, tests or fixtures.

## Concrete locations

- .github/workflows/test.yml: step Run comprehensive hermetic pytest gate (line ~109), env ORTUS_TEST_BUDGET_SCALE (~115), run block (~117-120).
- tests/conftest.py: _DURATION_BUDGET_SCALE, _DURATION_BUDGET, ci_gate_command(), ci_gate_flags(), pytest_runtest_call() (SIGALRM timeout), pytest_runtest_makereport() (budget), bd_template(), copy_bd_workspace(), _templates_root().
- pyproject.toml [project.optional-dependencies].dev pytest-xdist comment; docs/testing.md flag-parity section; tests/test_test_policy.py test_testing_guide_documents_flag_parity.
- Evidence: codegraph explore on pytest fixtures conftest duration budget test timeout surfaced the conftest hooks and the template harness; CI JUnit from runs 31893074541 and 36094936392.

## Resolved decisions

1. Scaled budget, not a serial leg: -n auto on all six legs with ORTUS_TEST_BUDGET_SCALE '5'.
2. -n auto rather than a fixed count, so macOS (3 cores) and Ubuntu (4 vCPU) each use their cores.
3. A test that breaks under xdist is fixed at its owner boundary; skipping or deselecting it is forbidden.
4. The 5s unscaled budget and the slow marker semantics stay unchanged.

## Compatibility constraints

Python 3.10-3.12 on Linux and macOS runners; pytest-cov 5+ supports xdist and combines worker data; junit.xml must still be written (xdist merges reports). The bd template harness builds one set of templates per worker process by design.

## Ordered steps

1. Run the gate selection locally with -n auto and the CI flags to list failures and flakes.
2. Make each failing test parallel-safe at its owner, re-running only that test under -n auto until it is stable.
3. Verify the per-test timeout still fires on a worker (a throwaway local probe, not committed).
4. Edit test.yml (-n auto, scale 5) and the comments/docs named in Scope.
5. Run tests/test_test_policy.py and the acceptance checks.

## Dependencies

Depends on the workflow-timeouts bead (ortus-scb1) because both edit the same test.yml step. The coverage-one-leg bead and the sleep-free budget-probe bead depend on this one. Consumers: tests/conftest.py ci_gate_flags(), tests/test_test_policy.py, docs/testing.md, every worker and verifier sweep that copies the gate flags.

## Edge cases

- Tests that chdir, set process-wide env without monkeypatch, bind ports or write to the repo tree collide under xdist.
- Session-scoped fixtures run once per worker; anything assuming exactly one session (such as bd_init_calls() == 1) must accept one per worker.
- The SIGALRM timer only works in a worker's main thread.
- Coverage data from workers must still combine into coverage.xml.

## Plan-gap guidance

If a test cannot be made parallel-safe without changing what it asserts, or the budget scale needed to stay green locally is above 5, record PLAN-GAP naming the test and measured durations instead of skipping, deselecting or raising the scale.

title: Put job and step timeouts on the CI test workflow
description:
## Objective

Give the pytest job and its comprehensive hermetic pytest gate step in .github/workflows/test.yml explicit timeout-minutes, so a hung leg fails in bounded time instead of burning GitHub's 360-minute default. CI goal checked afterwards: a hung leg fails within 30 minutes of its pytest step starting.

## Behavioral context

Before: test.yml has no timeout-minutes anywhere. Run 35547971118 (Sep 20) had legs that ran from 29 minutes to 5.6 hours, and in run 36041738556 (Sep 24) the macOS py3.12 pytest step ran 48 minutes, never reported completion and left no log or JUnit artifact. The per-test --test-timeout=180 guard is a SIGALRM around the test call only, so a hang in collection, setup, teardown, coverage reporting or a stuck runner is unbounded.

After: the pytest job carries timeout-minutes: 40 and the gate step carries timeout-minutes: 30, and the tagged release-smoke job carries its own job-level timeout-minutes: 60. Healthy legs are unaffected: the slowest green leg in the audit window was 26.5 minutes of pytest step (run 35973719012, Ubuntu py3.10, a slow runner), under the 30-minute step cap.

Audit evidence (2026-09-24, read-only test audit): green main runs went from a 9.3m wall / 8.2-8.7m Ubuntu pytest step with 907 tests (run 31893074541, Aug 15) to 18.2m wall / 13.0-14.0m Ubuntu and 15.5-17.6m macOS with 2677 tests (run 36094936392, Sep 24). JUnit shows 195 of about 2700 tests take 1s or more and hold 729s of the 784s Ubuntu per-leg total; the gate runs serially; almost all of that time is spent inside real bd subprocesses (about 1s each on a runner).

- Keep every existing step, flag and matrix entry byte-identical otherwise.

## Non-goals

- No change to the pytest command, markers, matrix, coverage or budget flags (other beads own those).
- No test is deleted, skipped, xfailed, loosened or re-marked to hit a time target (test-audit skill rule: slow is not a deletion reason); a test that must change keeps every assertion it had, and a merge carries every assertion into the keeper.

title: Label long absolute paths in tool summaries before applying the length cap
description:
## Objective

Make `judge_tools._render` reduce an absolute path argument to its repository-relative form, `[allowed-root]` or `[outside-roots]` before it applies the 120-character `_VALUE_CAP`, so a long absolute path is still labeled instead of collapsing to `<str:N>`, and so tests/test_core_judge_tools.py::test_allowed_roots_do_not_exempt_secret_reads passes on macOS and Linux.

## Behavioral context

Before (HEAD abea098, introduced by ortus-rj8i in 76b196f): `_render` checks `len(value) > _VALUE_CAP` first and returns `<str:N>` for any longer string, and only calls `_label` for shorter strings that start with "/". The label is what keeps host paths out of the judge request, and it is never longer than the repository-relative path, so the cap is applied to the wrong string. On macOS runners pytest's tmp_path is already resolved and long (/private/var/folders/.../pytest-of-runner/pytest-0/test_allowed_roots_do_not_exem0), which makes the test's file path 123 characters; the summary becomes `file_path=<str:123>` and the `[allowed-root]` assertion fails. macOS py3.10, py3.11 and py3.12 each fail exactly this one test out of about 2711 in CI runs 36097326477 (ortus-rj8i) and 36098790470 (ortus-fva5); Ubuntu passes because its tmp_path is short. This is not a symlink problem: both the repo and tmp_path in the failing job are already /private/var paths. The same loss happens on Linux for any absolute path over 120 characters, including a file inside the repository (reproduced: a 127-character in-repo path renders as `<str:127>` instead of its relative path), so the judge loses the one fact the label exists to give it.

After: an absolute string is labeled first; the length cap then applies to the label (a repository-relative label longer than the cap still becomes `<str:N>` or a bounded truncation, never the host path). Non-path strings keep today's cap. The existing test passes on both platforms and a new test pins the long-path case on Linux so it can no longer pass only because the runner's temporary directory is short.

- tests/test_core_judge_tools.py: keep test_allowed_roots_do_not_exempt_secret_reads unchanged in intent; add tests that build an allowed root and an in-repo file whose absolute paths exceed 120 characters (deep directory names under tmp_path) and assert the summary carries `[allowed-root]` and the repository-relative path, never the host path; add a case where the repository-relative label itself exceeds the cap and assert it is bounded and host-free.

## Non-goals

- No change to `_VALUE_CAP`'s value, the destructive-pattern set, the probability vector or grind behavior.
- Do not weaken the test by shortening paths or skipping macOS.
- Do not modify, stage or commit the untracked .feature-inbox/ directory or prd/PRD-jev-loop-middleware.md; do not run scripts/reinstall-cli.sh.
- No machine names, user names or host paths in code, docs, tests or fixtures.

## Concrete locations

- src/ortus/core/judge_tools.py: `_VALUE_CAP` (49), `_label()` (319), `_render()` (337), `_screened()` (352), `inspect_tool()` (373).
- tests/test_core_judge_tools.py: `repo` fixture (13), test_allowed_roots_do_not_exempt_secret_reads (116), summary assertions near 345 and 365.
- CodeGraph evidence: codegraph query allowed_roots -> inspect_tool (judge_tools.py:72 in index), decide_tool, test_allowed_roots_do_not_exempt_secret_reads (tests/test_core_judge_tools.py); codegraph explore on allowed roots and secret reads found no other consumer of the summary label. ## Resolved decisions

1. Product code is wrong, not only the test: the cap must bound what is sent, and what is sent for a path is its label.
2. Labels still never reveal host paths, account names or machine names.
3. Enforcement over prompt advice: the long-path case is pinned by a Linux-runnable test, not by a note about macOS.
4. Jev diamond model unchanged: this only changes the summary text Jev reads, not any gate.

## Compatibility constraints

Python 3.10-3.12 on Linux and macOS. `Path.is_relative_to` is available from 3.9. Summaries for short paths and non-path strings are byte-identical to today.

## Ordered steps

1. Run tests/test_core_judge_tools.py for a green Linux baseline.
2. Add the failing long-path tests (in-repo and allowed-root absolute paths over 120 characters).
3. Reorder `_render` so absolute strings are labeled before the cap and the cap applies to the label.
4. Run the targeted tests until green, then the judge hook and grind hook tests that read summaries.

## Dependencies

## Edge cases

- A relative path longer than the cap stays `<str:N>`.
- A repository-relative label longer than the cap is bounded and host-free.
- `_label` returning `[unresolved]` for an unresolvable path is unchanged.
- A long absolute path to a secret file is still denied by `_literal_reason` before any summary is built.

title: Record a cost for every worker window, including ones grind reaps
description:
## Objective

Make every worker window record a cost, including windows grind reaps after the done bar is met, and let `ortus cost` report cost per closed bead for a whole grind tree (planner plus workers).

## Behavioral context

Before (HEAD 7d44140): `cost._claude_facts` only reads usage and `total_cost_usd` from Claude's final `result` event. `grind._reap_reason` reaps a Claude worker as soon as the done bar is met ("done bar met (..., in sync); reaping worker"), because the /goal Stop hook would otherwise hold it, so the worker is killed before it emits `result`. `ortus cost` then shows null usage and null dollars for those sessions: 0 of 28 sessions in a recent 28-window Claude grind, 0 of 7 in an earlier judge-arm grind, and 0 of 1 in the Shelf A/B arm A run on 2026-09-24. `ortus cost` also reads only logs/grind-*.log, so planner cost needs a separate `--log logs/plan-*.log` call, and cost per closed bead across planner plus workers cannot be computed in one command, which the Jev A/B needs.

After: each Claude assistant event's `message.usage` is accumulated per message id (deduplicated) so a reaped window still has token buckets; the dollar figure comes from the provider's `total_cost_usd` when a result event exists, and otherwise from a versioned price table applied to those buckets and flagged `cost_source: "estimated"`. Grind gives a worker a short bounded grace to flush its result line before the reap signal where that is possible. `ortus cost` gains a whole-tree view that includes plan logs as a planner phase and prints total cost, closed beads and cost per closed bead.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

- src/ortus/core/cost.py `_claude_facts`: for `type == "assistant"` events read `message.id`, `message.model` and `message.usage` (input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, output_tokens). `_Window.absorb` keeps the largest usage seen per message id and sums across ids; when a `result` event arrives its totals and `total_cost_usd` win for that window.
- Cost source: `SessionCost` and `BeadCost` gain `cost_source` with values `provider`, `estimated` or null. A window with no provider dollars gets an estimate from a module-level, versioned price table (USD per million tokens for input, cache write, cache read and output, keyed by model family) and is marked estimated; an unknown model leaves dollars null and the row partial rather than guessing.
- src/ortus/commands/grind.py and src/ortus/core/claude.py: when `_reap_reason` returns a done-bar reason, wait a bounded grace (a few seconds, constant) for the worker's stream to emit its result line before SIGTERM, without changing reap reasons, timeouts or process-group handling.
- src/ortus/commands/cost.py and src/ortus/core/cost.py: add a whole-tree option (for example `ortus cost --tree`) that rolls up logs/plan-*.log as phase planner plus every grind log, and reports planner dollars, worker dollars, total, closed beads and cost per closed bead in text and `--json`, with counts of provider versus estimated sessions.
- docs/cost.md: document per-message usage, cost_source, the price table and the tree view.
- Tests: tests/test_cost_telemetry.py with a reaped-worker fixture (assistant events with usage, no result line) and a plan-log fixture; a grind-level test for the bounded grace.

## Non-goals

- No change to Codex, Grok or OpenCode parsing beyond keeping their current results.
- Do not make the price table a gate or budget limit; it only estimates spend.
- No change to what the done bar means or when a worker is considered finished.
- Do not modify, stage or commit the untracked .feature-inbox/ directory or prd/PRD-jev-loop-middleware.md; do not run scripts/reinstall-cli.sh.
- No machine names, user names or host paths in code, docs, tests or fixtures.

## Concrete locations

- src/ortus/core/cost.py: `_claude_facts()` (208), `EventFacts`, `UsageBuckets`, `_Window.absorb()` (523), `_Window.freeze()` (542), `parse_grind_log()` (584), `rollup_beads()` (687), `find_grind_logs()` (809), `LOG_GLOB`.
- src/ortus/commands/cost.py: the cost command and its `--json` rendering.
- src/ortus/commands/grind.py: `_reap_reason()` (1370, done-bar return near 1406), `_reap_worker()` (3033).
- src/ortus/core/claude.py: the runner's reap/SIGTERM path for the child process group.
- CodeGraph evidence: codegraph query parse_grind_log -> cost.py:584; rollup_beads -> cost.py:687; find_grind_logs -> cost.py:809 (test_find_grind_logs_returns_the_newest_first); _reap_worker -> grind.py:3033.

## Resolved decisions

1. Provider-reported dollars win whenever present; estimates are always labelled estimated and never silently mixed.
2. Per-message usage is deduplicated by message id because Claude repeats the usage block on every content event of one message.
3. An unknown model yields null dollars and a partial flag, never a guessed price.
4. The planner is part of the tree cost because the Jev A/B compares cost per closed bead across planner plus workers.
5. The grace before reaping is bounded and constant so a hung worker cannot extend a window.
6. Enforcement over prompt advice: behavior pinned by fixtures and tests.

## Compatibility constraints

Python 3.10-3.12 hermetic gate. Existing `ortus cost --json` keys stay; new keys are additive. Old logs parse and gain estimated rows where assistant usage exists. `ortus eval` keeps reading the same rollup.

## Ordered steps

1. Run tests/test_cost_telemetry.py for a green baseline.
2. Add a reaped-worker fixture log (harness markers plus Claude assistant events with usage and no result line) and a failing test that its session has no dollars today.
3. Accumulate per-message usage in `_claude_facts` and `_Window`, deduplicated by message id; keep result-event precedence.
4. Add cost_source and the versioned price table with the estimated path.
5. Add the bounded grace before a done-bar reap in grind/claude and a test for it.
6. Add the whole-tree rollup (plan logs plus grind logs) with cost per closed bead in text and JSON.
7. Update docs/cost.md and run the targeted tests until green.

## Dependencies

No open issue dependency. Consumers: `ortus cost`, `ortus eval` (harness_eval reads the rollup), tests/test_cost_telemetry.py, grind reaping.

## Edge cases

- A window with both assistant usage and a result event must not double count.
- Streaming assistant events can repeat one message id with growing output_tokens; keep the largest.
- A result event without usage stays partial.
- Plan logs without harness markers roll up as one planner session.
- A window reaped by timeout or SIGKILL still gets estimated tokens.
- Division by zero when no bead closed prints n/a, not zero.

## Plan-gap guidance

If current Claude pricing for a model family seen in the fixtures is not known from the repository or provider documentation, record PLAN-GAP naming the model instead of inventing a price. If a grace before reaping would conflict with the /goal Stop hook holding the worker indefinitely, keep the estimate path and record PLAN-GAP for the grace instead of lengthening windows.

## Targeted tests

comments.author: who
comments.text:
Every worker window now records a cost, including the ones grind reaps at the done bar, and `ortus cost --tree` reports cost per closed bead across planning and worker windows together.

How a reaped window gets billed. Each Claude `assistant` event states its own message's usage, repeated on every content block of that message, so the window keeps the largest reading per message id and sums across ids; a `result` event, where one exists, still wins outright with its totals and `total_cost_usd`. Measured against this repository's own logs, that reconstruction returns the provider's input buckets exactly — 126 / 180,869 / 8,965,389 on one window and 210 / 266,441 / 21,058,435 on another, matching their result events digit for digit — while the output count comes out near 1% of the session total, because each message reports what it had produced so far. So an estimate is a floor, and it is labelled: `cost_source` is `provider`, `estimated`, or null on every session and bead row, in the JSON and beside the dollars in the console block.

Dollars for an unbilled window come from a versioned, module-level price table keyed by model family, built from the published per-million input and output prices with the documented cache multipliers (read 0.1x input, write 2x at the one-hour TTL these windows are written under). A context marker such as `[1m]` or a dated snapshot suffix resolves to its family; a model the table does not name — including the stream's `<synthetic>` placeholder — keeps null dollars and marks the row partial rather than taking a guessed price. Against the two windows above the table lands within 1.5% of the provider's figure. Codex and Grok report no dollars of their own and are not priced here, so their rows are byte-for-byte what they were.

Grind now gives a worker that met the done bar a bounded five-second grace to flush its `result` line before the reap signal, returning the moment the line lands. Under the `/goal` Stop hook that line usually never comes, which is the whole reason the estimate path exists; the grace is a short constant, so a hung worker still meets the watchdog on schedule.

Criterion checks, all run against this tree: AC-1 `uv run pytest tests/test_cost_telemetry.py -k reaped -q` — 2 passed. AC-2 `-k provider -q` — 1 passed. AC-3 `-k unknown_model -q` — 1 passed. AC-4 `-k tree -q` — 5 passed. AC-5 `-k grace -q` — 3 passed. Targeted: `uv run pytest tests/test_cost_telemetry.py tests/test_harness_eval_report.py -q` — 50 passed. Also green on the changed surface: `tests/test_grind.py tests/test_grind_reap.py` (90 passed, 26 skipped) and `tests/test_dashboard.py tests/test_worker_failure_class.py tests/test_prompt_prefix.py` (its one wall-clock-sensitive header test failed once under `-n auto` and passes single-threaded; the log it reads carries no worker-stream events, so this change cannot reach it).

Follow-up filed as ortus-0x0j: the cache-write bucket is weighted at the one-hour rate because every write in this repository's logs arrives in the one-hour TTL field, which would overstate a repository running the five-minute TTL by 60% on that bucket. Splitting the bucket by TTL makes the estimate right under either.

title: Let ordinary worker tool calls reach Jev and park one bead instead of ending the grind
description:
## Objective

Make the pre_tool hook ask Jev about every tool call it cannot prove is clearly destructive, let an ordinary worker's development workflow proceed, turn a human outcome into a denied call or one parked bead instead of the end of the whole grind, and record every local-policy and Jev tool decision in logs/jev-decisions.jsonl.

## Behavioral context

Before (HEAD 7d44140): with `[judge] pre_tool = true`, `judge_tools.inspect_tool` only accepts Read, Write, Edit, Glob and Grep, and Bash commands whose first word is one of rm, cat, head, tail, touch, mkdir, cp, mv, pwd, curl or wget with no shell metacharacters. Every other call returns ToolAction.HUMAN locally (reasons opaque_shell, unsupported_command, unsupported_input, unsupported_options, unknown_target) without any Jev request. Even a call that reaches Jev is handed to a human by four fixed literals in `decide_tool` (confidence under 0.8, needs_human at or above 0.8, risk at or above 1.5). `judge_hook.main` then writes a human signal and denies the call, `HookRun.escalate` labels the bead human, and `grind` logs "judge pre_tool human; worker reaped" and `break`s out of the loop, ending the run. In the Shelf A/B arm A run on 2026-09-24 the first worker's first two calls, `Bash: ls && cat AGENTS.md | head -100` and `ToolSearch` (select:codegraph_explore), were both sent to a human; grind stopped 11 seconds into its first window with 0 of 19 READY beads closed. The local reasons were written nowhere except the Claude stream. docs/judge.md promises the hook covers irreversible tool calls, not every call.

After: local policy short-circuits only a short, enumerated list of clearly irreversible or destructive patterns (and still denies secrets in network arguments); every other call, including compound shell, pipes, bd, git, test runners, ls, ToolSearch and MCP tools, becomes one bounded Jev request. Following the diamond model, Jev's answers become a probability vector over allow, deny_call and park_bead, and System Two code takes the argmax with no confidence floor or needs_human threshold. deny_call denies that one call and lets the worker continue; park_bead reaps that worker, labels that bead human with a typed comment, and grind continues with the rest of the queue. Every tool decision, local or Jev, appends a typed record to logs/jev-decisions.jsonl.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

- src/ortus/core/judge_tools.py: shrink `inspect_tool`'s local short-circuit to an enumerated destructive set (recursive delete of the repository root, home or filesystem root or a path outside allowed_roots; `git push --force`/`-f`/`--force-with-lease` and `git reset --hard` against the integration branch; `rm -rf` style deletes outside allowed_roots; writes to configured sensitive_paths; secret values in network arguments stays DENY). Everything the current allowlist rejects for being unfamiliar (opaque_shell, unsupported_command, unsupported_input, unsupported_options, unknown_target, unknown tool names) no longer returns HUMAN locally; it produces a screened, bounded summary (tool name plus a tool_cap-bounded argument summary through `sanitize_field`) that goes to Jev.
- src/ortus/core/judge_tools.py `decide_tool`: delete the four fixed floors. Map Jev's typed answers into a normalized vector over allow, deny_call and park_bead and take the argmax in code, the same shape as `judge_stuck.decide_stuck_claim` and `judge_triage.route_triage`. A flat or low-confidence vector flattens toward uniform and resolves to allow (the class the call is already in), never to a human by default. Service failure keeps following failure_mode.
- src/ortus/core/judge_hook.py `main`: allow continues the normal permission flow; deny_call denies only this call with a typed reason; park_bead writes the existing human signal. Local destructive short-circuits deny the call (they do not park the bead). Shadow mode records the vector and applies allow for model decisions, never weakening a local denial.
- Decision records: the hook writes one typed JSON record per decision into its private temporary directory (the same inbox `HookRun.poll` already reads); `HookRun` appends them to logs/jev-decisions.jsonl through src/ortus/core/judge_log.py as a new `tool_decision` event (phase pre_tool, tool name, local reason or vector, applied action, failure, latency, token usage, no raw arguments). src/ortus/core/judge_replay.py accepts the new event so exports and replays of a log carrying it still load.
- src/ortus/commands/grind.py: on a pre_tool park, reap that worker, escalate that one bead through `HookRun.escalate`, log it, and continue the outer loop to the next READY bead instead of `break`. The claim is released or left for the existing flagged-claim path exactly as a worker PLAN-GAP park is today; triage (`triage_parked_bead`) sees it like any other park.
- docs/judge.md "Independent phases" section: replace the fixed-floor paragraph with the vector description, the enumerated destructive list and the per-bead park behavior.
- Tests (every change adds tests; enforcement lives in tests, not docs): tests/test_core_judge_tools.py, tests/test_judge_hook.py, tests/test_grind_judge_hooks.py, tests/test_judge_replay.py, tests/test_core_judge_log.py.

## Non-goals

- No change to the pre-turn gate, the model router, triage, the stuck-claim vector or the progress reaper.
- No new confidence floor, needs_human threshold or configurable gate anywhere; the diamond model forbids hard gates on those values.
- Do not make pre_tool support non-Claude backends.
- Do not send raw tool arguments, file contents or environment values to Jev or into the log; screened summaries only.
- Do not modify, stage or commit the untracked .feature-inbox/ directory or prd/PRD-jev-loop-middleware.md; do not run scripts/reinstall-cli.sh.
- No machine names, user names or host paths in code, docs, tests or fixtures.

## Concrete locations

- src/ortus/core/judge_tools.py: `inspect_tool()` (line 72), `_stop()` (59), `build_tool_questions()` (222), `decide_tool()` (228, floors near 285), `ToolAction`, `ToolDecision`, `ToolInspection`.
- src/ortus/core/judge_hook.py: `main()` (196), `_deny()`, `write_human_signal()`, `load_context()`, `HookReason`.
- src/ortus/core/judge_hooks.py: `HookRun` (57), `HookRun.poll()` (129), `HookRun.escalate()` (157), `check_pre_tool()`.
- src/ortus/commands/grind.py: `_reap_worker()` (3033) and the `if hook_run is not None and hook_run.requested:` block that logs "judge pre_tool human; worker reaped" and `break`s (near line 3097).
- src/ortus/core/judge_log.py: `write_decision()` (304), `_common()`, `_append()`, `LOG_NAME`; src/ortus/core/judge_replay.py event-kind validation.
- src/ortus/core/judge_stuck.py `decide_stuck_claim()` and src/ortus/core/judge_triage.py `route_triage()` as the vector/argmax pattern to copy.
- CodeGraph evidence: codegraph query inspect_tool -> judge_tools.py:72; decide_tool -> judge_tools.py:228; HookRun -> judge_hooks.py:57, poll 129, escalate 157; _reap_worker -> grind.py:3033; write_decision -> judge_log.py:304; codegraph callers decide_tool -> judge_hook.py:196 main plus tests/test_core_judge_tools.py (test_recursive_root_deletion_never_contacts_provider, test_opaque_shell_never_reaches_api, judged).

## Resolved decisions

1. Andy's diamond model is locked: Jev returns probability vectors to System Two code; no hard gate on confidence floors or needs_human thresholds. The four literals in `decide_tool` are removed, not moved into settings.
2. Local policy may short-circuit only clearly irreversible or destructive patterns, matching docs/judge.md's "irreversible tool calls"; unfamiliar is not destructive.
3. A local destructive match denies the call; only a Jev park_bead argmax parks the bead. A pre_tool outcome never ends the whole grind.
4. The existing test `test_opaque_shell_never_reaches_api` encodes the old behavior and is rewritten to the new contract (compound shell reaches Jev), not deleted silently.
5. Tool decision records go through the hook's private inbox and the parent writes them, because the repository tree is worker-owned.
6. Enforcement over prompt advice: the behavior is pinned by tests, not by worker prompt text.

## Compatibility constraints

Claude-only phase as today. Python 3.10-3.12 hermetic gate. Existing jev-decisions.jsonl files without tool_decision records still load in `ortus judge export`/`replay`. The hook keeps its 6-second watchdog and the judge timeout_seconds deadline; a missed deadline follows failure_mode. Repositories with pre_tool = false are byte-identical in behavior.

## Ordered steps

1. Run the targeted judge tool, hook and grind hook tests to record a green baseline.
2. Write failing tests: the Shelf arm A calls (`ls && cat AGENTS.md | head -100`, ToolSearch, `bd show x`, `git status`, `git commit -m msg`, an mcp__codegraph tool) produce a Jev request, not a local HUMAN; destructive patterns still short-circuit to deny.
3. Shrink `inspect_tool` to the enumerated destructive set and add the screened summary for everything else.
4. Replace the floors in `decide_tool` with the allow/deny_call/park_bead vector and argmax; add tests that a hedged vector resolves to allow and no floor exists.
5. Update `judge_hook.main` for deny_call versus park_bead and write per-decision records into the private inbox.
6. Teach `HookRun` to append those records as `tool_decision` events via judge_log, and judge_replay to accept them.
7. Change grind's pre_tool human handling from `break` to park-this-bead-and-continue; add a grind test with two READY beads where the first parks and the second still runs.
8. Update docs/judge.md and run the targeted tests until green.

## Dependencies

No open issue dependency. Consumers: tests/test_core_judge_tools.py, tests/test_judge_hook.py, tests/test_grind_judge_hooks.py, tests/test_judge_mvp_contract.py, tests/test_judge_replay.py, tests/test_core_judge_log.py, `ortus judge export`/`replay`, the triage path that reads parks.

## Edge cases

- A call Jev cannot answer in time or with a malformed body follows failure_mode (open = allow) and is logged with its failure.
- Secrets inside a Bash command: the summary is screened line by line and a secret still yields DENY for network arguments; never log the value.
- Oversized arguments are truncated to tool_cap in the summary rather than parking.
- The same tool call repeated many times must not flood the log beyond the existing MAX_EVENT_BYTES per record.
- A park on a resumed claim keeps its owner and dirty work as the current PLAN-GAP path does.
- Shadow mode never weakens a local destructive deny.

## Plan-gap guidance

If the TypeSafe tool answers cannot be mapped to a three-class vector without inventing a threshold, stop and record PLAN-GAP with the answer shapes rather than reintroducing a floor. If continuing the queue after a park conflicts with the flock or claim-ownership invariants in grind, record PLAN-GAP naming the invariant instead of breaking the run. If the destructive list needs a product decision beyond the patterns in Scope, record PLAN-GAP rather than guessing.

## Observable criteria

- AC-1: The Shelf arm A calls (Bash "ls && cat AGENTS.md | head -100" and ToolSearch) reach a Jev decision and are allowed on a benign vector instead of returning a local human. `uv run pytest tests/test_core_judge_tools.py -k shelf_arm_a -q`
- AC-2: bd, git status/diff/add/commit, test runner and codegraph MCP calls are no longer short-circuited locally. `uv run pytest tests/test_core_judge_tools.py -k ordinary_workflow -q`
- AC-3: Enumerated destructive patterns still deny without contacting the provider. `uv run pytest tests/test_core_judge_tools.py -k destructive -q`
- AC-4: decide_tool has no confidence floor or needs_human threshold; a hedged vector resolves to allow and the argmax picks the action. `uv run pytest tests/test_core_judge_tools.py -k vector -q`
- AC-5: A pre_tool park parks only that bead and grind continues to the next READY bead. `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_judge_hooks.py -k continues -q`
- AC-6: Local-policy reasons and Jev tool decisions appear as tool_decision records in logs/jev-decisions.jsonl and replay accepts them. `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_judge_hooks.py tests/test_judge_replay.py -k tool_decision -q`
- AC-7: The hook denies a single call on deny_call and signals a park only on park_bead. `uv run pytest tests/test_judge_hook.py -k park -q`

## Targeted tests

close_reason: Local policy stops only an enumerated irreversible set; every other call is judged as an allow/deny_call/park_bead vector with no floor, a refusal costs one call, a park costs one bead, and every decision lands in the run log

comments.author: who
comments.text:
Local policy in inspect_tool now stops only an enumerated set: a recursive delete of the filesystem root, the repository root, home or anywhere outside the allowed roots; any delete outside those roots; git push --force/-f/--force-with-lease; git reset --hard; a credential or configured sensitive path; and a secret env value in a network argument. Wrappers, leading NAME=value assignments and each segment of a compound line are read separately so sudo and pipelines cannot hide a match. Everything else is summarized and judged, including compound shell, bd, ordinary git, test runners, search and MCP tools.

decide_tool's four fixed literals are gone. The answers become a vector over allow, deny_call and park_bead and route_tool takes the argmax. Risk is read as a fraction of its scale; the human-need noul contributes only its lean past the coin flip, following the same reading the pre-turn packer uses, so a hedged answer argues for nothing and confidence only shrinks the vector toward uniform. There is no floor and no threshold. Service failure follows failure_mode (open allows, closed denies the call) and a malformed answer denies the call, since neither says anything about the bead.

The hook denies one call on deny_call and writes the human signal only on park_bead; a local match denies the call and never parks. Every decision is published as a typed record into the hook's private inbox, and HookRun appends each as a tool_decision event in logs/jev-decisions.jsonl with the tool name, the local reason or the vector, the applied action, failure, latency and reported usage, and no arguments. judge_replay accepts the event and older logs still load. On a park grind reaps that worker, escalates that one bead and continues to the next ready bead, honouring the iteration cap on the way out.

Scope note: prompt_audit.MOVED_RULES named inspect_tool as the owner of the wrapped-bd prompt rule. That hook held it only as collateral of refusing every compound shell line, so the claim is now false and was removed rather than repointed. Filed ortus-ncl2 to either return the wording to the audited text or give the rule a real owner; the audited prompt A/B is still running, which is why this did not edit that text.

title: Judge planner-sized beads by truncating screened text instead of dropping it
description:
## Objective

Make semantic readiness and the pre-turn packer judge real planner-sized beads by screening the whole field and then truncating it to a bounded, section-aware slice inside total_bytes_cap, instead of dropping the whole field, and record when text was truncated.

## Behavioral context

Before (HEAD 7d44140): `judge_state.sanitize_field` screens a field and returns `OmissionReason.OVERSIZE` with no value whenever the text is longer than its cap; it never truncates. `pack_state` caps description and design at `objective_cap` (1024 characters) and acceptance at `acceptance_cap` (1024). Planner-written beads routinely exceed that, so the description, design or acceptance field vanishes and `judge_readiness.evaluate_readiness` returns `{"status": "text_unavailable"}` without any Jev request or decision row. In the Shelf A/B arm A plan on 2026-09-24 every one of 19 READY beads came back text_unavailable (34 occurrences in the plan log) and logs/jev-decisions.jsonl gained no semantic_readiness rows. The same drop blanks the pre-turn gate's objective and acceptance lines for those beads, so the gate routes on metadata alone.

After: the full field is still screened first (a secret or sensitive path anywhere still omits the whole field), then an oversized field is truncated to its cap at a section or line boundary, preferring the Objective, Scope and Observable criteria sections, with a visible truncation marker. The packed state stays inside total_bytes_cap. A truncated field is recorded as an omission-style `truncated` reason and the semantic_readiness decision row carries which fields were truncated. Default caps are revisited so a typical planner bead fits.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

- src/ortus/core/judge_state.py: add a truncating path used for issue text: screen the entire string exactly as today, then, if it exceeds the cap, keep whole lines in priority order (for description: Objective then Behavioral context; for design: Scope, Concrete locations, Resolved decisions, then the rest; for acceptance: Observable criteria lines first) up to the cap, append a fixed truncation marker, and record `OmissionReason.TRUNCATED` (new member) with the field name. `sanitize_field` itself keeps its never-truncate contract for metadata, tool names and anything that is not issue text.
- `pack_state`: use the truncating path for title-independent issue text fields (description/objective, design, acceptance) in both the pre-turn and semantic_readiness phases; keep the existing total_bytes_cap reduction loop as the last resort.
- src/ortus/core/judge.py JudgeConfig defaults: raise `objective_cap` and `acceptance_cap` so a typical planner bead's key sections fit (for example 4096 each) and raise `total_bytes_cap` enough to carry them (for example 16384), keeping the defaults validated by `_parse_judge_values`.
- src/ortus/core/judge_readiness.py `evaluate_readiness`: only report text_unavailable when a field is empty, private or omitted as sensitive, never merely because it is long; include the list of truncated fields in the returned advice and in the decision event.
- src/ortus/core/judge_log.py: the decision payload for phase semantic_readiness carries a bounded `truncated_fields` list; src/ortus/core/judge_replay.py accepts it.
- docs/judge.md Semantic readiness section and the `[judge]` defaults table: document truncation, the new defaults and the truncation record.
- Tests: tests/test_core_judge_state.py, tests/test_semantic_readiness.py, tests/test_core_judge_config.py, tests/test_core_judge_log.py, tests/test_judge_replay.py.

## Non-goals

- No change to readiness schema v1 validation, which stays the deterministic structural gate.
- Semantic advice stays advisory: it never adds a label, blocks a claim or selects a backend.
- No LLM summarization step inside the packer; truncation is deterministic code.
- Do not weaken secret or sensitive-path screening: screening still runs on the full text before truncation.
- Do not modify, stage or commit the untracked .feature-inbox/ directory or prd/PRD-jev-loop-middleware.md; do not run scripts/reinstall-cli.sh.
- No machine names, user names or host paths in code, docs, tests or fixtures.

## Concrete locations

- src/ortus/core/judge_state.py: `sanitize_field()` (101), `_section()` (125), `pack_state()` (139), `clean()` inside pack_state (183), the total_bytes_cap reduction loop (near 250), `OmissionReason`, `Omission`, `PackedState`.
- src/ortus/core/judge_readiness.py: `evaluate_readiness()` (67, text_unavailable at 83), `readiness_questions()` (24).
- src/ortus/core/judge.py: `JudgeConfig` caps (objective_cap, acceptance_cap, total_bytes_cap), `_parse_judge_values()`.
- src/ortus/core/judge_log.py `write_decision()` (304) and `_decision_payload()`; src/ortus/core/judge_replay.py decision validation.
- Callers of evaluate_readiness: src/ortus/commands/validate.py, src/ortus/commands/plan.py, src/ortus/commands/ingest.py, src/ortus/commands/grind.py.
- CodeGraph evidence: codegraph query pack_state -> judge_state.py:139; sanitize_field -> judge_state.py:101; codegraph callers pack_state -> tests/test_core_judge_state.py (pack, test_secret_in_any_source_field_is_absent_from_output, test_labels_seat_and_tool_are_sanitized, test_ambient_secret_environment_is_screened) and tests/test_judge_packs.py (test_request_metadata_matches_event_hash_and_byte_budget). Grep fallback for text_unavailable: judge_readiness.py:83 only.

## Resolved decisions

1. Screen first, truncate second: a secret anywhere in the field still omits the whole field.
2. Truncation is deterministic and section-aware; no model call summarizes text.
3. Oversize is no longer a reason for text_unavailable; empty, private and sensitive still are.
4. Every truncation is recorded (omission reason plus truncated_fields in the decision row) so replay can separate full-text from truncated-text judgments.
5. Defaults rise so real beads fit; existing explicit caps in a project's .ortusrc are still honored.
6. Enforcement over prompt advice: behavior is pinned by tests and fixtures, not by planner prompt text asking for shorter beads.
7. Jev diamond model: semantic readiness remains probability advice to System Two with no floor or gate.

## Compatibility constraints

Python 3.10-3.12 hermetic gate. Existing logs without truncated_fields still load in export/replay. The request stays inside total_bytes_cap and the criteria hash still identifies the questions. Projects with explicit smaller caps keep them and now get truncation instead of omission.

## Ordered steps

1. Run the targeted judge state and semantic readiness tests for a green baseline.
2. Add a planner-sized bead fixture (description, design and acceptance each several kilobytes, readiness schema v1 shaped, no secrets) under tests and a failing test that it yields text_unavailable today.
3. Implement the screen-then-truncate path and OmissionReason.TRUNCATED in judge_state.
4. Use it in pack_state for issue text in both phases and keep the total budget loop.
5. Raise the default caps and update config validation tests.
6. Change evaluate_readiness and the decision payload to carry truncated_fields; update judge_replay.
7. Update docs/judge.md and run the targeted tests until green.

## Dependencies

No open issue dependency. Consumers: validate, plan, ingest and grind (semantic readiness), the pre-turn gate (`pack_state` in grind), tests/test_judge_packs.py byte-budget test, `ortus judge export`/`replay`.

## Edge cases

- A secret after the cap boundary must still omit the whole field.
- Multibyte text: truncate on characters and re-check the UTF-8 byte budget.
- A field with no recognizable sections truncates on line boundaries.
- A single line longer than the cap is cut at the cap with the marker.
- judge-private labels still suppress all issue text.
- total_bytes_cap smaller than the truncated fields still falls back to the existing field-drop loop.

## Plan-gap guidance

If raising the defaults breaks the documented latency or byte targets in docs/judge.md in a way that needs a product call, record PLAN-GAP with the measured sizes instead of picking new targets. If screening-then-truncating conflicts with an existing privacy test's contract, record PLAN-GAP naming that test rather than deleting it.
