comments.text: Oversized issue text is now screened in full and then cut to whole lines rather than dropped. truncate_field screens the entire field exactly as sanitize_field always did, so a secret past the cap boundary still omits the whole field; only after that does it keep lines, priority sections first (Objective and Behavioral context for the description, Scope/Concrete locations/Resolved decisions for the design, Observable criteria for the acceptance), closed by a visible marker and bounded by the cap it is announcing. sanitize_field keeps its never-truncate contract for metadata and tool names. Every cut field is reported as OmissionReason.TRUNCATED, and evaluate_readiness carries the sorted names into both the returned advice and the semantic_readiness decision row, which judge_replay accepts as optional so older logs still load. Default caps rose to 4096/4096 with a 16384 total budget so a typical planner bead's key sections fit. Length alone no longer produces text_unavailable; empty, private and sensitive text still do. Follow-up ortus-zlhl covers filling truncated_fields at the pre-turn gate's own decision writes, which this scope did not reach.

title: Restructure README into a short entry point with flat docs pages and enforced Markdown checks
description:
## Objective

Turn README.md into a short hierarchical entry point (at most 200 lines, modeled on astral-sh/uv, BurntSushi/ripgrep and cli/cli) and move the long-form material into flat docs/*.md pages, with the Markdown shape (length, no raw HTML, resolving links, mermaid diagrams, complete command reference, complete docs index) enforced by a new test file rather than by prose.

## Behavioral context

Before (HEAD 6cf97a4): README.md is 628 lines. It mixes Install, Quick start, a 14-verb table, cost telemetry, supported platforms, prerequisites, agent backends, a 169-line local-model section with repeated advice (text-only GGUF guidance about three times, llama-server --jinja repeated), Why ortus, full configuration, implementation readiness, "How a grind iteration finishes" (which duplicates the worker/reap paragraph under Agent backends), the generated state-graph block, CodeGraph lifecycle, runtime prompts, the generated glossary, the session-close protocol, development and license. The generated blocks use HTML comment markers and a raw details/summary element. LABELS.md and ZFC.md sit at the repo root. eval and judge export/replay are undocumented. The top-level help reads "Global CLI for bd-driven Claude Code workflows", which is Claude-only although grind is backend-neutral. After: README.md carries only the pitch, a mermaid how-it-works overview, Install, Quick start, Prerequisites (merged with supported platforms), an everyday-verbs table, Why ortus, a minimal .ortusrc, a Documentation index, a Development pointer and License. Every long-form topic has exactly one home under docs/. Generated blocks live in docs/grind.md and docs/glossary.md behind Markdown link-reference comment markers, LABELS.md and ZFC.md live under docs/, the help text is backend-neutral, and tests/test_docs_markdown.py fails if any of this regresses. All content the existing tests assert is moved, not deleted.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

New README.md, at most 200 lines, with exactly these level-2 headings in this order: How it works, Install, Quick start, Prerequisites, The verbs, Why ortus, Configuration, Documentation, Development, License. Content:
- Pitch paragraph above the first heading.
- How it works: one mermaid flowchart PRD -> ortus plan -> beads -> ortus validate -> ortus grind -> fresh worker -> commit, bd close, push, looping back to the queue.
- Install: keep the three install paths and the troubleshooting table; the curl one-liner appears once (not repeated in Quick start).
- Quick start: keep the prototype example line (ortus grind . --prototype).
- Prerequisites: the current Prerequisites plus Supported platforms content.
- The verbs: table of init, check, plan, ingest, validate, grind, tail, dashboard, then a link to docs/commands.md for the full list.
- Configuration: about a 10-line minimal .ortusrc example plus a link to docs/configuration.md.
- Documentation: a bulleted index linking every docs/*.md file.
- Development: a short pointer to docs/testing.md; License unchanged.

New flat docs pages (one home per topic, no duplicated paragraphs):
- docs/backends.md: choosing a backend and precedence, managed AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md blocks, /goal vs plain-prompt workers, per-backend sandbox, dirty checkout; mermaid flowchart of backend and profile selection (--backend > ORTUS_BACKEND > .ortusrc > claude; worker shape; sandbox).
- docs/local-model.md: the Serving a local model section de-duplicated (one statement each of the text-only GGUF advice and the llama-server --jinja requirement).
- docs/configuration.md: full .ortusrc reference, profiles, full vs prototype verification.
- docs/grind.md: implementation readiness gate, how a grind iteration finishes and reaps, the generated state-graph block, the session-close protocol; mermaid sequenceDiagram of one iteration: preflight/flock -> bd snapshot -> select_ready_issue -> readiness guard -> optional Jev gate -> compose work prompt -> fresh sandboxed worker implements, checks, commits, bd close, push -> compute_delta -> reap vs orphan / leftover in_progress / PLAN-GAP / stuck -> loop until the queue drains.
- docs/authoring.md: plan, interview, ingest, validate, spec; mermaid flowchart of work intake (PRD or interview -> plan -> validate -> one repair pass; ingest packet or stdin -> validate -> bd create or reject).
- docs/cost.md: cost telemetry plus eval; mermaid diagram of grind logs -> markers plus usage JSON -> billing-bucket normalization -> partial-usage flag -> per-bead rollup -> ortus cost --json and ortus eval.
- docs/codegraph.md: CodeGraph lifecycle with a mermaid lifecycle flowchart.
- docs/prompts.md: runtime prompts and ortus prompt list/show/eject with a mermaid diagram of resolution order (repo override -> user override -> bundled).
- docs/glossary.md: the generated glossary block.
- docs/commands.md: every verb and subcommand (init, plan, grind, interview, tail, human, check, unlock, spec, validate, dashboard, cost, eval, ingest, prompt list/show/eject, judge export/replay) with a one-line description and key flags matching each command's --help.
- docs/judge.md: add judge export/replay usage and a mermaid sequenceDiagram of Jev advice flow (probability vectors -> route as context, no withholding -> judge export -> replay -> calibration candidates, never auto-applied).
- git mv LABELS.md docs/labels.md and git mv ZFC.md docs/zfc.md; fix relative links inside them (for example ZFC's link to prd/PRD-goal-directive.md becomes ../prd/PRD-goal-directive.md) and every tracked reference.

Markdown-only rule: no raw HTML tags or HTML comments anywhere in README.md or docs/*.md outside fenced code blocks and inline code spans. Replace the details/summary element with plain Markdown (a heading or bold line plus the table). Replace HTML comment markers with Markdown link-reference comments, exactly [//]: # (BEGIN GENERATED: state-graph) / [//]: # (END GENERATED: state-graph), [//]: # (BEGIN GENERATED: glossary) / [//]: # (END GENERATED: glossary), and in docs/judge.md [//]: # (BEGIN two-seat rollout example) / [//]: # (END two-seat rollout example). The "Generated from ... Do not edit by hand" note line also becomes a [//]: # (...) comment without unbalanced parentheses inside.

Code and test changes:
- src/ortus/core/lifecycle.py and src/ortus/core/glossary.py: new BEGIN_MARKER/END_MARKER values, generated note as a Markdown comment, _machine_section emits plain Markdown instead of details/summary, docstrings and error messages name docs/grind.md and docs/glossary.md.
- src/ortus/core/attribution.py: _MD_BEGIN/_MD_END also match the [//]: # (BEGIN GENERATED: name) form, keeping the legacy HTML form for consumer repos.
- src/ortus/cli.py: backend-neutral top-level help naming Claude, Codex, Grok and opencode (no "Claude Code workflows").
- New tests/test_docs_markdown.py asserting: (a) README.md <= 200 lines; (b) no raw HTML tags or HTML comments in README.md and docs/*.md outside fenced code blocks and inline code spans; (c) every relative link in README.md and docs/*.md resolves to an existing file, and a #anchor resolves to a GitHub-slugged heading in the target when present; (d) README.md, docs/grind.md, docs/authoring.md, docs/backends.md, docs/cost.md and docs/judge.md each contain at least one mermaid fence; (e) every verb and group subcommand registered on the typer app in src/ortus/cli.py appears as ortus <verb> in docs/commands.md; (f) the README Documentation section links every docs/*.md file; (g) LABELS.md and ZFC.md no longer exist at the root, docs/labels.md and docs/zfc.md exist, and no tracked file outside .beads/ and CHANGELOG.md links the old root paths.
- Retarget tests/test_cli.py, tests/test_validate.py, tests/test_state_graph_docs.py, tests/test_glossary_docs.py, tests/test_judge_seat_isolation.py (and tests/test_test_policy.py if docs/testing.md changes) to the new files and headings; add a test_cli case that the top-level help is backend-neutral; add a tests/test_core_attribution.py case for the Markdown comment marker form.
- CLAUDE.md rule about regenerating the state-graph block points at docs/grind.md; pyproject.toml sdist include adds docs so README links resolve in the sdist.

## Non-goals

- No behavior change to grind, plan, ingest, validate, the readiness schema or Jev; this is docs plus the marker/renderer/help-text plumbing and tests.
- Do not change managed agent-file block markers written into consumer AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md by src/ortus/core/agent_files.py, or the ejected-prompt stamp in src/ortus/core/prompts.py; those are not docs pages.
- AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and CHANGELOG.md stay at the root; docs/testing.md and docs/judge.md keep their names.
- Do not rewrite historical content in .beads/ or CHANGELOG.md.
- Do not modify, stage or commit the untracked .feature-inbox/ directory or prd/PRD-jev-loop-middleware.md.
- No new nested docs directories; docs pages are flat.
- Do not run scripts/reinstall-cli.sh.

## Concrete locations

- README.md (628 lines at 6cf97a4; headings at 9 Install, 42 Quick start, 76 The verbs, 97 Cost telemetry, 120 Supported platforms, 129 Prerequisites, 142 Agent backends, 163 Serving a local model, 332 Why ortus, 339 Configuration, 419 Implementation readiness, 443 How a grind iteration finishes, 461 State graphs, 497 CodeGraph lifecycle, 543 Runtime prompts, 574 Glossary, 598 Session-close protocol, 611 Development, 626 License; generated markers at 469/495 and 584/596, details element at 485).
- docs/judge.md (rollout markers at 387/425), docs/testing.md, LABELS.md, ZFC.md, CLAUDE.md line 36, pyproject.toml sdist include.
- src/ortus/core/lifecycle.py: BEGIN_MARKER, END_MARKER, _machine_section(), render_readme_block(), readme_block(), mermaid_issue_graph().
- src/ortus/core/glossary.py: BEGIN_MARKER, END_MARKER, render_readme_block(), readme_block(), render_glossary_table().
- src/ortus/core/attribution.py: _MD_BEGIN, _MD_END, region_map().
- src/ortus/cli.py: app (typer.Typer help string at line 26).
- tests/test_cli.py: test_readme_documents_prompt_verbs(), test_readme_documents_init_managed_agent_files(), test_readme_lists_grok_backend(), test_readme_documents_prototype_verification() (wrap-sensitive needles such as "behavioral test\ncommands and the repo test suite" and "lowered\nbar").
- tests/test_validate.py: test_validate_is_discoverable() slices README from "## The verbs" to "## Prerequisites".
- tests/test_state_graph_docs.py: test_readme_contains_the_issue_graph_only(); tests/test_glossary_docs.py: test_readme_contains_the_glossary(), test_readme_block_matches_renderer().
- tests/test_judge_seat_isolation.py: rollout_example(); tests/test_core_attribution.py (HTML marker fixture near line 138).
- Grounding for diagrams: src/ortus/commands/grind.py _snapshot(), _compose_work_prompt(); src/ortus/core/grind_loop.py select_ready_issue(), compute_delta(); src/ortus/core/agent.py resolve_backend(); src/ortus/core/prompts.py resolve_prompt(); src/ortus/core/cost.py parse_grind_log(), rollup_beads(); src/ortus/commands/judge.py export(), replay().
- CodeGraph evidence: codegraph query render_readme_block and readme_block (glossary.py:268/285, lifecycle.py:326/342, imported by tests/test_state_graph_docs.py and tests/test_glossary_docs.py); _MD_BEGIN (attribution.py:46); rollout_example (tests/test_judge_seat_isolation.py:28); test_validate_is_discoverable (tests/test_validate.py:201); compute_delta and select_ready_issue (grind_loop.py:126/169); resolve_backend (agent.py:573); resolve_prompt (prompts.py:133); _compose_work_prompt (grind.py:1131); app (cli.py:24). Grep fallback: LABELS.md/ZFC.md are referenced only by prd/PRD-goal-directive.md (tracked), prd/PRD-jev-loop-middleware.md (untracked, leave alone) and ZFC.md's own link.

## Resolved decisions

1. Andy approved the README-as-entry-point structure and the flat docs page list above; README target is at most 200 lines.
2. GitHub-flavored Markdown only; mermaid code fences for diagrams; no raw HTML outside code.
3. Generated-block markers are Markdown link-reference comments; the state-graph block lives in docs/grind.md and the glossary block in docs/glossary.md.
4. Keep the public function names render_readme_block and readme_block to limit churn; only their target document, markers and messages change.
5. attribution.py accepts both marker forms, because consumer repos may still carry the HTML form.
6. Enforcement over prose: the shape rules live in tests/test_docs_markdown.py, not in a style note.
7. Every string an existing test asserts is moved to its new home with the same wrapping (or the needle updated in the same commit with identical meaning), never deleted.
8. Diagrams must match the code named in Concrete locations; if code and old prose disagree, the diagram follows the code.
9. docs pages are included in the sdist.

## Compatibility constraints

Renders on github.com (GFM plus mermaid). Python 3.10-3.12 hermetic gate. PyPI long description is still README.md, so README links should be relative paths that also resolve in the repo. Consumer repos keep working: agent_files block markers, prompt eject stamps and legacy HTML generated markers in attribution are unchanged. No CLI behavior change beyond the top-level help string.

## Ordered steps

1. Run the current doc-touching tests to record a green baseline.
2. Write tests/test_docs_markdown.py with checks (a) to (g) and watch it fail on the current tree.
3. Change markers, the generated note and the details output in lifecycle.py and glossary.py; extend attribution.py _MD_BEGIN/_MD_END; add the attribution test case.
4. Create docs/backends.md, local-model.md, configuration.md, grind.md, authoring.md, cost.md, codegraph.md, prompts.md, glossary.md and commands.md by moving README sections, de-duplicating and adding the mermaid diagrams.
5. git mv LABELS.md and ZFC.md into docs/, fix their internal links and tracked references (prd/PRD-goal-directive.md, CLAUDE.md).
6. Update docs/judge.md markers, add judge export/replay usage and the Jev advice sequence diagram.

8. Make the top-level help backend-neutral in src/ortus/cli.py and add the test_cli help test.
9. Retarget tests/test_cli.py, tests/test_validate.py, tests/test_state_graph_docs.py, tests/test_glossary_docs.py and tests/test_judge_seat_isolation.py; add docs to the pyproject sdist include.
10. Regenerate the generated blocks from the renderers and run the targeted tests until green.

## Dependencies

No open issue dependency. Consumers of the changed surfaces: tests/test_state_graph_docs.py and tests/test_glossary_docs.py (renderers), attribution.region_map used by grind's absorb step (marker regex), tests/test_core_attribution.py, tests/test_judge_seat_isolation.py (judge.md markers), tests/test_cli.py and tests/test_validate.py (README slices), CLAUDE.md contributor rule, pyproject.toml packaging.

If an existing test asserts README-specific wording that cannot live anywhere but README within the limit, record PLAN-GAP naming the test instead of deleting the assertion. If GitHub's renderer shows the [//]: # comment markers visibly in some context, record PLAN-GAP rather than falling back to HTML comments.

title: Run the model-router A/B from a terminal and set its default
description:
## Objective

Run the Hello World control-versus-model-router comparison from a plain
terminal and record its numbers, so `jev_model_router` gets a default chosen
by measurement rather than left at the unmeasured one.

## Behavioral context

Before: ortus-ltjz landed the shadow routing log, the report's control-versus
-treatment comparison and the arm recipe that actually enables the gate, but
could not run the cells. Both seats died at `ortus plan`: an agent launched
from inside a sandboxed Claude session nests its sandbox inside that session's
and every Bash call fails with `Sandbox is required but failed to initialize:
EPERM`, so no bead was ever created and neither arm measured anything. The
bead carries that null result as `jev_router_ab` metadata.

After: the two cells have run from a terminal, their cost per closed bead,
close rate, wall seconds and per-tier routing counts are recorded as
`jev_router_ab` metadata on this bead, and `DEFAULTS["jev_model_router"]`
plus `MEASURED_VERDICT` in `tests/test_jev_model_router.py` carry the verdict
the comparison produced.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

- Run the hello-world control cell and the hello-world model-router cell of
  the frozen recipe, from a terminal, with the repo's current code.
- Read the comparison out of `ortus eval <root> --json` and record thresholds,
  per-arm metrics and the verdict as `jev_router_ab` metadata on this bead.
- Apply the decision rule to `DEFAULTS["jev_model_router"]` and to
  `MEASURED_VERDICT`, which the default test asserts against.
- Repoint the model-router `Treatment.measured_by` at this bead once it holds
  the numbers.

## Non-goals

- Do not launch the cells from inside an agent session's Bash tool. A stored
  operational rule already records that a nested worker mux dies under that
  parent, and this bead exists because it did.
- Do not weaken the seat's `sandbox.failIfUnavailable` to make a nested run
  work; the seat's posture is the operator's, not a knob for this measurement.
- Do not invent thresholds without data. A cell that reports nothing keeps the
  default where it is.
- Do not re-run the prompt-audit or stable-prefix arms, and do not touch the
  beads measuring them.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/core/harness_eval.py` — `arm_commands()`, `TREATMENTS`,
  `ArmComparison.verdict`, `build_report()`.
- `src/ortus/core/config.py` — `DEFAULTS["jev_model_router"]`.
- `tests/test_jev_model_router.py` — `MEASURED_VERDICT`.
- `src/ortus/commands/eval.py` — `ortus eval --matrix` prints the two cells.
- CodeGraph evidence: `route_implement_profile` and `jev_router_enabled` live
  in `src/ortus/core/judge_routing.py` and are called from
  `src/ortus/commands/grind.py`; `ArmComparison` is read by `render_report`.

## Resolved decisions

1. The decision rule is fixed: adopt when the router's close rate is at least
   the control's and it is cheaper per closed bead or faster. It is already
   implemented as `ArmComparison.verdict`, so the verdict is read, not argued.
2. A null or partial result keeps the default off and is recorded as such.
3. Results live in bd metadata and a bd comment, never in a repo markdown file.
4. The arm's recipe enables the judge gate as well as the flag; without that
   the arm is the control arm and measures nothing.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux and macOS. The seats are throwaway directories under a temp root, not
tracked by this repository. `ORTUS_JEV_ROUTER=0` must still force the router
off whatever the default becomes.

## Ordered steps

1. Print the recipe with `ortus eval <root> --matrix` and take the two
   hello-world cells.
2. Run both cells from a terminal, each bounded to roughly 2400 seconds.
3. Collect `ortus eval <root> --json` and read the model-router comparison.
4. Write `jev_router_ab` metadata and a summary comment on this bead.
5. Set the default and `MEASURED_VERDICT` from the verdict, and repoint
   `measured_by` at this bead.

## Dependencies

Follows ortus-ltjz, which landed everything the measurement reads. Consumers
are `grind._route_model` and the eval report. No open issue dependency.

## Edge cases

- A cell times out or reports no cost: record the partial numbers honestly and
  leave the default where it is.
- Both arms close zero beads: null result, default unchanged.
- The router only ever picks the baseline tier: record the tier counts; the
  verdict still follows the rule.
- A seat whose planning step creates no bead is a failed cell, not a zero.

## Plan-gap guidance

If the cells cannot run from a terminal either, record the failure in
`jev_router_ab` and stop. Do not lower the seat's sandbox requirement, do not
hand-write metrics, and do not flip the default without a comparison behind it.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1: This bead carries `jev_router_ab` metadata holding both arms' metrics
  and a verdict.
- AC-2: The default matches the recorded verdict and the kill switch still
  forces the router off.
- AC-3: The model-router treatment names this bead as the issue that spends
  its numbers.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `bd search --has-metadata-key jev_router_ab --status all`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_jev_model_router.py -k default -q`
- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_harness_eval_report.py -k model_router -q`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_jev_model_router.py tests/test_harness_eval_report.py tests/test_core_config.py -q`

comments.author: who
comments.text:
PLAN-GAP (selection, not implementation): this bead is operator-terminal work and cannot be executed by a grind/goal worker at all, so it is flagged human and returned to open unstarted. Its own Non-goals are binding: 'Do not launch the cells from inside an agent session's Bash tool', and memory operational-rule-2026-08-11-launch-ortus-grind records the mechanism — a seat's planning agent nested inside an already-sandboxed session cannot bind its own mux socket, every Bash call returns 'Sandbox is required but failed to initialize: EPERM', ortus plan creates no bead, and both arms fail identically in a way that reads as a null result but is a launch-context error. This session is exactly that parent: a sandboxed agent Bash tool. No cell was launched, no metrics were hand-written, and the default was not touched.

Nothing was measured this window, so jev_router_ab metadata was deliberately not written: recording another 'not-measured' null here would duplicate what ortus-ltjz already carries and would let AC-1 be satisfied without the comparison the bead exists to run. Repository state confirmed against the spec while orienting: the model-router treatment's measured_by in src/ortus/core/harness_eval.py already names ortus-ib1w (AC-3 satisfied), and DEFAULTS['jev_model_router'] is False against MEASURED_VERDICT False in tests/test_jev_model_router.py (AC-2 consistent with the current keep-control null). Only AC-1 is outstanding, and it needs the operator to run the two hello-world cells from a plain terminal.

title: Jev stuck-worker detection from bounded log tails, shadow then reap
description:
## Objective

Detect looping workers during a worker window by periodically sending a bounded, sanitized log tail to Jev for progress-vs-looping probabilities, first in shadow/log mode with a measurable signal, then letting the reaper end looping workers before the 5400s worker timeout.

## Behavioral context

Before: grind's _reap_worker callback (polled every reap_poll=2s by the runner) reaps only on deterministic reasons from _reap_reason (done bar, flagged claim, hook exit); a worker that loops without progress runs until --worker-timeout 5400s kills it. After: every progress interval (default 300s) grind sends the last bounded slice of the worker log plus typed facts (elapsed seconds, HEAD advanced, bead status) to Jev (jev-1.13.0, 1.5s timeout) and records p_progressing / p_looping to a progress log joined to the eventual window outcome by run_id. A mode flag jev_progress_reaper (off / shadow / enforce, default shadow) controls use: shadow only logs; enforce lets _reap_reason return a jev_looping reason when the System Two rule over recent vectors says looping. A reaped worker goes through the normal post-window path (no human label). Jev failures skip the check (fail-open). Diamond model: Jev output feeds the reap decision as probabilities/advice; no new confidence-floor parking.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

- New module src/ortus/core/judge_progress.py: ProgressVerdict (p_looping, p_progressing, confidence or failure), evaluate_progress(tail, facts, config) with sanitized bounded input (at most 200 lines and 16 KB, secrets stripped via the existing judge state packing), and should_reap(history) as pure System Two.
- Config: jev_progress_reaper (off|shadow|enforce, default shadow) and jev_progress_interval_s (default 300) in DEFAULTS with validation; env override ORTUS_JEV_PROGRESS.
- grind: inside _reap_worker, when the interval has elapsed, run evaluate_progress on the tail of the worker log; append a record to logs/jev-progress.jsonl (run_id, issue_id, elapsed, vector, mode, would_reap, reaped).
- At window end, append the window outcome (closed, timeout, reaped) to the same run_id so the shadow signal can be scored (precision of would_reap vs timeouts and closes).
- enforce: when should_reap is true, _reap_reason returns jev_looping and the worker is reaped; the no-close counter and the post-window path handle it like any other no-close window.
- Hermetic tests with a mocked Jev client and fake clock.

## Non-goals

- No change to --worker-timeout default (5400s) or reap_poll.
- No human label from this path; no confidence floor or needs_human gate.
- Jev calls must not block the reap poll: bounded 1.5s timeout, at most one call per interval.
- No default flip to enforce in this bead; it ships as shadow by default and enforce is opt-in until the shadow signal is scored.
- No repo markdown artifacts.

## Concrete locations

- src/ortus/commands/grind.py: _reap_worker() closure, _reap_reason(), reap_reasons, worker_timeout option, runner.run(reap_when=..., on_poll=...).
- src/ortus/core/claude.py and src/ortus/core/agent.py: reap_when / reap_poll polling contract.
- src/ortus/core/judge_post.py: evaluate_outcome() as the bounded Jev request pattern.
- src/ortus/core/judge_log.py: event writers (pattern for a progress event); src/ortus/core/config.py DEFAULTS and validators.
- src/ortus/commands/tail.py and the tail decoders for turning stream-json worker logs into readable text.
- tests/test_grind_reap.py, tests/test_grind_worker_timeout.py, new tests/test_judge_progress.py.
- CodeGraph evidence: codegraph query _reap_worker (grind.py), _reap_reason (grind.py, tests in tests/test_grind_reap.py); rg reap_poll shows 2.0s default in claude.py and agent.py.

## Resolved decisions

1. Diamond model (Andy, locked): Jev supplies progress/looping probabilities; System Two decides; no confidence floor or human parking.
2. should_reap rule: shrink each p_looping toward 0.5 by its confidence, and reap when the last two consecutive shrunk values both exceed 0.5 and HEAD has not advanced since the first of them; this is a reap decision on a live process, not a parking gate.
3. Default mode shadow so the signal is measured before it acts; enforce is opt-in via config or env.
4. Fail-open: any Jev failure records failure in the log and never reaps.
5. Enforcement in code: detection and reaping live in grind/_reap_reason, not in worker prompt advice.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux/macOS, Python 3.10-3.12. mode off must be byte-identical to today's reaper. Works for claude, codex and grok backends' log formats via the existing tail decoding; unknown formats fall back to raw bounded text. Progress log is a new additive file.

## Ordered steps

1. Read _reap_worker, _reap_reason and the runner reap_when polling contract.
2. Add config keys and validation plus the env override.
3. Implement judge_progress.py (questions, bounded sanitized tail, evaluate_progress, should_reap).
4. Call it from _reap_worker on the interval; write progress records; keep the poll non-blocking.
5. Add jev_looping to _reap_reason for enforce mode.
6. Append window outcome to the progress log for scoring.
7. Add hermetic tests (mocked Jev, fake clock) and run the targeted tests.

## Dependencies

No open issue dependency. Related: bead 2 of this batch (stuck in_progress decision) consumes the no-close window that a jev_looping reap produces, but this bead works without it. Consumers: grind reaper, judge replay/calibration readers.

## Edge cases

- Log file missing or empty: skip the check.
- Jev timeout: record failure, no reap.
- Worker closes the bead between checks: the done-bar reason wins.
- HEAD advancing while text looks repetitive: no reap.
- Interval longer than the worker window: no checks, no behavior change.
- Tail containing secrets: sanitized before sending.

## Plan-gap guidance

If a backend's log cannot be decoded into bounded text without new decoder work, send raw bounded text and record PLAN-GAP for decoder quality only. If polling Jev inside _reap_worker would block the 2s poll, move the call to a background thread with the result read on the next poll rather than dropping the feature.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1: In shadow mode a mocked looping verdict writes a progress record with would_reap true and the worker is not reaped. `uv run pytest tests/test_judge_progress.py -k shadow -q`
- AC-2: In enforce mode two consecutive looping verdicts with no HEAD advance make _reap_reason return jev_looping before the worker timeout. `uv run pytest tests/test_judge_progress.py -k enforce -q`
- AC-3: A Jev failure or timeout never reaps and is logged as a failure. `uv run pytest tests/test_judge_progress.py -k fail_open -q`
- AC-4: The tail sent to Jev is bounded to 200 lines and 16 KB and sanitized. `uv run pytest tests/test_judge_progress.py -k bounded_tail -q`
- AC-5: Mode off leaves the existing reaper behavior unchanged. `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_reap.py -q`

## Targeted tests

uv run pytest tests/test_judge_progress.py tests/test_grind_reap.py tests/test_grind_worker_timeout.py -q
close_reason: A bounded log tail now reads a looping worker, shadow-recorded by default and reaped only under enforce, with every failure keeping the worker

comments.author: who
comments.text:
Landed the looping-worker signal as a ProgressWatch riding the reap poll: once
per interval it summarizes that window's own log into a bounded, per-line
screened tail (200 lines, 16 KB), sends it with the elapsed seconds, the
branch-advanced fact and the claim's tracker status, and reads one noul
probability back. should_reap takes the decision in code — two consecutive
readings above the coin flip on one unchanged commit — and _reap_reason answers
the poll with a jev_looping reason only in enforce mode. Records go to
logs/jev-progress.jsonl (a separate file, so the replay reader's validation of
the decision log is untouched), one per check plus the window's eventual
outcome joined by run_id, which is what makes the shadow readings scorable
against closes, timeouts and reaps.

Design call worth an operator's attention: the checks need judge.include_log_tail
as well as a mode other than off. That flag was inert but documented as "the
pre-turn packer never reads log tails", and this is the only phase that sends
worker transcript text to a provider, so honoring it was the honest reading. The
practical effect is that jev_progress_reaper = "shadow" ships as the default
while a seat that has not opted into sending log tails sees a byte-identical
reaper; ortus grind's dry run names which opt-in is missing. Also note the tail
carries its own 16 KB ceiling rather than judge.total_bytes_cap (8192): that
budget bounds the packed issue state, which this request does not send at all.

Fail-open throughout: no key, no SDK, a timeout, a malformed answer, an
unreadable log or an unexpected exception in the check each cost a reading and
never a worker, and a failure between two looping readings resets the evidence.
Scope notes: the watch is armed only on the backends that have a reap poll
(claude, grok); no per-backend log decoder was written — one summarizer handles
JSON-object lines generically and falls through to raw text — and enforce stays
opt-in, so nothing reaps until the shadow corpus has been scored.

Two pre-existing defects found on a clean checkout of HEAD, both outside this
claim and filed rather than fixed here: ortus-qznc (tests/test_judge_shadow.py
fails 44 parametrizations, unpacking a two-record decision log) and ortus-z2no
(an unused triage import fails ruff on the orchestrator module).

title: Jev triage of PLAN-GAP and readiness-failed parks into automatic routes
description:
## Objective

Triage parked PLAN-GAP beads and readiness-failed beads with Jev into pin-skew fix, planner auto-fix, or truly needs human, and route the two non-human classes to an automatic path while the deterministic readiness rule stays the actual gate.

## Behavioral context

Before: grind._flag_unready_for_human labels every readiness-failed leaf human and comments the diagnostic ("grind will not repair this packet"), and a worker or judge_post PLAN-GAP labels the bead human; pin_skew.tag_pin_skew_claims only annotates a human park with the pin-skew label and leaves it parked. Every class waits for an operator. After: a regex first pass (pin_skew.classify_plan_gap) still runs first; beads it does not classify get a Jev triage vector (p_pin_skew, p_planner_fix, p_needs_human). System Two routes by argmax: pin-skew releases the bead to open with the pin-skew label and a pin directive (lower the declared value, file a restore bead) and no human label; planner-fix runs one bounded planner re-spec of that bead's description/design/acceptance and re-runs readiness schema v1 validation, removing the human label only if the deterministic check passes; needs-human keeps today's human label and comments the probabilities as advice. Diamond model: Jev output feeds the routing as probabilities/advice; no new confidence-floor parking. The human label comes from the needs-human class winning, not from a confidence threshold.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

- New module src/ortus/core/judge_triage.py: TriageClass enum, TriageVector, triage_parked(issue, evidence, config) using one bounded Jev choice request with sanitized state (same pattern as judge_post.evaluate_outcome), and route_triage(vector) as pure System Two.
- Call it from grind._flag_unready_for_human (readiness-failed leaves) and from the PLAN-GAP park path after tag_pin_skew_claims (worker/judge PLAN-GAP parks).
- Pin-skew route: remove human label, keep/add PIN_SKEW_LABEL, comment the pin directive; the next work prompt carries the pin directive.
- Planner-fix route: one bounded planner re-spec turn for that bead (plan-phase profile), write the repaired fields with bd update, re-validate with the readiness schema v1 validator; on pass remove human label, on fail keep human with both diagnostics. At most one auto re-spec per bead, tracked by a marker comment.
- Needs-human route: current behavior plus the probability vector in the comment.
- Log every triage (vector, class, route, regex_hit, fail_open) to the judge decision log.
- Hermetic tests with mocked Jev and mocked planner runner.

## Non-goals

- The Jev vector never replaces the deterministic readiness check; a bead reaches the grind queue only by passing it.
- No change to the pin_skew regex classifier thresholds (it stays the conservative first pass).
- No confidence floor; no new needs_human gate.
- No repo markdown artifacts; no reinstall-cli.sh.
- Epics are not triaged.

## Concrete locations

- src/ortus/commands/grind.py: _flag_unready_for_human(), the tag_pin_skew_claims() call site, _release_parked_head(), _compose_work_prompt().
- src/ortus/core/grind_loop.py: select_ready_issue(on_unready=...).
- src/ortus/core/pin_skew.py: classify_plan_gap(), latest_plan_gap(), pin_skew_note(), tag_pin_skew_claims(), PIN_SKEW_LABEL.
- src/ortus/core/judge_readiness.py: evaluate_readiness(), readiness_context(); src/ortus/core/readiness.py (schema v1 validator used by ortus validate).
- src/ortus/core/judge_post.py: evaluate_outcome() as the Jev request pattern; apply_outcome() plan_gap branch.
- src/ortus/commands/plan.py (planner runner and plan profile) for the re-spec turn.
- tests/test_pin_dont_park.py, tests/test_readiness.py, new tests/test_judge_triage.py.
- CodeGraph evidence: codegraph query classify_plan_gap (pin_skew.py:113), tag_pin_skew_claims (pin_skew.py:174, imported by grind.py), _flag_unready_for_human (grind.py), select_ready_issue (grind_loop.py:169).

## Resolved decisions

1. Diamond model (Andy, locked): Jev passes the triage vector to System Two; routing is argmax; no confidence floor.
2. Regex pin-skew stays the first pass; a regex hit routes to pin-skew without calling Jev.
3. The deterministic readiness schema v1 rule is the only gate to the queue; planner-fix only proposes a repaired packet.
4. Human label only when needs-human wins, or on fail-open (Jev unavailable means today's behavior: human label).
5. Enforcement in code: routes are executed by grind and the pin directive is injected into the work prompt by code.
6. One auto re-spec attempt per bead bounds cost and prevents repair loops.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux/macOS, Python 3.10-3.12. With Jev off, behavior equals today (human label plus diagnostic comment). The readiness comment text keeps the bd label remove instruction for the needs-human class. pin-skew label semantics stay annotation-compatible for existing parks.

## Ordered steps

1. Read _flag_unready_for_human, the tag_pin_skew_claims call site and classify_plan_gap.
2. Implement judge_triage.py (questions, triage_parked, route_triage) with sanitized, bounded evidence (readiness diagnostic or latest PLAN-GAP comment).
3. Wire regex first pass then Jev triage into both park paths.
4. Implement the pin-skew route and the pin directive in the work prompt.
5. Implement the bounded planner re-spec turn plus deterministic re-validation and the one-attempt marker.
6. Implement needs-human route with the vector in the comment; log every triage.
7. Add hermetic tests (mocked Jev, mocked planner) and run the targeted tests.

## Dependencies

No open issue dependency. Related closed work: ortus-aesp (semantic readiness beside schema v1), pin-dont-park work in pin_skew.py. Consumers: grind main loop, select_ready_issue on_unready callback, ortus human queue listing.

## Edge cases

- Jev timeout or invalid answer: fail-open to human label.
- Planner re-spec output still fails readiness: keep human, comment both diagnostics, no second attempt.
- Bead closed concurrently: skip.
- Regex hit but Jev would say needs-human: regex wins (first pass), Jev is not called.
- Epic or missing comments: skip triage.
- Label/comment write failure: warn and continue with the next bead.

## Plan-gap guidance

If no reusable planner runner can re-spec a single bead within a worker window, land the triage, pin-skew route and needs-human route, keep planner-fix as a logged recommendation with the human label, and record PLAN-GAP for the re-spec runner only. Never bypass the readiness schema check to unpark a bead.

title: Jev decides continue/re-plan/escalate after one no-close window
description:
## Objective

After one no-close worker window on an in_progress bead, decide continue / re-plan / escalate from Jev post-turn probabilities instead of the fixed two-window wedge rule, and remove the 0.8 confidence-floor parking in judge_post.apply_outcome so low confidence feeds that decision as a probability.

## Behavioral context

Before: grind.py counts consecutive no-close windows in bd marker comments (_no_close_window_count) and escalates to the human queue only when the count reaches _WEDGED_WINDOW_THRESHOLD = 2 (_escalate_wedged_claim), so a clearly stuck bead burns two 90-minute windows and a clearly progressing one gets escalated anyway at two. Separately judge_post.apply_outcome labels the bead human with reason low_confidence whenever verdict.confidence < 0.8, a hard confidence floor that the diamond model forbids. After: once a window ends without a close, System Two builds a probability vector (p_continue, p_replan, p_escalate) from the Jev post-turn outcome verdict (choice plus confidence, shrunk toward uniform by confidence), the no-close window count and branch_advanced, and takes the action in code: continue resumes as today, replan resumes in a fresh window with a re-plan directive in the composed work prompt, escalate uses the existing _escalate_wedged_claim. Low confidence only flattens the vector; it never parks. When Jev is unavailable the current two-window rule runs unchanged (fail-open). Diamond model: Jev output feeds the decision as probabilities/advice; no new confidence-floor parking.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

- New pure System Two function decide_stuck_claim(verdict, windows, branch_advanced) returning a StuckDecision (action plus the probability vector) in src/ortus/core/judge_post.py (or a new src/ortus/core/judge_stuck.py).
- Wire it into both grind.py call sites that consult _WEDGED_WINDOW_THRESHOLD (the resume path using resume_no_close_count and the post-window judged_id path) after the first no-close window.
- replan action: resume the claim in a fresh window and pass a re-plan directive plus the stalled-window facts into _compose_work_prompt; record a replan marker comment so a second replan in a row is visible to the vector.
- Remove the verdict.confidence < 0.8 low_confidence human branch in apply_outcome; confidence is passed into decide_stuck_claim instead.
- Log each decision (vector, action, windows, fail_open flag) to the judge decision log.
- Hermetic tests with a mocked Jev client.

## Non-goals

- No change to judge_tools.py tool-guard thresholds or JudgeConfig human_threshold (pre-tool guards are out of scope).
- No new confidence floor or needs_human gate anywhere.
- Do not change the no-close marker comment format (cross-process store must stay stable).
- Do not change the closure_disagreement, tracker_closed or worker_timeout handling.
- Do not reset ortus-nudo, ortus-p810 or ortus-2637.

## Concrete locations

- src/ortus/commands/grind.py: _no_close_window_count(), _escalate_wedged_claim(), _WEDGED_WINDOW_THRESHOLD, _announce_wedged_escalation(), _compose_work_prompt(), the resume branch using resume_no_close_count and the post-window branch using judged_id / pending.
- src/ortus/core/judge_post.py: apply_outcome(), evaluate_outcome(), OutcomeVerdict, Outcome (done, plan_gap, flake, auth, needs_human, continue), WorkerOutcome.branch_advanced.
- src/ortus/core/judge_routing.py: _shrunk() as the reference shrink-toward-uniform pattern.
- tests/test_judge_post.py, tests/test_grind_judge.py, tests/test_grind_reap.py.
- CodeGraph evidence: codegraph query apply_outcome (judge_post.py:163, imported by grind.py and tests/test_judge_replay.py); codegraph query _escalate_wedged_claim and _no_close_window_count (grind.py); rg shows the only 0.8 floor in judge_post at the low_confidence branch.

## Resolved decisions

1. Diamond model (Andy, locked): Jev output feeds the stuck decision as a probability vector; System Two acts; no confidence-floor parking.
2. Vector construction: put the verdict confidence on the class mapped from the outcome choice (continue and flake map to continue; plan_gap maps to replan; needs_human and auth map to escalate), spread the remainder uniformly, then add a window-count prior that shifts mass from continue toward replan and escalate as windows grow, and toward continue when branch_advanced is true. Action is the argmax.
3. Decision happens after the first no-close window (windows >= 1), not two.
4. Fail-open: verdict.failure set or Jev disabled means the existing count >= _WEDGED_WINDOW_THRESHOLD rule runs unchanged.
5. Enforcement in code: the action is executed by grind, and the re-plan directive is injected by _compose_work_prompt, not left as prompt advice in markdown.
6. The existing plan_gap / auth / needs_human outcome annotations stay as they are except the low_confidence floor, which is removed.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux/macOS, Python 3.10-3.12. Seats with Jev off must see identical behavior to today (two-window escalation). Decision log records are additive. Shadow mode logs the decision but applies the fail-open baseline.

## Ordered steps

1. Read both _WEDGED_WINDOW_THRESHOLD call sites and apply_outcome.
2. Implement decide_stuck_claim and StuckDecision as pure functions with the vector rule above.
3. Remove the low_confidence branch from apply_outcome and return the verdict for the stuck decision.
4. Wire decide_stuck_claim into the resume and post-window paths; keep the two-window rule as the fail-open branch.
5. Add the replan directive parameter to _compose_work_prompt and the replan marker comment.
6. Log each decision with vector, action and fail_open.
7. Add hermetic tests with mocked Jev and run the targeted tests.

## Dependencies

No open issue dependency. Builds on closed ortus-3d2s (post-turn outcome) and ortus-22oi (scrap hard gate). Consumers: grind main loop resume and post-window paths; judge replay/calibration readers of the decision log (tests/test_judge_replay.py imports apply_outcome).

## Edge cases

- Jev returns an invalid answer: fail-open to two-window rule.
- Confidence 0: vector is uniform plus priors; no human label from confidence alone.
- Bead closed concurrently during the decision: do nothing (re-read tracker as apply_outcome does).
- Replan chosen twice in a row: the replan marker raises escalate mass; still no floor.
- Shadow mode: log only.
- bd comment write fails: log and continue with the baseline rule.

## Plan-gap guidance

If a replan cannot be expressed without a planner phase that does not exist in grind, keep replan as a fresh-window resume with the directive and record PLAN-GAP only for a dedicated planner path. If removing the 0.8 floor breaks a calibration/replay contract test that encodes the floor as required behavior, stop and record PLAN-GAP instead of re-adding a floor.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1: decide_stuck_claim maps mocked Jev verdicts to continue, replan and escalate by argmax of the probability vector after one no-close window. `uv run pytest tests/test_judge_post.py -k decide_stuck -q`
- AC-2: apply_outcome no longer labels a bead human for low confidence; a 0.5-confidence verdict produces no human label and no low_confidence reason. `uv run pytest tests/test_judge_post.py -k low_confidence -q`
- AC-3: With Jev failing or disabled, grind keeps the two-window escalation exactly as before. `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_judge.py -k stuck_fail_open -q`
- AC-4: A replan decision resumes the claim with the re-plan directive present in the composed work prompt. `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_judge.py -k stuck_replan -q`
- AC-5: Each stuck decision is logged with the vector, action, windows and fail_open flag. `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_judge.py -k stuck_decision_logged -q`

## Targeted tests

uv run pytest tests/test_judge_post.py tests/test_grind_judge.py tests/test_judge_replay.py -q
close_reason: Stuck claims now route by a continue/replan/escalate probability vector after one no-close window; the 0.8 post-turn confidence floor is gone and a missing verdict fails open to the old threshold rule

comments.author: who
comments.text:
Landed. The two-window wedge rule and the 0.8 post-turn confidence floor are both gone; a claim whose window ended without a close is now routed by a probability vector over continue / replan / escalate, with the argmax taken in code.

Vector: the verdict's confidence lands on the class its choice argues for (continue and flake and done -> continue, plan_gap -> replan, auth and needs_human -> escalate) and the remainder spreads uniformly, so zero confidence is the uniform vector rather than a park. The burned-window count then moves mass off continue (more of it to escalate as windows grow), a spent re-plan moves mass off replan, and a window that advanced the integration branch pulls mass back to continue.

Replan resumes the same claim in a fresh window whose prompt carries a directive naming the stalled-window facts and asking for a different route; a marker comment records each directive spent so a second replan in a row is a weaker bet than the first. No usable verdict (phase off, service failure, invalid answer) fails open to the old threshold rule unchanged; shadow mode logs the read action and applies that baseline.

Each decision is appended to logs/jev-decisions.jsonl as a stuck_decision record carrying the vector, windows, branch_advanced, fail_open, the action read and the action applied; the replay validator accepts the new shape.

One consequence worth flagging for the next reader: a post-turn answer no longer halts the grind loop by itself for a live in_progress claim. It is an input to the decision, which escalates, parks or resumes. A bead the answer labels human still leaves the queue via the existing excluded-label path.

The four vector constants were authored to satisfy the specified mapping, not measured. Filed as ortus-saqu (discovered-from this issue).

Criterion checks, all green:
- AC-1: uv run pytest tests/test_judge_post.py -k decide_stuck -q
- AC-2: uv run pytest tests/test_judge_post.py -k low_confidence -q
- AC-3: uv run pytest tests/test_grind_judge.py -k stuck_fail_open -q
- AC-4: uv run pytest tests/test_grind_judge.py -k stuck_replan -q
- AC-5: uv run pytest tests/test_grind_judge.py -k stuck_decision_logged -q
Plus the surrounding suites: tests/test_judge_post.py tests/test_grind_judge.py tests/test_judge_replay.py tests/test_grind.py tests/test_grind_reap.py tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py tests/test_judge_calibration.py tests/test_core_judge_policy.py -- 308 passed, 27 skipped (pre-existing skips).

title: Jev router: measure the A/B p810 skipped and set jev_model_router default
description:
## Objective

Measure the Jev per-bead model/effort router against the pinned implement profile on the Hello World eval fixture, record the thresholds and results on this bead, and make jev_model_router default-on in judge enforce mode (and log-only in shadow mode) if the router is not worse on close rate and is cheaper or faster.

## Behavioral context

Before: ortus-yjk4 landed route_implement_profile, CHEAP_CEILING=0.34 and FRONTIER_FLOOR=0.67, the routing log and the jev_model_router flag, but the flag defaults to False in src/ortus/core/config.py DEFAULTS and ORTUS_JEV_ROUTER is the only override; the router only acts in enforce mode. ortus-p810 (the A/B) closed without the work ("worker closed without Claims"), so the hand-picked thresholds have never been measured and harness_eval TREATMENTS still names ortus-p810 as measured_by for the model-router arm. After: one control-vs-model-router Hello World comparison has been run with fresh repo code (uv run ortus eval, not the stale installed ~/.local/bin/ortus), its cost per closed bead, close rate, wall time and per-tier routing counts are recorded as bead metadata on this issue (not as a repo markdown file), the default follows the verdict, and shadow mode logs the route it would have picked without changing the worker profile. Diamond model: Jev output feeds the route as probabilities/advice; no new confidence-floor parking or needs_human gate is introduced.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

- Run the Hello World fixture under the control arm and the model-router arm of the frozen eval set with the repo's current code.
- Record thresholds (CHEAP_CEILING, FRONTIER_FLOOR), per-arm cost per closed bead, close rate, wall-clock time and per-tier routing counts on this bead via bd metadata key jev_router_ab (JSON), plus a short bd comment summarising the verdict.
- If router close rate is not lower than control and router cost per closed bead or wall time is lower, flip jev_model_router to True in DEFAULTS; otherwise keep False and record the null result in the same metadata.
- Let shadow mode compute and log the route (logs/jev-model-routes.jsonl with an applied=false marker) without changing the implement profile, so shadow seats accumulate router evidence.
- Point the model-router Treatment.measured_by in harness_eval at this bead.
- Hermetic tests with a mocked Jev client for the default, the shadow log-only path, fail-open, and the control-vs-router comparison rendering.

## Non-goals

- No confidence floor, needs_human gate or parking inside the router; a tier boundary is not a gate.
- No change to JudgeAnswers fields or the criteria pack vectors.
- No run of the converter fixture or the prompt-audit / stable-prefix arms (those belong to ortus-2637 and ortus-nudo, which must not be reset or touched).
- No repo markdown results file; no reinstall-cli.sh run.
- Do not remove the ORTUS_JEV_ROUTER override; it stays as a per-run kill switch (ORTUS_JEV_ROUTER=0 forces off).

## Concrete locations

- src/ortus/core/judge_routing.py: route_implement_profile(), jev_router_enabled(), CHEAP_CEILING, FRONTIER_FLOOR, RouterTier, JEV_ROUTER_CONFIG_KEY.
- src/ortus/core/config.py: DEFAULTS["jev_model_router"], _validate_jev_model_router().
- src/ortus/commands/grind.py: _route_model(), _gate_turn(), _shadow_turn() (shadow must log the would-be route).
- src/ortus/core/judge_log.py: ModelRouteEvent, write_model_route().
- src/ortus/core/harness_eval.py: TREATMENTS (model-router Treatment, measured_by), ARMS, arm_commands(), cost_per_closed_bead / close_rate report fields.
- src/ortus/commands/eval.py: ortus eval --matrix / --run / --cell-timeout.
- tests/test_jev_model_router.py, tests/test_core_config.py, tests/test_harness_eval_report.py.
- CodeGraph evidence: codegraph query route_implement_profile (judge_routing.py, imported by grind.py and tests/test_jev_model_router.py); codegraph query jev_router_enabled; rg jev_model_router shows config.py DEFAULTS False and harness_eval model-router Treatment measured_by ortus-p810.

## Resolved decisions

1. Andy locked the diamond model: Jev (System One) passes probability vectors to System Two; the router maps them to a tier with no confidence floor and no needs_human gate.
2. Decision rule for the default: router default-on when router close rate >= control close rate AND (router cost per closed bead < control OR router wall time < control). Otherwise default stays off and the null result is recorded.
3. Results live in bd metadata (jev_router_ab) and a bd comment on this bead, never in a repo markdown artifact.
4. Evals run with fresh code: prepend the repo .venv/bin to PATH (or use uv run ortus) so the cell commands do not hit the stale installed ortus.
5. Enforcement over prompt advice: the route is applied in code (_route_model), not suggested in the worker prompt.
6. Jev failure or timeout (1.5s, jev-1.13.0) fails open to the pinned baseline profile, as today.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux/macOS, Python 3.10-3.12 hermetic gate. .ortusrc jev_model_router=false must still force the router off; ORTUS_JEV_ROUTER=0/1 still overrides config per run. Planner stays on the frontier profile. Existing jev-model-routes.jsonl records stay readable; the new applied field is additive.

## Ordered steps

1. Read route_implement_profile, jev_router_enabled, _route_model and _shadow_turn; confirm how mode gates the router today.
2. Print the recipe with uv run ortus eval /tmp/ortus-router-ab --matrix and pick the hello-world control and hello-world model-router cells.
3. Run those two cells with fresh repo code (in parallel if feasible, each bounded to about 2400s) and collect the report with uv run ortus eval /tmp/ortus-router-ab --json.
4. Write jev_router_ab metadata (thresholds, per-arm cost_per_closed_bead, close_rate, wall seconds, tier counts, verdict) on this bead with bd update --set-metadata, and add a one-paragraph bd comment.
5. Apply the decision rule: flip DEFAULTS jev_model_router to True or keep False; update harness_eval model-router measured_by to this bead.
6. Make _shadow_turn compute the route and write_model_route with applied=false, leaving the worker profile at baseline.
7. Add hermetic tests (mocked Jev): default matches recorded verdict, shadow logs without applying, Jev failure falls back to baseline, report renders control vs model-router comparison.
8. Run the targeted tests.

## Dependencies

Follows closed ortus-yjk4 (router) and ortus-p810 (closed without the measurement). Consumers: grind._route_model, grind._shadow_turn, harness_eval report. No open issue dependency. Must not touch ortus-nudo or ortus-2637.

## Edge cases

- Eval cell times out or reports no cost: record the partial numbers and null metrics honestly; do not flip the default on missing data.
- Both arms close zero beads: record null result, keep default off.
- Router picks only the baseline tier for Hello World: record tier counts; verdict still follows the rule.
- ORTUS_JEV_ROUTER=0 with default True must disable routing.
- Jev unavailable in shadow: no route log line, no crash.

## Plan-gap guidance

If the eval cannot run at all (backend auth failure, eval harness broken), record the failure in jev_router_ab metadata and a comment, keep the default off, still land the shadow logging and tests, and note PLAN-GAP for the measurement only. Do not invent thresholds without data, and do not add any confidence floor to make the router look safer.

## Observable criteria

- AC-1: DEFAULTS jev_model_router matches the verdict recorded in jev_router_ab and a test asserts it together with the ORTUS_JEV_ROUTER=0 kill switch. `uv run pytest tests/test_jev_model_router.py -k default -q`
- AC-2: In shadow mode the router computes and logs the would-be route with applied false while the worker keeps the baseline profile. `uv run pytest tests/test_jev_model_router.py -k shadow -q`
- AC-3: A mocked Jev failure or timeout falls back to the pinned baseline profile with no parking or human label. `uv run pytest tests/test_jev_model_router.py -k fail_open -q`

- AC-5: This bead carries jev_router_ab metadata with thresholds, per-arm metrics and the verdict. `bd search --has-metadata-key jev_router_ab --status all`
- AC-6: The router still has no confidence floor or needs_human gate. `uv run pytest tests/test_jev_model_router.py -k no_confidence_floor -q`

## Targeted tests

comments.author: who
comments.text:
Landed the router's observation path, the arm recipe that actually exercises it, and the comparison a default gets flipped on. Shadow mode now asks the router for the tier it would have picked and appends it to the routing log with applied=false, so a shadow rollout accumulates evidence while its worker keeps the pinned profile; the join that turns tiers into per-tier close rates skips those rows, because crediting a bead's outcome to a tier that never ran it would read a control arm's numbers as the router's. A judge that answered nothing writes no observation at all: a row with no tier and no vector is not evidence.

Found and fixed a defect in the arm itself. The router is only ever consulted from the enforcing pre-turn gate, and a fresh seat ships that gate off, so the recipe's single `jev_model_router = true` line left the model-router arm running the control's configuration with an unread flag in its config. The treatment now carries the extra `.ortusrc` lines that enable the gate, written below the flag so the table header cannot swallow the top-level key. The report gained a control-versus-treatment block that computes the verdict from the decision rule rather than leaving the subtraction to a reader scanning a wide table.

PLAN-GAP, measurement only. Both hello-world cells were launched here and both died at planning: the seats set sandbox.failIfUnavailable, and an agent launched from inside an already-sandboxed session cannot bind its own mux socket, so every Bash call in the nested planner failed with EPERM and neither arm created a bead. That is the failure mode the stored operational rule operational-rule-2026-08-11-launch-ortus-grind already predicts for a session-launched run; the cells belong in a plain terminal. Both arms are recorded as failed cells with null metrics in jev_router_ab metadata on this issue, along with the thresholds and the decision rule.

The default therefore stays off, and the test that pins it asserts against a named verdict constant rather than a preference, so flipping it later means editing the recorded verdict too. Filed ortus-ib1w to run the two cells from a terminal and set the default from the numbers, and pointed the model-router treatment's measured_by at that bead rather than at this one — naming a bead that did not produce the numbers is exactly the defect this issue was opened about.

title: Grok headless seats skip project CodeGraph MCP without --trust
description:
## Objective
Make Ortus-launched Grok plan/grind workers able to use the project-scoped CodeGraph MCP server that `ortus init --backend grok` already writes into `.grok/config.toml`.

## Behavioral context
Today `ortus plan`/`ortus grind` with `--backend grok` and `codegraph=required` fail the CodeGraph MCP handshake on a fresh temp repo even though `.grok/config.toml` registers `codegraph`, `ortus check` reports MCP registered, and the `codegraph` CLI plus `.codegraph/` index are present. Interactive Grok in a previously trusted folder (for example `~/code/ortus`) does see CodeGraph. After the fix, a headless `grok` spawn from Ortus in an untrusted checkout must observe CodeGraph MCP tools so the required handshake can succeed.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Teach `GrokRunner` launches to grant folder trust (or otherwise start the project-scoped CodeGraph MCP) the same way Codex already injects trust-independent MCP registration. Update/extend the store-only test so the argv (or equivalent launch surface) actually enables CodeGraph for headless seats. Optionally tighten `ortus check` so "MCP registered" is not a false comfort when Grok will refuse to start project servers without trust.

## Non-goals
No change to Claude or OpenCode CodeGraph wiring. Do not move CodeGraph into user-global `~/.grok/config.toml` as the primary fix. Do not weaken `codegraph=required` handshake policy. Do not patch around this only in e2e harness scripts.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/core/agent.py` — `GrokRunner.build_argv` (today stores capability and explicitly does not emit grok MCP/`-c` overrides; comment at the `codegraph is stored for later MCP wiring` leaf) and `GrokRunner.configure_codegraph`.
- `tests/test_agent.py` — `test_grok_codegraph_is_store_only` currently asserts no MCP wiring on argv.
- Contrast: `CodexRunner.build_argv` in the same file emits `-c mcp_servers.codegraph.command/args/enabled_tools=...` with an explicit comment that CLI overrides do not depend on repository trust state.
- Init already writes `.grok/config.toml` `[mcp_servers.codegraph]` via `BACKEND_TEMPLATES["grok"]` / init render; `src/ortus/commands/check.py` `_grok_mcp_registered` only checks that file.

## Resolved decisions
Smallest fix: pass Grok's headless folder-trust flag (`--trust`) on Ortus-owned `GrokRunner` launches so project-scoped `.grok/config.toml` MCP servers (including CodeGraph) are allowed to start. Grok docs state headless startup with project MCP/hooks/instructions requires `--trust` or a prior grant in `~/.grok/trusted_folders.toml`. Prefer argv `--trust` over mutating the global trust store. Keep writing project `.grok/config.toml` as today.

## Compatibility constraints
Must keep working for already-trusted folders (flag should be idempotent). Readonly verifier launches should still be able to use CodeGraph for orientation if required policy demands it; apply the same trust grant there unless a safer Codex-style `-c` override path is chosen instead. Linux WSL seats using `bwrap` sandbox remain supported.

## Ordered steps
1. Reproduce with `grok mcp doctor` in an untrusted temp repo that has Ortus-written `.grok/config.toml`: expect `folder untrusted` for `codegraph`.
2. Add `--trust` to `GrokRunner.build_argv` (or an equivalent launch-time trust/MCP enablement that does not depend on prior interactive grant).
3. Replace/adjust `test_grok_codegraph_is_store_only` to assert the trust/MCP enablement is present when `configure_codegraph` has been called.
4. Add a focused regression that a required-codegraph plan handshake can observe a CodeGraph tool event under grok (unit with transcript fixture and/or live-gated test).
5. Optionally extend `_grok_mcp_registered` / `ortus check` messaging to mention folder trust when only the file is present.

## Dependencies
No issue dependency — standalone bugfix. Callers are `plan`/`grind` via `make_runner("grok")` and `configure_codegraph`.

## Edge cases
Nested git worktrees are separate trust workspaces per Grok docs. Sandbox profiles that refuse persisting trust still honor session `--trust`. If Grok later adds Codex-like `-c mcp_servers.*` overrides, that remains an acceptable alternate implementation as long as headless untrusted checkouts get CodeGraph without an interactive grant.

## Plan-gap guidance
If Grok's `--trust` semantics change or disappear, record PLAN-GAP naming the current doctor remediation text and the `trusted_folders.toml` store path; do not silently fall back to skipping the CodeGraph handshake under `codegraph=required`.

- AC-2 (proves-new): With `codegraph=required`, an Ortus grok plan against a fresh untrusted repo that already has `.grok/config.toml` `[mcp_servers.codegraph]` observes a CodeGraph MCP capability (handshake success path), rather than failing with "planning agent reported no CodeGraph MCP tool capability". `uv run pytest tests/test_core_codegraph.py -k grok -q`

title: Grind leaves head-of-queue beads stuck in_progress and miscounts them at exit
description:
## Objective

Stop ortus grind from leaving head-of-queue beads stuck in_progress without a recorded worker claim, and make the session-exit summary count every open and in_progress bead — including human-labeled ones — so operators see the real queue.

## Behavioral context

Before. A grind session (logs/grind-20260923-221044.log, night of 2026-09-23/24 PT) selected ortus-nudo (00:31:39), ortus-p810 (00:42:29), and ortus-2637 (01:11:10) as head via iter prep worker-will-claim and goal-prompt-ready lines. None of the three produced a worker claimed line; each ended with claim flagged human / reaping worker, then no worker claim observed in bd while judging the readiness-passing head, then not resuming because of the human label with claim and work stay parked. All three remained in_progress after exit. The console progress line printed done — 15 landed this session, 0 in_progress, 0 open while three beads were still in_progress and two human-parked beads (ortus-yod4, ortus-onq7) were still open. Exit counts come from _snapshot which applies EXCLUDED_LABELS (human) to open and in_progress, so human-labeled beads disappear from the summary.

After. A head that is human-flagged mid-window is reverted to open (or otherwise left non-in_progress) before the loop continues, so no bead stays stuck in_progress without a worker claimed attribution. The exit progress line reports true open and in_progress counts that include human-labeled beads (loop control may still exclude them). Secondary: yod4 and onq7 were human-parked for missing design sections after ortus-04a5 closed at 00:16 — the long-running process likely still had pre-04a5 code; 04a5's validate-then-create gate commit 0fdf2ca is on main now and must stay there.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

- Fix the post-window path in src/ortus/commands/grind.py that logs no worker claim observed / not resuming … stay parked so a human-flagged head is not left in_progress.
- Fix the session-end progress line (done — N landed this session, X in_progress, Y open) so X and Y are raw bd counts including human-labeled beads; keep EXCLUDED_LABELS for loop control and orphan detection only.
- Add or extend targeted tests covering (a) human-flag mid-window leaves the bead open not in_progress, and (b) exit summary counts include human-labeled open and in_progress beads.

## Non-goals

- Do not remove EXCLUDED_LABELS from list_ready, queue_drained, or orphan-detection diffs.
- Do not change the WorkerFailure taxonomy or readiness schema.
- Do not re-open or rewrite ortus-nudo / ortus-p810 / ortus-2637 work specs beyond whatever status repair operators already did.
- Do not add a --judge requirement; this is harness-loop accounting.

## Concrete locations

- src/ortus/commands/grind.py — _snapshot (approx line 662): today passes exclude_labels=EXCLUDED_LABELS into count_by_status for open and in_progress and into in_progress_ids; the exit progress at approx lines 2915-2919 reads final_snapshot.in_progress / final_snapshot.open.
- src/ortus/commands/grind.py — post-window attribution around lines 2728-2745 (worker claimed vs no worker claim observed in bd; judging the readiness-passing head) and the not resuming … stay parked branch that follows a claim flagged human reap.
- src/ortus/core/grind_loop.py — EXCLUDED_LABELS (line 46), StateSnapshot / queue_drained (lines 67-142), select_ready_issue (line 169), apply_orphan_policy (line 330).
- src/ortus/core/bd.py — count_by_status (line 433) and in_progress_ids (line 481) already honor exclude_labels; callers choose whether to pass human.
- tests/test_grind_loop.py, tests/test_grind.py, tests/test_grind_reap.py — existing coverage for queue_drained, orphan policy, and claim hand-back.

## Resolved decisions

1. Loop control keeps excluding human-labeled beads from ready selection and drain checks (EXCLUDED_LABELS stays).
2. Operator-facing exit summary must not exclude human; under-counting is the bug.
3. A head that ends the window human-flagged must not remain in_progress: revert to open (label kept) before continuing, matching the hand-back spirit of _hand_back_comment.
4. 04a5's shared validate-then-create gate (commit 0fdf2ca on main) is already the correct filing path; this issue does not re-implement it, only requires it remain present.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux/WSL2 and macOS grind hosts. bd JSON list/count APIs and the existing EXCLUDED_LABELS contract for ready/orphan paths must keep working. Log line shapes (iter prep / goal-prompt ready / worker claimed / no worker claim observed / grind ended) may gain a revert/hand-back line but must not drop the attribution milestones operators grep for.

## Ordered steps

1. Reproduce the miscount in a unit test: build a snapshot path where human-labeled in_progress and open beads exist and assert today's exit progress would report 0/0.
2. Split accounting: keep _snapshot for loop control with EXCLUDED_LABELS; add a raw count (or a flag) used only by the exit progress line.
3. On claim flagged human / not resuming stay parked, revert the bead to open (keep human) before the next iter prep, and log the hand-back.
4. Prove with targeted tests that a human-flagged head is open after the window and that the exit line includes human-labeled counts.
5. Confirm git show / merge-base that 0fdf2ca (ortus-04a5) remains on main; if absent, PLAN-GAP.

## Dependencies

No open blocker. Evidence depends on closed ortus-04a5 (readiness bounce) already on main. Code consumers: operators reading grind console/log exit lines; Herdr seat ortus restart after drain.

## Edge cases

- Multiple human-labeled in_progress leftovers at startup: leftover_claims already uses exclude_labels; do not change startup resume of non-human leftovers.
- Human-labeled open beads that were never claimed must still appear in the exit open count.
- A genuine worker claim that also gets human later in the same window must still emit worker claimed when bd state showed the claim, then hand back on reap.
- Codex vs Claude backends share the grind.py attribution path; fix once for both.

## Plan-gap guidance

If handing back a human-flagged head would race a live assignee that is not the grind actor, or if raw exit counts cannot be obtained without a second bd round-trip that destabilizes flock holders, stop, record PLAN-GAP with the exact bd show fields and call site, preserve candidate edits, and route to human — do not drop EXCLUDED_LABELS from ready selection to paper over the summary bug, and do not close human-labeled beads automatically.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1 (proves-new): after a window that human-flags the selected head, that bead is open (not in_progress) while still carrying human.
- AC-2 (proves-new): the session-end progress line reports in_progress and open counts that include human-labeled beads when such beads exist.
- AC-3 (guards-existing): queue_drained and list_ready still ignore human-labeled beads so the loop does not spin on human-only queues.
- AC-4 (guards-existing): ortus-04a5's validate-then-create commit remains on main (git merge-base --is-ancestor of 0fdf2ca).

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: uv run pytest tests/test_grind_reap.py tests/test_grind.py -k "human and (hand_back or reclaim or flagged or parked)" -q
- AC-2: uv run pytest tests/test_grind.py tests/test_grind_loop.py -k "snapshot or exit or landed or summary or exclude" -q
- AC-3: uv run pytest tests/test_grind_loop.py -k "queue_drained or exclude" tests/test_core_bd.py -k "exclude_labels" -q
- AC-4: git merge-base --is-ancestor 0fdf2ca06b2a5debafc57418813cc6f5094c47b9 HEAD

## Targeted tests

uv run pytest tests/test_grind_loop.py tests/test_grind_reap.py tests/test_core_bd.py tests/test_grind.py -k "exclude or queue_drained or snapshot or human or hand_back or orphan" -q
