A head that ends its window carrying an excluded label is now released: the claim reverts to open, the label and packet are untouched, and one comment names the window and the label that parked it. The queue already continued past such a head, so leaving the claim on it stranded the issue in_progress with no window able to resume it and no worker able to finish it.

The exit summary now reports unfiltered bd counts, so human-labelled open and in_progress issues appear in the operator's session-end line instead of vanishing from it. Loop control is unchanged — drain checks, ready selection, and orphan detection keep applying the excluded-label filter, and each raw count is floored at the loop's own figure so a failed query degrades to the smaller view rather than to zero.

AC-1 covered by the released-claim tests in the reap suite; AC-2 and AC-3 by the exit-summary and snapshot tests beside the grind suite; AC-4 confirmed by ancestry of 0fdf2ca on HEAD. All four criterion checks passed.

title: Worker-filed follow-ups must pass ingest readiness or bounce in-session
description:
## Objective
Force grind-worker follow-up and cleanup beads through the same readiness gate as ortus ingest, so an unready packet is bounced back to the worker in-session instead of being created, skipped, labeled human, and dropped from the queue.

## Behavioral context
Tonight 2026-09-23 PT, one ortus grind run (logs/grind-20260923-221044.log) had the live worker file three follow-ups mid-run without passing readiness. Grind then skipped each leaf, labeled it human, and left it out of the queue, requiring hand repair plus bd label remove id human:
- ortus-m6cn (P0 CI fix) failed design/compatibility constraints, design/dependencies, design/plan gap guidance (log 2652-2653).
- ortus-nudo failed acceptance_criteria/criterion checks with AC-1: no runnable command (log 3352-3353).
- ortus-p810 failed the same AC-1 criterion-check gap (log 3354-3355).
Operator and agents must not hand-repair worker-filed beads for this class of failure. Enforcement beats prompt advice: the filing path itself must refuse unready creates the way ortus ingest already does.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
- Make the grind worker follow-up / leftover filing path go through the same validate-then-create gate as `ortus ingest` (packet assemble + `validate_issue` before any `bd create`), or an equivalent hook/check that rejects in-session `bd create` from a grind worker unless the candidate validates.
- On nonzero / UNREADY result, return the readiness diagnostic to the worker in the same session so it can complete the packet; do not create the bead, do not label `human`, and do not park it out of the queue.
- Update bundled worker instructions (`work-issue` / `goal-prompt`) so follow-up filing names the ingest/gated path rather than raw `bd create`.
- Add regression coverage that a worker-shaped follow-up missing readiness sections or runnable AC commands creates nothing and surfaces gaps.

## Non-goals
- Changing the claim-time readiness skip for already-open legacy leaves (`select_ready_issue` / `_flag_unready_for_human`) beyond ensuring worker-filed creates never land in that path unready.
- Softening readiness schema v1 or adding hard confidence gates (diamond model: schema/readiness gate only).
- Hand-repairing or retouching ortus-nudo / ortus-p810 (other helper owns those).
- Starting, stopping, or unclaiming the live grind seat.
- Herdr or non-Ortus repos.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/prompts/conditions/work-issue.txt` -- pin-able skew instructs file a follow-up bead with no ingest/readiness gate (line ~21); symbol/surface: bundled work-issue condition text.
- `src/ortus/prompts/goal-prompt.md` -- leftover work File leftover work as new beads / follow-up bead language without ingest (line ~12).
- `src/ortus/commands/ingest.py` -- `ingest()`, `build_candidate()`, `validate_issue` before create; fail-closed UNREADY creates nothing.
- `src/ortus/core/readiness.py` -- `validate_issue()` (readiness schema v1).
- `src/ortus/core/grind_loop.py` -- `select_ready_issue()` calls `validate_issue` and reports unready via on_unready; `EXCLUDED_LABELS = ("human",)`.
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` -- `report_unready` / `_flag_unready_for_human()` (approx lines 1299-1339, 2227-2270) labels human and warns It stays open, labeled human, and out of the queue.
- `src/ortus/core/bd.py` -- `BdClient.create()` used by raw creates and by ingest after validation.
- Evidence log: `logs/grind-20260923-221044.log` readiness skip lines for ortus-m6cn / ortus-nudo / ortus-p810.
- CodeGraph: codegraph node _flag_unready_for_human, codegraph node select_ready_issue, codegraph callers validate_issue, codegraph query ingest.

## Resolved decisions
- Enforcement over prompt advice: a prompt line alone is insufficient; the create path must validate or call ingest.
- Preferred shape: worker writes a packet and runs `ortus ingest --packet <path>` (exit nonzero returns gaps in-session). Equivalent: a grind-worker hook/check that rejects `bd create` unless `validate_issue` passes.
- A worker-filed bead that fails readiness is bounced to the worker to complete, never silently parked `human`.
- Diamond model applies: no hard confidence gates; this remains a schema/readiness gate.

## Compatibility constraints
- External `ortus ingest` CLI contract and fail-closed semantics stay; reuse them rather than inventing a parallel validator.
- Existing claim-time human label for pre-existing unready leaves remains the operator escape hatch for non-worker-filed debt.
- Prompt overrides via `ortus prompt eject` must still resolve; update bundled defaults and tests.

## Ordered steps
1. Trace every worker-facing instruction that tells the model to file follow-ups or leftover beads (work-issue, goal-prompt, related audited copies) and point them at packet + ortus ingest (or the gated create helper).
2. Implement the gate: either call ingest from the worker filing path, or add a grind-worker-side check that runs validate_issue before BdClient.create and refuses unready candidates with the same diagnostic ingest prints.
3. Ensure failure returns gaps to the active worker session (nonzero exit / structured message) and performs no create, no human label, and no queue park.
4. Add tests covering (a) unready follow-up packet creates nothing, (b) ready follow-up packet creates a bead that validate_issue accepts, (c) prompt content names the gated path.
5. Confirm with a bounded grind-loop or ingest CLI test that the three failure classes from 2026-09-23 (missing design sections; AC with no runnable command) bounce rather than park.

## Dependencies
None -- independent of open harness-efficiency A/B beads (ortus-nudo, ortus-p810); do not edit those beads while landing this.

## Edge cases
- Worker calls raw bd create despite prompt: hook/check must still refuse or the harness must detect create-without-validate in the worker session and treat it as incomplete filing.
- Ingest not on PATH inside the worker sandbox: ship an in-process helper (same validate-then-create as ingest) rather than depending on shell discovery alone.
- Partial packet write then crash: no bead exists (fail-closed); worker retries with a complete packet.
- True planning gap on the parent claim remains PLAN-GAP + human; only the follow-up filing path is gated here.

## Plan-gap guidance
If the only safe enforcement requires intercepting every bd binary invocation inside the sandbox and that conflicts with beads/Dolt single-writer or existing hooks, stop with PLAN-GAP naming the missing intercept surface; ship the ingest-based worker filing helper plus prompt update and tests, and record why a full bd create ban needs a separate decision.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: An unready worker-style follow-up packet (missing a required design section or an AC line with no runnable command) creates no bead and returns a nonzero readiness diagnostic. `uv run pytest tests/test_worker_ingest_gate.py -k unready_bounces -q`
- AC-2: A readiness-complete follow-up packet filed through the worker gate becomes an open bead that validate_issue reports ready, with no human label applied by the filing path. `uv run pytest tests/test_worker_ingest_gate.py -k ready_creates -q`
- AC-3: Bundled work-issue and/or goal prompt instruct follow-up or leftover filing via ortus ingest or the gated helper, not raw ungated bd create. `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py -k worker_ingest -q`
- AC-4: Goal prompt still resolves after the edit. `ortus prompt show goal`

## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_worker_ingest_gate.py tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py -k worker_ingest_or_unready_or_ready -q`
close_reason: Worker follow-ups file through the shared validate-then-create gate; unready packets bounce in-session with no bead and no human label

comments.text:
**Changes**
- `file_if_ready` + `FilingVerdict` in `src/ortus/commands/ingest.py`: one fail-closed validate-then-create gate every filing path shares. An unready candidate returns a verdict carrying the `ortus validate` row shape and no bead id; an epic (exempt, so readiness cannot vouch for it) is refused outright; only a ready candidate reaches `BdClient.create`.

title: Pin-dont-park: pin env/version skew instead of PLAN-GAP human park
description:
## Objective
Stop workers from parking pin-able environment/version mismatches as PLAN-GAP + `human` label; instead instruct and enforce pin-now + follow-up bead to restore, so grind keeps draining the ready queue.

## Behavioral context
Evidence from otel-judge 2026-09-22 Codex grind: `wrangler` `compatibility_date` 2026-09-01 exceeded `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` 0.22.0 workerd max 2026-08-22. Codex PLAN-GAP'd, labeled beads `human`, harness excluded human labels (`EXCLUDED_LABELS = ("human",)`), and grind exited after 1 close with queue blocked / human-only. Claude on the same skew pinned to 2026-08-22, filed a restore follow-up, and continued. Today `src/ortus/prompts/conditions/work-issue.txt` and `goal-prompt.md` tell workers that any work-spec contradiction is PLAN-GAP + `bd human`. After this bead, pin-able env/version skew is defined as pin-and-continue with a restore follow-up bead, with enforcement that fits Ortus (prompt line tied to that transcript plus classification/hook or readiness check where practical).
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
- Add a targeted worker instruction (goal / work-issue bundled prompts) defining pin-able environment/version mismatches: pin to the installed tool's supported value, file a follow-up bead to restore the newer pin, continue the claim.
- Tie the instruction to the otel-judge wrangler/vitest-pool-workers transcript behavior.
- Add whatever enforcement fits Ortus controls (e.g. classify env-skew PLAN-GAP comments, hook/check, or post-turn outcome tagging) so the model cannot ignore the line.
- Keep summaries as bullets in beads; do not re-inject raw file bodies.

## Non-goals
- Implementing unlock `--revert-claims` blindness to human-labeled claims (related, separately unfiled).
- Making scaffold/plan pin compat date with the installed pool (related, separately unfiled).
- Changing EXCLUDED_LABELS semantics globally beyond what pin-dont-park needs.
- Asking the model to conserve tokens.
- Touching Herdr or non-Ortus repos.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/prompts/conditions/work-issue.txt` ? PLAN-GAP + `bd human` procedure for spec contradictions (primary instruction surface grind injects via `inject_issue`).
- `src/ortus/prompts/goal-prompt.md` ? PLAN-GAP / human labeling instructions for criterion/window defects.
- `src/ortus/core/grind_loop.py` ? `EXCLUDED_LABELS`, `inject_issue()`, `format_issue_details()`.
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` ? `_claim_excluded_labels()`, `_escalate_wedged_claim()` (human label path).
- `src/ortus/core/prompts.py` ? `resolve_prompt()`, `bundled_prompt_text()`, `ortus prompt` surfaces.
- `tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py` ? existing prompt content contracts (`test_worker_prompt_plan_gap_for_unrunnable_checks`).
- Source: https://x.com/ericzakariasson/status/2102853511637774551 (quirks worth a targeted line; tie instructions to transcript behavior).

## Resolved decisions
- Enforcement > prompt advice: the new line is necessary but not sufficient; pair with classification or a check/hook Ortus owns.
- Pin-able means a version/date/env knob the worker can set in-repo to match an already-installed tool ceiling, with a restore follow-up bead; credential gaps and true missing decisions stay PLAN-GAP + human.
- One `ortus grind` process owns the backlog; do not route around human labels by starting another grind.

## Compatibility constraints
- Existing PLAN-GAP path for real planning gaps must remain.
- Prompt overrides via `ortus prompt eject` must still resolve; update bundled default and tests.
- bd `human` label remains the operator escape hatch for non-pin cases.

## Ordered steps
1. Write the pin-dont-park definition and examples (wrangler compatibility_date vs vitest-pool-workers workerd max) into work-issue and/or goal bundled prompts as plain definitions, not MUST/NEVER spam.
2. Add enforcement: classify PLAN-GAP comments that match env-skew patterns and/or add a grind/post-turn check that prefers pin+follow-up over human for those patterns; log the classification.
3. Extend `tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py` (and any classifier tests) so the pin path is asserted and generic PLAN-GAP still works for true gaps.
4. Document out-of-scope siblings (unlock revert-claims vs human; scaffold compat pin) as non-goals only.

## Dependencies
None ? independent of telemetry; may be validated later by bead 8.

## Edge cases
- Worker pins wrong direction (newer than tool allows): still a failure; do not auto-close.
- Multiple pins needed: one follow-up bead listing restores, or one bead per pin ? pick the smaller durable record.
- False positive: real missing product decision misclassified as env-skew ? classifier must require version/date/tool evidence; otherwise leave PLAN-GAP.

## Plan-gap guidance
If enforcement cannot distinguish env-skew from true planning gaps without semantic judgment forbidden by ZFC, stop with PLAN-GAP describing the classification limit and ship only the targeted instruction line plus logging of candidate PLAN-GAP texts for later criteria rewrite.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: Bundled work-issue and/or goal prompt defines pin-able env/version skew as pin plus restore follow-up bead, covering the wrangler/vitest-pool-workers class of failure. `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py -k pin_dont_park -q`
- AC-2: A true non-pin PLAN-GAP (contradiction or missing decision) still instructs PLAN-GAP plus human. `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py -k plan_gap -q`
- AC-3: An enforcement path (classifier, hook, or check) tags or redirects env-skew PLAN-GAP differently from generic human parking. `uv run pytest tests/test_pin_dont_park.py -q`
- AC-4: Goal prompt still resolves after the edit. `ortus prompt show goal`

## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py tests/test_pin_dont_park.py -q`

comments.author: who
comments.text:
**Changes**
- Both bundled worker contracts now define a declared version, date, or toolchain value past what the installed tool supports as pin-plus-restore-follow-up, not a park: the work-issue condition carries the definition with the compatibility-date-vs-bundled-runtime example, and the goal loop's implement step carries the one-line rule. The planning-gap paragraph beside it narrows to gaps no pin resolves, and names what still parks (a credential nobody supplied, an uninstalled tool, an unmade decision).

title: Cost per closed bead telemetry
description:
## Objective
Record per closed bead the price-weighted token cost and related run stats (tokens by billing type, turns/sessions, worker errors, wall time, backend+model+effort) by rolling up existing Codex/Claude JSON already written into grind logs, and expose a queryable surface so judge-vs-plain A/B cost can be compared.

## Behavioral context
Today `ortus grind` tees worker JSONL into `logs/grind-<ts>.log` via `_log_path` / `_spawn_logged`, and `ortus tail` already renders usage lines for Claude (`cache_read_input_tokens`), Codex (`cached_input_tokens`), and OpenCode (`tokens.cache.read`). Judge events in `jev-decisions.jsonl` only keep coarse `input_tokens` / `output_tokens` / `measured_cost_usd`. Operators cannot ask "what did this closed bead cost by billing type across backends?" Without that rollup, harness-efficiency A/B (beads 7 and 8) has no primary metric. After this bead, a single ortus subcommand (or a documented extension of dashboard/tail/judge export) prints per-bead and per-run cost telemetry for both claude and codex workers.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
- Parse Claude and Codex usage fields already present in grind JSONL logs (and OpenCode if already decoded) into billing buckets: output, uncached input, cached input, plus derived cache hit rate.
- Attribute usage to a bead id / session / grind run (issue id from Bound issue contract / work-issue injection, run timestamps from log path).
- Persist or emit a queryable rollup (prefer a small `ortus` subcommand or an extension of `ortus judge` export / dashboard / tail that fits existing code; do not invent a parallel store if logs already suffice).
- Cover claude and codex backends as first-class; document OpenCode if decoder already exposes the fields.
- Enable judge-vs-plain A/B cost comparison (foundation for beads 7 and 8).

## Non-goals
- Changing Claude/Codex CLI request assembly or provider billing APIs (Ortus drives the CLIs; the CLIs own caching and request bodies).
- Asking the model to conserve tokens.
- Hard gates on confidence floors or needs_human.
- Implementing the Jev model/effort router (bead 7) or the fixed eval set (bead 8).
- Touching Herdr seats or any non-Ortus repo.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` ? `_log_path()`, grind entry that chooses log file under `logs/grind-<ts>.log`.
- `src/ortus/core/claude.py` ? `ClaudeRunner.build_argv()`, `ClaudeRunner.run()`, `_spawn_logged()` tee worker JSON to log_path.
- `src/ortus/core/agent.py` ? `CodexRunner.build_argv()` (`codex exec --json`, `-m`, `model_reasoning_effort`).
- `src/ortus/commands/tail.py` ? Claude usage render (`usage.input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`, `output_tokens`); Codex `turn.completed` usage (`cached_input_tokens`); OpenCode `tokens.cache.read`.
- `src/ortus/core/judge_typesafe.py` ? `JudgeUsage` (input_tokens, output_tokens only today).
- `src/ortus/core/judge_log.py` / `src/ortus/core/judge_replay.py` ? `USAGE` field set and `jev-decisions.jsonl` writers; candidate extension points for richer billing fields or a sibling rollup.
- `src/ortus/commands/judge.py` ? existing export/replay surface.
- `src/ortus/commands/dashboard.py` ? `worker_seconds`, run snapshot helpers if rollup joins dashboard.
- Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/claude-stream-events.jsonl`, `tests/fixtures/codex-exec-events.jsonl`, `tests/fixtures/eval-cost-sample.jsonl`.
- Source claim: https://x.com/ericzakariasson/status/2102853511637774551 (measure per task not per request; weight tokens by billing type).

## Resolved decisions
- Primary metric is cost per closed bead (whole tree later), not per request.
- Prefer rolling up existing grind JSONL over inventing a second instrumentation path; only add fields Ortus already sees in worker streams.
- Query surface should fit an existing verb (judge export, dashboard, or a focused new subcommand) rather than a one-off script outside the package.
- Must work for both claude and codex; field names differ per backend and must be normalized into billing buckets.

## Compatibility constraints
- Do not break existing `ortus tail` rendering or `jev-decisions.jsonl` schema consumers without a versioned additive path.
- CLI behavior of grind/plan unchanged unless a new opt-in flag or subcommand is added.
- ASCII-safe log and export formats.

## Ordered steps
1. Inventory Claude vs Codex vs OpenCode usage JSON fields from tail.py and fixtures; define a normalized billing record (output / uncached input / cached input / cache hit rate / turns / wall time / backend / model / effort / issue_id / run_id).
2. Implement a parser that reads one grind log (and optionally jev-decisions.jsonl) and emits per-session and per-bead rollups; attribute via Bound issue / work-issue id already in the prompt and log markers grind already writes.
3. Wire a queryable CLI entry (subcommand or judge/dashboard/tail extension) that prints rollups for a run or issue id.
4. Add bounded unit tests over the golden fixtures proving billing buckets and attribution for claude and codex.
5. Document how beads 7 and 8 will consume this as the primary cost metric.

## Dependencies
None ? foundation bead; beads 7 and 8 will depend on this after ingest.

## Edge cases
- Missing usage on a turn (provider omitted fields): record nulls, never invent tokens (same rule as JudgeUsage).
- Mixed backends in one grind run: roll up per backend then sum with explicit backend tags.
- Resume / multiple sessions on one bead: sum sessions; keep session count.
- Worker timeout / abort mid-stream: partial usage still attributed; flag incomplete.
- Cache fields named differently per backend: normalize, do not drop.

## Plan-gap guidance
If Claude or Codex streams no longer expose cached vs uncached input in the logged JSON, or attribution to issue id cannot be done from existing grind markers without new worker protocol, stop with PLAN-GAP naming the missing field paths and do not invent billing numbers.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: Claude grind-log fixture rollup prints billing buckets (output, uncached input, cached input, cache hit rate) plus turns, wall time, backend, model, effort. `uv run pytest tests/test_cost_telemetry.py -k claude -q`
- AC-2: Codex grind-log fixture rollup prints the same normalized buckets from Codex field names. `uv run pytest tests/test_cost_telemetry.py -k codex -q`
- AC-3: Rollup attributes usage to an issue id present in log markers; missing attribution is an explicit null or error. `uv run pytest tests/test_cost_telemetry.py -k attribution -q`
- AC-4: Null or missing provider usage fields stay null in the rollup (never inferred). `uv run pytest tests/test_cost_telemetry.py -k null_usage -q`
- AC-5: The new query surface appears in ortus help for the chosen verb. `ortus --help`

## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_cost_telemetry.py -q`
close_reason: Grind-log rollup normalizes Claude, Codex, and OpenCode worker usage into per-bead billing buckets behind ortus cost

comments.author: who
comments.text: Landed the per-bead cost rollup as a new core module plus the ortus cost verb, reading the grind logs that already exist rather than adding a second instrumentation path. Iteration markers open and close worker windows and attribute each window to a bead; a window with no marker naming one keeps an explicit null id. Claude, Codex, and OpenCode usage events are normalized into output, uncached-input, cached-input, cache-write and reasoning buckets, with the Codex total-input inclusion rule handled as a subtraction. Unreported provider fields stay null and flag the row partial rather than becoming zeros; dollars appear only where the provider reported them, so Codex rows carry a null cost. Verified against the golden backend fixtures and against 176 real grind logs in this repo (142 beads, 385 sessions, 80 with provider-reported dollars). Criterion checks AC-1 through AC-4 and the targeted suite pass; AC-5 confirmed in ortus --help. Grok streams are still undecoded and roll up empty - filed as ortus-s0jn.

title: CI: restore judge shadow baseline after ortus-aesp semantic advice
description:
## Objective

Restore green main `test` workflow hermetic pytest for `tests/test_judge_shadow.py::test_shadow_matches_baseline_for_all_decisions` on who/ortus HEAD `309dca5` after ortus-aesp injected advisory semantic readiness into goal-prompt composition.

## Behavioral context

Before: recent main Actions (ortus-5fvp, ortus-ajqb, ortus-22oi) were green. After ortus-aesp push `309dca5`, Actions run https://github.com/who/ortus/actions/runs/35543587563 fails the hermetic pytest gate on every finished ubuntu/macos py3.10-3.12 cell because shadow and baseline composed goal prompts no longer match for all Claude and Codex verdict parametrizations. After this fix: that shadow baseline test passes under the hermetic gate so CI can go green for this surface while semantic advice remains advisory (diamond: no hard escalate).
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Make shadow and baseline `_compose_work_prompt` outputs equal again under `test_shadow_matches_baseline_for_all_decisions` for all Claude and Codex verdict params, accounting for `semantic_advice` added by ortus-aesp. Prefer updating the shadow path / test harness so both sides include the same advisory text (or both omit it when advice is empty) rather than reverting semantic readiness. Verify with bounded pytest and push.

## Non-goals
Do not revert ortus-aesp semantic readiness. Do not introduce hard escalate on low semantic confidence. Do not expand into full matrix CI locally as the worker default. Do not paste secrets from CI logs.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` — `_compose_work_prompt(..., semantic_advice=...)`
- `tests/test_judge_shadow.py` — `test_shadow_matches_baseline_for_all_decisions`
- related judge prompt helpers touched by ortus-aesp that feed goal-prompt composition
CodeGraph/Read fallback: `rg -n "semantic_advice|_compose_work_prompt|shadow_matches_baseline" src/ortus tests`

## Resolved decisions
1. Actions run https://github.com/who/ortus/actions/runs/35543587563 on HEAD `309dca568928e39b716c46aba68ae9e0fd3e92fc` is the authoritative bug signal.
2. Keep diamond model: semantic readiness is advisory / logged for System Two; structural readiness stays the hard gate.
3. Fix production prompt composition and/or shadow harness to restore equality; do not weaken the shadow contract by deleting the test.

## Compatibility constraints
Linux and macOS; Python 3.10-3.12 hermetic gate. Public goal-prompt loop behavior for workers without semantic advice must remain unchanged when `semantic_advice` is empty. Existing GateDecision / diamond no-hard-escalate semantics stay compatible.

## Ordered steps
1. Reproduce with `uv run pytest tests/test_judge_shadow.py::test_shadow_matches_baseline_for_all_decisions -q --test-timeout=30`.
2. Diff baseline vs shadow `_compose_work_prompt` inputs/outputs for one failing verdict; locate where `semantic_advice` diverges.
3. Align shadow and baseline so advice is applied identically (or both skip when empty); update harness expectations only if the intentional product prompt changed.
4. Re-run the named shadow test (and a narrow related grind prompt test if touched) and push the fix.

## Dependencies
None — standalone CI regression from ortus-aesp landing; does not depend on other open beads.

## Edge cases
1. Empty `semantic_advice` must keep prompts identical to pre-aesp baseline for backends that never inject advice.
2. Non-empty advisory text must appear in both shadow and baseline if the product path injects it, or in neither if shadow intentionally disables Jev for hermetic equality.
3. Claude and Codex parametrizations must both stay green after the fix.

## Plan-gap guidance
If restoring equality requires changing the locked diamond model (hard escalate on semantic low confidence) or deleting semantic readiness entirely, stop: comment PLAN-GAP with conflicting commit/bead evidence, label human, and leave the issue in_progress for operator/planning instead of improvising a contract change.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: shadow baseline equality passes for all params — `uv run pytest tests/test_judge_shadow.py::test_shadow_matches_baseline_for_all_decisions -q --test-timeout=30`
- AC-2: related grind prompt content still green if touched — `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py -q --test-timeout=30`
- AC-3: semantic readiness remains advisory (no hard escalate) — `rg -n "semantic.?readiness|hard.?escalat|diamond" src/ortus/core/judge.py src/ortus/core/judge_policy.py docs/judge.md`

## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_judge_shadow.py::test_shadow_matches_baseline_for_all_decisions -q --test-timeout=30`
close_reason: Restored shadow baseline equality with matched semantic advice across all verdicts and both backends; criterion checks passed

comments.author: who
comments.text: Fixed the shadow comparison by holding semantic readiness advice equal in baseline and shadow runs. Empty and non-empty advice now cover all verdicts for Claude and Codex; full prompt, worker settings, and tracker equality remain asserted. Production semantic readiness is unchanged. Passed: uv run pytest tests/test_judge_shadow.py::test_shadow_matches_baseline_for_all_decisions -q --test-timeout=30 -n auto (44 passed); uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py -q --test-timeout=30 -n auto (38 passed, 1 existing skip); rg -n "semantic.?readiness|hard.?escalat|diamond" src/ortus/core/judge.py src/ortus/core/judge_policy.py docs/judge.md (exit 0). git diff --check passed. The inherited untracked PRD is outside this issue.

title: Scrap Jev hard gate; keep shadow decision log
description:
## Objective

Scrap the Jev hard gate in Ortus judge so confidence floors and soft risk never block or human-escalate a claim. Keep the shadow decision log. Prefer learning from logged decisions over hard-stopping the worker.

## Behavioral context

Before: with judge enabled in enforce path, Jev answers that clear route confidence but miss risk_confidence / low_confidence floors (or set needs_human) can force effective_action=human and stop the claim from reaching the configured worker backend.

After: pack issue text (include_issue_text default true), call Jev, append the full typed decision vector to logs/jev-decisions.jsonl (or current path), then always proceed with the intended/configured backend. Fail-open on service failure stays. needs_human is logged and does not hard-stop for v0. Existing .ortusrc confidence-floor keys are ignored on the escalate path or removed from it; document the behavior change on the bead.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Ortus judge / gate path that turns Jev JudgeAnswers into GateDecision / effective_action for grind claims. Decision log append path for jev-decisions.jsonl. .ortusrc judge keys for confidence floors and include_issue_text. Docs/bead note that v0 does not hard-stop on needs_human.

## Non-goals

Redesigning Jev model prompts. Changing TypeSafe auth. Turning judge off. Changing ortus-test grinding unless needed later for smoke AC. Reintroducing soft gates under new names.

## Concrete locations

- src/ortus/core/judge.py - GateReason (low_confidence, needs_human, high_risk), JudgeConfig floors (route/noul/risk confidence, human_threshold, low_confidence policy), include_issue_text
- src/ortus/core/judge_state.py - pack/include_issue_text payload assembly
- Judge evaluate / gate adapter that maps JudgeAnswers -> GateDecision and sets effective_action
- Decision log writer for logs/jev-decisions.jsonl (answers, intended_action, effective_action, reason)
- .ortusrc [judge] keys for confidence floors
- Tests under tests/test_core_judge*.py and any grind/judge integration covering enforce vs shadow

## Resolved decisions

- Andy locked: scrap the hard gate; shadow/log-only is the useful default for learning.
- include_issue_text defaults true (empty payload is GIGO); if text is off, enforce should refuse or force shadow - prefer default true + document.
- Explicit needs_human from Jev: do NOT hard-stop for v0; log and proceed. Do not reintroduce a soft gate.
- Fail-open on Jev service failure stays.
- Confidence-floor .ortusrc keys: ignore in enforce escalate path or remove from escalate path; document on bead.
- Grind backend for implementing this bead: Claude or default per .ortusrc - Andy did not require Codex.

## Compatibility constraints

- Typed decision vector logging must remain complete (answers + intended_action + effective_action + reason).
- reason must not be a low_confidence-gated escalate when proceeding.
- Do not break fail-open on service failure.
- Do not require --judge for the grind that implements this change unless already on.

## Ordered steps

1. Trace enforce-path gate: where low_confidence / risk_confidence floors / needs_human set effective_action=human.
2. Remove or disable those hard escalate branches for enforce; keep shadow log append.
3. Default include_issue_text true; document refuse/force-shadow if text off.
4. Ensure every Jev call appends decision row with effective_action=proceed (or backend name) when not service-fail.
5. Ignore or stop applying .ortusrc confidence floors on escalate path; note on bead.
6. Add/adjust unit tests for former low_confidence-human case now proceeding.
7. Smoke: ortus-test or dry path shows proceed after a real Jev answer that previously would have been low_confidence human.

## Dependencies

None beyond existing TypeSafe/Jev wiring and judge enablement for smoke.

## Edge cases

- Jev returns needs_human=true with high route confidence: log, proceed (v0).
- Jev service failure: fail-open (unchanged).
- include_issue_text false: prefer not silent GIGO - refuse enforce or force shadow.
- Legacy .ortusrc floors present: must not re-arm hard escalate.

## Plan-gap guidance

If gate logic lives behind an adapter not named in Concrete locations, extend design with the real module path before coding; do not invent a second escalate path.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1: With judge enabled, a claim where Jev returns high route confidence but low risk_confidence still proceeds to the worker backend (does not set effective_action=human for low_confidence).
- AC-2: Every Jev call appends a decision row to logs/jev-decisions.jsonl (or current path) with answers, intended_action, effective_action=proceed (or backend name), and reason that is not low_confidence-gated escalate.
- AC-3: include_issue_text defaults true, or enforce refuses / forces shadow when text is off (prefer default true and document).
- AC-4: Explicit needs_human from Jev does not hard-stop for v0; it is logged and the claim proceeds (issue body notes implementers must not reintroduce a soft gate).
- AC-5: Existing .ortusrc keys for confidence floors are ignored in enforce or removed from the escalate path, and the behavior change is documented on the bead.
- AC-6: Smoke path shows proceed after a real Jev answer that previously would have been low_confidence human.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `rg -n "low_confidence|risk_confidence|effective_action|GateReason|GateAction" src/ortus/core/judge.py src/ortus/core/judge_state.py`
- AC-2: `rg -n "jev-decisions|intended_action|effective_action" src/ortus/core src/ortus/commands -g "*.py"`
- AC-3: `rg -n "include_issue_text" src/ortus/core/judge.py src/ortus/core/judge_state.py tests/test_core_judge_config.py tests/test_core_judge_state.py`
- AC-4: `rg -n "needs_human|NEEDS_HUMAN|GateReason" src/ortus/core/judge.py`
- AC-5: `rg -n "route_confidence|risk_confidence|human_threshold|low_confidence" src/ortus/core/judge.py`
- AC-6: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_judge_config.py tests/test_core_judge_state.py -q`

## Targeted tests

uv run pytest tests/test_core_judge_config.py tests/test_core_judge_state.py -q
close_reason: Pre-turn gate now routes and logs; confidence, human-need and risk answers are recorded instead of escalating, and issue text is on by default

comments.author: who
comments.text:
Scrapped the pre-turn hard gate. decide_pre_turn no longer reads
route_confidence, noul_confidence, risk_confidence, human_threshold,
risk_threshold or low_confidence: a well-formed answer always routes, and the
confidence, human-need and risk values ride along in the typed decision vector
written to logs/jev-decisions.jsonl. An offered `human` route names no worker,
so the baseline runs and the answer is logged with intended_action=human,
effective_action=proceed. Only three things still withhold a pre-turn worker: a
caller policy denial, an existing human label or requires_human constraint, and
a fail-closed service failure or invalid answer. A `skip` route still stops the
invocation, which is a routing choice rather than an escalation.

BEHAVIOR CHANGE for AC-5: the six confidence/threshold keys are still parsed and
validated, so existing .ortusrc tables and packs keep loading unchanged, but no
value of theirs can change a pre-turn decision. They are now documentation of
the vocabulary an offline calibration pass compares, nothing more. This
supersedes the pre-turn escalation ordering added by ortus-xaq5; that ordering
existed to keep a human signal from being erased by fail-open, and there is no
longer a human signal to preserve at that point.

include_issue_text now defaults to true. Metadata alone is too thin to route on,
so the default packet carries the screened title, first Objective line and AC
lines. Turning it off is still supported and yields the metadata-only packet;
the judge-private label still suppresses issue prose unconditionally, and every
existing screening, cap and omission rule is unchanged.

Deliberately out of scope: the pre-tool hook in judge_tools.py keeps its own
hard-coded 0.8/1.5 floors because it authorizes irreversible tool actions rather
than a worker launch. Filed ortus-ajqb for the operator to decide whether that
exception stands. Post-turn outcome handling is likewise untouched.

Criterion checks run: AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, AC-4 and AC-5 rg commands all return the
expected matches; AC-6 `uv run pytest tests/test_core_judge_config.py
tests/test_core_judge_state.py -q` passed (151 tests). For the AC-6 observable
smoke, the offline synthetic replay through the real adapter and the grind CLI
covers it: the unconfident_route and dangerous_action cases in
tests/fixtures/jev/replay.jsonl previously expected effective_action=human and
now expect proceed, and human_credentials now proceeds on the baseline. No live
provider call was made; no key is configured here and live smoke remains
optional operator work. The bounded fast gate was also run: 1973 passed, with
19 pre-existing failures in tests/test_grind_judge_hooks.py that fail
identically on a clean checkout because this sandbox mounts /tmp read-only.

title: CI: macOS recursive-root rm /tmp/.. classifies as path_escape
description:
## Objective
Make Bash recursive-root hard guards classify macOS-resolved root-equivalent deletes as recursive_root_deletion so the hermetic pytest gate stays green on macos-latest.

## Behavioral context
Before: on Linux, m -r /tmp/.. is denied with reason recursive_root_deletion before any provider call. On macOS GitHub Actions runners, the same command is denied with path_escape because /tmp resolves through /private/tmp to /private, so the root-equality check misses. After: every parametrized recursive root-delete command in tests/test_core_judge_tools.py::test_recursive_root_deletion_never_contacts_provider returns DENY with reason recursive_root_deletion on both Linux and macOS without contacting the provider.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Fix the recursive Bash rm hard guard in src/ortus/core/judge_tools.py so root-equivalent operands still match after platform path resolution (macOS /tmp -> /private/tmp). Keep deny-before-provider behavior and the existing reason string recursive_root_deletion for the current parametrized cases. Adjust or extend hermetic tests only as needed to lock the macOS case without weakening Linux coverage.

## Non-goals
No changes to TypeSafe/Jev provider clients, network hard guards, secret-file rules, or CI workflow YAML. Do not rename the path_escape reason for ordinary outside-repo paths. Do not require a full local multi-OS matrix from the worker.

## Concrete locations
CodeGraph/Read: src/ortus/core/judge_tools.py inspect_tool() recursive rm operand loop that compares (root / operand).resolve() to Path("/"); decide_tool() hard-guard path that must keep client_factory uncalled. Tests: tests/test_core_judge_tools.py::test_recursive_root_deletion_never_contacts_provider (param including m -r /tmp/..). Evidence: GitHub Actions who/ortus run https://github.com/who/ortus/actions/runs/35501946117 (push 0423ae1) jobs pytest (macos-latest / py3.10) and pytest (macos-latest / py3.11) failed hermetic pytest gate with AssertionError assert 'path_escape' == 'recursive_root_deletion'; ubuntu-latest counterparts passed.

## Resolved decisions
Treat platform-normalized paths that are filesystem-root equivalent (including macOS /tmp/.. resolving under /private) as recursive_root_deletion, not path_escape. Prefer fixing the guard predicate over rewriting the test to accept path_escape, because the reason string is part of the observable hard-guard contract and the test already forbids provider contact. Keep DENY action unchanged.

## Compatibility constraints
Linux and macOS; Python 3.10-3.12. Preserve existing deny reasons for true path escapes and for Linux recursive root deletes. Gate-off and CLI surfaces unchanged. Progress uses ortus.core.output.progress() on stderr when adding non-interactive verbs (none expected here). Tests covering the changed surface must pass; CI catches regressions elsewhere.

## Ordered steps
1. Reproduce the failing parametrized case locally if possible and confirm Linux still expects recursive_root_deletion for m -r /tmp/...
2. Update the recursive-root predicate in inspect_tool so macOS-resolved root-equivalent operands match without calling the provider.

title: Jev: diamond calibration ? compare soft candidates (no hard escalate) and publish runbook
description:
## Objective

Rewrite and implement threshold-candidate comparison for the diamond model: Jev (System One) emits typed probability vectors (route, needs_human/noul, risk + confidences) that are passed into System Two (any backend) as context. Calibration compares a bounded set of soft/logging/rewrite candidates against labeled replay without applying them and without re-arming hard escalate.

## Behavioral context

Andy locked 2026-09-20 (diamond): no hard gates on confidence floors or needs_human; scrap hard escalate (shipped in ortus-22oi). Pre-tool floors kept in ortus-ajqb must be treated as soft/log-only under this policy ? calibration must not restore claim-blocking escalate. Operator can review measured tradeoffs (false-proceed vs over-caution signals, latency/cost) for rewrite criteria later; production config is never mutated by this task.
design:

v1

## Non-goals

No learned model. No automatic threshold edits or live provider calls. No reintroduction of hard escalate on low_confidence, risk_confidence floors, or needs_human (claim gate or pre-tool). Implementing epic ortus-cuyd reports is out of scope except as a consumer of this calibration output later.

## Concrete locations

CodeGraph: src/ortus/core/readiness.py validate_issue() guards executable tasks; predecessor interfaces in src/ortus/core/judge_replay.py summarize() and src/ortus/commands/judge.py replay(). Claim-gate scrap: src/ortus/core/judge.py (ortus-22oi). Pre-tool floors note: ortus-ajqb. New tests/test_judge_calibration.py and tests/fixtures/jev/labeled_replay.jsonl; update docs/judge.md. Proposed new files/tests/symbols are task-owned additions; existing references traced through CodeGraph.

## Resolved decisions

- Diamond lock (Andy 2026-09-20): System One passes probability vectors into System Two; do not hard-gate claims. ortus-22oi already logs confidence/risk instead of escalating them.
- SUPERSEDES prior text that said "retain hard guard policy." Hard escalate is scrapped. Candidate tables may describe soft bands, rewrite triggers, or reporting thresholds only.
- Pre-tool hook floors (ortus-ajqb): if present, calibration and runbook must treat them as non-blocking (log/shadow), never as claim stops. Do not add tests that expect effective_action=human from low risk_confidence alone.
- Replay only already-recorded typed answers through decide_pre_turn/decide_tool; never infer labels from worker prose or call the SDK.
- Output each candidate metrics and sample counts alongside current production soft settings; no automatic ranking, optimization, config edits, or learned model.
- Fixed synthetic labeled cases test mechanics, not calibration quality.
- Runbook: operator-reviewed pilot labels; measured p50<500ms, p95<1500ms, relative cost<=0.1 of measured coding turns where cost data exists; explicitly state diamond policy (probabilities in, no hard escalate).

## Compatibility constraints

- Must remain compatible with ortus-22oi shadow/log claim path (effective_action proceeds; vector logged).
- Must not break fail-open on service failure.
- readiness-v1 must still pass after rewrite.

## Ordered steps

1. Rewrite this bead body (done by operator/chief-of-staff) to diamond policy.
2. Align judge_replay / calibration scaffolding and docs with no-hard-escalate.
3. Implement --thresholds TOML compare path (bounded, reproducible, no prod mutation).
4. Add tests proving candidates cannot re-arm hard escalate; soft metrics still report.
5. Publish runbook section documenting diamond + how to review candidates without applying them.
6. Leave applying any production soft settings as a later human decision (not this claim close).

## Dependencies

ortus-22oi closed (scrap hard gate). ortus-ajqb closed (pre-tool floors documented ? treat as soft under diamond).

## Edge cases

- Candidate TOML that encodes old hard-escalate floors: reject or coerce to soft/log-only; never apply as claim blockers.
- Empty labeled replay: fail closed with clear error; create nothing in prod config.
- include_issue_text false historical rows: document GIGO; do not use as calibration quality evidence.

Order under existing flock: deterministic readiness and backend preflight, fresh atomic claim, reload packet, sanitize and judge, append decision, apply action. Proceed uses bound id and selected execution bundle. Human adds human label plus one typed-reason comment and progress banner, releases only fresh unused claims to open, and stops this run; no external notifications. Skip releases a fresh unused claim, keeps issue ready, and stops this invocation to prevent a hot loop or starvation; next invocation may retry. A resumed claim is never released or reset by skip/human; preserve tree and in_progress, label human when required and stop. Missing key/SDK or provider failure in open mode proceeds with original backend, existing verification/closure, and logged fallback; enabled fail-closed escalates. --dry-run prints resolved safe config without judge, claim or log writes. iterations counts only actual worker spawns and tasks counts only bd closes. ## Behavioral context

design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope

## Non-goals
No pre-tool hook, post-turn classification, multi-seat rollout or changes to unrelated backends in this task. Implement only the outcome and interfaces named in Scope; preserve predecessor contracts.

## Concrete locations

New src/ortus/core/judge_typesafe.py TypeSafeJudge.evaluate(), build_questions(); uses new OrtusJudge in src/ortus/core/judge.py. New tests/test_core_judge_typesafe.py and tests/fixtures/jev/pre_turn.json. Proposed new files, tests and symbols are explicitly task-owned additions; existing references were traced through CodeGraph, with the stated Read fallbacks for unindexed documents or omitted source spans.

## Resolved decisions
Use typesafe_sdk.AsyncTypeSafeClient.system_one with model jev-1.13.0, Choice route, Noul needs_human and Score action_risk with three criteria. Official sources: https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python and https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python/api/clients/sync ; upstream pyproject at https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-python declares 0.7.0 and Python>=3.10. Disable SDK retries with RetryPolicy(max_retries=0); pass timeout_seconds and wrap each call in asyncio.wait_for at that same deadline, invoked by asyncio.run at the synchronous OrtusJudge.evaluate boundary. This uses the official SDK async equivalent to the PRD's sync example so timeout cancellation closes sockets instead of abandoning threads. Missing SDK/key, timeout, HTTP errors and invalid answers return typed failure enums, never raw response bodies. No HTTP fallback is planned because the SDK supports the repository's Python baseline. title: Codex grind completion instructions contradict the outer loop
description:
## Objective

Make the Codex grind worker's completion instructions agree with the outer loop so a successful implementation can finish verification, commit/push and close its issue instead of stopping at an unconsumed handoff.

## Behavioral context

A downstream repository ran `ortus grind --backend codex` on 2026-09-07. The run resumed one claimed schema task. CodeGraph handshake succeeded, the worker corrected a database fixture, passed disposable PostgreSQL checks and Prisma validation, and recorded evidence. It then explicitly said the injected implementation-phase contract required leaving the issue open with uncommitted candidate edits for verification.

Redacted log sequence:

```text
13:56:17 backend=codex; verification=full
13:56:30 spawning codex (single-issue worker)
13:56:42 implementation CodeGraph handshake succeeded
[worker] The injected implementation-phase contract explicitly says not to close the issue and to leave candidate edits for verification.
[worker] remains open, with uncommitted candidate edits ... session-close was not performed.
14:00:02 no worker claim observed in bd; judging the readiness-passing head [resumed issue]
14:00:03 resumed window ended with no close and no new commits on master (no-close window 1 of 2)
14:00:03 left [resumed issue] in_progress for the next window
14:00:05 done: 0 landed, 1 in_progress, 8 open
```

The worker exited normally; no verifier or finalizer ran in that log. Candidate edits remained intact. The operator saw an apparent early bailout despite successful work. A subsequent unchanged attempt can consume the wedged-claim threshold.

Important qualification: current checked-out source has `_IMPLEMENTATION_INSTRUCTION` explicitly requiring session-close, and the loop is intentionally one subprocess per issue. Therefore the observed contradiction is established, but its provenance is not yet established. An installed-version mismatch, a generated prompt, or a repository override may supply the stale phase-only text. Trace the actual composed prompt before assuming a missing multi-phase state machine is the intended fix.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Trace effective Codex grind prompt composition, correct stale phase-only instructions or incompatible overrides, and test completion and resumed-claim accounting under the existing one-worker-per-issue loop. Make actionable contract mismatches visible before another model run is spent.

## Non-goals

Do not implement downstream application changes, revive retired candidate journals or a separate multi-phase orchestrator, switch backend as a workaround, weaken acceptance checks, auto-close on exit code alone, or commit unrelated dirty files. Do not change supported platforms or invoke live providers in regression tests.

## Concrete locations

CodeGraph exploration located `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` grind(), `_IMPLEMENTATION_INSTRUCTION`, `_record_no_close_window()` and the judged_status in_progress branch. The latter increments the resumed no-close counter when the integration tip is unchanged and then breaks. Current `_IMPLEMENTATION_INSTRUCTION` says to session-close; comments in grind() describe retired journal/compose/finalize handling.

Inspect `src/ortus/core/prompts.py` and the prompt/override paths reached by grind(), plus `src/ortus/core/agent.py` CodexRunner, to locate the effective input boundary. Relevant existing coverage: `tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py`, `tests/test_core_prompts.py`, `tests/test_grind_loop.py`, `tests/test_grind_orphan_policy.py` and `tests/test_grind_finalization.py`. Add `tests/test_grind_completion_contract.py` for focused regression cases. Follow `docs/testing.md` and its copy_bd_workspace fixtures.

## Resolved decisions

The supported loop remains one fresh backend worker per issue; the worker must perform the issue's checks and session-close under repository policy. Its prompt must not tell it to wait for an outer verification/finalization stage that the loop never schedules. Preserve intentional prototype versus full verification settings.

First record executable/version provenance and effective prompt layers. If the stale instruction originates in an installed/generated asset or repo override, fix its authoritative source and regeneration path, not just the live string. Do not silently overwrite a user-authored override: report the conflicting source and required correction before spawning if it cannot be reconciled safely.

A worker's claim of passing tests and normal process exit are not completion evidence by themselves. Successful landing remains observable issue state and repository close state. Candidate file changes may aid diagnostics but must not grant indefinite exemption from genuine stall detection. Do not simply raise the wedged-window threshold.

The historical profile lines naming implement/verify/finalize are not evidence those phases ran. Any retained console/profile wording must describe the active execution model accurately.

## Compatibility constraints

Preserve Claude and other backend completion semantics, existing resume behavior, human/PLAN-GAP handling, CodeGraph prerequisite enforcement, task caps, push failure handling and inherited dirty paths. Linux/macOS support and hermetic tests remain unchanged. Do not embed downstream project names, issue identifiers, local usernames or absolute home paths in committed evidence or fixtures.

## Ordered steps

1. Reproduce with a canned Codex runner in a temporary seeded bd/git workspace: one resumed in_progress issue, dirty candidate edits, unchanged integration tip and a normal worker exit that obeys a leave-open instruction.
2. Trace the installed executable and composed prompt through all effective templates/overrides; identify the exact layer supplying phase-only language and compare it with the current source contract.
3. Correct the authoritative completion instruction and any shipped/generated copies, or add an actionable pre-spawn incompatibility diagnostic for an unmodifiable stale override.
4. Exercise a successful one-issue worker that verifies and session-closes; assert one landed task and no false no-close increment. Cover task-cap and next-ready-issue behavior.
5. Exercise genuinely unfinished work, worker failure, failed checks, failed push and human handling; preserve candidates and honest stall accounting without false closure.
6. Run focused tests and the relevant prompt/loop/orphan/finalization modules. Record the traced instruction provenance and actual fix; CI owns comprehensive platform coverage.

## Dependencies

No implementation blocker established. The initial read-only tracker query could not open its database, so check for an existing matching issue before starting implementation. Prompt composition, CodexRunner and the bd-state loop are the interacting code components. The downstream run is evidence only and is not needed for hermetic reproduction.

## Edge cases

Fresh claim versus resumed claim; inherited dirty files versus task-owned candidates; legitimate multi-window work; normal exit with no work; worker closed status without successful landing; failed checks or push; explicit human flag; custom prompt overrides; stale installed package with newer checkout; repeated restarts; full versus prototype verification; misleading legacy profile labels.

## Plan-gap guidance

If the effective runtime prompt cannot be recovered, preserve the observed contradiction as confirmed and its source as unresolved. Do not invent a missing verifier or restore retired machinery. Record PLAN-GAP with the executable/version and prompt source needed to reproduce. If an existing issue already owns the exact fix, link the evidence and avoid parallel conflicting implementations.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1: The effective stock Codex grind prompt requires complete one-issue verification/session-close and contains no incompatible instruction to leave candidate edits for an unscheduled phase. Supported custom overrides retain their intended content; a conflicting stale override is rejected with its source and actionable guidance before spawning.
- AC-2: A resumed issue with a valid implementation can verify, commit/push and close in one grind run; the run counts exactly one landed task and does not increment its no-close counter. Fresh claims and task caps remain correct.
- AC-3: Normal exit without completion, failed verification/push and human-blocked work cannot be reported as landed. Candidates and unrelated inherited dirty files are preserved; genuine resumed stalls retain bounded accounting.
- AC-4: Existing prompt composition, loop, orphan and finalization regression coverage passes; new tests are hermetic and require no provider credentials.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_completion_contract.py -k prompt -n auto --test-timeout=60`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_completion_contract.py -k completion -n auto --test-timeout=60`
- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_completion_contract.py -k failure -n auto --test-timeout=60`
- AC-4: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py tests/test_core_prompts.py tests/test_grind_loop.py tests/test_grind_orphan_policy.py tests/test_grind_finalization.py -n auto --test-timeout=60`

## Targeted tests

title: Implement ortus ingest validate-then-create core
description:
## Objective
Implement `ortus ingest` that reads a readiness packet and creates a bd issue only when `validate_issue` reports READY.

## Behavioral context
Before: no first-class ingest path; callers shell out to multiline `bd create`.
After: `ortus ingest --packet DIR` (or `--stdin` JSON) exits 0 with the new id on stdout alone, or exits nonzero with validate-style gaps and creates nothing.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
- Add `src/ortus/commands/ingest.py` and register `ingest` on the top-level Typer app in `src/ortus/cli.py` (single command, no subcommands).
- Packet dir: `description.md`, `design.md`, `acceptance.md` (`acceptance_criteria.md` alias); `--stdin` JSON with description/design/acceptance keys aligned with `github_bead`.
- Flags: `--title`, `--type`, `--priority`, `--repo` (default cwd), `--packet` / `--stdin`.
- Assemble fields, run `validate_issue` on a pre-create dict (synthetic id ok), then `BdClient.create` only if READY.
- Exit 0: print only the new issue id. Exit nonzero: print UNREADY diagnostic matching `ortus validate` style; no `bd create`.
- Reuse `BdClient.create` and `validate_issue`; do not change readiness schema or grind.

## Non-goals
- No create/fill/ready subcommands.
- No LLM repair.
- No updating existing issues.
- Help/discovery copy is a sibling task; core may have minimal help text.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/commands/ingest.py` — new command (`ingest` function)
- `src/ortus/cli.py` — `app.command(name="ingest")`
- `src/ortus/core/bd.py` — `BdClient.create`
- `src/ortus/core/readiness.py` — `validate_issue`
- `src/ortus/core/github_bead.py` — packet field naming reference

## Resolved decisions
- Verb is `ortus ingest`.
- Fail closed: never create an UNREADY bead.
- Markdown packet bodies may contain backticks; files are the transport.

## Compatibility constraints
- Linux/WSL; Windows callers use `wsl -e ortus ingest …`.
- Packet contract is readiness schema v1 from `ortus spec`.

## Ordered steps
1. Packet loader (dir + stdin) with clear errors.
2. Pre-create validate_issue.
3. BdClient.create on READY; id-only stdout.
4. Wire cli.py.
5. Unit tests for loader + ready/unready paths in this module's tests file (or shared test file started here).

## Dependencies
- None beyond existing BdClient/readiness.

## Edge cases
- Missing md file → error before validate.
- Incomplete packet → UNREADY, no create.
- Non-JSON stdin → error, no bd call.

## Plan-gap guidance
If validate_issue cannot run without a persisted bd id, use a synthetic id for validation only; never create-then-delete. If impossible, PLAN-GAP and stop.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: `ortus ingest --help` exists as a single command (no create/fill/ready children).
- AC-2: READY packet creates a bead that `ortus validate` reports READY; stdout is only the id.
- AC-3: UNREADY packet exits nonzero, prints gaps, creates no bead.
- AC-4: `uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q` covers ready and unready paths.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: `uv run ortus ingest --help`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q -k ready`
- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q -k unready`
- AC-4: `uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q`

## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q`
close_reason: Already shipped by ortus-82bn / 2599c18

comments.author: who
comments.text: Already implemented by closed ortus-82bn (commit 2599c18, src/ortus/commands/ingest.py). Closing as duplicate of shipped work.

title: Document ortus ingest discovery in CLI help
description:
## Objective
Make `ortus --help` and `ortus ingest --help` the discovery surface for sidecar agents filing beads.

## Behavioral context
Before: Ortus-backed grokbots would not know ingest exists unless told out-of-band.
After: help alone states packet shape (`ortus spec`), exit-code contract, and that ingest is the filing path.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
- Top-level `ortus --help` ingest one-liner: file readiness beads via ingest (not multiline bd create).
- `ortus ingest --help`: packet layout (description.md/design.md/acceptance.md or stdin JSON), point at `ortus spec`, document exit 0 = id on stdout / nonzero = gaps and no create.
- Brief README command-table row for ingest.
- Tests that help text contains the required discovery phrases.

## Non-goals
- No shared Grok Bot skill or user-memory fan-out in this task.
- No behavior change to validate-then-create beyond help strings.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/cli.py` — ingest command help string
- `src/ortus/commands/ingest.py` — Option/command help and docstring
- `README.md` — command table
- `tests/test_ingest_cli.py` — help assertion tests

## Resolved decisions
- Discovery lives in Ortus CLI help (operator-confirmed).
- Schema is not restated in full; point to `ortus spec`.

## Compatibility constraints
- Help must stay accurate if exit-code contract changes in the core task — land after or with core.

## Ordered steps
1. Write ingest command help + top-level help.
2. README row.
3. Assert help strings in tests.

## Dependencies
- Depends on ingest command existing (core task). Use `bd dep add` if epic children linking is available; otherwise note in design that help lands after core lands on same branch.

## Edge cases
- Help must not claim create/fill/ready subcommands.

## Plan-gap guidance
If Typer cannot attach rich multi-paragraph help, put the contract in the command docstring/epilog; do not invent a separate docs site.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: `ortus --help` lists ingest and mentions filing readiness beads via ingest.
- AC-2: `ortus ingest --help` mentions `ortus spec`, packet md files, and exit 0 vs nonzero behavior.
- AC-3: README command table includes ingest.
- AC-4: Help discovery assertions pass in ingest tests.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: `uv run ortus --help`
- AC-2: `uv run ortus ingest --help`
- AC-3: `rg -n "ingest" README.md`
- AC-4: `uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q -k help`

## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q -k help`

Two help-discovery tests assert the wording against whitespace-flattened output so rich's wrapping cannot break them. README already carried the ingest command-table row.
