title: Add ortus ingest: file a readiness-passing bead from a packet
description:
## Objective
Add a single `ortus ingest` command that consumes a readiness packet and files a bd issue that already passes readiness schema v1 / `ortus validate`.

## Behavioral context
Before: agents filing beads from Windows/PowerShell assembled multiline `bd create` bodies and hit quoting/Auto-review failures (Waystone ws-s4w).
After: `ortus ingest` runs inside WSL, reads a packet (dir or stdin JSON), creates the bead only when it validates READY, and prints the new id — or prints readiness gaps and creates nothing.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
- Discovery: `ortus --help` and `ortus ingest --help` document the ingest path so sidecar agents find it without a separate memo.
- One top-level command: `ortus ingest` (no create/fill/ready subcommands).
- Inputs: `--packet DIR` with description.md, design.md, acceptance.md (acceptance_criteria.md alias) and/or `--stdin` JSON with description, design, acceptance/acceptance_criteria; plus `--title`, `--type`, `--priority` (and optional `--repo`).
- Behavior: assemble the issue fields, run `validate_issue` on the assembled payload *before* `bd create`. If UNREADY, print the same diagnostic style as `ortus validate` and exit nonzero with no bead created. If READY, `BdClient.create` and print the new id; exit 0.
- Reuse `BdClient.create`, `validate_issue`, and packet field naming from `github_bead` where practical.
- Register in `cli.py` as a normal command (not a nested typer app with subcommands).
- Tests for happy-path READY create, UNREADY reject-without-create, and packet/stdin loading.
- Brief README command-table line.

## Non-goals
- No `create`/`fill`/`ready` subcommands.
- No second CLI.
- No LLM repair of unready packets.
- No update/patch of existing issues in this issue (ingest = file new only).
- Do not change readiness schema v1 or grind claim-time behavior.
- Packet files remain ephemeral transport; beads are the only durable record.

## Concrete locations
- src/ortus/cli.py — register `ingest`
- src/ortus/commands/ingest.py — new command
- src/ortus/core/bd.py — BdClient.create (existing)
- src/ortus/core/readiness.py — validate_issue (unchanged)
- src/ortus/core/github_bead.py — packet field conventions to align with
- tests/test_ingest_cli.py — new tests
- README.md — command table

## Resolved decisions
- Verb is `ortus ingest` (not bead).
- Single shot: validate-then-create; fail closed (no partial bead on UNREADY).
- Operator/agent fixes the packet and re-runs ingest; no fill loop in-scope.

## Compatibility constraints
- Linux/WSL primary; Windows callers use `wsl -e ortus ingest …`.
- Must accept the same readiness section contract as `ortus spec`.

## Ordered steps
1. Packet loader (dir + stdin JSON) with clear missing-field errors.
2. Build issue dict and run validate_issue before any bd write.
3. On READY, BdClient.create; print id.
4. On UNREADY, print diagnostic; exit 1; no create.
5. Wire cli.py + README + tests.

## Dependencies
- Existing BdClient and readiness.validate_issue.
- Motivated by Waystone filing friction; no waystone code dependency.

## Edge cases
- Missing packet section → error before validate.
- READY epic exemption does not apply to ingest (ingest files tasks/bugs/features/chores with full packets).
- Stdin non-JSON → clear error, no bd call.
- Title/type/priority flags required or defaulted consistently with BdClient.create defaults.

## Plan-gap guidance
If validate_issue cannot run on a pre-create dict without a bd id, adapt with a synthetic id placeholder for validation only; do not create then delete. If that is impossible, PLAN-GAP naming the validator assumption and stop.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: `ortus ingest --help` describes a single ingest command (no create/fill/ready subcommands).
- AC-2: ingesting a readiness-shaped packet creates a bd issue that `ortus validate` reports READY.
- AC-3: ingesting an incomplete packet exits nonzero, prints an UNREADY-style diagnostic, and does not create a bd issue.
- AC-4: Targeted tests cover READY create and UNREADY reject paths.
- AC-5: `ortus --help` lists ingest with a summary that readiness beads are filed via ingest.
- AC-6: `ortus ingest --help` tells callers to shape packets per `ortus spec`, and documents exit 0 = id on stdout / nonzero = gaps, no create.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: `uv run ortus ingest --help`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q -k ready`
- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q -k unready`
- AC-4: `uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q`
- AC-5: `uv run ortus --help`
- AC-6: `uv run ortus ingest --help`

## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q`
close_reason: ortus ingest lands as one verb: packet dir or stdin JSON, readiness-validated before any bd write, fail-closed on unready. AC-1..AC-4 checks passed at 2599c18.

comments.author: who
comments.text: Operator decision: CLI verb is ortus ingest (create/fill/ready), not ortus bead. Packet md/JSON remains ephemeral transport only. Implement and document as ingest.

comments.author: who
comments.text: Scope rewrite: single ortus ingest command only — validate-then-create READY bead from packet/stdin. No create/fill/ready subcommands. Prior grind for multi-subcommand UX was stopped.

comments.author: who
comments.text:
Completed. `ortus ingest` is one verb: it loads a packet from --packet DIR (description.md, design.md, acceptance.md with the acceptance_criteria.md alias) and/or --stdin JSON, assembles the fields through the shared packet assembler, and runs the readiness validator on the candidate before any bd write. UNREADY prints the same row shape ortus validate prints and creates nothing; READY creates the bead and prints its id bare on stdout. Epics are refused because the readiness epic exemption would let a container through with no work spec. Flags override packet fields; an explicit --priority 0 is preserved rather than defaulted.

Deviation to note: repo is a positional argument, not --repo, matching every other ortus verb (resolve_repo, $PWD default, no walk-up).

Criterion checks run: uv run ortus ingest --help (AC-1); uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q -k ready (AC-2, 2 passed); uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q -k unready (AC-3, 1 passed); uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py -q (AC-4, 11 passed). Changed-surface: uv run pytest tests/test_ingest_cli.py tests/test_cli_verbs.py tests/test_cli.py -q -> 58 passed.

Follow-up filed as ortus-nvsw (filed by ingest itself, validates READY): the shared assembler coerces an explicit priority 0 to 2.

comments.author: who
comments.text: Operator addendum: discovery requirement. `ortus --help` must list ingest with a one-line summary that filing readiness beads goes through ingest (not multiline bd create). `ortus ingest --help` must state: shape packet per `ortus spec` (description.md/design.md/acceptance.md or stdin JSON); exit 0 prints new id only; nonzero prints validate-style gaps and creates nothing. Sidecar/manager agents discover the capability from help alone.

title: ci flake: git auto-maintenance writes maintenance.lock into the read-only bare bd template
description:
## Objective
The shared bare bd test template cannot be mutated by git background maintenance, so the read-only-template guard stops failing grind tests on a random CI leg with a maintenance.lock write.

## Behavioral context
Before. tests/conftest.py builds one bare bd template per xdist worker in `_build_bare` (bd init + git config + a baseline commit) and treats it as an immutable master that `copy_bd_workspace` copies per test. The template git repo leaves auto gc and maintenance enabled, so git can fire background maintenance during a run and write `.git/objects/maintenance.lock` into the template. The read-only guard (~conftest.py:655) then sees the template changed and fails every test that copied it. Observed non-deterministically on a single matrix leg of otherwise-green commits: run 33910574201 (ubuntu py3.12) failed 35 grind tests, each with "the bare bd template was modified after it was built: [.git/objects/maintenance.lock]". Earlier commits (t2kn.7 era, d333.9) hit the same flake, and main is green whenever the race does not fire, which is why it looks intermittent.
After. The template repo disables auto gc and maintenance at build time so git never writes into `.git/objects/` after the template is built, and the guard also ignores transient .git lock files so a stray lock can never fail a run.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1
## Scope
Disable git auto gc and maintenance on the bare template when it is built in tests/conftest.py `_build_bare`, and make the read-only-template guard ignore transient `.git` lock files. Add tests that the built template has maintenance off and that the guard tolerates a planted lock file.
## Non-goals
Do not change what the template contains (prefix, branch, identity, baseline commit) or `copy_bd_workspace` semantics. Do not disable gc/maintenance globally on the runner, only on the template repo. Do not loosen the guard beyond lock files; a real content change to the template must still fail. Do not touch product code; this is test-infra only.
## Concrete locations
tests/conftest.py: `_build_bare` (~468, add the git config disables after bd init and before the baseline commit) and the read-only-template guard (~640-660, the block raising "Templates are read-only masters"). Reference: `copy_bd_workspace` (~583) and the `_git` helper.
## Resolved decisions
1. Prevent the write at the source: set gc.auto 0, maintenance.auto false, and gc.autoDetach false in the template repo config in `_build_bare`, so no background gc or maintenance runs against it.
2. Also make the guard ignore paths ending in .lock under .git/, as defense in depth against any other transient git lock, without weakening detection of real changes.
3. Keep both fixes: the config disable is the primary cause fix, the guard tolerance ensures a single stray lock can never redden a run.
4. Scope config changes to the template repo only, never the runner global git config.
## Compatibility constraints
Test-infra only; no product behavior changes and no consumer-visible change. The guard still fails on any non-lock modification to the template, so the protection it exists for is intact. gc and maintenance being off on a short-lived test template has no downside.
## Ordered steps
1. In `_build_bare`, after bd init, set gc.auto 0, maintenance.auto false, and gc.autoDetach false on the template.
2. In the guard, filter out .git lock paths before deciding the template changed.
3. Add a test that the built bare template reports those config values, and a test that the guard does not fail when a maintenance.lock is planted under .git/objects.
4. Run the previously-flaking grind test files to confirm they pass.
## Dependencies
No blockers. Affects every grind/bd test that copies the bare template.
## Edge cases
A git version that ignores gc.auto but honors maintenance.auto, or the reverse: setting all three covers both. A lock file that is a real change indicator (there is none for these tests): the guard still catches non-lock changes. xdist: each worker builds its own template, so the disable must live in `_build_bare`, which every worker calls.
## Plan-gap guidance
If disabling gc and maintenance does not stop the write on the CI git version (a scheduled git maintenance run outside repo config), stop and record PLAN-GAP: the fix then needs a process-level env disable, decided before shipping.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1 (proves-new): the built bare template has gc.auto=0 and maintenance.auto=false in its git config.
- AC-2 (proves-new): the read-only-template guard does not fail when a maintenance.lock file is present under the template .git.
- AC-3 (guards-existing): the previously-flaking grind test files pass.
## Criterion checks
- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_fixture_template.py -k template_disables_git_maintenance -q`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_fixture_template.py -k guard_ignores_git_lock_files -q`
- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind.py tests/test_grind_local_preflight.py tests/test_grind_codegraph.py -q`
## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_fixture_template.py tests/test_grind_local_preflight.py -q`
close_reason: Template config disables gc and maintenance, and the pristine guard ignores transient .git lock files

comments.author: who
comments.text: Disabled gc.auto, gc.autoDetach, and maintenance.auto on the bare template in _build_bare, so git never writes maintenance.lock into a built master, and made _digests skip .lock paths under .git on both the baseline and comparison sides so a stray lock cannot fail the pristine guard (or lose a read race). A real content change still fails the guard. tests/test_fixture_template.py covers the config assertion and the planted-lock/changed-file pair. Criterion checks passed: AC-1 uv run pytest tests/test_fixture_template.py -k template_disables_git_maintenance -q; AC-2 same file -k guard_ignores_git_lock_files -q; AC-3 uv run pytest tests/test_grind.py tests/test_grind_local_preflight.py tests/test_grind_codegraph.py -q (81 passed, 26 skipped).

title: opencode: resolve the opencode binary and preflight it, or grind crashes with a raw traceback
description:
## Objective
The local/opencode backend finds the opencode binary at its canonical install path when it is not on PATH, and grind preflight verifies the binary is launchable before claiming — so a standard opencode install runs, and a genuinely missing binary aborts with an actionable message instead of an unhandled FileNotFoundError.

## Behavioral context
Before. OpenCodeRunner spawns opencode by the bare name "opencode" (BACKEND binary map local/opencode -> "opencode"). opencode installs to ~/.opencode/bin/opencode, which is NOT on the default non-login PATH, so on a clean install `ortus grind --backend local` passes the server/CodeGraph/opencode.json preflight, claims nothing, then dies at subprocess.Popen with `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: opencode` and a full traceback (observed 2026-09-04 in ~/code/localtest during the ortus-t2kn.9 audition; the 184 MB binary was present at ~/.opencode/bin/opencode but unresolved). Grind preflight probes server reachability and opencode.json but never checks the binary. After. OpenCodeRunner resolves the binary via shutil.which("opencode") then a fallback to ~/.opencode/bin/opencode (opencode installer default); grind preflight and ortus check assert the resolved binary is executable and abort/report with an install/PATH remediation before any claim; a truly missing binary yields a clean message, never a traceback.

## Design
See design field.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1
## Scope
Add opencode binary resolution (PATH then ~/.opencode/bin/opencode fallback) used by OpenCodeRunner and the check/preflight probes; add a binary-launchable preflight to grind for the opencode backend (mirror the server-reachability abort) and a check row; unit tests with the binary present/absent and PATH/fallback.
## Non-goals
Do not change the codex/claude/grok binary resolution. Do not install opencode for the user. Do not add arbitrary search paths beyond PATH and the documented ~/.opencode/bin. Do not swallow a real launch error after a resolved binary starts (that stays a normal nonzero exit).
## Concrete locations
src/ortus/core/agent.py (the BACKEND binary map + OpenCodeRunner.build_argv/run — resolve the path once), src/ortus/core/local_backend.py or a small resolver helper (shutil.which + fallback), src/ortus/commands/grind.py (opencode preflight near the server-reachable probe, ~line 1212), src/ortus/commands/check.py (check_opencode binary row), tests/test_core_agent.py, tests/test_grind_local_preflight.py, tests/test_check.py.
## Resolved decisions
1. Resolution order: an explicit config/override if present, else shutil.which("opencode"), else ~/.opencode/bin/opencode if executable, else fail. 2. The fallback path is exactly opencode installers default (~/.opencode/bin); other locations are the operators PATH responsibility. 3. Preflight failure is a clean abort BEFORE claiming (no stranded issue), with the message naming both fixes: add ~/.opencode/bin to PATH, or install opencode. 4. The resolved absolute path is what Popen receives, so the child inherits it regardless of PATH.
## Compatibility constraints
claude/codex/grok binary handling unchanged. When opencode IS on PATH, behavior is identical to today (which returns it first). The fallback only adds a path; it never overrides an on-PATH opencode. Existing opencode argv tests still pass (argv[0] becomes the resolved path — update the assertion to accept the resolved path).
## Ordered steps
1. Add the resolver (which -> ~/.opencode/bin fallback) and use it in OpenCodeRunner. 2. Add the binary-launchable preflight to grind for opencode, aborting before claim with remediation. 3. Add the check row. 4. Tests: on-PATH, fallback-only, missing-entirely (clean abort, no traceback, no claim); run them.
## Dependencies
Discovered-from ortus-t2kn.9 (the audition). Touches t2kn.2 (runner) and t2kn.6 (preflight) surfaces already shipped. No blockers.
## Edge cases
opencode on PATH AND at ~/.opencode/bin: PATH wins (no behavior change). ~/.opencode/bin/opencode present but not executable: treat as missing, name the chmod. A relative/symlinked opencode: resolve to an absolute path for Popen. Windows: out of scope (backend is unsupported there).
## Plan-gap guidance
If opencode ships a different canonical path on some platform than ~/.opencode/bin, do not hardcode a second guess — record PLAN-GAP and require PATH, rather than probing arbitrary locations.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1 (proves-new): with opencode absent from PATH but present at ~/.opencode/bin/opencode, OpenCodeRunner resolves and launches it.
- AC-2 (proves-new): with opencode missing entirely, grind --backend local aborts BEFORE claiming with a PATH/install message and no traceback and no in_progress issue.
- AC-3 (guards-existing): with opencode on PATH, resolution and argv are unchanged and other backends are unaffected.
## Criterion checks
- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_agent.py -k opencode_binary_fallback -q`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_local_preflight.py -k opencode_missing_binary_aborts -q`
- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_agent.py tests/test_grind_local_preflight.py -q`
## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_core_agent.py tests/test_grind_local_preflight.py tests/test_check.py -q`
close_reason: opencode resolves via PATH then ~/.opencode/bin; grind, check, and init preflight the binary so a missing install aborts before any claim with the PATH/install fix instead of a FileNotFoundError traceback

comments.author: who
comments.text: Resolved the opencode executable through one helper, resolve_opencode_binary in local_backend.py: an explicit path is taken as given; a bare name is looked up on PATH first, then at the installer's ~/.opencode/bin, returned absolute with symlinks resolved. A present-but-not-executable file names the chmod; a binary that is nowhere names both fixes (add the directory to PATH, or install opencode). make_runner resolves once and hands OpenCodeRunner the absolute path, so Popen receives it regardless of PATH and a missing binary is a BackendError, never a FileNotFoundError traceback. grind resolves it in the served-model preflight before the flock and before any bd read, so the abort claims nothing; the check binary row and provisioned row resolve the same way and report the launched path; init accepts a standard install as the run backend. Tests fake the home directory throughout so a developer's real ~/.opencode never answers for the suite. title: opencode: ortus init writes the mcp.codegraph entry into opencode.json
description:
## Objective
`ortus init --backend opencode` registers the CodeGraph MCP server in `opencode.json`, so a freshly provisioned repo passes the `opencode mcp` row of `ortus check --backend opencode` without hand-editing.

## Behavioral context
Before. init merges only `provider.ortuslocal` into `opencode.json`; the `mcp.codegraph` entry the spike proved opencode runs client-side has to be pasted by the operator, and `ortus check --backend opencode` fails the `opencode mcp` row on every fresh repo. After. init merges `mcp.codegraph = {"type": "local", "command": ["codegraph", "serve", "--mcp"], "enabled": true}` beside the provider entry, keyed the same way and preserving everything else in the file; check passes the row; under `codegraph = "off"` no entry is written.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1
## Scope
Extend the keyed `opencode.json` merge to own `mcp.codegraph` the way it owns `provider.ortuslocal`: create the entry when absent, rewrite it when drifted, leave the rest of the `mcp` table and the file untouched, and write nothing when it is already current. Gate on the resolved CodeGraph policy so `off` writes no entry. Expose the expected entry as one constant that `ortus check` reads for its remediation hint too.
## Non-goals
No change to check's rows (they already read the entry). No `opencode mcp add` subprocess: the file is the registration and init must stay deterministic. No global `~/.config/opencode` config. No codex-local changes.
## Concrete locations
src/ortus/core/init_render.py (`merge_opencode_config`, `read_opencode_config`), src/ortus/core/local_backend.py (an `opencode_mcp_entry()` beside `opencode_provider_block`), src/ortus/commands/init.py (`_write_opencode_config`), src/ortus/commands/check.py (`_opencode_mcp_entry`, `OPENCODE_MCP_HINT` — reuse the new constant), tests/test_init.py, tests/test_init_render.py, tests/test_check.py.
## Resolved decisions
1. The entry is exactly the shape recorded in bd memory opencode-q1-mcp: type local, command codegraph serve --mcp, enabled true. 2. The command names the bare `codegraph` executable, not a resolved path, so the file stays portable across machines. 3. Keyed merge, same as the provider entry: Ortus owns `mcp.codegraph` only.
## Compatibility constraints
Existing `opencode.json` content survives outside the two Ortus-owned keys; other backends' init output is unchanged; `codegraph = "off"` writes no entry and check under off already passes the codegraph row. Linux and macOS.
## Ordered steps
1. Add the entry function in local_backend.py and point check's hint at it.
2. Merge it in merge_opencode_config under the resolved codegraph policy.
3. Tests: fresh file, existing file with a foreign mcp entry, drifted entry, off policy.
4. Run them.
## Dependencies
Parent ortus-t2kn; follows ortus-t2kn.4, whose `opencode mcp` row observes the entry. Consumers: `ortus check --backend opencode` and the grind CodeGraph handshake for opencode workers (ortus-t2kn.6).
## Edge cases
An `mcp` key that is not an object: refuse before writing, as `read_opencode_config` does for `provider`. An operator's own `mcp.codegraph` with a different command: rewrite it (Ortus owns the key) and say so in the progress line. `--force` re-init: idempotent, no rewrite when current.
## Plan-gap guidance
If opencode's schema requires a field the spike did not record (for example a mandatory `environment` map), stop and record PLAN-GAP rather than guessing a shape init cannot verify.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1 (proves-new): init on a fresh opencode repo writes `mcp.codegraph` with the verified shape beside the provider entry.
- AC-2 (proves-new): an existing `opencode.json` with a foreign mcp entry keeps it, and a drifted `mcp.codegraph` is rewritten.
- AC-3 (guards-existing): the provider merge and other backends' init output are unchanged.
## Criterion checks
- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_init.py -k opencode_mcp_entry -q`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_init_render.py -k opencode_mcp_merge -q`
- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_init.py tests/test_init_render.py -q`
## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_init.py tests/test_init_render.py tests/test_check.py -q`

Criterion checks passed: AC-1 uv run pytest tests/test_init.py -k opencode_mcp_entry -q (3 passed); AC-2 uv run pytest tests/test_init_render.py -k opencode_mcp_merge -q (4 passed); AC-3 uv run pytest tests/test_init.py tests/test_init_render.py -q (140 passed). title: opencode: retire the codex-local machinery once opencode-local works
description:
## Objective
Remove the codex-specific machinery the local backend no longer uses once it drives via opencode: the mcp_shim usage on local, the codex JSON decoder routing for local, and the codex provider/capability coupling — so there is one local engine (opencode) and no dead codex-local code.

## Behavioral context
Before. LocalRunner subclasses CodexRunner; local logs decode as codex; local MCP goes through mcp_shim (namespace flatten + developer-role demotion + chunked decode); local config renders codex -c overrides; tests couple local to codex (test_local_backend_uses_codex_decoder, test_backend_conflict_treats_local_as_codex, test_probe_local_takes_codex_capability_path, test_profiles_local_accepts_codex_efforts, test_list_bundled_local_uses_codex_config). After. Local uses only OpenCodeRunner + the opencode decoder + opencode.json; the shim and codex-local paths are deleted or, if the shim is used by no backend, removed entirely; the coupling tests are replaced by opencode equivalents.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1
## Scope
Delete the codex-local code paths superseded by t2kn.2-.6: LocalRunner-as-CodexRunner, the codex decoder routing for local, the codex MCP shim usage on local (and src/ortus/core/mcp_shim.py itself if no backend uses it), the codex context/web_search tuning, and the codex-coupling tests; replace with opencode equivalents. Pure removal + test migration.
## Non-goals
Do not touch the real codex backend (codex remains a first-class backend for hosted use). Do not remove anything still referenced by codex/grok. Do not change behavior of the opencode path — this is dead-code removal after the pivot works.
## Concrete locations
src/ortus/core/agent.py (LocalRunner removal/replacement), src/ortus/core/mcp_shim.py (delete if unused), src/ortus/core/local_backend.py (codex-provider rendering), src/ortus/core/runstate.py (codex-for-local routing), and the coupling tests in tests/test_tail.py, tests/test_check.py, tests/test_core_config.py, tests/test_dashboard.py, tests/test_core_codegraph.py, tests/test_init_render.py.
## Resolved decisions
1. Removal happens ONLY after t2kn.2-.6 are green so the opencode path is proven before the codex path is deleted. 2. mcp_shim.py is deleted only if grep confirms no backend imports it; if codex (hosted) somehow needs it, keep it and remove only the local usage. 3. Each deleted coupling test is replaced by an opencode-behavior test, not just dropped.
## Compatibility constraints
The real codex backend (hosted codex exec) keeps every capability it has now — this removes codex-as-local-engine, not codex. claude/grok untouched. No net loss of coverage: coupling tests become opencode tests.
## Ordered steps
1. Confirm t2kn.2-.6 green. 2. Grep for mcp_shim / codex-local usage; delete the local paths. 3. Delete mcp_shim.py iff unreferenced. 4. Migrate the six coupling tests to opencode equivalents. 5. Run the full suite.
## Dependencies
Blocked by t2kn.2, t2kn.3, t2kn.4, t2kn.5, t2kn.6 (the opencode path must exist and pass first). Predecessor context: ortus-d333.14/.15/.16 built the shim now being retired.
## Edge cases
mcp_shim referenced by a test only, not src: still safe to delete with the test. A coupling test that also guards a non-codex behavior: split it, keep the general half. If the codex backend re-uses any removed helper, keep the helper and narrow the deletion to the local wiring.
## Plan-gap guidance
If removing the codex-local decoder would also break the hosted codex backends decoding (shared code), stop and record PLAN-GAP: separate the shared path first rather than breaking codex to retire local.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1 (proves-new): no src module routes the local/opencode backend through CodexRunner, the codex decoder, or mcp_shim (grep-clean).
- AC-2 (proves-new): mcp_shim.py is deleted (or a comment records its single remaining non-local user), and the migrated coupling-test files pass.
- AC-3 (guards-existing): the hosted codex backend and claude/grok keep their behavior and tests.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `rg -n "mcp_shim|CodexRunner" src/ortus/core/agent.py src/ortus/core/local_backend.py src/ortus/core/runstate.py`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py tests/test_check.py tests/test_core_config.py tests/test_core_codegraph.py tests/test_init_render.py -q`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_core_agent.py tests/test_agent.py tests/test_tail.py tests/test_check.py tests/test_core_codegraph.py -q`

title: opencode: grind preflight and read-only verify sandbox posture
description:
## Objective
grind on the opencode backend aborts before claiming when the provider is unreachable, and runs the verify phase under a posture that cannot write to the repository — the sandbox guarantee grind relies on today from codex --sandbox read-only.

## Behavioral context
Before. LocalRunner leans on codex --sandbox read-only for the verifier and codex workspace-write for implement. After. OpenCodeRunner applies the read-only posture the spike proved for opencode (permission config that denies writes, and/or an outer bwrap read-only wrap like ClaudeRunner._readonly_argv), and grind preflight probes provider reachability before a claim.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1
## Scope
Add opencode grind preflight (provider /models reachability, CodeGraph policy enforcement) and implement OpenCodeRunner._readonly_argv/preflight_readonly to yield a real read-only verify posture per the spike, plus the implement posture that permits tool use.
## Non-goals
No decoder/config/check. Do not weaken any other backends posture. Do not implement ortus-side sandboxing beyond wrapping opencode (bwrap) or setting opencode permission config.
## Concrete locations
src/ortus/commands/grind.py (preflight before claim; cf. the local preflight), src/ortus/core/agent.py (OpenCodeRunner readonly posture; cf. ClaudeRunner._readonly_argv and CodexRunner._readonly_argv), tests/test_grind_local_preflight.py (opencode sibling), tests/test_core_agent.py.
## Resolved decisions
1. The read-only mechanism is exactly what opencode-q1-sandbox recorded: opencode permission config that denies writes, an outer bwrap wrap, or both. 2. If opencode permissions alone cannot guarantee no-write, grind wraps opencode in the Claude-style bwrap read-only root and preflights it like ClaudeRunner.preflight_readonly. 3. Preflight reuses the t2kn.4 reachability probe.
## Compatibility constraints
Other backends preflight and posture unchanged. The verify posture must be provably non-writable — a verifier that can write is a correctness failure, not a WARN.
## Ordered steps
1. Add opencode preflight (reachability + CodeGraph policy). 2. Implement the read-only + implement postures from the finding. 3. If wrapping in bwrap, add the preflight-executes probe. 4. Tests: server-down aborts, reachable launches, verify cannot write; run them.
## Dependencies
Blocked by ortus-t2kn.1 (sandbox finding) and t2kn.2 (the runner it configures). Pairs with t2kn.4 (shared reachability probe).
## Edge cases
Provider reachable but MCP down under required mode: abort with the CodeGraph message. Verify posture that blocks opencode from starting at all (like the codex outer-wrap lesson): prefer the native permission config, mirror CodexRunner._readonly_argv reasoning. Server 5xx mid-run: classify as retryable per the audition finding.
## Plan-gap guidance
If neither opencode permissions nor a bwrap wrap can produce a non-writable verify posture that still lets opencode run, stop and record PLAN-GAP — grinds verify contract cannot be met and the pivot needs a design decision, not a verifier that might write.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1 (proves-new): grind --backend opencode aborts before claiming when the provider is unreachable, with remediation text.
- AC-2 (proves-new): the verify posture cannot write to the repo (a write attempt under it fails or is absent from the advertised tools).
- AC-3 (guards-existing): other backends preflight and postures are unchanged and their tests pass.
## Criterion checks
- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_local_preflight.py -k opencode_server_down_aborts -q`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_agent.py -k opencode_verify_readonly -q`
- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_local_preflight.py tests/test_core_agent.py -q`
## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_grind_local_preflight.py tests/test_core_agent.py -q`
close_reason: Grind on the opencode backend now enforces CodeGraph policy at the probe: opencode_mcp_registration_gap folds the opencode.json mcp.codegraph entry into availability, so a required run aborts before any claim (missing/unreadable file, missing entry, enabled:false) and auto reports it as the fallback; other backends unchanged. The served-model preflight abort names the launched backend with the serving hint (reachability reuses probe_models). Verify posture decided and recorded: OPENCODE_PERMISSION denial of edit/write/bash is the whole read-only posture, no bwrap, preflight_readonly a no-op; a real-spawn test proves the denial reaches the child over a shell-exported allow. Criterion checks passed: AC-1 (1 passed), AC-2 (1 passed), AC-3 (44 passed); sweep of codegraph/check/agent suites 123 passed. Follow-up spike ortus-t2kn.12 filed for permission-scope precedence. Commit 0b29470.

comments.author: who
comments.text: SANDBOX FINDING (opencode-q1-sandbox, 2026-09-03): opencode permission is TOOL-level not OS-level. permission={edit:deny,write:deny,bash:deny} = true read-only (write/edit/bash tools removed). permission with bash:allow is NOT read-only — bash 'printf > file' writes. So pick a verify design: (1) recommended NO-BASH-VERIFY — verify agent runs bash:deny (read-only tools + CodeGraph only), grind runs the criterion-check commands itself; no bwrap needed. OR (2) BASH-VERIFY-WRAPPED — if the verify agent runs bash, wrap opencode in the Claude bwrap read-only root (ClaudeRunner._readonly_argv, nested_claude_sandbox fixture) since opencode has no OS --sandbox flag. Implement posture is free (headless auto-approves). git/bd proven non-interactive.

comments.author: who
comments.text:
Implemented. CodeGraph probe (src/ortus/core/codegraph.py) now folds the opencode.json mcp.codegraph registration into availability for backend=opencode via opencode_mcp_registration_gap: a missing file, an unreadable file, a missing entry, and enabled:false each stop a required run at the probe with the CodeGraph remediation (before any claim; no MCP RPC attempted) and report as the auto fallback otherwise. grok/claude/codex/local verdicts unchanged. Grind phase 0b abort now names the launched backend ("opencode backend: local server unreachable ..." plus the serving hint); reachability reuses probe_models exactly as check does. Runner decision recorded in OpenCodeRunner docstrings: NO bwrap. The OPENCODE_PERMISSION denial of edit/write/bash (opencode-q1-sandbox check A) is the whole verify posture; preflight_readonly stays a no-op because the verifier runs no commands. New test drives the real spawn path with a stand-in binary: the denial reaches the child over an allow exported in the shell; implement inherits the shell untouched; no project file written.

Criterion checks passed: AC-1 uv run pytest tests/test_grind_local_preflight.py -k opencode_server_down_aborts -q (1 passed). AC-2 uv run pytest tests/test_core_agent.py -k opencode_verify_readonly -q (1 passed). AC-3 uv run pytest tests/test_grind_local_preflight.py tests/test_core_agent.py -q (44 passed). Changed-surface sweep tests/test_core_codegraph.py tests/test_grind_codegraph.py tests/test_check.py tests/test_agent.py: 123 passed. Ruff: 3 findings in grind.py identical at HEAD (pre-existing, not touched).

Follow-up filed: ortus-t2kn.12, a host-side spike on whether an agent-scoped, user-scoped, or OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT permission can re-allow a denied tool under the verify denial. That precedence is the one scope the finding did not cover; the posture is proven only against the project permission table.

title: opencode: decode opencode --format json events in runstate and tail
description:
## Objective
runstate/tail classify opencode run --format json events — assistant text, tool calls, CodeGraph MCP calls, and turn/finish — so grind logging, the dashboard, and ortus tail render an opencode worker at parity with the codex/grok decoders.

## Behavioral context
Before. A local worker log is decoded as codex JSONL (test_local_backend_uses_codex_decoder). After. It is decoded as opencode events using the exact event-type vocabulary the spike recorded; the codex decoder path for local is retired in t2kn.7. CodeGraph MCP calls are recognised for the required-mode handshake.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1
## Scope
Add an opencode event decoder in src/ortus/core/runstate.py (classify_line/_describe, cf. is_grok_event/_describe_codex_item) and route local/opencode logs to it in tail; recognise the CodeGraph MCP tool event so the implementation handshake is detected.
## Non-goals
No runner/config/check. Do not remove the codex decoder yet (t2kn.7 flips the routing after this lands). Do not change claude/codex/grok decoding.
## Concrete locations
src/ortus/core/runstate.py (event classifier + GROK_EVENT_TYPES-style set), src/ortus/commands/tail.py, src/ortus/core/codegraph.py (parse_transcript MCP-call recognition for opencode), tests/test_core_runstate.py, tests/test_tail.py, tests/test_codex_tail_decoder.py (add an opencode sibling).
## Resolved decisions
1. Event-type names come verbatim from the t2kn.1 capture (opencode-q1), not assumption. 2. The decoder never retains tool payloads (same privacy rule as the codex/grok decoders). 3. The CodeGraph handshake event is whatever opencode emits for an MCP tool call — recorded by the spike.
## Compatibility constraints
claude/codex/grok decoding byte-identical and green. The local routing still points at the codex decoder until t2kn.7 flips it, or this leaf flips it and t2kn.7 only deletes dead code — sequence recorded so no window decodes with the wrong decoder.
## Ordered steps
1. Add the opencode event classifier from the recorded vocabulary. 2. Recognise the MCP-call event for the handshake. 3. Route opencode logs to it. 4. Tests from a captured opencode JSONL fixture; run them.
## Dependencies
Blocked by ortus-t2kn.1 (event vocabulary). Pairs with t2kn.6 (the handshake gate reads this). Precedes t2kn.7 (which removes the codex-for-local decoder path).
## Edge cases
Reasoning/thinking events gated by verbosity like the codex decoder. A tool call with an empty or dotted name (seen on some servers): classify without crashing. A truncated final event: decode what exists.
## Plan-gap guidance
If opencode --format json is not line-delimited JSON (e.g. a single aggregate object or SSE), record PLAN-GAP: the decoder and the log-tee assume JSONL, and a different framing changes _spawn_logged handling, decided before coding.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1 (proves-new): a captured opencode JSONL fixture decodes to assistant/tool/finish events with correct types.
- AC-2 (proves-new): a CodeGraph MCP tool event in that fixture is recognised as the implementation handshake.
- AC-3 (guards-existing): codex/grok/claude decoders are unchanged and their tests pass.
## Criterion checks
- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_runstate.py -k opencode_events -q`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py -k opencode_codegraph_handshake -q`
- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py tests/test_core_runstate.py -q`
## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_core_runstate.py tests/test_tail.py -q`

AC-1/AC-2/AC-3 criterion checks passed; decoder, codegraph, dashboard suites green. Committed 5aa68f7. Dashboard log_backend follow-up filed as ortus-t2kn.11.

comments.text:
Implemented the opencode run --format json decoder from the ortus-t2kn.1 capture.

title: opencode: ortus check --backend opencode verifies binary, provider/model, MCP, and sandbox posture
description:
## Objective
ortus check --backend opencode reports, before grind runs, whether the opencode binary is present, the configured provider/model is served, the CodeGraph MCP server is registered for opencode, and the sandbox/permission posture is the intended one — failing fast with remediation instead of a hung worker.

## Behavioral context
Before. check --backend local verifies the codex binary, the Responses provider, and the codex MCP path. After. check --backend opencode verifies the opencode binary, GETs the provider /models to confirm the model is served, confirms opencode has the CodeGraph MCP server registered, and reports the resolved permission posture; codex-only rows do not appear.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1
## Scope
Add opencode check rows: binary probe, provider /models reachability + model match, CodeGraph MCP registration (opencode mcp list or config inspection per the spike), and a permission-posture report. Two-tier like the other backends (WARN for provisioned siblings).
## Non-goals
No runner/config/decoder work. Do not execute a full worker. Do not police model quality. Do not remove codex-local check rows yet (t2kn.7).
## Concrete locations

1. MCP registration is detected by the method the spike recorded (opencode mcp list vs opencode.json mcp block). 2. The provider probe reuses the existing /models reachability check against the configured base_url. 3. The posture row reports the resolved permission config without launching a worker.

check stays read-only and two-tier; provisioned-but-not-run backends stay WARN and never flip the exit code. Existing backend check tests pass unchanged.

## Dependencies

opencode binary missing: actionable install message. Provider up but model not listed: name the served ids. MCP not registered: name the exact opencode mcp add command. Posture unknown: report it, do not guess a pass.

If MCP registration cannot be detected without launching opencode, record PLAN-GAP rather than shelling a full worker inside check.

title: opencode: provider/model config and opencode.json generation
description:
## Objective
The local/opencode backend reads its provider base_url and model from Ortus config and materializes a valid opencode.json custom-provider block, so `ortus init` sets up a self-served model with one command and no hand-editing.

## Behavioral context
Before. The [local] table feeds codex -c model_providers overrides (Responses). After. The same operator inputs (base_url, model, optional api_key_env) render an opencode.json provider block (npm @ai-sdk/openai-compatible + options.baseURL + models) that OpenCodeRunner points -m at; ortus init writes it.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1
## Scope
Extend the config surface so the backend produces an opencode.json provider block from base_url/model/api_key_env; ortus init writes/updates it idempotently; validation errors name the missing key. Reuse the [local] table or a renamed key per the spike.
## Non-goals
No runner (t2kn.2), no check probes (t2kn.4). Do not delete the codex [local] plumbing yet (t2kn.7). Do not manage the model server lifecycle. Do not put secrets in opencode.json (api_key_env indirection only).
## Concrete locations
src/ortus/core/local_backend.py (config parse/validate), src/ortus/core/init_render.py + src/ortus/commands/init.py (BACKEND_TEMPLATES, opencode.json emission), tests/test_core_local_backend.py, tests/test_init.py, tests/test_init_render.py.
## Resolved decisions
1. The provider block shape is exactly the one the t2kn.1 spike verified. 2. api_key_env stays indirection; the value never lands in opencode.json or argv. 3. init merges the provider block without clobbering a user-authored opencode.json (managed markers or a keyed merge, matching how init treats other config files).
## Compatibility constraints
Existing backends generate their current config files unchanged. If opencode.json already exists with user content, init preserves it. The config keys either stay [local] or move under the renamed backend per t2kn.2s decision, consistently.
## Ordered steps
1. Add opencode.json rendering from the config inputs. 2. Wire init to emit/merge it for the backend. 3. Validation messages for missing model/base_url. 4. Tests for render, merge-preserve, and validation; run them.
## Dependencies
Blocked by ortus-t2kn.1 (provider block shape). Pairs with t2kn.2 (runner reads the model/provider). Consumed by t2kn.4 (check reads the same config).
## Edge cases
A keyless local provider (no api_key_env): render without an auth block. base_url without /v1 or trailing slash: normalize. A served model id opencode cannot use as a bare model name: record the alias in the models map.
## Plan-gap guidance
If the spike found opencode requires a provider mechanism other than opencode.json (e.g. a global auth store only), stop and record PLAN-GAP rather than inventing a config path init cannot reproduce deterministically.

title: opencode: OpenCodeRunner and backend registration
description:
## Objective
An OpenCodeRunner drives a headless opencode worker for the local backend, and the backend registry, resolver, factory, worker-prompt composer, and profiles route the local backend through it instead of codex.

## Behavioral context
Before. make_runner("local") returns a LocalRunner (subclass of CodexRunner) that shells `codex exec` at a Responses provider. After. It returns an OpenCodeRunner that shells `opencode run --format json -m <provider>/<model>` at a chat-completions provider; compose_worker_prompt keeps the plain-objective shape (no /goal); profiles/SUPPORTED_EFFORTS map opencode effort variants. Claude/codex/grok argv unchanged.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1
## Scope
Add OpenCodeRunner (build_argv, run, readonly posture, configure_codegraph) in src/ortus/core/agent.py; point make_runner/local at it; keep compose_worker_prompt(local) plain-objective; set SUPPORTED_EFFORTS/profile mapping for opencode variants. Unit tests for argv and prompt shape.
## Non-goals
No decoder (t2kn.5), no check/init (t2kn.4), no config-file generation (t2kn.3), no codex-local removal (t2kn.7). Do not change claude/codex/grok. Do not send /goal.
## Concrete locations
src/ortus/core/agent.py (OpenCodeRunner beside LocalRunner; make_runner; compose_worker_prompt), src/ortus/core/profiles.py (SUPPORTED_EFFORTS, BackendName), tests/test_core_agent.py, tests/test_agent.py. Reference: GrokRunner (sibling, not a CodexRunner subclass — opencode flags are not codex flags).
## Resolved decisions
1. OpenCodeRunner is a sibling dataclass like GrokRunner, NOT a CodexRunner subclass — opencode argv (run --format json -m provider/model --agent) shares nothing with codex exec. 2. argv shape and the read-only posture come verbatim from the t2kn.1 spike findings (opencode-q1, opencode-q1-sandbox). 3. model is provider/model form; the provider id and model come from config (t2kn.3).
## Compatibility constraints
Every existing backend keeps byte-identical argv and tests. The pivot may keep the backend name `local` or rename to `opencode` per the spike recommendation; if renamed, resolve_backend/BACKENDS and the config keys move together in this leaf and the rename is called out.
## Ordered steps
1. Read opencode-q1/opencode-q1-sandbox findings. 2. Add OpenCodeRunner with build_argv from the finding. 3. Route make_runner/local (or the new name) to it. 4. Map profiles/SUPPORTED_EFFORTS. 5. Add argv + prompt tests; run them.
## Dependencies
Blocked by ortus-t2kn.1 (spike findings define argv, effort variants, read-only posture). Consumers: grind/plan/interview _make_runner. Precedes t2kn.4/.5/.6/.7.
## Edge cases
opencode needing an API-key env for a keyless local provider: OpenCodeRunner passes the config-named env only. A served model id with slashes/colons vs opencode -m provider/model parsing: use the alias the spike recorded. readonly verify posture: apply exactly the spike-proven mechanism.

If the spike found opencode has no non-interactive read-only posture, do NOT ship a verifier that can write — stop and record PLAN-GAP; the posture is a precondition of this runner, resolved in t2kn.6, not improvised here.

title: Pivot the local backend from codex to opencode (chat-completions + client-side MCP)
description:
Add opencode as a first-class Ortus agent backend so ortus grind can drive the bd queue with a local (or any) model through opencode instead of codex.

Motivation (from the 2026-09-02 local/codex audition, epic ortus-d333): codex drives local models through its Responses API, and every hard failure was codex meeting llama.cpp's /v1/responses endpoint — the developer-role template 500 (ortus-d333.15) and the silently-dropped namespace MCP tools (ortus-d333.13/.14). opencode 1.18.27 speaks /v1/chat/completions and executes MCP client-side, so BOTH failure classes disappear and the namespace shim (mcp_shim.py) is unnecessary on this backend. opencode run --format json emits a raw JSON event stream, -m provider/model selects the model, opencode mcp manages MCP servers, and a custom OpenAI-compatible provider is one opencode.json block (npm @ai-sdk/openai-compatible + options.baseURL).

Claude remains the default. The outer Python scheduler still owns claim, verify, close, commit, push; workers still may not close/commit/push. The termination shape is the codex-style plain objective prompt (opencode has no /goal slash command and does not need one) — compose_worker_prompt already handles this per backend.

The load-bearing UNKNOWN is the sandbox story: codex gives grind an OS-level --sandbox workspace-write/read-only posture that LocalRunner/CodexRunner._readonly_argv rely on; opencode has app-level permissions (--auto, permission config), not OS isolation. Running an abliterated/uncensored model unattended is exactly where OS sandboxing matters, so the spike must resolve how grind gets an equivalent read-only verify posture (opencode permission config, an outer bwrap wrap like the Claude backend, or a documented gap).

Constraints and inspiration: the shipped Claude/Codex/Grok/local adapters (src/ortus/core/agent.py — ClaudeRunner, CodexRunner, GrokRunner, LocalRunner), the local epic ortus-d333 checklist, and PRD-local-backend.md. Do NOT reuse mcp_shim.py here (opencode does MCP itself). Windows stays unsupported.

Children, in spike-first order:
1. Q1 spike — headless opencode drives the local model with tool use, a parseable JSON stream, MCP (CodeGraph), a sandbox/permission posture, and non-interactive session close; record findings before any runner leaf.
2. OpenCodeRunner + BACKENDS + resolve_backend + make_runner + compose_worker_prompt.
3. Provider/model config surface (.ortusrc [opencode] or reuse [local]; opencode.json generation) + profiles + SUPPORTED_EFFORTS.
4. ortus init / ortus check / CodeGraph MCP registration via opencode mcp.
5. tail/runstate decoder for opencode --format json events.
6. grind preflight + sandbox/read-only verify posture.
7. README/help/docs.

## Success Criteria

- ortus grind --backend opencode launches an opencode worker for a claimed issue and judges the result from observable bd state, same as the other backends.
- Claude remains the default; existing claude/codex/grok/local argv and stream tests stay green.
- CodeGraph MCP composes with NO shim (client-side execution), proven by a worker completing one codegraph query.
- Worker prompt is the plain-objective shape; no /goal is ever sent to opencode.
- ortus check --backend opencode verifies the opencode binary, the provider/model, MCP registration, and the sandbox posture without emitting codex/claude-only files.
- The read-only verify posture is real (OS wrap or opencode permission config), not a gap that lets a verifier write.
close_reason: Pivot complete and validated end-to-end. The local backend now drives via opencode (chat-completions + client-side MCP): OpenCodeRunner + registration (.2), opencode.json config + MCP entry (.3/.10), check (.4), event decoder (.5), preflight + read-only verify posture (.6), codex-local machinery retired incl. mcp_shim.py deleted (.7), docs (.8), binary resolution (.16), and follow-ups (.11/.13/.14/.15). Q1 spike proved tool use + client-side MCP with NO shim; the Q3 audition (.9) drove a real 27B through a full grind loop to a working commit. All children closed; suite green (1244 passed); README documents the backend and the audition. Supersedes the codex-local epic ortus-d333.

title: grind: a human-labelled in_progress claim wedges every later worker's continue rule
description:
## Objective

A grind worker never inherits an in_progress claim that carries the human label: the goal prompt's continue rule skips such claims as the operator's, and grind releases the claim a reaped worker put on an issue that was already human-labelled when the window began, so the next window starts clean.

## Behavioral context

Before. Observed 2026-09-02 in logs/grind-20260902-185058.log. Iteration 2's worker ran bd ready and claimed a human-labelled spike (the first non-epic in the list) instead of the bug grind had predicted; two seconds later grind reaped that worker with 'claim flagged human', but the claim stayed in_progress. Iteration 3's worker followed the goal prompt's 'If any issue is in_progress, continue that id' and inherited an operator-only issue it could not complete, while grind's own snapshot excluded that claim and expected the predicted bug to move. Every later window repeats this until a human unclaims the issue, and the inherited worker is not reaped because a claim flagged before the window began is excluded from the reap check.

After. A worker orienting on an in_progress issue labelled human treats it as not its own and proceeds to bd ready. When grind reaps a worker for a flagged claim on an issue that was open and human-labelled at window start, it reverts that claim to open, keeps the label, and comments why. A worker that labels its own claim human on the PLAN-GAP exit is unchanged: that claim stays in_progress for the operator, as today.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Two small changes. (1) src/ortus/prompts/goal-prompt.md steps 1 and 2: read labels in the in_progress listing and continue only an in_progress issue that is not labelled human; when the only in_progress ids are human-labelled, proceed to bd ready as if nothing were in progress. (2) src/ortus/commands/grind.py: snapshot the open human-labelled ids at window start beside flagged_at_start; when _reap_reason returns 'claim flagged human' for an id in that snapshot, revert the claim to open through BdClient and add one comment naming the window. Tests in tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py and tests/test_grind_reap.py.

## Non-goals

Do not change EXCLUDED_LABELS or the snapshot exclusion. Do not touch src/ortus/prompts/conditions/work-issue.txt (the harness-select path names its issue and never runs bd ready). Do not change the PLAN-GAP exit: a worker that labels its own claim human keeps that claim in_progress for the operator. Do not unclaim flagged claims that predate the window; those were excluded at startup and belong to the operator. Do not edit any packet field on the reverted issue.

## Concrete locations

src/ortus/prompts/goal-prompt.md: step 1 (bd list --status=in_progress --json --brief) and step 2 (the continue rule). src/ortus/commands/grind.py: _reap_reason and _flagged_claims (CodeGraph: _flagged_claims confirms each candidate by its labels via bd.show), the worker poll in grind() that builds flagged_at_start, and the reap branch that logs 'claim flagged human'. src/ortus/core/grind_loop.py: EXCLUDED_LABELS. src/ortus/core/bd.py: BdClient.in_progress_ids, show, add_comment, and the status-update method the revert uses. Tests: tests/test_grind_reap.py (test_reap_reason_fires_when_claim_gains_human_label, test_reap_reason_ignores_claim_flagged_before_window), tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py.

## Resolved decisions

1. An in_progress issue labelled human is the operator's; the worker never continues it and never claims a human-labelled issue from bd ready (the second half is already the rule).
2. The revert applies only to a claim the reaped worker created on an issue that was open and human-labelled when the window began; the self-flag PLAN-GAP path is untouched because that claim carries the worker's own comment for the operator.
3. Revert means status open with the label kept and one comment; no packet edit, so the readiness hash is untouched.
4. A tracker error during the revert is logged and the claim is left as is; the loop never crashes on the revert.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux and macOS. Every existing tests/test_grind_reap.py case keeps passing; the work-issue prompt and EXCLUDED_LABELS are byte-identical. Claude, Codex, Grok, and local workers all read the same goal prompt, so the rule change applies to every backend.

## Ordered steps

1. Edit goal-prompt.md steps 1 and 2 so the continue rule excludes human-labelled claims and falls through to bd ready.
2. In grind(), snapshot open human-labelled ids at window start next to flagged_at_start.
3. On a 'claim flagged human' reap, revert each flagged id that is in the snapshot to open with a comment; leave the others.
4. Add the prompt-content test and the two reap tests (mis-claim reverted, self-flag left alone).
5. Run the targeted tests.

## Dependencies

No issue dependency. Callers: _reap_reason is called from the worker poll in grind(); the goal prompt is read by the goal-prompt loader in src/ortus/prompts. Evidence: the mis-claim of ortus-d333.11 on 2026-09-02, handed back by hand in that issue's comment thread.

## Edge cases

Two flagged claims in one window: revert each that qualifies. An issue in_progress and human-labelled at window start: untouched. A bd error while reverting: log and continue. A worker that claims a human-labelled issue and closes it anyway: the done bar wins and nothing is reverted. A prompt reader that needs labels but the brief listing omits them: use the label-aware query the harness already uses (bd list with --json and labels) rather than a second bd show per id.

## Plan-gap guidance

If BdClient cannot list open ids by label without parsing bd list text or adding a bd subcommand, stop and record PLAN-GAP rather than scraping output. If the goal prompt cannot express the rule without a bd show per in_progress id, record PLAN-GAP with the listing shape observed.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1 (proves-new): the goal prompt tells the worker not to continue a human-labelled in_progress claim.
- AC-2 (proves-new): grind reverts a reaped worker's claim on an issue that was open and human-labelled at window start, and leaves a self-flagged claim in_progress.
- AC-3 (guards-existing): the reap and prompt-content suites pass.

title: local backend: shim must normalize codex requests llama-server rejects (developer role, chunked bodies)
description:
## Objective

A codex worker on the local backend completes turns against llama-server: the shim rewrites the two request shapes llama-server cannot execute — a developer-role input message (fatal today) and a chunked request body (latent) — so the first live audition failure mode cannot recur.

## Behavioral context

Before. Verified 2026-09-02 against llama-server on [redacted]2:8080 serving 0bserverx/Qwen3.8-27B-Heretic-Abliterated-Uncensored-GGUF:Q4_K_M, reproducing the failed first audition run in ~/code/localtest (logs/grind-20260902-184235.log). codex 0.147.0 sends instructions plus an input[] whose first item is a message with role developer. llama-server maps developer to system when rendering chat messages, the model template raises "Jinja Exception: System message must be at the beginning", the server returns HTTP 500, codex retries five times printing "We are currently experiencing high demand", and the turn fails before any tool call — observed identically with and without the shim in the path, so every local worker dies at launch. Replaying codex's captured 47KB request verbatim with the developer role demoted to user returns 200 with a completed response. Separately, the shim's _forward() reads the request body via Content-Length only; a Transfer-Encoding: chunked POST is forwarded upstream as zero bytes (mechanically proven against a fake upstream). codex sends Content-Length today, so this is latent, not the audition failure.

After. The shim's request leg demotes input[] message roles developer and system to user (order preserved; instructions stays the sole system message) and decodes chunked request bodies before forwarding with an accurate Content-Length. The audition run in a scratch repo reaches tool calls instead of turn.failed.

## Design

See design field.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Two request-leg fixes in src/ortus/core/mcp_shim.py: (1) extend the request rewriter so input[] items of type message with role developer or system become role user; (2) make _forward() read a Transfer-Encoding: chunked body by decoding the chunk framing from self.rfile before rewriting. Tests for both in tests/test_mcp_shim.py.

## Non-goals

Do not touch codex, llama-server, or the model template — the shim is the compatibility seam by the recorded SHIM decision (bd memory local-backend-mcp-decision). Do not merge developer text into instructions (demotion is the replay-proven shape; merging re-orders content). Do not rewrite response legs — the failure is entirely on the request. Do not special-case Ollama: demotion is harmless on servers that accept developer roles, so the rewrite is unconditional. Do not add retry logic — codex owns retries.

## Concrete locations

src/ortus/core/mcp_shim.py: flatten_request() (~line 130) and _rewrite_request_bytes() (~line 353) for the role demotion; _Handler._forward() (~line 252, the Content-Length-only read at line 253-254) for chunked decoding; _flatten_input() (~line 104) shows the existing input[]-walking pattern to extend. Tests: tests/test_mcp_shim.py (fake-upstream harness already in place). Consumers: LocalRunner in src/ortus/core/agent.py points codex at the shim; no signature changes.

## Resolved decisions

1. Role demotion is unconditional and applies to every input[] message with role developer or system; instructions passes through untouched as the single system message. Proven 2026-09-02: the verbatim captured codex request 500s, the demoted variant returns 200 (same server, same model).
2. Demotion happens inside the existing flatten_request() pass so one parse serves both rewrites, and a request that needs neither rewrite still forwards its original bytes.
3. Chunked decoding follows RFC 9112 framing (size line, data, trailing CRLF, terminated by a zero-size chunk; trailers read and dropped) and the decoded body is forwarded with Content-Length — the upstream leg never re-chunks.
4. A request that is neither valid JSON nor decodable stays byte-forwarded as today; the shim never turns a malformed request into a crash.
5. The `namespace` flattening already covers codex's second namespace tool (multi_agent_v1) observed in the captured request; no change needed there — noted so the reviewer does not scope-creep.

## Compatibility constraints

Every existing tests/test_mcp_shim.py case must pass unchanged: requests without namespace tools, developer roles, or chunked bodies are still forwarded byte-identical. Backends claude, codex, grok untouched (shim runs only for local). The Ollama path keeps working — demotion is a no-op semantically on a server that accepted developer roles.

## Ordered steps

1. Add the role-demotion walk to flatten_request()/_flatten_input() with its unit tests (developer demoted, system demoted, user/assistant untouched, byte-identical passthrough when nothing changes).
2. Add chunked-body decoding to _Handler._forward() with a raw-socket test proving the fake upstream receives the full body and an accurate Content-Length.
3. Run the targeted tests.

## Dependencies

Follows ortus-d333.14 (the shim this extends; closed). Evidence: bd memories local-backend-mcp-decision and local-backend-q1. Blocks the operator audition ortus-d333.11 — the audition cannot pass while every local turn dies at the template.

## Edge cases

input[] items that are not messages (function_call, function_call_output) pass through the demotion walk untouched. An input message with no role or a non-string role is left as is. A chunked body with trailers: trailers dropped. A chunked body that ends mid-stream: forward what decoded with accurate length is wrong — treat as malformed and return 400 to codex rather than sending a truncated body upstream. Both rewrites composing on one request (chunked body containing namespace tools and a developer role) must produce a single coherent forward.

## Plan-gap guidance

If demotion alone still yields a template exception on some model (a template that rejects any non-alternating roles), stop and record PLAN-GAP with the server error text rather than inventing message merging.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1 (proves-new): a request whose input[] starts with a developer-role message reaches the fake upstream with that role rewritten to user, other items untouched.
- AC-2 (proves-new): a Transfer-Encoding chunked POST reaches the fake upstream with the full decoded body and an accurate Content-Length.
- AC-3 (guards-existing): a request with no namespace tools, no developer roles, and a Content-Length body is forwarded byte-identical, and the full shim suite passes.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_mcp_shim.py -k "demotes_developer_role" -q`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_mcp_shim.py -k "decodes_chunked_request_body" -q`
- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_mcp_shim.py -q`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_mcp_shim.py tests/test_core_agent.py -q`

comments.text: Shim request leg now demotes developer and system input messages to user in place (instructions stays the sole system message) and decodes Transfer-Encoding chunked request bodies before forwarding with an accurate Content-Length; a body that ends mid-chunk is refused with a 400 instead of forwarded short. Both rewrites live in the existing flatten_request pass, so a request needing neither is still forwarded byte-identical. Criterion checks passed: the demotes_developer_role and decodes_chunked_request_body selections, the full tests/test_mcp_shim.py suite (19 passed), and the targeted set with tests/test_core_agent.py (42 passed); ruff check and format clean. title: local backend: MCP shim flattens namespace tools between codex and the local server
description:
## Objective

A codex exec worker on the local backend completes CodeGraph MCP tool calls against an OpenAI-compatible server, through an in-process shim that flattens Responses namespace tools into plain functions and restores the namespace on the way back.

## Behavioral context

Before. codex 0.147.0 unconditionally sends each MCP server as one Responses tool of type namespace (bd memory local-backend-mcp). Verified 2026-09-02 against the operator's real server (llama.cpp llama-server on [redacted]2:8080, model 0bserverx/Qwen3.8-27B-Heretic-Abliterated-Uncensored-GGUF:Q4_K_M): the namespace entry returns HTTP 200 but is silently dropped from the rendered prompt (input_tokens 69 vs 333 for the flat control), the model never sees the tool, and the call comes back as raw <tool_call> text in a message item — codex observes no function_call and skips MCP without error. The identical tool sent flat as mcp__codegraph__codegraph_explore returns a well-formed function_call item with the exact name and valid JSON arguments. Ollama 0.23.0 fails the same way in kind. Decision SHIM is recorded in bd memory local-backend-mcp-decision.

After. When the local backend launches a worker with CodeGraph overrides, codex talks to a loopback shim instead of the server directly. The shim rewrites request tools[] (each type=namespace entry becomes flat type=function entries named <namespace>__<tool>) and rewrites response function_call items whose flat name belongs to a flattened namespace back into the namespace+name shape codex routes on, for both streaming SSE (response.output_item.added / response.output_item.done) and non-streaming bodies. A worker completes one codegraph_explore call and reaches turn.completed. Without CodeGraph overrides the shim is not started and behavior is unchanged.

## Design

See design field.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Add an MCP namespace shim module and wire it into the local backend launch path: a loopback HTTP forwarder started before the codex subprocess and stopped after it exits, with the provider base_url override pointed at the shim and the shim forwarding to LocalConfig.base_url. Request-side tools[] flattening, response-side function_call name restoration (SSE and non-streaming), passthrough for everything else. Unit tests against a fake upstream server.

## Non-goals

Do not patch codex or the inference server. Do not translate wire protocols (requests and responses stay /v1/responses shaped; only tools[] entries and function_call names are rewritten). Do not shim the claude, codex, or grok backends — the shim starts only for backend local with CodeGraph overrides present. Do not add retry/backoff for upstream 5xx (record behavior; Q4 territory). Do not buffer whole SSE streams.

## Concrete locations

New src/ortus/core/mcp_shim.py (forwarder + rewriters). src/ortus/core/agent.py: LocalRunner.build_argv() / run() — the -c model_providers.ortus_local.base_url override must point at the shim's 127.0.0.1:<port>/v1 when the shim is active; CodexRunner.build_argv() shows the three mcp_servers.codegraph -c overrides the namespace names derive from. src/ortus/core/local_backend.py: LocalConfig.base_url / origin() — the shim's upstream. Tests: new tests/test_mcp_shim.py; existing tests/test_core_agent.py local-runner argv tests must show the swapped base_url. CodeGraph evidence: LocalRunner callers are make_runner and the grind/plan/interview _make_runner seams.

## Resolved decisions

1. The shim is in-process (a daemon thread running an http.server-style loop on 127.0.0.1 with an ephemeral port), started by LocalRunner.run() when codegraph overrides are configured and torn down in a finally block — no new subprocess, no new dependency, matching the few-dozen-lines cap from ortus-d333.12 decision 2.
2. Flat names use the double-underscore join <namespace>__<tool> — verified accepted and echoed back exactly by both llama-server (2026-09-02) and Ollama 0.23.0 (ortus-d333.12).
3. The shim tracks, per request, which namespaces it flattened, and restores only function_call names that match a flattened namespace prefix; all other names pass through untouched, so a model inventing an unknown tool name still surfaces as codex's normal unsupported-call error.
4. Streaming is line-by-line SSE passthrough with rewriting applied only to response.output_item.added and response.output_item.done payloads carrying type=function_call; every other event line is forwarded byte-faithful and unbuffered.
5. Loopback egress from the codex sandbox to the shim is already proven: the Q1 spike ran codex exec against 127.0.0.1:11434 successfully.
6. Auth headers from LocalConfig (api_key_env) are attached by the shim on the upstream leg only; codex-to-shim stays unauthenticated on loopback.

## Compatibility constraints

Backends claude, codex, and grok are untouched: the shim starts only under backend local with CodeGraph configured, so every existing argv and grind test stays green. LocalConfig parsing and the FR-006/FR-007 probes keep talking to the real server directly (probes bypass the shim). The recorded serving contract (README, serving_hint()) is unchanged — the shim is invisible to the operator.

## Ordered steps

1. Write mcp_shim.py: request rewriter (tools[] flattening), response rewriter (name restore for SSE and non-streaming), loopback forwarder with ephemeral port, start/stop API.
2. Wire LocalRunner.run(): start the shim when codegraph is configured, point the provider base_url override at it, tear down in finally.
3. Update the LocalRunner argv tests for the swapped base_url; add tests/test_mcp_shim.py against a fake upstream asserting flattening, restoration (streaming and non-streaming), passthrough, and teardown.
4. Run the targeted tests.

## Dependencies

Decision input: bd memories local-backend-mcp and local-backend-mcp-decision (ortus-d333.13). Code consumers: make_runner and the grind launch path that constructs LocalRunner. The docs leaf ortus-d333.10 should land after this so the serving contract documents working CodeGraph composition.

## Edge cases

A request with no namespace tools passes through byte-identical (assert in tests). Multiple namespace entries flatten independently; a name collision between a flattened name and a pre-existing flat tool is left to codex (both are forwarded; log a warning). Upstream connection refused surfaces to codex as the same connection error it would see today (the shim does not mask outages, so grind preflight remains the failure authority). Worker killed mid-stream: the finally teardown closes the listener without leaking the thread.

## Plan-gap guidance

If codex 0.147.x routing rejects the restored namespace+name shape produced by the response rewriter (the split the codex router resolves on differs from the captured request shape), stop and record PLAN-GAP with the captured event JSON instead of guessing at alternate name spellings.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1 (proves-new): a request whose tools[] carries a namespace entry reaches the fake upstream with flat function tools named <namespace>__<tool>.
- AC-2 (proves-new): a function_call item returned flat is restored to the namespace shape on both streaming and non-streaming paths.
- AC-3 (proves-new): LocalRunner argv points the provider base_url at the shim when CodeGraph is configured, and at LocalConfig.base_url when it is not.
- AC-4 (guards-existing): requests without namespace tools pass through byte-identical, and the full existing local-backend and agent test files stay green.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_mcp_shim.py -k "flattens_namespace_tools" -q`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_mcp_shim.py -k "restores_function_call_names" -q`
- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_agent.py -k "local_runner_base_url_targets_shim" -q`
- AC-4: `uv run pytest tests/test_mcp_shim.py tests/test_core_agent.py tests/test_local_backend.py -q`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_mcp_shim.py tests/test_core_agent.py tests/test_local_backend.py -q`
