title: local backend: decide the MCP composition path (shim, Ollama upgrade, or documented limitation)
description:
## Objective
Choose how the local backend composes CodeGraph MCP tools with codex exec against an OpenAI-compatible server, now that ortus-d333.12 has shown codex 0.147.0 emits every MCP server as a Responses namespace tool with no flag, provider key, or model-catalog field that flattens it.

## Behavioral context
Before. bd memory local-backend-mcp records MCP_BROKEN codex-namespace-unconditional: the namespace spec is built unconditionally in the codex MCP handler, a provider without the namespace capability drops the tools instead of flattening them, Ollama 0.23.0 returns function_call name "" for a namespace call, and Ollama 0.33.0 and later expand namespaces but return a dotted name without the namespace field the codex router resolves on. The LocalRunner leaf cannot compose CodeGraph until a path is chosen. After. Exactly one path is recorded under bd memory local-backend-mcp-decision as SHIM, OLLAMA_UPGRADE, or LIMITATION with the reasoning, and the implementation leaf for that path is filed under ortus-d333.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Operator decision only. The three candidate paths and what each needs:
1. SHIM: an in-process request and response rewriter between codex and the server. Request side flattens each namespace entry in tools[] into plain functions named <namespace>__<tool> (Ollama 0.23.0 returns that name correctly). Response side splits the returned name back into namespace plus name on function_call items in response.output_item.added and response.output_item.done of the SSE stream. Both directions, running with grind; ortus-d333.12 decision 2 caps it at a few dozen lines.
2. OLLAMA_UPGRADE: Ollama commit 35f71382 (PR 17593, first shipped in v0.33.0, latest v0.33.2) expands namespace declarations into flat chat tools named <namespace>.<tool>, but its output function_call carries only name, so codex build_tool_call would resolve functions/mcp__codegraph.codegraph_explore and miss the registry key. Needs a live run of the Q1 run-2 argv on the upgraded host and very likely still the response-side split.
3. LIMITATION: document that CodeGraph MCP composition is unsupported on the local backend and make LocalRunner degrade the CodeGraph policy explicitly (required becomes a printed, fail-fast refusal or an explicit off) so grind never launches a worker that loops on nameless calls.

## Non-goals
No code in this bead. Do not patch codex or Ollama source. Do not change the claude, codex, or grok argv or defaults. Do not record the operator Linux username or any downstream project name in the decision memory, comments, or follow-up beads.

## Concrete locations
- bd memory local-backend-mcp: the finding, the probe method, and artifact paths.
- bd memory local-backend-q1: the original mechanism and the Q1 argv.
- src/ortus/core/agent.py: LocalRunner and CodexRunner.build_argv, where a shim or a policy degrade would attach in the follow-up leaf.
- src/ortus/core/codegraph.py: CodeGraphAdapter.probe, where the policy fallback would be resolved.
- $TMPDIR/local-mcp (worker sandbox, ephemeral): fake.py, probe.sh, summarize.py, runs/<label>/req-1.json, replay-*.sse.

## Resolved decisions
1. Provider id ortus_local and wire_api responses stay whatever the path.
2. The decision is stored as a bd memory token so the implementation leaf reads it instead of re-deriving the evidence.
3. Whatever the path, ortus check and the grind preflight must fail fast with the serving command rather than launch a worker that hangs (epic success criterion).

## Compatibility constraints
Linux and macOS. Existing backends stay byte-identical. No repository writes from this bead.

## Ordered steps
1. Read bd memories local-backend-mcp and local-backend-q1.
2. Pick one path. If OLLAMA_UPGRADE, upgrade the host service first and rerun the Q1 run-2 argv live before committing to it.
3. bd remember --key local-backend-mcp-decision "<SHIM|OLLAMA_UPGRADE|LIMITATION> <reasoning>".
4. File the implementation leaf under ortus-d333, then remove the human label from this bead and close it.

## Dependencies
Depends on ortus-d333.12 (the finding). Blocks ortus-d333.10, whose serving-contract text must state the MCP composition status. Informs ortus-d333.9.

## Edge cases
A newer codex release that adds a flattening switch or a namespace-less provider path changes the answer; re-check codex features list and the provider capabilities before deciding. If the host Ollama is upgraded and the live run completes with a routed codegraph_explore call, the decision is OLLAMA_UPGRADE with the minimum version recorded.

## Plan-gap guidance
This bead is the operator interview; a worker must not pick a path. If the operator wants evidence a worker can produce, such as a shim prototype or a live run on a newer Ollama, file that as a separate probe leaf rather than doing it here.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1 (proves-new): bd memory local-backend-mcp-decision exists and starts with SHIM, OLLAMA_UPGRADE, or LIMITATION. `bd memories local-backend-mcp-decision`
- AC-2 (guards-existing): bd memory local-backend-mcp is untouched and still starts with MCP_BROKEN. `bd memories local-backend-mcp`

## Targeted tests
None. The decision is recorded in bd memory; no repository code change.

Implementation leaf filed as ortus-d333.14; docs leaf ortus-d333.10 now depends on it. OLLAMA_UPGRADE rejected (operator runs llama.cpp; response-side split needed regardless); LIMITATION rejected (shim provably works and this repo pins codegraph=required).

title: local backend: flatten codex MCP namespace tools for OpenAI-compatible servers
description:
## Objective
Make CodeGraph MCP tool calls work when codex exec drives a local OpenAI-compatible server, by finding or building the seam that presents MCP tools as plain function tools instead of Responses namespace tools.

## Behavioral context
Before. codex 0.147.0 sends each MCP server as one Responses tool of type namespace (name mcp__codegraph, nested tools). Ollama 0.23.0 /v1/responses renders that entry as a nameless function, drops the nested tools, and returns the model's call with an empty name; codex logs unsupported call and the turn loops until the worker timeout. Plain runs without MCP overrides complete normally. After. A codex exec run against the local provider with the CodeGraph overrides completes one codegraph_explore call and reaches turn.completed, or the epic records that MCP composition is unsupported on this server and the local backend degrades CodeGraph policy explicitly.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Test the candidate seams in order: a codex config or model-catalog switch that emits plain function tools (model_catalog_json with tool_mode, any flag in codex features list that mentions MCP tools), a newer Ollama or a llama-server that accepts namespace tools, and finally a minimal request-rewriting shim. Record the working seam in bd memory local-backend-mcp and leave the LocalRunner leaf to wire it.

## Non-goals
Do not edit CodexRunner.build_argv or add the local backend here. Do not patch Ollama or codex source. Do not change the Claude or Grok backends. Do not audition the 27B reference model.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/core/agent.py` — `CodexRunner.build_argv()` emits the three mcp_servers.codegraph overrides; the seam must sit before or beside it, not inside it.
- `src/ortus/core/codegraph.py` — `CodeGraphAdapter.probe()` builds the `CodeGraphCapability` the overrides come from.
- bd memory `local-backend-q1` — the captured mechanism, argv, and artifact paths.
- `codex features list` and `~/.codex/models_cache.json` — the flag inventory and the model metadata field set (tool_mode, use_responses_lite).

## Resolved decisions
1. Provider id stays ortus_local; wire_api stays responses.
2. A seam that requires patching codex or Ollama source is out of scope; a request-rewriting shim is acceptable only if it is a few dozen lines and runs in-process with grind.
3. If no seam works, the outcome is a documented limitation plus a CodeGraph policy fallback decision for the LocalRunner leaf, not an improvised workaround.

## Compatibility constraints
Linux and macOS. Existing claude, codex, and grok argv stay byte-identical. No repository writes during probing beyond bd memories and comments.

## Ordered steps
1. Replay the captured codex request body from the Q1 artifacts to /v1/responses to confirm the empty-name result still holds on the installed Ollama.
2. Try codex-side switches: a model_catalog_json entry for qwen3:4b with tool_mode direct, and any feature flag whose description mentions MCP tools; rerun the CodeGraph probe after each.
3. If codex cannot flatten, check whether an installed llama-server or a newer Ollama accepts namespace tools with the same replay.
4. If neither, prototype the shim and rerun the probe through it.
5. Record the outcome under bd memory local-backend-mcp and comment this issue with argv and artifact paths.

## Dependencies
Depends on ortus-d333.1 (the finding). Blocks the LocalRunner leaf's CodeGraph probe path. No code callers change here.

## Edge cases
Ollama not running or qwen3:4b missing: stop, flag human. A seam that works only with tool_choice forced is not a pass. A model that narrates instead of calling the tool is a model defect, not a seam failure; note it and keep the seam.

## Plan-gap guidance
If codex 0.147.0 emits namespace tools unconditionally and no config touches it, record PLAN-GAP with the evidence and stop; the choice between shim, server upgrade, and documented limitation belongs to the operator.

title: local backend: grind preflight aborts before claiming when the local server is down
description:
## Objective
Before `ortus grind --backend local` claims any issue, prove the local server is reachable and serves the configured model; otherwise abort at scheduler level with the serving command, so no claim is burned on a worker that cannot start.

## Behavioral context
Before. With `--backend local` grind would resolve the backend, probe CodeGraph, pass the sandbox smoke test, claim an issue, and spawn `codex exec` against a dead endpoint; the window would fail or hang and the claim would need manual recovery. After. Right after the sandbox smoke test, grind runs `probe_models`; on failure it prints `local backend: <error>` with the remediation hint and exits 1 with nothing claimed; on success it logs `local server reachable: <display>` and proceeds. `--dry-run` prints a `local:` line with host and model. Other backends never run the probe.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`grind.py`: load `LocalConfig` inside the existing resolve/config `try`, run the probe after `sandbox.smoke_test()`, dry-run line, `--backend` help text. One new test module.

## Non-goals
No retry or wait-for-server loop (the server is operator-managed). No tool-calling probe here (check owns the expensive probe; grind runs the cheap `/models` subset only). No changes to claim, verify, or finalize. No worker-timeout default change.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py`: `grind()` at line 843; the `try` at lines 947-971 (`resolve_backend`, `load_config`, profiles); `sandbox.smoke_test()` at line 1071; dry-run block at lines 1017-1035; `--backend` option help at lines 930-936; start line at 1091 (`backend={resolved_backend}` — unchanged, `local` matches the dashboard regex).
- `src/ortus/core/local_backend.py`: `load_local_config`, `probe_models`, `LocalServerError`, `LocalConfig.display`.
- `tests/test_grind.py` lines 220-260: the `_bd_repo`, `_fake_sandbox`, `NeverRuns`, and `_make_runner` monkeypatch pattern to mirror.
- New `tests/test_grind_local_preflight.py`.

## Resolved decisions
1. Inside the existing `try` (after `load_config`): `local_config = load_local_config(config) if resolved_backend == "local" else None`; a `ProfileError` there already routes to `output.error` and exit 1.
2. After the `sandbox.smoke_test()` block and only when `not dry_run` and `local_config is not None`: call `probe_models(local_config)` (imported by name into `grind.py` so tests can patch `grind_mod.probe_models`). On `LocalServerError` call `output.error(f"local backend: {exc}", hint=exc.remediation)` and `raise typer.Exit(code=1)`. On success `output.progress("grind", f"local server reachable: {local_config.display}")`.
3. Dry-run: after the `backend:` line print `output.info(f"local:          {local_config.display}")` when local.
4. `--backend` help becomes `claude, codex, grok, or local; overrides ORTUS_BACKEND and .ortusrc ('all' is an init provisioning option, not a run backend).`
5. The probe runs before the flock and before any bd read, so a failed preflight leaves the tracker untouched.
6. The runner at line 1301 is built with `_make_runner(resolved_backend, repo=target)` (from the runner leaf); nothing else in the loop changes.

## Compatibility constraints
Claude, codex, and grok runs never call the probe (guard test). Exit code 1 on preflight failure matches the sandbox and CodeGraph abort paths. Linux and macOS.

## Ordered steps
1. Import `load_local_config`, `probe_models`, `LocalServerError` into `grind.py`.
2. Load `local_config` in the resolve `try`.
3. Add the probe after the sandbox smoke test with the error and progress lines.
4. Add the dry-run line and widen the help text.
5. Write `tests/test_grind_local_preflight.py` per the criteria and run it.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the runner leaf and the probes leaf. Callers: `cli.py` registers `grind`. Related: the check leaf shares the probe and its messages.

## Edge cases
`--backend local` with no `[local]` table exits 1 naming `local.model` before any probe. A server that is up but does not list the model aborts with the served ids. `--dry-run` never contacts the server. The probe runs once per grind invocation, not per iteration; a server dying mid-run surfaces as a failed window, which is out of scope here.

## Plan-gap guidance
If the sandbox smoke-test block cannot be followed by the probe without reordering the flock acquisition, record `PLAN-GAP` naming the lines rather than probing after the claim.

title: local backend: ortus check --backend local reports config, endpoint, tools, and context
description:
## Objective
Make `ortus check --backend local` tell the truth before a grind window is spent: codex binary, `[local]` config, server reachable with the configured model served, tool calling enabled, advertised context size, and CodeGraph via the codex injection path.

## Behavioral context
Before. `ortus check --backend local` exits with `unsupported check backend 'local'` from `_run_all`. After. The table shows the codex binary row, `.codex/config.toml`, then four local rows (`[local]`, `local endpoint`, `local tools`, `local context`), then the usual repo rows; a down server, a missing model, or a template without tools each FAIL with the exact remediation; a small context WARNs but never fails; a repo that provisions `[local]` but runs another backend gets an informational `local (provisioned)` row that never touches the network.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`check.py`: `_run_all` local branch, `check_local_rows`, `check_codegraph` local path, `check_provisioned_backend` binary mapping and local discovery, `--backend` help text. Tests in `tests/test_check.py` with monkeypatched probes.

## Non-goals
No grind or init changes. No server lifecycle. No new probe logic: the rows call the probe module and render its errors. `check` stays read-only and spawns no agent.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/commands/check.py`: `_run_all()` (line 581) backend dispatch; `check_codegraph()` (308) `if backend == "codex":` at line 341; `check_provisioned_backend()` (540) `shutil.which(backend)`; the provisioned loop at line 638 (`(repo / BACKEND_TEMPLATES[other]).parent.is_dir()`); `check()` option help at line 655.
- `src/ortus/core/local_backend.py`: `load_local_config`, `probe_models`, `probe_tool_calling`, `probe_context_size`, `LocalServerError`, `MIN_RECOMMENDED_CONTEXT`.
- `src/ortus/core/agent.py`: `BACKEND_BINARIES`.
- `src/ortus/core/config.py`: `read_recorded_local` (provisioning discovery).
- `tests/test_check.py`: `_healthy_repo`, `_all_binaries_present`, `_fake_sandbox_ok` helpers; `test_check_help_lists_grok_backend` as the help pattern; `test_provisioned_backend_rows_are_informational`.

## Resolved decisions
1. `_run_all`: `elif backend == "local": backend_binary = check_codex; settings_check = check_codex_settings; settings_label = ".codex/config.toml"`, and `repo_checks` gets `(check_local_rows, "[local]")` inserted directly after the `(settings_check, settings_label)` entry so the table order is codex binary, codex config, local rows, then the shared repo rows and the codegraph row.
2. `check_local_rows(repo) -> list[CheckResult]` returns exactly four rows named `[local]`, `local endpoint`, `local tools`, `local context`. It loads config via `load_config` + `load_local_config`; on `ProfileError` the first row FAILs with that text and the other three FAIL with `skipped: [local] config invalid`. When `api_key_env` is set but absent from `os.environ`, the `[local]` row FAILs with `api_key_env=<NAME> is not set in the environment — export it or drop the key`. The `[local]` PASS message is `base_url=<url> model=<model> key=<NAME|none>`.
3. `local endpoint`: `probe_models`; FAIL message is the error text plus ` — ` plus the first line of its remediation; PASS is `reachable; model <model> served`. When it fails, `local tools` and `local context` report `skipped: endpoint failed` (FAIL and WARN respectively).
4. `local tools`: `probe_tool_calling`; PASS `function call returned`; FAIL text as above.
5. `local context` is `level="info"`: `n_ctx` None → ok True `context size not exposed by this server`; below `MIN_RECOMMENDED_CONTEXT` → ok False `n_ctx=<n> below the recommended 32768 — restart with --ctx-size 32768`; otherwise ok True `n_ctx=<n>`.
6. `check_codegraph`: `if backend in ("codex", "local"):` — CodeGraph is injected per child for local exactly as for codex.
7. `check_provisioned_backend`: replace `shutil.which(backend)` with `shutil.which(BACKEND_BINARIES[backend])`; for `local` the gaps are `.codex/config.toml` missing, codex CLI missing, and `[local]` table missing or invalid (`read_recorded_local(repo)` empty or `load_local_config` failing) with remediation `run ortus init --backend local --local-model <id>`; it never probes the network and its message says so: `provisioned; endpoint not probed — run ortus check --backend local`.
8. Provisioned-row discovery in the `_run_all` loop: extract `backend_provisioned(repo, backend) -> bool` returning `bool(read_recorded_local(repo))` for `local` and the existing config-dir test otherwise.
9. Help text: `Agent backend to verify (claude|codex|grok|local); defaults from .ortusrc.`
10. Tests monkeypatch `check_mod.probe_models`, `check_mod.probe_tool_calling`, `check_mod.probe_context_size` (import them into `check.py` by name so the seams exist); no fake HTTP server in this file.

## Compatibility constraints
Exit code semantics unchanged: strict rows drive it, info rows only WARN. Claude/codex/grok tables are byte-identical (assert in a guard test that a codex repo has no `local` rows). `check` performs no writes.

## Ordered steps
1. Import the probe seams and `BACKEND_BINARIES`; add the `_run_all` local branch and `check_local_rows`.
2. Update `check_codegraph`, `check_provisioned_backend`, and the discovery helper.
3. Widen the help text.
4. Write the tests listed in the criteria, using `_healthy_repo` plus a `[local]` table written into the repo `.ortusrc`.
5. Run the targeted tests.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the runner leaf (`BACKEND_BINARIES`, `local` in `BACKENDS`) and the probes leaf. Callers: `cli.py` registers `check`; `init` documentation points operators at `ortus check --backend local`.

## Edge cases
`--backend local` on a repo with no `.codex/config.toml` FAILs that row with the existing `missing at` message. `[local]` present but the run backend is claude → informational row only. `api_key_env` set and exported → the `[local]` row shows the name, never the value. `local context` on Ollama → PASS `not exposed`.

## Plan-gap guidance
If ordering the local rows after the settings row would require restructuring `_run_all` beyond inserting into `repo_checks`, record `PLAN-GAP` rather than appending them after the codegraph row; the order is the spec.
acceptance_criteria:

- AC-2 (proves-new): a healthy local repo with all three probes patched green exits 0 and shows the four local rows in order after `.codex/config.toml`.
- AC-3 (proves-new): a refused endpoint FAILs `local endpoint` with `llama-server` and `--jinja` in the message and exits 1.

title: local backend: endpoint, model, tool-calling, and context probes with a fake server
description:
## Objective
Provide the four HTTP probes that check and grind share — served models, configured model present, tool calling works, advertised context size — each failing with a distinct message that carries the exact serving command.

## Behavioral context
Before. Nothing in Ortus can tell whether a local server is up, serves the configured model, or has tool calling enabled; the first place a mis-served model would surface is a hung grind window. After. `probe_models`, `probe_tool_calling`, and `probe_context_size` in `local_backend.py` answer those questions in seconds, raising `LocalServerError` with a `kind` and a `remediation` string; a hermetic fake HTTP server exercises every branch in tests.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Probe functions, `LocalServerError`, `serving_hint`, and a `ThreadingHTTPServer` test fixture with canned routes. Stdlib `urllib.request` only.

## Non-goals
No check rows or grind wiring (next leaves). No server lifecycle (start/stop). No streaming. No retries beyond a single request per probe. No `chat/completions` path: codex 0.147.0 uses the Responses API only, so the tool probe must hit the endpoint the harness will use.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/core/local_backend.py`: add `class LocalServerError(RuntimeError)` with attributes `kind` (one of `unreachable`, `model-missing`, `tools-unsupported`, `auth-demanded`) and `remediation`; `serving_hint(config: LocalConfig) -> str`; `probe_models(config, *, timeout: float = 5.0) -> tuple[str, ...]`; `probe_tool_calling(config, *, timeout: float = 120.0) -> None`; `probe_context_size(config, *, timeout: float = 5.0) -> int | None`; private `_request_json(method, url, *, body=None, headers=None, timeout)`.
- `tests/test_core_local_backend.py`: `fake_server` fixture built on `http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer` bound to `127.0.0.1:0`, with a per-test route table.
- Reference for message style: `src/ortus/core/sandbox.py` `smoke_test()` (multi-line remediation text).

## Resolved decisions
1. `probe_models`: `GET {base_url}/models`; connection error, timeout, or non-2xx → `LocalServerError(kind="unreachable")` whose message is `local server unreachable at {base_url}: {reason}` and whose remediation is `serving_hint(config)`. On success return the `data[*].id` tuple; when `config.model` is absent raise `kind="model-missing"` with message `model {model!r} is not served; served: a, b, c` and remediation `set local.model to a served id or load the model`.
2. `probe_tool_calling`: `POST {base_url}/responses` with body `{"model": model, "input": "Call the ortus_ping tool once.", "tools": [{"type": "function", "name": "ortus_ping", "description": "Readiness probe.", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}, "additionalProperties": false}}], "tool_choice": "required", "max_output_tokens": 64, "stream": false}`. Success = HTTP 2xx and an item in `output` with `type == "function_call"` and `name == "ortus_ping"`. HTTP 401 or 403 → `kind="auth-demanded"` with remediation naming `local.api_key_env`. HTTP 400/404/422/500 whose body mentions `tool`, `template`, or `jinja`, or HTTP 2xx without a function_call item → `kind="tools-unsupported"` with message `server answered without calling the tool` and remediation `restart llama-server with --jinja (and a tool-capable chat template)`. Connection failure → `unreachable`.
3. `probe_context_size`: `GET {config.origin}/props` (llama-server; origin strips `/v1`); on 2xx return `default_generation_settings.n_ctx` as int when present; on 404, connection error, timeout, or missing key return `None` (Ollama and vLLM do not expose it). Never raises.
4. Authorization: when `config.api_key_env` is set and the variable is present in `os.environ`, every probe sends `Authorization: Bearer <value>`; the value is read at call time and never logged or included in any exception text.
5. `serving_hint` returns the reference llama-server command for the configured base_url port: `llama-server -hf <repo>:<quant> --alias <model> --jinja --ctx-size 32768 --flash-attn on --host 127.0.0.1 --port <port>` with a second line for Ollama (`ollama serve` plus `ollama pull <model>`, base_url `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`).
6. `_request_json` uses `urllib.request.urlopen` with `Content-Type: application/json`, decodes JSON, and maps `urllib.error.HTTPError` to a `(status, body_text)` pair for the callers; `socket.timeout` and `URLError` become `unreachable`.

## Compatibility constraints
No new runtime dependency (pyproject stays typer, rich, textual, jinja2, tomli, portalocker). Tests bind 127.0.0.1 only and finish under the 5s hermetic budget (fake server responds immediately; probe timeouts in tests are 1s). Linux and macOS.

## Ordered steps
1. Add `LocalServerError`, `serving_hint`, and `_request_json`.
2. Implement `probe_models`, `probe_tool_calling`, `probe_context_size` per decisions 1-3.
3. Build the `fake_server` fixture with a route table (`(method, path) -> (status, json)`), recording received headers and bodies.
4. Write the tests listed in the criteria.
5. Run the targeted tests.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the `[local]` config leaf (`LocalConfig`). Consumers: `check.py` local rows and `grind.py` preflight (next leaves), the live e2e test.

## Edge cases
Server up but `/models` returns an empty `data` list → `model-missing` listing none. `/responses` returning a `function_call` with a different name → `tools-unsupported`. `/props` returning `n_ctx` as a string → coerced to int, non-numeric → None. `base_url` ending in `/v1/` (normalised earlier) still hits `/v1/models`. A 2xx `/models` body that is not JSON → `unreachable` with reason `unparseable JSON`. `api_key_env` set but the variable absent → no header sent (check reports that separately).

## Plan-gap guidance
If the Responses API on the reference servers rejects `tool_choice: "required"` outright (the Q1 artifact will show the server's shape), record `PLAN-GAP` with the response body rather than silently downgrading the probe to `auto` and treating narration as success.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1 (proves-new): `probe_models` returns the served ids from a fake `/models` route.
- AC-2 (proves-new): a refused connection raises `unreachable` whose remediation contains `llama-server` and `--jinja`.
- AC-3 (proves-new): a served list without the configured model raises `model-missing` listing the served ids.
- AC-4 (proves-new): a fake `/responses` returning a `function_call` item named `ortus_ping` passes; a text-only answer raises `tools-unsupported`; HTTP 401 raises `auth-demanded`.
- AC-5 (proves-new): `probe_context_size` reads `n_ctx` from `/props` and returns None on 404.
- AC-6 (proves-new): with `api_key_env` set and exported, the fake server sees a Bearer header whose value never appears in any exception text.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: uv run pytest tests/test_core_local_backend.py -k probe_models_lists_served_ids -q
- AC-2: uv run pytest tests/test_core_local_backend.py -k probe_models_unreachable_names_serving_command -q
- AC-3: uv run pytest tests/test_core_local_backend.py -k probe_models_missing_model_lists_served -q
- AC-4: uv run pytest tests/test_core_local_backend.py -k "tool_calling_accepts_function_call_item or narration_is_tools_unsupported or 401_is_auth_demanded" -q
- AC-5: uv run pytest tests/test_core_local_backend.py -k "context_size_reads_props or context_size_none_when_unexposed" -q
- AC-6: uv run pytest tests/test_core_local_backend.py -k probes_send_bearer_only_from_env -q

## Targeted tests
uv run pytest tests/test_core_local_backend.py tests/test_core_config.py -n auto --test-timeout=30
notes: llama-server README (fetched 2026-09-02) documents POST /v1/responses (converted to chat completions), GET /v1/models (id = model path or --alias), GET /props with default_generation_settings.n_ctx, and tool calling behind --jinja. Ollama 0.23.0 binary serves /v1/responses and /v1/models but has no /props.

title: local backend: add LocalRunner and register local as a fourth backend
description:
## Objective
Make `backend = "local"` a legal Ortus backend whose runner is the codex argv plus `ortus_local` provider overrides read from `LocalConfig`, with the codex plain-prompt shape and the codex CodeGraph registration path.

## Behavioral context
Before. `BACKENDS` is claude, codex, grok; `make_runner("local")` is unreachable; `resolve_backend("local")` raises. After. `resolve_backend` accepts `local`; `make_runner("local", repo=...)` returns a `LocalRunner` that subclasses `CodexRunner`; its argv is the codex argv followed by `-c model_providers.ortus_local.name="ortus_local"`, `-c model_providers.ortus_local.base_url="<url>"`, `-c model_providers.ortus_local.wire_api="responses"`, optionally `-c model_providers.ortus_local.env_key="<NAME>"`, then `-c model_provider="ortus_local"`, then `-m <configured model>` unless a profile model is set. `compose_worker_prompt("local", task)` returns exactly the codex plain prompt. Claude, codex, and grok argv and prompts are byte-identical to today.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`agent.py`: `Backend`, `BACKENDS`, new `BACKEND_BINARIES`, `LocalRunner`, `make_runner(backend, *, repo=None)`, `compose_worker_prompt` test pin. `codegraph.py`: `CodeGraphAdapter.probe` takes the codex branch for `local`. Thread `repo=` through the three `_make_runner` seams in `grind.py`, `plan.py`, `interview.py`. Unit tests.

## Non-goals
No check/init/grind preflight rows (later leaves). No help-string widening outside `agent.py` (later leaf). No new event decoder: a local log is a codex log. No `--oss`. No `requires_openai_auth` override unless the Q2 memory says `NEEDS_EXPLICIT_FLAG`.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/core/agent.py`: `Backend` (line 27), `BACKENDS` (28), `CodexRunner.__init__`/`build_argv` (40-110), `resolve_backend()` (254), `make_runner()` (272), `compose_worker_prompt()` (280). Add `BACKEND_BINARIES: dict[Backend, str] = {"claude": "claude", "codex": "codex", "grok": "grok", "local": "codex"}` and `class LocalRunner(CodexRunner)`.
- `src/ortus/core/local_backend.py`: `LocalConfig`, `load_local_config`, `LOCAL_PROVIDER_ID`, `LOCAL_WIRE_API` (from the config leaf).
- `src/ortus/core/codegraph.py`: `CodeGraphAdapter.probe()` line 150 `if backend == "codex":` becomes `if backend in ("codex", "local"):`.
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` line 104 `_make_runner(backend="claude")` and line 1301-1303 call; `src/ortus/commands/plan.py` line 42 and lines 79/99; `src/ortus/commands/interview.py` line 23 and line 89.
- `tests/test_core_agent.py`, `tests/test_agent.py`, `tests/test_core_codegraph.py`.

## Resolved decisions
1. `LocalRunner(CodexRunner)` with `__init__(self, local: LocalConfig, codex_binary: str = "codex", *, extra_env=None, codegraph=None, sandbox_mode="workspace-write")`; stores `self.local`. Subclassing is right here because the argv IS codex argv plus overrides; the Grok objection (foreign flag surface) does not apply.
2. `build_argv` calls `super().build_argv(...)` then appends, in this order, `-c` pairs for `model_providers.ortus_local.name`, `.base_url`, `.wire_api`, `.env_key` (only when `api_key_env` is set), then `-c model_provider=...`, then `-m <local.model>` only when `profile is None or profile.model is None`. Every value is rendered with `json.dumps` exactly like the CodeGraph block, so strings are TOML-quoted. The profile model, when set, wins; the argv then carries the profile `-m` from the superclass and no second `-m`.
3. `env_key` carries the variable NAME; codex reads the value at launch. No key material ever enters argv, `extra_env`, or logs.
4. Read bd memories `local-backend-q1` and `local-backend-q2` first. `PROVIDER_BROKEN` or `LOGIN_REQUIRED` is a plan gap. `NEEDS_EXPLICIT_FLAG` adds `-c model_providers.ortus_local.requires_openai_auth=false` after the `wire_api` pair. `NO_AUTH_NEEDED` adds nothing.
5. `make_runner(backend, *, repo: Path | None = None)`: for `local`, `load_local_config(load_config(repo=repo))`; a `ProfileError` is re-raised as `BackendError` with the same text so existing `except BackendError` sites report it. Other backends ignore `repo`.
6. The three command seams become `_make_runner(backend: str = "claude", *, repo: Path | None = None)` and the non-claude call sites pass `repo=target` (grind, interview) or `repo=repo` (plan). Zero-argument `_make_runner()` for claude is untouched, so test lambdas that take no arguments keep working.
7. `compose_worker_prompt` keeps its structure; `local` falls into the codex branch and a test pins `compose_worker_prompt("local", t) == compose_worker_prompt("codex", t)`.
8. `_readonly_argv` and `preflight_readonly` are inherited from `CodexRunner` unchanged (`--sandbox read-only`, no bwrap wrap).

## Compatibility constraints
`BACKENDS` order stays claude, codex, grok, local so `resolve_backend`'s error text lists them in that order. `make_runner("claude"|"codex"|"grok")` return types and argv are unchanged. Linux and macOS.

## Ordered steps
1. Confirm both spike memories exist with legal tokens; stop on plan gap otherwise.
2. Extend `Backend`, `BACKENDS`, add `BACKEND_BINARIES`.
3. Implement `LocalRunner.__init__` and `build_argv`.
4. Extend `make_runner` with `repo=` and the `local` branch.
5. Update `CodeGraphAdapter.probe`.
6. Thread `repo=` through the grind, plan, and interview seams.
7. Write the tests listed in the criteria and run them.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the Q1/Q2 spike and the `[local]` config leaf. Callers: `grind._make_runner`, `plan._make_runner`, `interview._make_runner`, `check` (later leaf) and `CodeGraphAdapter.probe`. Tests that patch `_make_runner` with `lambda: ...` (tests/test_grind.py, tests/test_interview.py) rely on decision 6.

## Edge cases
`make_runner("local")` with no `[local]` table raises `BackendError` naming `local.model`. `api_key_env` unset in the environment is not checked here (check does that). A profile with `reasoning_effort` yields the inherited `-c model_reasoning_effort=...` pair before the provider pairs. `readonly=True` yields `--sandbox read-only` with the provider pairs still present.

## Plan-gap guidance
If either spike memory is missing, `PROVIDER_BROKEN`, or `LOGIN_REQUIRED`, stop and record `PLAN-GAP` on this issue; do not default to `--oss`, a proxy, or a Claude wrap. If `codegraph.py` needs a fourth branch rather than joining the codex branch (e.g. capability injection fails for local), record the reason as `PLAN-GAP` instead of registering CodeGraph through a user config file.

title: local backend: [local] config table, LocalConfig, and profile support
description:
## Objective
Give Ortus a validated `[local]` table in `.ortusrc` (`base_url`, `model`, optional `api_key_env`) exposed as an immutable `LocalConfig`, and teach the profile and config validators that `local` is a backend name.

## Behavioral context
Before. `load_config` knows nothing about a `[local]` table, `validate_profile_values("local", ...)` raises "expected claude, codex, or grok", and `INIT_ONLY_BACKEND_MESSAGE` names three backends. After. A `[local]` table loads into `LocalConfig`; a table missing `model` fails with a message naming `local.model`; `backend = "local"` pinned without a table fails the same way; `[profiles.local.<phase>]` accepts the codex effort set; every backend-list message says "claude, codex, grok, or local". Existing configs without a `[local]` table load unchanged.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
New module `src/ortus/core/local_backend.py` with constants, `LocalConfig`, and `load_local_config`. Validation hook `_validate_local` in `config.py` called from `load_config`, plus `read_recorded_local` for init. `BackendName` and `SUPPORTED_EFFORTS["local"]` in `profiles.py`. Message widening at `config.py` lines 47-50 and 165-168 and `profiles.py` line 59. Unit tests.

## Non-goals
No `LocalRunner`, no `BACKENDS` change, no HTTP probes (later leaves). No `wire_api` config key: codex 0.147.0 supports only `responses`, so it is a constant, not configuration. No secret values in config: `api_key_env` is an environment variable name only.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/core/local_backend.py` (new): `DEFAULT_LOCAL_BASE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1"`, `LOCAL_PROVIDER_ID = "ortus_local"`, `LOCAL_WIRE_API = "responses"`, `MIN_RECOMMENDED_CONTEXT = 32768`, `@dataclass(frozen=True) class LocalConfig(base_url: str, model: str, api_key_env: str | None = None)` with properties `origin` (base_url with a trailing `/v1` removed, for llama-server `/props`) and `display` (`local (<host:port>) model=<model>`; never key material), and `load_local_config(cfg: Config) -> LocalConfig`.
- `src/ortus/core/config.py`: `INIT_ONLY_BACKEND_MESSAGE`, `_validate_profiles()` message, new `_validate_local(values)` called from `load_config()` after `_validate_profiles`, new `read_recorded_local(repo: Path) -> dict[str, Any]` beside `read_recorded_facts()`.
- `src/ortus/core/profiles.py`: `BackendName`, `SUPPORTED_EFFORTS`, `validate_profile_values()` message.
- `tests/test_core_config.py`, new `tests/test_core_local_backend.py`.

## Resolved decisions
1. Table shape: `[local]` with `base_url` (string, default `DEFAULT_LOCAL_BASE_URL`, must start with `http://` or `https://`, trailing slash stripped), `model` (required non-empty string without whitespace), `api_key_env` (optional, must match `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`). Unknown keys are rejected with a message listing the three expected keys.
2. `_validate_local` raises `ProfileError` (the type `load_config` callers already catch). It accepts an absent table. It rejects a present table that is not a TOML table or that violates rule 1. When `values["backend"] == "local"` and the table is absent or lacks `model`, it raises `backend local needs a [local] table in .ortusrc with model = "<id as GET {base_url}/models reports it>"`.
3. `load_local_config(cfg)` re-applies rule 1 to `cfg.get("local")` so callers that resolve `local` from `--backend`/`ORTUS_BACKEND` without a pinned `backend` key get the same message; it returns a `LocalConfig` with the default base_url filled in.
4. `SUPPORTED_EFFORTS["local"] = frozenset({"low", "medium", "high", "xhigh"})` — a separate frozenset equal to the codex set, because the value is forwarded verbatim as codex `model_reasoning_effort` and the codex 0.147.0 reference lists `minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh`. The PRD's extra `none` is dropped: codex would receive an unknown value.
5. `local_backend.py` imports `Config`/`ProfileError` from `config.py` only inside `load_local_config` (or via TYPE_CHECKING) to avoid a circular import, since `config.py` must not import `local_backend.py` at module level except for the constants; put `DEFAULT_LOCAL_BASE_URL` in `local_backend.py` and import it lazily in `_validate_local` if needed, or duplicate nothing — a plain import of `local_backend` from `config.py` is fine as long as `local_backend.py` does not import `config` at module level.
6. `read_recorded_local(repo)` reads only the project `.ortusrc` (no layering, same rationale as `read_recorded_facts`) and returns the raw `[local]` table or `{}`.

## Compatibility constraints
Configs without `[local]` load byte-for-byte as before; `~/.ortusrc` and project layering merge the table like any other. Python 3.10+ via the existing tomllib/tomli shim. Linux and macOS.

## Ordered steps
1. Create `local_backend.py` with the constants, `LocalConfig`, `origin`, `display`, and `load_local_config`.
2. Add `_validate_local` to `config.py`, call it from `load_config`, widen `INIT_ONLY_BACKEND_MESSAGE` and the profile message.
3. Add `read_recorded_local`.
4. Add `local` to `BackendName` and `SUPPORTED_EFFORTS`; widen the `validate_profile_values` message.
5. Write the tests listed in the criteria, including a parametrised case in `test_invalid_profile_configuration_is_actionable` for `profiles.local` with an effort outside the set.
6. Run the targeted tests.

## Dependencies
No issue dependency; runs in parallel with the Q1/Q2 spike. Consumers added later: `LocalRunner` (runner leaf), the probe module, check, grind, init. Existing callers of `load_config` (`plan`, `agent.resolve_backend`, `check`, `grind`) must see no change for non-local configs.

## Edge cases
`base_url` with a trailing slash or a `/v1/` suffix normalises to no trailing slash. `model = ""` or `model = "a b"` fails naming `local.model`. `api_key_env = "OPENAI_API_KEY"` is stored as the name; its value is never read here. `[local]` in `~/.ortusrc` with `model` overridden in the project file merges to the project value. `backend = "local"` plus a valid table loads.

## Plan-gap guidance
If `load_config` cannot call `_validate_local` without a circular import that cannot be broken by a lazy import, record `PLAN-GAP` naming both modules rather than moving `LocalConfig` into `config.py`.

title: Optional local-model backend (llama.cpp / OpenAI-compatible server) for grind
description:
Add `local` as a fourth Ortus agent backend so `ortus grind` can drive the bd queue with a model the operator serves themselves (llama.cpp `llama-server` first, Ollama and vLLM through the same seam), for privacy, air-gapped work, cost, or community fine-tunes no vendor hosts.

Ortus needs an agent harness, not a model. The Codex CLI already is that harness: `codex exec` runs tools inside its own `workspace-write` sandbox, emits the `--json` stream that `runstate.py` and `ortus tail` decode, and accepts trusted `-c key=value` overrides at launch (the CodeGraph MCP block today). Codex supports custom model providers natively (`[model_providers.<id>]` with `base_url`, `wire_api`, optional `env_key`; selected with `model_provider=<id>` and `-m <model>`). So `local` is `LocalRunner(CodexRunner)`: the codex argv plus provider overrides read from a `[local]` table in `.ortusrc`. The model is data in config, never code.

Planning findings that reshape the PRD (verified 2026-09-02): codex-cli 0.147.0 rejects `wire_api = "chat"` (the binary says: set `wire_api = "responses"`; the config reference says `responses` is the only supported value and the default). The serving contract is therefore the OpenAI Responses API at `POST {base_url}/responses`, which llama-server documents (converted internally to chat completions) and the installed Ollama 0.23.0 binary serves. The provider config keys are `name` (required), `base_url` (required), `env_key`, `wire_api`, `requires_openai_auth` (default false); the reference says a provider can connect without authentication when no credential source resolves. `--oss`/`oss_provider` exists but is rejected here: it hardwires lmstudio/ollama and cannot point at an arbitrary base URL.

Children, in order:
1. Q1/Q2 spike: codex exec drives an unauthenticated local provider; stream shape and MCP composition unchanged.
2. `[local]` config table, `LocalConfig`, profile support, message widening.
3. `LocalRunner`, `BACKENDS`, `make_runner`, `compose_worker_prompt`, CodeGraph probe path.
4. Endpoint, model, tool-calling, and context probes with a hermetic fake server.
5. `ortus check --backend local` rows.
6. `ortus grind` preflight: server down aborts before a claim.
7. `ortus init --backend local` and `--backend all` provisioning.
8. Help strings, tail, and dashboard treat `local` as a codex log.
9. Live opt-in end-to-end test.
10. README and serving contract docs.
11. Q3 audition of the reference 27B model (human-run, non-blocking).

Out of scope: Ortus-managed server lifecycle (spawn/reap llama-server, VRAM checks), per-phase mixed backends, other local harnesses, Anthropic-wire proxying for Claude, Windows, any change to existing backends' argv or defaults.

## Success Criteria

- Existing claude/codex/grok argv, prompts, and defaults are byte-identical; Claude stays the default.
- `ortus grind --backend local` against a served model claims, implements, verifies, and closes an issue with the scheduler judging from bd state.
- `ortus tail` and the dashboard render local logs through the existing codex decoders, unmodified.
- With the server down, the wrong model loaded, or tool calling disabled, `ortus check --backend local` and the grind preflight fail fast with the exact serving command, never by launching a worker that hangs.
- Swapping the served model touches only `.ortusrc` and the operator's serving command.
notes: CodeGraph orientation confirmed the seam: grind -> _make_runner -> make_runner -> CodexRunner.build_argv (`-c` overrides), CodeGraphAdapter.probe(backend=) codex branch, check._run_all per-backend rows, init_render.BACKEND_TEMPLATES. Environment audited 2026-09-02: codex-cli 0.147.0, ollama 0.23.0 (no models pulled, server not running), no llama-server on PATH.
close_reason: All children closed. The local backend it delivered (codex-driven) is superseded by the opencode pivot ortus-t2kn; the codex-specific leaves (.10/.11/.17) were closed as superseded there. Its shim/config/probe machinery is scheduled for retirement in ortus-t2kn.7 once opencode-local ships.

title: readiness: unbounded full-suite commands pass validation and exceed a worker window
description:
## Objective

Readiness schema v1 rejects criterion-check and targeted-test
commands that invoke an unbounded full suite, so a worker-executed
work spec can never carry a check that cannot finish inside a worker
window.

## Behavioral context

Before. `validate_issue` checks that each criterion carries one
runnable command, but nothing inspects the command's scope. The
contract's own guidance says "do not make a full local matrix the
worker default", yet an AC like "three consecutive full-suite runs of
`pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots test`" validates as READY. Observed
2026-08-16 in the downstream repo `500`: exactly that AC (issue
fh-aqi, ~20+ minutes of suite runs) passed readiness, then killed two
consecutive worker windows until a human re-bounded it to the single
affected spec file.

After. A criterion check or targeted-test command that invokes a
whole suite with no narrowing argument — bare `pytest`/`uv run
pytest` with no path, `pnpm`/`npm`/`yarn` `test` with no file
arguments after `--`, `go test ./...`, bare `cargo test` — fails
readiness with an actionable message telling the author to bound the
check or route it to a human-run AC. Bounded commands validate
exactly as before, and `ortus spec` documents the rule.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Add an unbounded-suite detector to readiness validation: a helper
that classifies a normalized command as an unbounded suite
invocation, applied to every parsed criterion-check command and to
targeted-test commands inside `validate_issue`. Emit a shape failure
naming the offending AC and the bound requirement. Document the rule
in the generated spec output.

## Non-goals

Do not execute or time commands — this is a static pattern check, not
a sandbox. Do not inspect `bash -c` bodies or shell constructs
(opaque commands pass; the command grammar is a separate bead). Do
not change the worker prompt or grind's resume behavior (sibling
beads). Do not add per-repo configurability yet — a `.ortusrc`
override can follow if the heuristic misfires in the field.

## Concrete locations

`src/ortus/core/readiness.py`: new `_is_unbounded_suite()` helper
beside `looks_like_command()`; enforcement inside `validate_issue()`
where `parse_criterion_checks` results and `targeted_test_command()`
are evaluated; rule text in `_shape_rules()` /`spec_markdown()`.
Command parsing already normalizes via `_normalize_command()`.
Tests: `tests/test_core_readiness.py` and `tests/test_readiness.py`.

## Resolved decisions

1. Unbounded means: a recognized test runner invoked with no
   narrowing argument — `pytest`/`python -m pytest`/`uv run pytest`
   with no path or `-k` argument; `pnpm|npm|yarn` `test` (including
   `-r` and `--filter <pkg>` forms) with nothing after `--`;
   `go test ./...`; bare `cargo test` with no filter string.
2. Detection is a failure, not a warning — readiness is binary and a
   warning would repeat the advisory-gate mistake fixed in
   ortus-ts3z. The escape hatch for a legitimately-needed full run is
   explicit: a human-run AC or a bounded proxy, as the failure
   message states.
3. Commands the detector cannot classify (unknown runners, `bash
   -c`, `make`) are accepted unchanged — false negatives are
   preferred over false positives that block queues.
4. The failure message names the AC id and reads: "unbounded suite
   command; bound it to specific files/tests or move the full run to
   a human-run criterion".

## Compatibility constraints

Existing bounded specs must validate byte-identically — every spec in
this repo's own tracker uses path-bounded pytest commands and must
stay READY. The detector runs at both authoring surfaces
(`ortus plan` repair and grind's claim-time gate) purely through
`validate_issue`, so no caller changes are needed.

## Ordered steps

1. Implement `_is_unbounded_suite()` with the recognized-runner
   patterns from resolved decision 1.
2. Apply it in `validate_issue()` to parsed criterion-check commands
   and the targeted-test command, emitting the shape failure.
3. Add the rule to `_shape_rules()` so `ortus spec` teaches it.
4. Add positive and negative tests to `tests/test_core_readiness.py`;
   verify existing readiness tests still pass.

## Dependencies

None — sibling beads (goal-prompt background rule, grind escalation
counter) layer the same field incident independently. Callers of
`validate_issue`: grind's readiness gate, `ortus plan`, and the
repair prompt.

## Edge cases

`pytest tests/` has a path — bounded, accepted. `pytest -k name` is
bounded by the filter. `pnpm --filter x test -- test/file.spec.ts`
is bounded. `uv run pytest` with only flags (`-q`) is unbounded.
Repeat-run wrappers (`bash -c 'for ...'`) are opaque — accepted, by
resolved decision 3. A spec whose only check is unbounded fails with
one failure per offending AC, deduped per section like other shape
failures.

## Plan-gap guidance

If bounding cannot be decided statically for a mainstream runner
form (ambiguous grammar where the same token is both filter and
subcommand), stop and record PLAN-GAP listing the form, rather than
shipping a detector that misclassifies bounded commands as failures.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1 (proves-new): a criterion check carrying a bare full-suite
  command (for example `pnpm --filter pkg test` with no file
  arguments) fails readiness with the unbounded-suite message.
- AC-2 (proves-new): bounded commands (path, `-k`, or post-`--` file
  arguments) still validate as READY.
- AC-3 (proves-new): `ortus spec` output documents the bound
  requirement.
- AC-4 (guards-existing): the existing readiness suite passes
  unchanged.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_readiness.py -k unbounded_suite_command_fails -q`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_readiness.py -k bounded_commands_stay_ready -q`
- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_readiness.py -k spec_documents_bound_rule -q`
- AC-4: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_readiness.py tests/test_readiness.py -q`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_core_readiness.py tests/test_readiness.py -q`

title: grind: wedged leftover claim is resumed forever with no escalation counter
description:
## Objective

Grind escalates a wedged leftover claim to the human queue after
repeated no-close windows instead of resuming it forever, so a defect
that kills every worker window stops consuming workers.

## Behavioral context

Before. A session that resumes a leftover `in_progress` claim and
sees the worker exit without closing prints "left <id> in_progress
for the next window", breaks, and tells the operator to run
`ortus grind` again — unconditionally, with no memory of how many
windows the same claim has already burned. Observed 2026-08-16 in the
downstream repo `500`: issue fh-aqi carried an acceptance check that
cannot finish inside a worker window; two consecutive workers died on
it identically, and each grind session ended "0 landed" with the same
"run grind again" hint until a human repaired the spec.

After. Grind counts consecutive resumed windows in which the claim
stayed `in_progress` and HEAD did not advance. At the threshold it
labels the issue `human`, comments a diagnostic naming the burned
windows, and stops resuming it — matching how the readiness gate
already routes unworkable specs to operators. A window that advances
HEAD resets the counter.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Track no-close windows per claim across grind invocations, persisted
in bd (a structured grind comment on the claimed issue). On resume,
read the count; when a resumed window ends with the claim still
`in_progress` and no new commits on the integration branch, increment
it; at the threshold label the issue `human`, comment the diagnostic,
and take the existing no-ready exit instead of resuming. Update the
session-end hint to reflect escalation.

## Non-goals

Do not change the `--orphan-policy` flag semantics (warn/revert/
escalate still govern startup handling of claimed-but-unclosed
issues). Do not revert or un-claim the issue — the human label plus
`in_progress` status is the escalation, preserving worker-tree
context. Do not change the goal prompt (sibling bead) or readiness
validation (sibling bead). Do not add a persistent state file —
bd is the only cross-process store.

## Concrete locations

`src/ortus/commands/grind.py`: resume detection where
`leftover_claims`/`resume_issue_id` are computed (~line 1016), the
`left <id> in_progress for the next window` break (~line 1621), and
the session-end "run `ortus grind` again" hint (~line 1666).
`BdClient.add_comment()`, `comments()`, and `add_label()` in
`src/ortus/core/bd.py`. Labeling precedent:
`_flag_unready_for_human()` in `grind.py`. Tests:
`tests/test_grind.py`.

## Resolved decisions

1. The counter persists as a marker comment on the issue (for
   example `ortus-grind: no-close window <n>`), because grind sessions
   are separate processes and bd state is the recorded ground truth;
   `BdClient.has_comment` shows the marker-scan pattern.
2. Threshold is 2 consecutive no-close windows without HEAD movement,
   as a module constant — the field case burned exactly two workers
   before a human stepped in. A flag can come later if needed.
3. HEAD advancing on the integration branch during the window resets
   the counter: a worker making commits is progressing, not wedged.
4. Escalation reuses the human-label convention: label `human`,
   comment why (windows burned, last close status), leave
   `in_progress` so the operator sees it in `bd list
   --status=in_progress`. Repair instruction mirrors the readiness
   wording: fix the spec, then `bd label remove <id> human`.
5. A failed counter-comment write warns and still resumes — a bd
   hiccup must not strand a healthy claim.

## Compatibility constraints

Works for all backends (the counter is grind-side, backend-agnostic).
Existing `--orphan-policy` behavior, the readiness guard's resume
exemption, and single-window-per-session semantics are unchanged.
The marker comment format must be stable across versions since old
comments are re-read by newer grinds.

## Ordered steps

1. Add a helper that reads the consecutive no-close count for an
   issue from its grind marker comments.
2. Record the integration-branch tip at resume; after the window, if
   the claim is still `in_progress` and the tip is unchanged, write
   the incremented marker comment.
3. At resume time, when the count has reached the threshold, label
   `human`, comment the escalation diagnostic, and exit via the
   existing queue-blocked path instead of spawning a worker.
4. Update the session-end hint to name the escalation when it fired.
5. Add tests for escalate-at-threshold, reset-on-HEAD-advance, and
   first-resume-still-spawns; run the targeted tests.

## Dependencies

None — independent of the goal-prompt rule and readiness heuristic
beads that address the same field incident. Callers: `grind()` only.

## Edge cases

Worker closes the issue on the final allowed window: no escalation,
counter comments become inert history. Multiple leftover claims:
existing more-than-one handling is untouched (resume only fires for
exactly one). Operator manually clears the `human` label without
fixing the spec: the counter is already at threshold, so the next
no-close window re-escalates immediately rather than granting a fresh
budget. Marker comments authored by an older version with the same
prefix: parse leniently, treat unparseable markers as count zero.

## Plan-gap guidance

If bd comments cannot round-trip a machine-readable marker (comment
ordering or encoding makes the count ambiguous), stop and record
PLAN-GAP rather than inventing a filesystem side-store.

- AC-3 (guards-existing): a single leftover claim below the threshold

## Criterion checks

- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind.py -k leftover_claim_resumes_below_threshold -q`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_grind.py -q`
