title: local backend: 32k context floor and unmanaged codex context overflow a real worker
description:
## Objective

`ortus check --backend local` recommends a context large enough that a real grind worker does not overflow it mid-run, and the operator is told that codex cannot auto-manage context for a model it has no metadata for — so the audition fails with an actionable message instead of a raw server 400.

## Behavioral context

Before. `MIN_RECOMMENDED_CONTEXT = 32768` (src/ortus/core/local_backend.py:44); the context probe only WARNs below 32k and the serving_hint reference command prints `--ctx-size 32768`. Measured 2026-09-02 against llama-server on [redacted]2:8080 (0bserverx/Qwen3.8-27B-Heretic-Abliterated-Uncensored-GGUF:Q4_K_M): codex 0.147.0's launch request is already ~17.5k tokens before any work — instructions 4532, its 14 built-in tools 6417 (multi_agent_v1 alone 2329, web_search present), worker prompt + repo input ~6600 — measured via the server's /tokenize. A real grind run (~/code/localtest, logs/grind-20260902-205449.log) then failed with HTTP 400 exceed_context_size_error: request 74016 tokens vs n_ctx 65536, i.e. accumulated context (a large CodeGraph explore tool result fed back into a later turn) blew a 64k window. codex emitted "Model metadata for <id> not found. Defaulting to fallback metadata", so its own context management never trimmed — it grew the transcript until the server rejected it. A 32k-passing check is therefore a false green for the codex harness.

After. The context floor reflects codex-harness reality (recommend >= 128k for the codex path, still a WARN not a hard fail); the serving_hint reference command shows the larger window with KV-cache quantization; and when the model is unknown to codex (no metadata), check and/or the grind failure classifier says so and names the two fixes (raise ctx-size, or register model metadata) instead of surfacing a bare upstream 400. Optionally, the local launch drops codex built-in tools ortus never uses (web_search, multi_agent_v1) via `-c` to reclaim ~2.4k tokens — decide in scope.

## Design

See design field.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Three parts, the third optional and to be decided during implementation. (1) Raise MIN_RECOMMENDED_CONTEXT to a codex-harness-realistic value (>= 131072) and update serving_hint() to emit that ctx-size plus `--cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0`. (2) Teach the grind failure path (or the check) to recognise the codex "Model metadata ... not found / fallback metadata" line and the exceed_context_size_error 400, and print the two remedies rather than the raw server body. (3) Optionally add `-c tools.web_search=false` and any codex switch that drops multi_agent_v1 to LocalRunner.build_argv so the request carries only the tools ortus uses; if codex 0.147.0 has no such switch, record that and skip.

## Non-goals

Do not change the claude/codex/grok backends' context handling — only the local path. Do not implement ortus-side context compaction or transcript trimming; context management is codex's job and the fix is giving it a window and metadata, not reimplementing it. Do not raise the floor to a value that will not fit a 24 GB card at Q4 — 128k with q8 KV cache is the target, note the VRAM math. Do not gate the audition on this: the operator can raise ctx-size by hand today; this makes the tool tell the truth.

## Concrete locations

src/ortus/core/local_backend.py: MIN_RECOMMENDED_CONTEXT (line 44), serving_hint() (~line 199-210), probe_context_size() (~line 303). Grind failure classification: src/ortus/commands/grind.py failure/summary path and any codex error decoder in src/ortus/core/runstate.py. LocalRunner.build_argv in src/ortus/core/agent.py for the optional tool-trim `-c` overrides. Tests: tests/test_core_local_backend.py (floor + serving_hint text), tests/test_local_backend.py, and a grind-side test for the new message if part 2 lands there.

## Resolved decisions

1. The floor is a WARN, never a hard fail — a small model on a small card is a legitimate config, and the operator owns the tradeoff. The change is the recommended number and the reasoning, not a new gate.
2. 128k is the recommended target: codex overhead ~17.5k at launch plus CodeGraph explore payloads (thousands of tokens each) plus multi-turn growth needs headroom well past 64k, and 128k with q8_0 KV cache fits a 32 GB card at 27B Q4 (measured context of this failure: 74k on a single overflow).
3. The unknown-model-metadata condition is worth surfacing because it is the actual reason context grows unbounded; it is a codex catalog gap, not an ortus bug, so the remedy text points at ctx-size and metadata, and ortus does not pretend to fix codex.
4. The tool-trim (part 3) is optional and evidence-gated: only add a `-c` switch that codex 0.147.0 actually honors; a switch that silently does nothing is worse than none.

## Compatibility constraints

check stays two-tier: the context row is informational/WARN and never flips the run backend's exit code. serving_hint output is documentation consumed by README/init and the Q3 docs; only the numbers and one KV-cache flag change. No change to LocalConfig parsing, probe reachability, or the other backends. If part 3 lands, existing LocalRunner argv tests must be updated for the added `-c` flags and every other backend's argv stays byte-identical.

## Ordered steps

1. Raise MIN_RECOMMENDED_CONTEXT and update serving_hint() text; fix the tests that assert the old number and command.
2. Add the unknown-metadata / exceed-context recognition and remedy message to the grind failure path (or check), with a test feeding the recorded 400 body.
3. Decide part 3: probe whether codex 0.147.0 honors a tools.web_search / multi-agent disable `-c`; implement and test if it does, else record the finding in a comment and skip.
4. Run the targeted tests.

## Dependencies

Follows the shim work (ortus-d333.14, .15, .16) and informs the audition ortus-d333.11 — the audition should run against a >=128k server, which this makes the tool recommend. No code dependency on .11.

## Edge cases

A server that does not expose n_ctx via /props (probe returns None): the recommendation is still printed, the WARN is simply skipped, unchanged. A model codex DOES have metadata for (a future codex catalog entry) would self-manage context — the remedy message must not claim metadata is missing when it is present, so key the message on the actual log line, not on the backend being local. A card too small for 128k: the WARN fires, the operator lowers ctx-size and accepts shorter runs — that path must stay usable.

## Plan-gap guidance

If raising the recommended context is not enough because CodeGraph explore payloads alone can exceed any reasonable local window on a large repo, stop and record PLAN-GAP: the real fix is bounding CodeGraph payload size for the local backend, which is a separate design, not a bigger number here.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1 (proves-new): MIN_RECOMMENDED_CONTEXT is at least 131072 and serving_hint() emits that ctx-size with a KV-cache-quantization flag.
- AC-2 (proves-new): the recorded exceed_context_size_error 400 and the codex "fallback metadata" line produce an actionable ortus message naming both remedies, not the raw server body.
- AC-3 (guards-existing): the context probe still WARNs (never fails the check), other backends are byte-identical, and the local-backend suites pass.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_local_backend.py -k "recommended_context_and_serving_hint" -q`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_local_backend.py -k "context_overflow_message" -q`
- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_local_backend.py tests/test_local_backend.py tests/test_core_agent.py -q`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_core_local_backend.py tests/test_local_backend.py tests/test_core_agent.py -q`
notes: 2026-09-02 web_search finding (live audition, ~/code/localtest against llama-server): codex 0.147.0 enables web_search by DEFAULT in exec mode — it is NOT in the operator's ~/.codex/config.toml, and a -c tools.web_search=false override could not be verified to drop it (capture harness flaky; treat the switch as unproven). llama-server rejects it every turn ('unsupported Responses tool type web_search skipped') — cosmetic, non-fatal: the server strips it before advertising tools, so the model is never offered it and cannot attempt-and-loop. It costs ~14 tokens and one warning line per turn and is useless to every ortus phase (grind/plan/verify operate on the local repo + CodeGraph + bd; none need internet). IMPLEMENTATION REVISION for part 3: strip web_search in the SHIM, not via a codex -c switch. flatten_tools() in src/ortus/core/mcp_shim.py already walks tools[] (the 'for entry in tools' loop, ~line 91); drop any entry whose type is 'web_search' there — guaranteed regardless of codex version/config, and it lives beside the namespace flattening that's already the shim's job. Same loop can drop multi_agent_v1 (~2329 tok, another namespace ortus never uses) if desired. This supersedes design decision 4 / scope part 3's 'optional codex -c switch' approach.
close_reason: Superseded by the opencode pivot (ortus-t2kn). This bead tuned codex's context floor and proposed a shim strip of codex's web_search tool — both are codex-Responses-specific and moot once the local backend drives via opencode's chat-completions path (no codex overhead, no web_search builtin, no shim). Not lost: the finding that a real worker needs a large context window carries into the opencode audition.

title: local backend: run the request shim for every local worker, not only with CodeGraph
description:
## Objective

Every local-backend worker talks to the served model through the loopback shim, so the developer-role demotion and chunked-body decoding on its request leg apply whether or not CodeGraph is configured.

## Behavioral context

Before. `LocalRunner.run` in src/ortus/core/agent.py starts the shim only when `self.codegraph` is set and otherwise spawns codex straight at the configured server. The shim request leg now carries fixes a llama-server turn needs regardless of MCP: codex opens every turn with a developer-role input message, llama-server renders that role as a second system message, and the chat template raises "System message must be at the beginning", so a worker launched without CodeGraph (policy `off`, or any caller passing no capability) still dies at launch with HTTP 500 and five "high demand" retries before any tool call. Verified 2026-09-02 on the operator server; the shim path with the demotion returns 200.

After. The shim runs for every local worker, the provider base_url override always names its port, and the namespace flattening is a no-op on a request that carries no namespace tools.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Make `LocalRunner.run` start the shim unconditionally and keep `provider_base_url` pointing at the shim while one runs. Update the LocalRunner class docstring and the mcp_shim module docstring sentence that says the shim starts only with CodeGraph configured. Tests in tests/test_core_agent.py.

## Non-goals

Do not change the shim rewrites themselves (ortus-d333.15 owns them). Do not touch claude, codex, or grok argv. Do not add a config switch to bypass the shim: the SHIM decision (bd memory local-backend-mcp-decision) makes it the compatibility seam for this backend. Do not route the probes in src/ortus/core/local_backend.py through the shim; they send no developer role.

## Concrete locations

src/ortus/core/agent.py: `LocalRunner.run` (the early return when `self.codegraph is None`), `LocalRunner.provider_base_url`, the class docstring. src/ortus/core/mcp_shim.py: module docstring. tests/test_core_agent.py: the existing LocalRunner run and shim cases.

## Resolved decisions

1. The shim is unconditional for local: what it now papers over is a server-side template constraint, not an MCP feature.
2. No opt-out flag.
3. The shim stays scoped to `run`: it starts before the argv is built and closes in `finally`, as today.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux and macOS. Existing tests asserting the shim starts with CodeGraph keep passing; any test asserting no shim without CodeGraph flips to asserting one. `ortus check --backend local` rows keep reading the configured server outside `run`.

## Ordered steps

1. Remove the early return in `LocalRunner.run` so every run starts the shim.
2. Update the two docstrings.
3. Add or flip the test: a run without CodeGraph still points codex at a loopback shim port and closes the shim after the child exits.
4. Run the targeted tests.

## Dependencies

Follows ortus-d333.15 (the request rewrites this makes reachable). Child of ortus-d333.

## Edge cases

A shim that cannot bind must fail before codex is spawned, not hang. A run that ends by reap, timeout, or interrupt still closes the shim (the existing `finally`). A request with no namespace tools and no demoted roles is still forwarded byte-identical.

## Plan-gap guidance

If a check or probe path turns out to read `provider_base_url` during `run` expecting the server, stop and record PLAN-GAP rather than adding a bypass flag.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1 (proves-new): a `LocalRunner` with no CodeGraph capability launches codex with a provider base_url naming a loopback shim port, and the shim is closed after the child exits.
- AC-2 (guards-existing): the LocalRunner and local-backend suites pass.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_agent.py -k "shim_without_codegraph" -q`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_agent.py tests/test_local_backend.py -q`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_core_agent.py tests/test_local_backend.py tests/test_mcp_shim.py -q`

title: output: Rich markup swallows bracketed text such as [local] in warn, error, success, and table cells
description:
## Objective
Make every operator-facing line rendered through `ortus.core.output` print bracketed text literally, so a message naming the `[local]` table (or any `[word]`) reaches the terminal intact.

## Behavioral context
Before. `output.warn`, `output.error`, `output.success`, and `output.table` hand caller text to Rich with markup enabled, so `[local]` is parsed as a style tag and dropped: `output.warn("[local] table missing")` prints `warn:  table missing`, and `ortus check --backend local` renders its `[local]` row name as an empty cell and its gap text `[local] table missing — run ...` without the table name. Only `output.progress` escapes its argument. `ortus init` currently works around it by escaping its own `[local]` messages at the call site. After. The four helpers escape caller text (or render it with markup off) so `[local]`, `[profiles.codex.plan]`, and similar TOML table names print literally in every verb; the call-site escape in `init.py` becomes redundant and is removed.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`src/ortus/core/output.py`: `success`, `warn`, `error` (message and hint), and `table` cells. Remove the call-site `escape_markup` uses in `src/ortus/commands/init.py` once the helpers own it. Tests in `tests/test_output.py` (create if absent) and the `[local]` rows in `tests/test_check.py`.

## Non-goals
No change to `output.progress` (already escapes). No change to the coloured prefixes (`[green]✓[/green]`, `[yellow]warn:[/yellow]`, `[red]error:[/red]`), which are the helpers' own markup. No new logging layer.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/core/output.py`: `success()`, `warn()`, `error()`, `table()`; `_escape_markup` is already imported and used by `progress()`.
- `src/ortus/commands/init.py`: `_summarize_backends()` and `_resolve_local_table()` wrap their `[local]` text in `escape_markup` today.
- `src/ortus/commands/check.py`: `LOCAL_ROW_NAMES` (the `[local]` row) and `check_provisioned_backend()` gap strings name `[local]`.

## Resolved decisions
1. Escape at the helper, not at call sites: callers pass plain text and must not need to know the renderer. No caller passes intentional markup to these helpers (surveyed 2026-09-02 with rg over `src/ortus`).
2. `error()` escapes both `message` and `hint`.
3. `table()` escapes every cell; headers are ortus-owned literals and stay as they are.

## Compatibility constraints
Output that carries no square brackets is byte-identical. Linux and macOS. No exit-code changes.

## Ordered steps
1. Escape the message in `success`, `warn`, `error` (and the hint), and each cell in `table`.
2. Remove the `escape_markup` import and wrappers from `init.py`; the init tests that assert `[local] left commented` must still pass.
3. Add tests that a bracketed message survives each helper and a `[local]` table cell survives `table()`.
4. Run the check tests that assert the `[local]` rows.

## Dependencies
None — the fix is local to the output module; callers are every verb that prints through it, and `init.py` is the only one with a workaround to remove.

## Edge cases
A message that already contains a backslash-escaped bracket (`\[x]`) must not be double-escaped into a literal backslash; none exist today outside `progress()` itself. Text containing `[/]` closing tags must print literally too.

## Plan-gap guidance
If some caller turns out to rely on passing live markup to `warn`/`error`/`success`, stop and record `PLAN-GAP` rather than adding a `markup=` opt-in per call.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1 (proves-new): `output.warn("[local] table missing")` prints the literal `[local]` on stderr.
- AC-2 (proves-new): `output.error("invalid [local] field", hint="fix the [local] table")` prints both bracketed spans literally.
- AC-3 (proves-new): `output.table` renders a cell `[local] table missing` with the bracketed name present.
- AC-4 (guards-existing): the init summary line still reads `[local] left commented in .ortusrc` after the call-site escapes are removed.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: uv run pytest tests/test_output.py -k warn_prints_bracketed_text -q
- AC-2: uv run pytest tests/test_output.py -k error_prints_bracketed_text_and_hint -q
- AC-3: uv run pytest tests/test_output.py -k table_cell_keeps_bracketed_text -q
- AC-4: uv run pytest tests/test_init.py -k init_all_renders_commented_local_block -q

## Targeted tests
uv run pytest tests/test_output.py tests/test_init.py tests/test_check.py -n auto --test-timeout=60

comments.text: Done. success, warn, error (message and hint) and table in src/ortus/core/output.py now escape caller text; table passes rich Text cells through unchanged so ortus check keeps its styled status glyph (check.py _row builds Text glyphs; the packet's caller survey missed that markup-in-a-cell site, and escaping every cell would have printed the markup literally). title: grind: Claude worker that flags human is held by the /goal Stop hook until the worker timeout
description:
## Objective
Let a Claude worker that takes the goal prompt's PLAN-GAP exit (comment PLAN-GAP, label the issue human, stop) actually exit, instead of being re-prompted by the /goal Stop hook until grind's worker timeout kills it.

## Behavioral context
Before. Step 3 of the goal prompt tells a worker whose criterion checks cannot run to comment PLAN-GAP, label the issue human, and stop. The /goal condition grind composes says the goal is achieved only when the issue is closed and HEAD is in sync with origin, and the Claude Stop hook re-prompts the worker every time it tries to stop. Grind passes no reap_when callback for the Claude backend (only the grok branch builds one), so nothing on the harness side notices the human label. The worker re-answers the hook until the 5400-second worker timeout SIGTERMs the group, and the run records a timeout for what was a correct exit. Observed 2026-09-02 on a spike whose server precondition was missing: the worker flagged human within minutes and was then blocked by the hook on every stop.

After. When the issue the worker claimed this window gains the human label, or the done bar is met, grind reaps the Claude worker within one poll interval, logs the reason, and the iteration ends as a flagged claim rather than a timeout.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Give the Claude backend a reap_when callback in the grind iteration loop that fires when the worker's claimed in_progress issue gains the human label, or when _done_bar_met reports the done bar, and log the reap reason so it is not reported as a timeout.

## Non-goals
Do not change what the worker does on PLAN-GAP (comment, label, stop). Do not change the orphan policy or the EXCLUDED_LABELS semantics. Do not change Codex or Grok argv or their termination shape. Do not add a journal, handoff, or finalize write.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` — the `reap_when = None` assignment before `runner.run(...)` in the iteration loop, where only the grok branch builds `_reap_on_done_bar`; `_done_bar_met()`; `_GOAL_POINTER`.
- `src/ortus/core/claude.py` — `_wait_logged()` already polls `reap_when` every `reap_poll` seconds and kills the process group when it returns true.
- `src/ortus/core/grind_loop.py` — `EXCLUDED_LABELS`.
- `src/ortus/core/bd.py` — `BdClient.in_progress_ids(exclude_labels=...)` for a cheap poll of which in_progress ids are not human-flagged.
- `src/ortus/prompts/goal-prompt.md` — step 3 PLAN-GAP exit, unchanged.

## Resolved decisions
1. Reap on the harness side rather than loosening the worker's Stop hook: the hook is Claude's mechanism, and grind already owns the reap path for grok.
2. The flagged-claim check compares `bd.in_progress_ids()` with `bd.in_progress_ids(exclude_labels=EXCLUDED_LABELS)`; an id present in the first set and absent from the second is a flagged claim. Tracker errors during a poll return False, because a poll must never kill a live worker; this matches `_done_bar_met`.
3. Reuse `_done_bar_met` for Claude as well, so a worker that closed and pushed but keeps answering the hook is also reaped.
4. A reap logs `iter N: <reason>; reaping worker` and is not counted as a timeout.

## Compatibility constraints
Linux and macOS. `reap_when` and `reap_poll` already exist on `ClaudeRunner.run`; no argv change for any backend. Existing grok reap behaviour stays byte-identical.

## Ordered steps
1. Extract the grok `_reap_on_done_bar` closure into a backend-neutral helper that also checks for a newly human-flagged in_progress id.
2. Pass that helper as `reap_when` for the claude backend as well as grok.
3. Distinguish a reap from a timeout in the rc handling and the log line.
4. Add tests in a new `tests/test_grind_reap.py` covering: human label appears on the claimed id, reap; tracker error, no reap; done bar met, reap; label present before the window started, no reap.

## Dependencies
No issue dependencies. Callers: the grind iteration loop; `ClaudeRunner.run` and `_wait_logged` consume `reap_when`.

## Edge cases
- The human label was present before the worker started (a leftover flagged claim): the startup sweep already excludes it, and the poll must only fire for an id that was unflagged when the window began.
- bd unavailable mid-poll: return False, never reap.
- The worker flags human and then closes anyway: the done bar wins; either way the reap is correct.
- Reap granularity of one `reap_poll` interval is acceptable.

## Plan-gap guidance
If `ClaudeRunner.run` no longer accepts `reap_when`, or `_wait_logged` cannot tell a reap apart from a timeout without changing its return contract, record PLAN-GAP naming the symbol and stop; do not loosen the /goal condition text as a substitute.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1 (proves-new): a Claude iteration whose claimed issue gains the human label is reaped within one poll and logged as a flagged-claim reap, not a timeout. `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_reap.py -q`
- AC-2 (guards-existing): the existing grind loop and orphan-policy tests still pass. `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_loop.py -q`

## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_grind_reap.py tests/test_grind_loop.py -q`
close_reason: Grind now arms reap_when for Claude as well as grok: a claim that gains the human label during the window, or the done bar, reaps the worker within one poll and logs the reason instead of a timeout. Criterion checks passed: uv run pytest tests/test_grind_reap.py -q (12 passed) and uv run pytest tests/test_grind_loop.py -q (40 passed). Commit f6f176c.

comments.author: who
comments.text:
Completion: grind now reaps a Claude worker that flags its claim human, within one reap_poll, instead of leaving it to the /goal Stop hook until --worker-timeout.

What changed. The grok-only _reap_on_done_bar closure in the grind iteration loop became two module-level helpers in src/ortus/commands/grind.py: _flagged_claims(bd) nominates in_progress ids by the difference between bd.in_progress_ids() and bd.in_progress_ids(exclude_labels=EXCLUDED_LABELS), then confirms each candidate by its own labels via bd.show, so a failure on the excluding query alone (which in_progress_ids answers with an empty set) cannot make every live claim look flagged; a tracker error on the confirmation propagates. _reap_reason(bd, git, baseline_closed=, flagged_at_start=, integration_branch=) returns the done-bar label first, then a claim newly flagged since the window began, and None on any error or when a baseline could not be read (that check is skipped, never guessed). The loop arms reap_when for both claude and grok with baseline_closed and flagged_at_start captured before the spawn; a reap logs 'iter N: <reason>; reaping worker' where reason is 'done bar met (closed A->B, in sync)' or 'claim flagged human (<ids>)'. The grok wording 'reaping grok /goal review' is replaced by the neutral line; no test or decoder read the old text. Codex keeps reap_when=None (own turn loop, termination shape unchanged). _wait_logged already returns the child's rc on a reap without raising TimeoutExpired, so the TIMEOUT line and the timeout branch cannot fire for a reap; no runner contract changed.

Tests. New tests/test_grind_reap.py: fake-driven unit tests for each _reap_reason branch (newly flagged -> reap; flagged before the window -> no reap; unflagged -> no reap; listing empty / show raising / listing raising -> no reap; excluding query failed but labels say unflagged -> no reap; done bar -> reap; done bar preferred over flag; None baselines skip their check), one integration test that the claude spawn receives a callable reap_when that answers False under a no-op worker, and one slow integration test (AC-1) running grind with a fake claude that claims the leaf, runs 'bd label add <id> human', and sleeps 120 under --worker-timeout 90: the log carries 'claim flagged human (<id>); reaping worker' and no TIMEOUT, and the issue stays in_progress with the human label.

Checks that passed: 'uv run pytest tests/test_grind_reap.py -q' (12 passed, AC-1), 'uv run pytest tests/test_grind_loop.py -q' (40 passed, AC-2), 'uv run pytest tests/test_grind.py -k "done_bar or reap" -q' (5 passed, grok path), 'uv run pytest tests/test_grind_worker_timeout.py -q' (4 passed, shared reap/timeout path). ruff check and format are clean on the new test module; ruff reports three findings in grind.py (unused CodeGraphProbe import, impl_started, implementation_timed_out) that are identical on HEAD and outside this diff, left alone.

Observation, not a change: each reap poll now costs two bd list calls plus the done-bar's bd count and three git reads, so with reap_poll=2.0 the harness effectively polls bd continuously (about one poll per 4-5 s) while a claude or grok worker runs; the spec accepted one-poll granularity and the flagged-claim check as designed, and the show confirmation only runs when a candidate appears.

title: local backend Q3: audition the reference 27B model on llama-server and record the verdict
description:
## Objective
Serve the reference model (`0bserverx/Qwen3.8-27B-Heretic-Abliterated-Uncensored-GGUF:Q4_K_M`) with llama-server, drive one real issue through `ortus grind --backend local`, and record a written verdict on tool-call fidelity, edit success, termination honesty, tokens per second, context fit, mid-task server failure behaviour, and served-id spelling.

## Behavioral context
Before. The pipeline is model-agnostic and unaudited; nobody has evidence of what a 27B Q4_K_M does under the worker contract. After. `bd memories local-backend-q3` holds the verdict memo, this issue carries the run log paths, and the README gains a What to expect paragraph. The verdict never blocks the epic: a weak model is a config swap, not an Ortus defect.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Operator-run audition on the GPU host (labelled `human`: it needs a 17 GB download, llama-server install, and GPU access that grind workers do not have). Records findings; the only code change is one README paragraph.

## Non-goals
No fine-tuning, no model evaluation beyond the worker contract, no Ortus code changes, no retry logic for 5xx windows (record the behaviour only).

## Concrete locations
- `README.md` Serving a local model subsection — append the What to expect paragraph.
- `src/ortus/core/local_backend.py` `serving_hint()` — the command to run verbatim.
- `tests/test_local_backend_live.py` — run it first as the smoke gate.
- `tests/fixtures/sample-prds/tiny-3-task.md` — source of the scratch repo's one leaf; `ortus spec` for the packet shape.
- bd memories `local-backend-q1`, `local-backend-q2` — prior findings to cite.

## Resolved decisions
1. Install llama-server from the llama.cpp GitHub releases (CUDA build) or `brew install llama.cpp`; record the build id.
2. Serve with the README command plus `--alias qwen3-27b-heretic`; `model = "qwen3-27b-heretic"` in the scratch repo's `.ortusrc`. Record both spellings `GET /v1/models` reports for llama-server (alias) and, if Ollama is also tried, the Ollama tag — that is the Q5 answer.
3. Scratch repo: `ortus init $TMPDIR/local-audit --backend local --local-model qwen3-27b-heretic`, one hand-authored readiness-valid leaf (a small function plus a pytest), then `ortus grind . --backend local --tasks 1 --worker-timeout 7200` launched from a plain terminal, never from inside an agent session.
4. Verdict memo fields: `harness` (PASS/FAIL: pipeline claimed, verified, closed), `tool_fidelity`, `edit_success`, `termination`, `tokens_per_second`, `context_fit` (peak prompt tokens vs 32768), `q4_5xx` (kill llama-server mid-turn once: codex exit code and last stream event), `q5_ids`, `verdict` (one of `WORKER_CAPABLE`, `MARGINAL`, `NOT_CAPABLE`).
5. README paragraph states the verdict token, tokens per second, and the context fit in two or three sentences; no PRD or issue references.

## Compatibility constraints
Linux host with the RTX 5090 (32 GB); the 17 GB download needs network. Runs only against the scratch repo; this repository is touched only by the README paragraph and the bd memory.

## Ordered steps
1. Install llama-server, serve the model with the README command, confirm `ortus check --backend local` is fully green.
2. Run the live test module with the smoke variable and record its duration.
3. Create the scratch repo and leaf; run grind once; capture `logs/` paths and the llama-server throughput lines.
4. Kill llama-server during a second run to record the 5xx behaviour; restart it.
5. `bd remember --key local-backend-q3 "<memo>"`; comment this issue with artifact paths.
6. Append the README paragraph.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the docs leaf (the README command must exist first) and, through it, by check, grind preflight, init, and help strings. Related: the live test leaf.

## Edge cases
The model does not fit or the download fails: record `NOT_RUN <reason>` in the memory and stop; do not substitute a different model without saying so in the memo. A harness PASS with a `NOT_CAPABLE` model verdict is a valid, useful outcome.

## Plan-gap guidance
If `ortus check --backend local` is green but grind never reaches the runner, that is an Ortus defect: file a bug leaf with the log excerpt and record `PLAN-GAP` here instead of hand-driving codex.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1 (proves-new): the Q3 memory exists and ends with one of the three verdict tokens. `bd memories local-backend-q3`
- AC-2 (proves-new): the README carries the What to expect paragraph. `rg -n "What to expect" README.md`
- AC-3 (guards-existing): the state-graph block is untouched. `uv run pytest tests/test_state_graph_docs.py -q`

## Targeted tests
None — operator-run audition; the live test module and the grind logs are the evidence.
notes: Labelled human by design: needs GPU, a 17 GB download, and a terminal-launched grind (session-launched grinds have died mid-run on this host). Ollama 0.23.0 is installed as the fallback server.
close_reason: Superseded by the opencode audition under ortus-t2kn. The codex+shim audition is abandoned with the codex-local engine; the question it answered (can the 27B drive a full grind loop) is re-run on opencode. Partial evidence carried forward: the 27B makes clean chat-completions tool calls (2026-09-02) and codex's own turn loop drove it to sustained multi-turn tool use before the pivot decision.

title: local backend: document the fourth backend and the serving contract
description:
## Objective
Teach the README how to run Ortus against a self-served model: the backend table, the `[local]` config, the llama-server and Ollama serving contract (Responses API, `--jinja`, 32k context), and the worker-timeout guidance.

## Behavioral context
Before. The README names three backends and its `.ortusrc` example has no `[local]` table. After. Prerequisites, verbs, the Agent backends section, and the Configuration example cover `local`; a Serving a local model subsection gives the exact llama-server command, the Ollama equivalent, the required endpoints, and what `ortus check --backend local` verifies.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
README edits only. No PRD section references and no bd issue ids in the README (repository principle).

## Non-goals
No code or help-string edits (done in earlier leaves). No model-quality claims: the Q3 audition appends its own paragraph later.

## Concrete locations
- `README.md` line 77 (verbs table, `--backend all|claude|codex|grok`), line 106 (prerequisites row), lines 112-120 (Agent backends), line 158 (`.ortusrc` example `backend` comment), lines 176-190 (profiles example), line 291 (CodeGraph paragraph naming the backends).
- `src/ortus/core/local_backend.py` `serving_hint()` — the README command must match it word for word.
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` lines 874-884 — the `--worker-timeout` default (5400s) to cite.

## Resolved decisions
1. Prerequisites row: `**local** | any OpenAI-compatible server exposing /v1/models and /v1/responses, driven through the Codex CLI | llama.cpp llama-server / Ollama`.
2. Agent backends paragraph: `local` reuses `codex exec` as the harness with an `ortus_local` provider override; the wire API is the Responses API because codex-cli 0.147.0 supports nothing else; a local log is a codex log for `tail` and the dashboard; the model is configuration, so swapping models touches only `.ortusrc` and the serving command.
3. Serving subsection with a fenced block: the llama-server command (`-hf 0bserverx/Qwen3.8-27B-Heretic-Abliterated-Uncensored-GGUF:Q4_K_M --alias qwen3-27b-heretic --jinja --ctx-size 32768 --flash-attn on --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080`, with the `--cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0` note), the Ollama alternative (`ollama serve`, `ollama pull <tag>`, base_url `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`), the rule that `--jinja` is required for tool calling, the 32k minimum context, and that `model` must be the id `GET /v1/models` reports (llama-server: the path or `--alias`; Ollama: the tag).
4. Configuration example gains `[local]` with `base_url`, `model`, and a commented `api_key_env`, plus `[profiles.local.implement]` with `reasoning_effort = "medium"`.
5. A short `Wall clock` note: local decode is slower; raise `--worker-timeout` above the 5400s default for large models, and the default is unchanged for other backends.
6. Line 291 lists `Claude, Codex, Grok, or local`.

## Compatibility constraints
No generated block markers are touched (`tests/test_state_graph_docs.py` guards the state graph block; leave it). The README stays free of PRD references and issue ids.

1. Edit the prerequisites and verbs tables.
2. Extend the Agent backends section and add the serving subsection.
3. Extend the `.ortusrc` example and the CodeGraph paragraph.
4. Run the criterion checks.

Blocked by the check, grind preflight, init, and help-string leaves so the documented commands exist. Related: the Q3 audition appends a What to expect paragraph after this lands.

## Edge cases
The README must not promise Ollama `/props` context reporting (Ollama has none). The example model id must match the `--alias` in the serving command.

## Plan-gap guidance
If `serving_hint()` and this README disagree on the command, fix the README to match the code; if the code is wrong, record `PLAN-GAP` on this issue and stop rather than documenting a command that check does not print.

title: local backend: opt-in live test against a running local server
description:
## Objective
Add a `live_provider`-marked test module that, when an operator points it at a running local server, proves the real probes pass and a real `LocalRunner` child completes one bounded CodeGraph query.

## Behavioral context
Before. Only fake-server and argv tests cover the backend; nothing exercises a real `codex exec` against a real local endpoint. After. `ORTUS_RUN_LOCAL_BACKEND_SMOKE=1 ORTUS_LOCAL_BASE_URL=... ORTUS_LOCAL_MODEL=... uv run pytest tests/test_local_backend_live.py -m live_provider` runs two tests; without the opt-in variable the module skips, and CI never selects it.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
One new test module mirroring `tests/test_codegraph_codex_live.py`.

## Non-goals
No fixture-queue grind run (the Q3 audition does that by hand). No CI wiring. No model download. No changes to production code.

## Concrete locations
- New `tests/test_local_backend_live.py` with `pytestmark = [pytest.mark.live_provider, pytest.mark.slow]`.
- `tests/test_codegraph_codex_live.py` — the shape to mirror (`CodeGraphAdapter().probe(repo, CodeGraphMode.REQUIRED, backend=...)`, `runner.run(..., timeout=...)`, `parse_transcript(...).capability_observed`).

1. Configuration comes from environment variables, not a repo `.ortusrc`: `ORTUS_LOCAL_BASE_URL` (default `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1`), `ORTUS_LOCAL_MODEL` (required when the smoke variable is set; missing → `pytest.skip` with a message naming it), optional `ORTUS_LOCAL_API_KEY_ENV`.

3. Confirm the module skips cleanly without the variable.

Server up but model missing → test 1 fails with the served-id list (a real finding, not a skip). A model that narrates instead of calling `codegraph_explore` fails test 2 with `capability_observed` false, which is the intended signal.

title: local backend: widen backend help strings and route local logs through the codex decoders
description:
## Objective
Every `--backend` help string and the init verb description name `local`, `ortus tail --backend local` decodes the log as codex JSONL, and the dashboard treats a grind start line naming `local` as agreeing with codex events.

## Behavioral context
Before. Help text says `claude, codex, or grok`; `ortus tail --backend local` resolves the backend but then picks the Claude decoder because `codex=resolved_backend == "codex"`; the dashboard would emit `PLAN-GAP: named backend=local disagrees with event backend=codex`. After. Help strings list four backends; tail decodes local logs with the codex path and renders them identically to a codex log; the dashboard reports no conflict for `local` against codex events.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
String widening in `cli.py`, `plan.py`, `interview.py`, `tail.py`; decoder selection in `tail.py`; `backend_conflict` aliasing in `dashboard.py`. Tests in `tests/test_tail.py`, `tests/test_dashboard.py`, `tests/test_cli_verbs.py`.

## Non-goals
No new decoder (a local log is a codex log). No changes to `grind.py` help (the preflight leaf owns it) or `check.py` help (the check leaf). No README (docs leaf). No change to `runstate.py`: its `backend=([a-z]+)` regex already captures `local`.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/cli.py` line 57: init help `Bootstrap a fresh repo for Claude, Codex, Grok, or a local model.`
- `src/ortus/commands/plan.py` line 143 and `src/ortus/commands/interview.py` line 52: `claude, codex, grok, or local; defaults from .ortusrc`.
- `src/ortus/commands/tail.py` line 1155 help `Log backend (claude|codex|grok|local); defaults from .ortusrc.` and line 1207 `codex=resolved_backend in ("codex", "local")`.
- `src/ortus/commands/dashboard.py` `backend_conflict()` (line 613) and `log_backend()` (line 600).
- `tests/test_tail.py`, `tests/test_dashboard.py`, `tests/test_cli_verbs.py`; fixture `tests/fixtures/codex-exec-events.jsonl` and golden `tests/fixtures/codex-tail-golden.txt`.

## Resolved decisions
1. `tail` selects the codex decoder for both `codex` and `local`; the `--codex` shorthand keeps meaning `--backend codex`.
2. `backend_conflict(named, log)` normalises `named == "local"` to `codex` before comparing, so a start line `backend=local` with codex events yields an empty string; `local` against grok or claude events still reports the PLAN-GAP line naming `local`.
3. `log_backend` is unchanged: events decide, and local events are codex events.
4. Help strings are the only text edits; no prose elsewhere.

## Compatibility constraints
`ortus tail --backend codex` and `--codex` output are byte-identical against the golden fixture. `backend_conflict("grok", "codex")` still reports a conflict. No exit-code changes.

## Ordered steps
1. Widen the four help strings.
2. Change the tail decoder selection.
3. Alias `local` in `backend_conflict`.
4. Add the tests listed in the criteria and run them.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the runner leaf (`resolve_backend("local")` must succeed). Related: the check and grind leaves own their own help strings.

## Edge cases
A log whose start line says `backend=local` but carries Claude events still conflicts. `ortus tail --backend local` in a repo with no `[local]` table still tails (tail never loads `LocalConfig`).

## Plan-gap guidance
If `tail` needs `LocalConfig` for anything, stop and record `PLAN-GAP`; decoding must not depend on server config.

- AC-1 (proves-new): `ortus tail --backend local` renders the codex fixture identically to `--backend codex`.
- AC-2 (proves-new): `backend_conflict("local", "codex")` is empty and `backend_conflict("local", "claude")` is not.
- AC-3 (proves-new): the init, plan, interview, and tail help texts each mention `local`.
- AC-4 (guards-existing): the codex tail golden test still passes.

title: local backend: ortus init --backend local and --backend all provision the [local] table
description:
## Objective
Let `ortus init` provision the local backend: `--backend local --local-model <id>` writes `.codex/config.toml` plus an active `[local]` table in `.ortusrc`, `--backend all` writes a commented `[local]` reference block while still pinning claude, and a forced re-init preserves an existing `[local]` table.

## Behavioral context
Before. `ortus init --backend local` is rejected as unrecognised; `--backend all` provisions three config directories. After. `ortus init . --backend local --local-model qwen3-27b` writes `.codex/config.toml`, pins `backend = "local"`, and renders `[local]` with `base_url` and `model`; omitting `--local-model` on a first local init fails with a hint naming the flag; `--backend all` renders every backend directory plus a commented `[local]` block with the reference serving command and reports `local` in the summary as provisioned-but-unpinned; `ortus init --force` on a repo whose `.ortusrc` already has `[local]` keeps its values when the flags are omitted.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`init.py` flags and summary, `init_render.py` template map, render context and de-duplication, `.ortusrc.jinja` local block, `config.read_recorded_local` consumption. Tests in `tests/test_init.py`, `tests/test_init_flags.py`, `tests/test_init_render.py`.

## Non-goals
No new template file: `local` shares `.codex/config.toml`. No server start. No `[local]` validation logic here (the config leaf owns it). No change to the claude default under `--backend all`.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/core/init_render.py`: `BACKEND_TEMPLATES` (line 34) gains `"local": ".codex/config.toml"`; `RenderContext` (line 96) gains `local_base_url: str = DEFAULT_LOCAL_BASE_URL` and `local_model: str | None = None` exported in `as_dict()`; `render_all()` (line 135) de-duplicates rendered names while preserving order; `list_bundled("local")` (line 165) returns `.codex/config.toml` then `.ortusrc`.
- `src/ortus/templates/.ortusrc.jinja`: after the `codegraph` line, `{% if backend == "local" %}` an active `[local]` table with `base_url = "{{ local_base_url }}"` and `model = "{{ local_model }}"` `{% else %}` a commented block showing the same two keys, `# api_key_env = "..."`, and the reference `llama-server ... --jinja --ctx-size 32768` command `{% endif %}`.
- `src/ortus/commands/init.py`: `_backend_cli()` (line 200) takes `BACKEND_BINARIES[name]`; `_summarize_backends()` (line 272); `init()` options (line 354-404) gain `--local-model` and `--local-base-url`; the `backend not in BACKENDS` check (413) accepts `local` automatically; the bd Claude-scaffold removal set at line 536 becomes `{"codex", "grok", "local"}`; `RenderContext(...)` construction at line 573.
- `src/ortus/core/config.py`: `read_recorded_local(repo)`; `src/ortus/core/local_backend.py`: `DEFAULT_LOCAL_BASE_URL`, `probe_models`, `LocalServerError`.
- `tests/test_init.py` (`test_init_codex_creates_only_codex_config`, `test_init_default_all_provisions_every_backend`), `tests/test_init_flags.py` (`test_help_advertises_new_flags`, `test_force_reinit_preserves_recorded_facts`), `tests/test_init_render.py` (`test_list_bundled_matches_constant`, `test_rendered_ortusrc_validates_as_toml`).

## Resolved decisions
1. New options: `--local-model` (string, no default) and `--local-base-url` (string, default `DEFAULT_LOCAL_BASE_URL`). Precedence per key: explicit flag, then the recorded `[local]` value from `read_recorded_local(target)`, then (for base_url only) the default. When the run backend resolves to `local` and no model is available from flag or record, `init` errors before writing anything: `--backend local needs --local-model <id as GET {base_url}/models reports it>`.
2. Under `--backend all` the run backend stays `claude`; `.ortusrc` gets the commented reference block; `_summarize_backends` prints a WARN-style line for `local`: `local: .codex/config.toml written; [local] left commented in .ortusrc — pin it with ortus init --backend local --local-model <id>, then ortus check --backend local` (never an error, whatever the codex CLI state, because `local` is not the pinned run backend). The codex line keeps its existing behaviour.
3. Under a concrete `--backend local`, after rendering, init calls `probe_models` once with a 3s timeout and prints `output.success("local server reachable: <display>")` or `output.warn("local server not reachable at <base_url>: <reason>; start it with: <first line of serving hint>")`; it never exits nonzero on that probe because the server may legitimately be down at bootstrap.
4. `_summarize_backends` and `_backend_cli` resolve the binary through `BACKEND_BINARIES` so `local` looks for `codex`.
5. `render_all` renders `.codex/config.toml` once even though both `codex` and `local` map to it (dedupe with an ordered set).
6. A recorded `[local]` table's `api_key_env` is carried through unchanged on re-init (pass it into the render context as `local_api_key_env: str | None` and render `api_key_env = "..."` only when set).

## Compatibility constraints
`ortus init` for claude/codex/grok writes byte-identical files except for the new commented `[local]` block in `.ortusrc`, which stays valid TOML. `RECORDED_INIT_KEYS` is unchanged (`[local]` is recorded through `read_recorded_local`, not through it). `--force` semantics are otherwise unchanged. Linux and macOS.

## Ordered steps
1. Extend `BACKEND_TEMPLATES`, `RenderContext`, `render_all`, `list_bundled`.
2. Edit `.ortusrc.jinja` with the conditional local block.
3. Add the two flags, the precedence resolution, and the first-init error to `init()`.
4. Update `_backend_cli`, `_summarize_backends`, the scaffold-removal set, and the post-render probe.
5. Write the tests listed in the criteria and run them.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the `[local]` config leaf (`DEFAULT_LOCAL_BASE_URL`, `read_recorded_local`) and the probes leaf (`probe_models`); the runner leaf supplies `BACKEND_BINARIES` and `local` in `BACKENDS`. Related: the check leaf (init messages point at `ortus check --backend local`).

## Edge cases
`--local-model` given with `--backend codex` is accepted and ignored with a progress note (`--local-model applies only to --backend local`). `--backend all --local-model x` renders the commented block only (no active table) and notes the same. `--force` with a recorded `[local]` plus an explicit `--local-model` prints the `re-detected` change line like other facts. A recorded `[local]` table that fails validation makes `init` error with the config message and a repair hint, never silently re-rendering defaults.

## Plan-gap guidance
If `render_all`'s name expansion cannot map `local` onto `.codex/config.toml` without also changing what `list_bundled("codex")` returns, record `PLAN-GAP` rather than adding a second copy of the codex template.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1 (proves-new): `ortus init <tmp> --backend local --local-model m1` writes `.codex/config.toml`, no `.claude/` or `.grok/` directory, and an `.ortusrc` whose `[local]` table has `model = "m1"` and the default base_url.
- AC-2 (proves-new): `ortus init <tmp> --backend local` without `--local-model` exits 1 naming the flag and writes nothing.
- AC-3 (proves-new): `ortus init <tmp>` (all) renders every backend directory, pins claude, and its `.ortusrc` parses as TOML with no active `[local]` table but a commented reference block containing `--jinja`.
- AC-4 (proves-new): a forced re-init of a repo whose `.ortusrc` has `[local]` keeps `model` and `base_url` when the flags are omitted.
- AC-5 (proves-new): the rendered local `.ortusrc` validates as TOML and `list_bundled("local")` returns the codex config then `.ortusrc`; `render_all` with all backends writes `.codex/config.toml` once.
- AC-6 (proves-new): `ortus init --help` advertises `--local-model` and `--local-base-url`.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: uv run pytest tests/test_init.py -k init_local_writes_codex_config_and_local_table -q
- AC-2: uv run pytest tests/test_init.py -k init_local_requires_local_model -q
- AC-3: uv run pytest tests/test_init.py -k init_all_renders_commented_local_block -q
- AC-4: uv run pytest tests/test_init.py -k init_force_preserves_local_table -q
- AC-5: uv run pytest tests/test_init_render.py -k "rendered_ortusrc_local_table_validates or list_bundled_local_uses_codex_config or render_all_does_not_duplicate_codex_config" -q
- AC-6: uv run pytest tests/test_init_flags.py -k help_advertises_local_flags -q

## Targeted tests
uv run pytest tests/test_init.py tests/test_init_flags.py tests/test_init_render.py -n auto --test-timeout=60
notes: CodeGraph: init -> render_all -> render_template; BACKEND_TEMPLATES callers are init.py, check.py, init_render.py. Templates are hidden files under src/ortus/templates (.ortusrc.jinja, .codex/config.toml.jinja); rg needs --hidden to list them.

title: readiness: command runner allowlist rejects npx, grep, and Node toolchain binaries
description:
## Objective

`looks_like_command()` recognises `npx`, `grep`, `vitest`, `jest`, `tsc`, `eslint`, and `prettier` as command runners, so a Node/vitest repository can write Criterion-checks commands the way its `package.json` scripts and docs already spell them.

## Behavioral context

Before. `_COMMAND_RUNNERS` in `src/ortus/core/readiness.py` is Python-shaped: `npm`, `node`, `rg`, and `bash` are present but `npx` and `grep` are not, and no Node toolchain binary is listed. A criterion line such as `- AC-1: Run `npx vitest run tests/client.test.ts -t "createImport"`.` or `- AC-2: Run `grep -E "Recommended scope" docs/security/key-scope.md`.` is classified as prose, so the criterion fails with `AC-1: no runnable command`. Observed 2026-08-29 in the downstream repo `logicfirst-mcp`: `ortus grind` skipped all 13 open leaves with `acceptance_criteria/criterion checks` failures on packets that `ortus plan` itself had written. The workaround was to hand-rewrite every packet (`npx vitest run X` → `npm test -- X`, `grep` → `rg`).

After. The seven runners above are on the allowlist. `npx vitest run tests/x.test.ts` and `grep -q foo README.md` satisfy `## Criterion checks` and command-bearing `## Observable criteria` lines exactly as `npm test -- tests/x.test.ts` and `rg foo README.md` do today. Every packet that validates today validates identically; the change is purely additive.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Add `npx`, `grep`, `vitest`, `jest`, `tsc`, `eslint`, and `prettier` to `_COMMAND_RUNNERS` in `src/ortus/core/readiness.py` and cover the new tokens with acceptance tests in `tests/test_core_readiness.py`.

## Non-goals

Do not touch `_TEST_INVOCATION` or `targeted_test_command()` — widening Targeted-tests recognition is ortus-sju4. Do not loosen `looks_like_command()` beyond the allowlist (no heuristic such as "any token followed by a path"). Do not add shell keywords (`for`, `if`, `while`); the documented escape is `bash -c`. Do not add per-repo configurable runners from `.ortusrc`; note it as follow-up only if the widened builtin list proves insufficient. Do not change the rendered `ortus spec` text — teaching the allowlist is a sibling bead.

## Concrete locations

`src/ortus/core/readiness.py`: `_COMMAND_RUNNERS` (frozenset at ~line 259) and `looks_like_command()` (~line 329), which takes the first token after `_COMMAND_LEAD_IN` and requires it in the set. Consumers: `extract_check_command()` (~line 340) and, through it, `targeted_test_command()` and `validate_issue()`. Tests: `tests/test_core_readiness.py` (currently a single guard test importing `ready_issue` from `tests/test_readiness.py`). CodeGraph: `looks_like_command` callers are `extract_check_command` only.

## Resolved decisions

1. `grep` joins the allowlist for the same reason `rg` is already there: it is a read-only assertion tool that a check line legitimately leads with.
2. `npx` is a runner, not a package name: `npx <binary> …` is the canonical way to invoke a project-local binary in a Node repository, so the first token is what the allowlist must recognise.
3. `vitest` and `jest` are listed as bare binaries because `package.json` `test` scripts and CI logs spell them without `npx`, and the planner copies that spelling.
4. `tsc`, `eslint`, and `prettier` are listed because they are the typecheck/lint/format gates a Node `package.json` usually names, the Node counterpart of `mypy` and `ruff`, which are already listed.
5. The allowlist stays a flat frozenset; no ecosystem grouping. The set is small and the lookup is by basename after `rsplit("/", 1)`, so `./node_modules/.bin/vitest` also resolves.

## Compatibility constraints

Additive only: every string `looks_like_command()` accepts today it must still accept, and every existing readiness test must pass unchanged. The rendered `ortus spec` output does not enumerate runners today, so `spec_markdown()` is byte-identical before and after (the sibling teaching bead changes that deliberately). No CLI, stored-data, or platform change.

## Ordered steps

1. Add the seven tokens to `_COMMAND_RUNNERS` next to the existing `npm`/`node` entries.
2. Add tests in `tests/test_core_readiness.py`: `looks_like_command` is true for `npx vitest run tests/x.test.ts`, `grep -q foo README.md`, `vitest run tests/x.test.ts`, `jest tests/x.test.ts`, `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint src/`, and `prettier --check src/`.
3. Add a test that `extract_check_command("- AC-1: Run `npx vitest run tests/x.test.ts -t \"createImport\"`.", "AC-1")` returns the command with no error, and the same for the `grep -E` form from the report.
4. Add a guard that a prose line with no runner token (`- AC-1: Confirm the import succeeds.`) still reports `no runnable command`.
5. Run `uv run pytest tests/test_core_readiness.py tests/test_readiness.py -q`.

## Dependencies

No blocking issues. Related: ortus-sju4 (Targeted-tests matcher) — once both land, `Run `npx vitest run tests/x.test.ts`.` satisfies `## Targeted tests` too, because the runner gate and the test-invocation match compose. Related: the sibling spec-teaching bead, which renders this allowlist into `ortus spec`. Code consumers of `looks_like_command()`: `extract_check_command()` and every validator path above it.

## Edge cases

`npx` followed by a package that is not a test runner (`npx prettier --check .`) is a command and passes — correctness of the command is not readiness's job. A criterion carrying two command spans (`npx vitest …` and `grep …` on one line) is still ambiguous and fails, unchanged. `grep` inside prose after the lead-in (`Verify grep output is empty`) is not matched because `_first_token` after `_COMMAND_LEAD_IN` is `grep` — this is accepted as a command, matching how `rg` already behaves; document it in the test rather than special-casing. Path-prefixed binaries (`./node_modules/.bin/jest`) resolve by basename and pass.

## Plan-gap guidance

If adding a token causes an existing test in `tests/test_readiness.py` to fail because a fixture relied on that token being prose, stop and record PLAN-GAP naming the fixture rather than editing the fixture to keep the token out.

title: readiness: Targeted tests matcher accepts only pytest-style invocations
description:
## Objective

`## Targeted tests` accepts real bounded test invocations from
non-Python ecosystems, and `ortus spec` documents the command
grammar's shell-construct rule, so the section is usable in every
repo ortus itself initializes.

## Behavioral context

Before. `_TEST_INVOCATION` in readiness matches only
`pytest|unittest|python -m pytest`, so in a vitest workspace a real
bounded command like `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots test --
test/hardPlay.spec.ts` can never satisfy `## Targeted tests` — even
though `pnpm` is on the runner allowlist and the identical command is
accepted in `## Criterion checks`. Observed 2026-08-16 in the
downstream repo `500` (a repo `ortus init` itself classifies as
polyglot): every TypeScript issue must use the `None — <why>` escape
and smuggle its test commands into Criterion checks. Relatedly, the
command grammar rejects shell constructs (`for i in 1 2 3; do … done`
fails as "no runnable command" because `for` is not a runner token)
and nothing in `ortus spec` says so or names the `bash -c` escape.

After. Targeted-test recognition accepts common runner test forms —
`pnpm`/`npm`/`yarn` `test`, `vitest`, `jest`, `cargo test`,
`go test`, `make test` — alongside the pytest family, still gated by
the existing runner allowlist, and the generated spec output states
that shell constructs must be wrapped in `bash -c '…'`.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Widen test-invocation recognition in readiness: extend
`_TEST_INVOCATION` (or replace it with a small classifier beside
`looks_like_command()`) to accept the runner test forms listed in
the objective, update `targeted_test_command()` accordingly, and add
the shell-construct/`bash -c` rule to `_shape_rules()` so
`spec_markdown()` teaches it. Add ecosystem-coverage tests.

## Non-goals

Do not loosen `looks_like_command()` or add runners to
`_COMMAND_RUNNERS`. Do not accept bare loop keywords (`for`, `while`)
as commands — the documented `bash -c` wrapper is the escape. Do not
add per-repo configurable test patterns from `.ortusrc` yet; note it
as follow-up if the widened builtin list proves insufficient. Do not
change Criterion-checks validation.

## Concrete locations

`src/ortus/core/readiness.py`: `_TEST_INVOCATION` (~line 253),
`targeted_test_command()`, `_shape_rules()` (the Targeted-tests rule
already embeds a `_TEST_INVOCATION`-proven example via `_example()`),
and `spec_markdown()`. Tests: `tests/test_core_readiness.py` and
`tests/test_readiness.py`.

## Resolved decisions

1. Recognition stays regex/token-based over the normalized command,
   matching either the pytest family or a known runner followed by a
   test-ish invocation (`test` subcommand or a `vitest`/`jest`
   binary) — no execution, no filesystem probing.
2. The runner gate stays: a matching test form whose lead token is
   not allowlisted still fails, exactly as today.
3. `make test` counts as a test invocation — it is the conventional
   bounded entry point in Make-based repos; its opacity is the repo
   owner's contract.
4. The `_example()` self-proving pattern in `_shape_rules()` must
   keep passing: update the taught example set to include one
   non-Python form so the docs demonstrate the widened rule.
5. Shell-construct documentation is one added shape-rule bullet:
   loops/conditionals are not commands; wrap them in `bash -c '…'`.

## Compatibility constraints

Every spec that validates today must validate identically — the
change only widens acceptance of `## Targeted tests`. The
`None — <why>` explained-absence escape keeps working. Generated
spec output is consumed by `ortus spec`, the plan/repair prompts,
and the readiness memory pointer; only additive wording changes.

## Ordered steps

1. Widen `_TEST_INVOCATION`/add the classifier with the runner test
   forms from resolved decision 1.
2. Update `targeted_test_command()` and its callers if the signature
   shifts.
3. Add the shell-construct bullet and a non-Python example to
   `_shape_rules()`.
4. Add acceptance tests per ecosystem (pnpm/vitest, cargo, go, make)
   plus a prose-only rejection guard; run targeted tests.

## Dependencies

None. Callers of `targeted_test_command()`: readiness validation and
any repair-prompt rendering that quotes the section.

## Edge cases

`pnpm test` with no bounding argument: accepted by this bead's
matcher — scope bounding is the sibling unbounded-suite bead's job,
and the two must compose (a widened match that the sibling then
rejects as unbounded yields the unbounded failure, not silence).
`yarn jest path/to.spec.ts` — accepted. `node --test` — not in the
initial list; note as follow-up if requested. Prose mentioning the
word "test" without a runner token still fails.

## Plan-gap guidance

If widening collides with the sibling unbounded-suite detector such
that a command is simultaneously required and rejected with no
bounded spelling available in some ecosystem, stop and record
PLAN-GAP naming the ecosystem instead of special-casing one repo.

- AC-3 (proves-new): `ortus spec` output documents the `bash -c`

- AC-4 (guards-existing): prose without a runner token still fails

## Criterion checks

title: lessons: lexical-first-N memory selection hides owner policy from workers
description:
## Objective

Owner-policy memories actually reach grind workers: lesson selection
prioritizes policy/decision memories instead of lexical-first-N, a
dropped lessons block is logged instead of silent, and the goal
prompt requires checking `bd memories` before authoring or re-scoping
beads.

## Behavioral context

Before. Grind injects at most 3 memories into each worker prompt,
chosen by `select_lessons` in strict lexical key order and clipped to
220 characters — relevance plays no role, so in any repo with more
than three memories an owner decision is invisible unless its key
sorts early. The whole lessons block is also dropped silently when
the composed Claude prompt nears the 4,000-character cap. And the
goal prompt's only authoring instruction is "file leftover work as
new beads" — no memory check. Observed 2026-08-16 in the downstream
repo `500`: with the owner decision recorded as bd memory
`ci-policy-owner-decision-2026-08-16-github` ("heavy simulations are
skipped under CI"), a worker filed fh-r9w whose explicit non-goal was
the exact opposite of that policy; a human had to supersede it.

After. Memories whose keys carry policy/decision markers are selected
first (then lexical fill as today), dropping the lessons block logs a
line naming the omission, and goal-prompt step 3 directs the worker
to run `bd memories <keyword>` before filing or re-scoping a bead and
to treat owner-decision memories as binding on Non-goals and
Resolved-decisions sections.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Three surfaces, one contract: (1) `select_lessons()` gains a priority
tier — keys containing `policy` or `decision` as hyphen-delimited
tokens are selected before the lexical fill, still bounded by the
same limit and clipping. (2) The lessons-drop branch in grind's
prompt composition logs which keys were omitted and why (cap)
instead of dropping silently. (3) `goal-prompt.md` step 3 gains the
authoring rule: before filing or re-scoping any bead, run
`bd memories <keyword>` for the task's subject; owner-decision
memories bind the new bead's Non-goals and Resolved decisions.

## Non-goals

Do not implement semantic or embedding-based relevance ranking. Do
not raise `_LESSONS_MAX_COUNT` or `_LESSON_MAX_CHARS` — the fix is
ordering and visibility, not volume. Do not inject full memory
bodies into the prompt beyond the existing clipped form. Do not
change `bd prime` or interactive-session priming.

## Concrete locations

`select_lessons()` and `_clip_lesson()` in `src/ortus/core/bd.py`.
`_compose_work_prompt()` and `_lessons_contract()` in
`src/ortus/commands/grind.py` (the silent drop is the
`len(task) + len(lessons_text) <= wrap_limit` branch).
`src/ortus/prompts/goal-prompt.md` step 3. Tests:
`tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py` (existing `select_lessons`
coverage lives there) and `tests/test_grind.py`.

## Resolved decisions

1. Priority is keyed on hyphen-delimited tokens `policy` or
   `decision` in the memory key — deterministic, no new metadata, and
   it matches the field convention
   (`ci-policy-owner-decision-2026-08-16-github`). Document the
   convention in the rule text `select_lessons` tests assert.
2. Within each tier, ordering stays lexical so selection remains
   deterministic across runs.
3. The drop log line is grind-side (`write_log`), listing omitted
   keys — composition stays pure; the caller detects the omission by
   comparing composed output against the lessons it passed, or via a
   returned flag if the signature must change.
4. The goal-prompt rule is one sentence plus the binding clause; the
   readiness-contract memory stays excluded from injection as today.

## Compatibility constraints

Selection stays deterministic and bounded: same limit, same clipping,
stable output for stores without policy-token keys (pure lexical, as
today). The composed Claude `/goal` condition must stay under the
4,000-character cap; the goal-prompt edit adds at most two sentences
fetched via `ortus prompt show goal`, not counted against the cap.

## Ordered steps

1. Add the two-tier ordering to `select_lessons()` with tests
   covering priority, tie-order, and no-policy-key stores.
2. Surface the lessons-drop omission as a `write_log` line in
   `_compose_work_prompt`'s caller in `grind()`.
3. Add the `bd memories` authoring rule to `goal-prompt.md` step 3.
4. Add a prompt-content test asserting the authoring rule, and a
   grind test asserting the drop log line; run targeted tests.

## Dependencies

None. Callers: `_lessons_contract()` in grind is the only
`select_lessons` consumer besides tests; the goal prompt is consumed
by all backends via `compose_worker_prompt()`.

## Edge cases

More policy-token memories than the limit: the priority tier fills
the whole budget lexically — acceptable, the budget is the contract.
A key like `decision-log` that is not an owner decision: selected by
token match — acceptable false positive, the tier only reorders.
Empty memory store or bd failure: existing empty-section fallback
unchanged. Lessons that fit exactly at the cap: injected, no log
line.

## Plan-gap guidance

If surfacing the drop requires changing `_compose_work_prompt`'s
signature in a way that breaks the dry-run path or existing callers,
stop and record PLAN-GAP instead of duplicating composition logic.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1 (proves-new): a memory keyed with a `policy` or `decision`
  token is selected ahead of lexically-earlier non-policy keys.
- AC-2 (proves-new): when the lessons block is dropped for the cap,
  the grind run log names the omitted memory keys.
- AC-3 (proves-new): the composed worker prompt directs running
  `bd memories` before filing or re-scoping beads and binds
  owner-decision memories on Non-goals/Resolved decisions.
- AC-4 (guards-existing): stores without policy-token keys select in
  pure lexical order as before.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py -k policy_lessons_selected_first -q`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind.py -k logs_dropped_lessons -q`
- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py -k worker_prompt_checks_memories_before_authoring -q`
- AC-4: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py -k select_lessons -q`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py tests/test_grind.py -q`

title: Host prose duplicating the managed agent block goes undetected by init and check
description:
## Objective

Duplicated agent guidance becomes visible: when host prose outside the managed markers in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md repeats headings that the managed ortus block owns, `ortus init` warns at apply time and `ortus check` reports a WARN row — instead of both staying silent while agents read stale pre-marker instructions first.

## Behavioral context

Before (field report /tmp/ortus-init-force-report.md, 2026-08-16): a consumer repo bootstrapped by pre-marker ortus (0.1.5.dev5, whole-file AGENTS.md) was force re-inited by apv5-era ortus. _write_agent_files appended the fresh `<!-- BEGIN ortus block=agents schema=1 -->` block and — by design — left everything outside the markers untouched. Result: the legacy unmarked sections ("Issue tracking with bd", "Orchestrator (ortus grind)", "Session-close protocol") now appear twice: once stale above the markers (old grind flags like `--idle-sleep 0`, references to goal.sh/ralph.sh, a session-close list missing `bd close`) and once current inside them. Agents reading top-down hit the stale copy first. `ortus check` reported "AGENTS.md block=agents schema=1 current" — green — and the operator only found the duplication by reading the file. Because init only ever rewrites between the markers, the stale copies would never be cleaned up automatically.

After: the same re-init prints a warning naming the duplicated headings and the file, and `ortus check` carries an info-level WARN row whenever host prose outside the markers contains a heading the managed block also renders — pointing the operator at the manual cleanup. Host prose is still never modified.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Duplicate-heading detection for the managed agent files: a shared helper that compares markdown headings in the host prose (outside the markers) against headings rendered by the managed block, a warn in init's _write_agent_files path, and an info-level CheckResult row in check's agent-file section, with tests.

## Non-goals

- Never modify, migrate, or delete host prose: the byte-for-byte preservation promise (apv5.4, README-guarded by test_readme_documents_init_managed_agent_files) stays absolute. Automated migration of pre-marker content is a possible future issue, not this one.
- No detection of semantic contradictions in prose that does not reuse the block's headings (the report's CLAUDE.md always-push-vs-conservative example is explicitly out of scope, as the report itself suggests).
- The WARN must not fail `ortus check` — use the existing info level (CheckResult level="info", src/ortus/commands/check.py:52-59), matching the provisioned-sibling-backend rows.

## Concrete locations

- src/ortus/core/agent_files.py — home for the detector, e.g. duplicated_headings(host_text_outside_markers, rendered_block_body) -> tuple[str, ...]; reuse the existing block parsing (ParsedBlock, src/ortus/core/agent_files.py:117) to isolate text outside the markers, and render_block (src/ortus/core/agent_files.py:163) for the block body; heading extraction can mirror the ATX-heading regex approach used by ortus.core.readiness._sections.
- src/ortus/commands/init.py:119-145 — _write_agent_files(); after apply_block succeeds, run the detector and output.warn a line naming the file and the duplicated headings.
- src/ortus/commands/check.py:387 — check_agent_file(); add the info-level duplicate-headings row per managed file.
- src/ortus/templates/blocks/agents.md and the pointer block template — the source of the managed headings being matched.
- tests/test_init.py and tests/test_check.py — coverage.

## Resolved decisions

- Detect by heading equality, not content similarity: compare normalized markdown ATX headings (case-insensitive, whitespace-collapsed — the same normalization philosophy as readiness's _normalise_heading) appearing both outside the markers and inside the rendered block. Rationale: the field case is exact heading reuse from an older whole-file render; heading match is cheap, deterministic, and has an obvious remediation, while fuzzy prose matching invites false positives.
- Warn in both surfaces: init warns at the moment the duplication is created or re-encountered (the operator is present), and check warns durably (the next operator may not have run init). The report shows check-green-with-duplicates is the dangerous state.
- Wording includes the word "duplicates" plus the heading list and the manual action, e.g.: `AGENTS.md host prose duplicates managed-block headings: Session-close protocol — delete the stale copies outside the ortus markers`.
- Applies to both managed files and both block types (agents, pointer), not just AGENTS.md.

## Compatibility constraints

- `ortus check` exit code is unchanged in every existing scenario (the new row is info-level); repos with clean files see no new output.
- Init output gains at most one warn line per managed file; tests that assert init's success lines (tests/test_cli_verbs.py progress-line tests) must be unaffected on clean fixtures.
- The detector must tolerate files with no markers (pre-init state: nothing to compare — no warning) and files that are entirely the managed block.

## Ordered steps

1. Add the heading-extraction and duplicated_headings helper to src/ortus/core/agent_files.py with unit tests covering: exact duplicate, case/whitespace variants, heading only outside markers (no warn), heading only inside (no warn), file without markers (no warn).
2. Call the helper from _write_agent_files after a successful apply_block and output.warn the composed line when duplicates exist.
3. Add the info-level row to check_agent_file with the same composed line.
4. Extend tests/test_init.py with a pre-marker-migration fixture (legacy unmarked sections + forced re-init) asserting the warn, and tests/test_check.py asserting the WARN row and the unchanged exit code.
5. Run the acceptance commands.

## Dependencies

None blocking in bd. Related but independent report siblings: the re-detection clobber and the .gitignore rewrite issues; either order works. Code consumers: check's row renderer (info-level rows already render as WARN) and init's warn stream; the block templates are read-only inputs.

## Edge cases

- Generic headings that collide by coincidence (a host "## Development" would not match today's block headings, but keep the comparison scoped to the block's own headings so ortus never warns about headings it does not manage).
- Multiple managed blocks in one file (agents + pointer both present): compare host prose against the union of present blocks' headings.
- A heading duplicated more than once outside the markers: report it once.
- Setext-style host headings (underlined with === or ---): out of scope for matching (the legacy renders used ATX); note in the helper docstring.

## Plan-gap guidance
