title: Grind readiness-skip remediation omits the human label it applies
description:
## Objective

Make grind's readiness-skip remediation complete: an operator who follows the printed follow-up verbatim ends with the repaired issue back in grind's queue, instead of a permanently invisible open issue.

## Behavioral context

Before: when the ready queue holds only unready leaves, grind labels each one `human` (_flag_unready_for_human, src/ortus/commands/grind.py:678) and prints "follow-up: bd update <id> --description/--design/--acceptance to readiness schema v1, then re-run: ortus grind <target>" (src/ortus/commands/grind.py:1306-1308) plus the console warn "It stays open and unclaimed. Run ortus plan or edit the work spec." (src/ortus/commands/grind.py:1268). Neither message mentions the label, and grind counts open/ready with exclude_labels=("human",) (src/ortus/core/grind_loop.py:39), so after the operator repairs the spec exactly as instructed, the next run reports the issue invisible. Observed 2026-08-16 with ortus-oamr and ortus-trex: both repaired to schema v1 and validating READY, yet `ortus grind` reported "initial state: open=0 ... queue already drained; nothing to do" until `bd label remove <id> human` was run by hand.

After: the follow-up (and the skip warn) name the label and include the exact unlabeling command, so the printed remediation is sufficient: repair the spec, remove the label, re-run grind.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Message-text change in src/ortus/commands/grind.py: extend the readiness-skip follow-up error and the skip warn to name the `human` label and the `bd label remove <id> human` step, plus matching test updates in tests/test_grind.py.

## Non-goals

- Do NOT auto-remove the `human` label when a spec becomes ready. The label is also grind's escalation channel (escalate_fn at src/ortus/commands/grind.py:1061 applies the same label when a worker hands an issue to a human); auto-clearing on readiness would silently un-park issues a human parked deliberately.
- No change to _flag_unready_for_human's labeling or commenting behavior, to EXCLUDED_LABELS, or to the readiness validator.
- No new grind flags or verbs.

## Concrete locations

- src/ortus/commands/grind.py:1304-1308 — the follow_up string ("follow-up: bd update <id> ... then re-run: ortus grind <target>"); add the label-removal step, e.g. "... to readiness schema v1, then: bd label remove <id> human, then re-run: ortus grind <target>".
- src/ortus/commands/grind.py:1264-1270 — the console warn ending "It stays open and unclaimed. Run ortus plan or edit the work spec."; append that grind has labeled it `human` and the label must be removed after repair.
- src/ortus/commands/grind.py:663-697 — _flag_unready_for_human(); the bd comment it posts ("readiness schema v1 failed; grind will not repair this packet.") should also name the removal command, since the comment is what a later session reads on the issue.
- tests/test_grind.py:254 — test_grind_unready_flags_human() and siblings (lines 291, 324, 359) assert on labels and log text; extend the relevant assertions to cover the new wording.

## Resolved decisions

- Fix the messages, not the mechanism: the label's queue-exclusion behavior is intentional (human-flagged issues must not keep the queue non-empty), and the escalation path shares the label, so the safe, minimal fix is telling the operator about the label everywhere the skip is reported (console follow-up, console warn, bd comment).
- Include the literal command with the concrete issue id (`bd label remove <id> human`), not prose — the surrounding follow-up already interpolates the id and target, and operators copy-paste these lines.

## Compatibility constraints

- Log-line consumers: tests/test_grind.py greps grind's log and console output; wording changes must update those assertions in the same commit. No other machine consumer parses these strings (the log is operator-facing).
- The bd comment format gains a line; bd comments are free text, no schema.

## Ordered steps

1. Extend the follow_up string at src/ortus/commands/grind.py:1304-1308 with the `bd label remove <id> human` step.
2. Extend the skip warn at src/ortus/commands/grind.py:1264-1270 to say grind labels the issue `human` and repair alone does not re-queue it.
3. Extend the bd comment in _flag_unready_for_human (src/ortus/commands/grind.py:690-692) with the same removal command.
4. Update the assertions in tests/test_grind.py (test_grind_unready_flags_human and the tests at lines 291, 324, 359) to match, asserting the removal command appears in the follow-up/log/comment.
5. Run the acceptance commands.

## Dependencies

None blocking — independent of the CI-red fixes (ortus-oamr, ortus-trex, and the smoke-fixture issue); touches only grind messaging. Code consumers of the changed strings: tests/test_grind.py only.

## Edge cases

- A failed `bd label add` already warns and continues (src/ortus/commands/grind.py:679-686); in that path the issue is NOT labeled, so the new message must not claim it was — either keep the existing not-labeled warn as-is or word the follow-up so it reads correctly in both cases (e.g. "if labeled human, remove it: ...").
- Multiple unready leaves print one follow-up each; each must carry its own id in the removal command.
- The dedupe of skip warnings (console-only dedupe keyed on issue id, src/ortus/commands/grind.py:1150) must keep deduping after the wording change.

## Plan-gap guidance

If implementation reveals another consumer of the `human` label or of these log strings beyond tests/test_grind.py (e.g. a dashboard or the repair path parsing comments), stop, record PLAN-GAP on this issue with what was found, preserve candidate state, and route to planning rather than choosing new semantics for the label.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1 (proves-new): the follow-up names the label removal — `rg -q "bd label remove" src/ortus/commands/grind.py`
- AC-2 (guards-existing): the grind suite passes with the new wording — `uv run pytest tests/test_grind.py -q`
close_reason: Readiness-skip remediation now names the human label everywhere the skip is reported (follow-up, warn, bd comment) with the literal bd label remove command; AC-1 rg check and AC-2 tests/test_grind.py both pass

comments.author: who
comments.text: Done: every surface reporting the readiness skip now names the human label and the way back into the queue. The exit follow-up and the bd comment posted by _flag_unready_for_human carry the literal 'bd label remove <id> human' step; the selection-time console warn words it conditionally since it fires before labeling and a ready sibling can preempt flagging. Label removal stays in the follow-up on label-add failure (removing an absent label is harmless; the warn already reports the refusal). AC-1: rg -q 'bd label remove' src/ortus/commands/grind.py — pass. AC-2: uv run pytest tests/test_grind.py -q — 50 passed, 26 skipped (pre-existing f2he.2 skips).

title: README: document init managed agent files and --backend all
description:
## Objective

Update `README.md` so `ortus init` is documented as: default `--backend all` provisions every backend's config, pins a concrete run backend, writes managed AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md blocks without clobbering host prose, and `ortus check` reports agent-file drift plus informational rows for sibling backends.

## Behavioral context

Before: Quick start and The verbs say init takes `--backend claude|codex|grok` and adds AGENTS.md plus "the selected backend's config directory". Agent backends says "Claude remains the default" and select Codex/Grok at creation. Check is described as verifying the selected agent only. Session-close says the generated AGENTS.md repeats the protocol.

After: init's default is `all` (provision three configs, pin `backend = "claude"` unless a concrete `--backend` is passed). AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are managed blocks (`block=agents` / `block=pointer`); re-init is safe; `AGENTS.override.md` is never touched. Check is two-tier. Claude remains the *run* default so existing README tests keep that sentence.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

- Quick start note: list files init writes, including CLAUDE.md; say host prose outside Ortus markers is preserved; do not list runtime prompt files.
- Verbs table `ortus init` row: `--backend all|claude|codex|grok`, default `all` is provisioning-only; `.ortusrc` backend is always concrete.
- Agent backends: keep "Claude remains the default" as the run default; explain `all` vs a concrete pin; reject documenting `backend = "all"` as valid config.
- Configuration example: keep `backend = "claude"`; add a one-line note that `all` is invalid there.
- Mention `ortus check` warnings for provisioned-but-not-runnable sibling backends and errors for missing/malformed/gitignored agent-file blocks.
- Session-close sentence can keep "the generated AGENTS.md repeats this"; add that the protocol lives inside the managed block.
- Extend README tests so `--backend all` and CLAUDE.md / managed-block wording cannot silently vanish.
- Do not edit generated state-graph or glossary blocks.

## Non-goals

- No `ortus prompt` README work (sibling leaf).
- No implementation of init/check. Document what .4 and .5 shipped.
- No new markdown file under `docs/`.

## Concrete locations

- `README.md` — `## Quick start` (the file-list note after the code block), `## The verbs` init row, `## Agent backends`, `## Configuration`, `## Session-close protocol`.
- `tests/test_cli.py` — `test_readme_lists_grok_backend()`.
- `src/ortus/commands/init.py` — landed `--backend` help; README must match it.
- `src/ortus/commands/check.py` — landed check table (WARN vs FAIL).

## Resolved decisions

1. Wait for .4 and .5 so the README describes shipped flags and check rows, not the draft spec.
2. "Claude remains the default" stays, meaning the run backend. Init default `all` is explained in the same section without deleting that sentence (`test_readme_lists_grok_backend` requires it).
3. Do not paste the full agents/pointer block templates into the README. Point at the markers and `ortus init` / `ortus check`.
4. Generated regions stay machine-owned.

## Compatibility constraints

- Public README; no downstream names.
- Grok 10k / Codex 32 KiB caps are implementation constraints, not README requirements, unless a one-line "keep your own AGENTS.md short" note is already natural.
- Existing `backend = "claude"` TOML example remains valid.

## Ordered steps

1. Read landed `ortus init --help` and `ortus check` output/copy.
2. Patch Quick start, verbs, Agent backends, Configuration, and the session-close AGENTS.md sentence.
3. Add or extend README assertions for `all`, CLAUDE.md, and managed blocks.
4. Run Targeted tests. Confirm generated spans are untouched.

## Dependencies

Blocked by ortus-apv5.4 (managed blocks + check agent-file) and ortus-apv5.5 (`--backend all` + two-tier check).

## Edge cases

- If .5 pins something other than claude under `all`, document the landed pin.
- If check warning wording differs from the spec, quote the landed message.
- Quick start code block can stay `ortus init .` with no flag; the default is `all`.

## Plan-gap guidance

Stop if landed init help and the spec disagree on default or on whether CLAUDE.md is always written. Do not document `backend = "all"` as legal. Do not hand-edit generated blocks.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1 (proves-new): README documents init --backend all and CLAUDE.md as a managed pointer file. `rg -n "backend all|CLAUDE.md" README.md`
- AC-2 (proves-new): a test fails if those phrases disappear from the README. `uv run pytest tests/test_cli.py -q --test-timeout=30`
- AC-3 (guards-existing): Agent backends still says Claude remains the default and still names grok. `uv run pytest tests/test_cli.py::test_readme_lists_grok_backend -q --test-timeout=30`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_cli.py tests/test_glossary_docs.py tests/test_state_graph_docs.py -n auto --test-timeout=30`

title: README: document ortus prompt list/show/eject
description:
## Objective

Update `README.md` so a human can discover the runtime-prompt door: `ortus prompt list`, `show`, and `eject`, the three-layer resolution order, and that `ortus init` never copies those files into a consumer repo.

## Behavioral context

Before: The verbs table lists init through unlock and has no `prompt` verb. Quick start and Agent backends never mention inspecting or overriding bundled prompts. The prompt-subsystem spec says human-facing discovery of `ortus prompt list` belongs in the README, not in AGENTS.md.

After: The verbs table includes `ortus prompt`. A short operator section (not inside the generated glossary or state-graph blocks) documents list/show/eject, `--origin`, `--user`/`--force` on eject, resolution (repo override, user override, bundled), and check warnings for stale or unknown overrides. AGENTS.md is not told to point at these verbs.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

- Add `ortus prompt` to the verbs table in `README.md` (`## The verbs`).
- Add a short section (heading decided in this leaf, placed near Configuration or after The verbs) covering: `list [<repo>]`, `show <name> [<repo>]` (stdout is the prompt; header on stderr; `--origin`), `eject <name> <repo>` and `eject --user` / `--force`, no `eject --all`, first-hit-wins layers (`.ortus/prompts/`, `~/.ortus/prompts/`, bundled), check warns on stamp drift / unstamped / unknown filenames.
- State explicitly that init does not write runtime prompts and that AGENTS.md does not point at them.
- Extend `tests/test_cli.py` (or a sibling README assertion) so a missing `ortus prompt` row or missing list/show/eject names fails the suite.
- Do not edit `<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: state-graph -->` or `<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: glossary -->` blocks.

## Non-goals

- No AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / `--backend all` README work (sibling leaf).
- No implementation of the verbs; this leaf only documents what .1 and .2 shipped.
- No new operator guide file; README only.

## Concrete locations

- `README.md` — `## The verbs` (line 73), `## Quick start` (line 42), `## Configuration` (line 148).
- `tests/test_cli.py` — `test_readme_lists_grok_backend()` is the existing README assertion pattern; add a prompt-verbs assertion beside it.
- `src/ortus/cli.py` — `app.command` list; the README row must match the shipped sub-app.

## Resolved decisions

1. Document the verbs after they exist (.1 and .2). Do not invent flag names; copy `--help` from the landed CLI.
2. Keep the section short. Resolution table plus three verbs. No copy-paste of goal-prompt.md.
3. Generated README regions stay machine-owned.
4. `test_readme_lists_grok_backend` must still pass; do not weaken "claude remains the default" (that is the run default, not init `--backend all`).

## Compatibility constraints

- Public README; no downstream project names or issue ids.
- Linux/macOS only already stated; do not add Windows.
- Glossary `session-close` row still points at `goal-prompt.md` until a glossary leaf exists; do not hand-edit that generated row.

## Ordered steps

1. Read landed `ortus prompt --help` / list / show / eject and the check warning copy.
2. Patch the verbs table and add the prompt section.
3. Add a README assertion test for the new verb names.
4. Run Targeted tests. Confirm generated markers are untouched (`git diff README.md` has no hits inside the BEGIN/END generated spans).

## Dependencies

Blocked by ortus-apv5.1 (list/show) and ortus-apv5.2 (eject + check warnings). Documenting flags that have not landed is a plan-gap.

## Edge cases

- If the landed CLI uses a different subcommand layout than `ortus prompt list|show|eject`, document what shipped, not the spec draft.
- Quick start stays a short bootstrap; do not stuff eject into the first code block. One line or a "see Runtime prompts" pointer is enough.
- Zip-backed bundled path: do not claim `--origin` prints a filesystem path for bundled.

## Plan-gap guidance

Stop if .1/.2 shipped a different verb name, or if documenting eject would require pasting a full prompt into the README. Do not edit generated blocks to mention the prompt subsystem.

title: Dashboard think feed paints each Grok think word as its own line
description:
## Objective

Stop the dashboard Grok think feed from painting each streamed think token as its own line. Consecutive `thought` words from one paragraph must share one `think` row.

## Behavioral context

Before. Grok writes one JSON event per token: `{"type":"thought","data":"Now"}` then `{"type":"thought","data":"git"}` then `{"type":"thought","data":"push"}` (see grind logs). `classify_crumb` turns every event into a `Crumb`. `ingest_crumbs` appends each. `crumb_panel` joins crumbs with newlines. The live think animation is therefore:

```
think  Now
think  I
think  need
think  to
```

`ortus tail` already coalesces the same stream (`_expand_grok_paragraph` in `src/ortus/commands/tail.py`): consecutive thought/text events without a newline in `data` are one paragraph.

After. Consecutive same-kind `thought` (and `text`) tokens that do not contain a newline append onto the current crumb (space-joined). The feed shows `think  Now I need to run git push`. A newline in `data`, or a kind change (tool), starts a new crumb. `CRUMB_FEED_LINES` still bounds paragraphs, not tokens. Claude stays sparse.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Coalesce token-stream think/text crumbs in `ingest_crumbs` (or a helper next to `classify_crumb`). Update dashboard crumb tests that assume one thought event = one feed line. Do not change tail except to keep the same paragraph rule.

## Non-goals

Do not change tool crumbs or the tool row. Do not change Claude panels. Do not raise `CRUMB_FEED_LINES`. Do not re-parse the whole log each tick. Do not change grind's thought JSON.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/commands/dashboard.py` — `classify_crumb`, `ingest_crumbs`, `crumb_panel`, `CRUMB_THINK`, `CRUMB_FEED_LINES`.
- `src/ortus/commands/tail.py` — `_expand_grok_paragraph` (the paragraph rule to match).
- `tests/test_dashboard.py` — `test_grok_feed_is_bounded_to_newest_n` (40 thought events would become one paragraph; bound on paragraph breaks instead) plus a new token-stream case.
- CodeGraph: `ingest_crumbs` `classify_crumb` `crumb_panel` (2026-08-15).

## Resolved decisions

Coalesce in the dashboard ingest path. Match tail: no newline in `data` means same paragraph; `\n` in `data` starts a new crumb. Join tokens with a single space. Clip the coalesced line with `CRUMB_TEXT_CHARS`. Tool events flush the open paragraph.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux + macOS. Textual dashboard, Grok backend only. Incremental `events` tail must still work: a token on tick N+1 appends to the last think crumb from tick N when kinds match.

## Ordered steps

1. When ingesting a thought/text crumb, if the feed's last crumb is the same kind and the new token has no newline, append to that crumb instead of pushing a new one.
2. Keep `arrived` as the count of events classified (rate), not new rows.
3. Rewrite the bounded-N test to use paragraph breaks; add a word-at-a-time think test.
4. Run `tests/test_dashboard.py`.

## Dependencies

None. Follow-on to ortus-dp36 / ortus-haxd, not blocked by them.

## Edge cases

Empty `data` stays dropped. A thought then a tool then a thought is two think crumbs. Replay and live share `ingest_crumbs`. A 10k token burst still caps at `CRUMB_FEED_LINES` **paragraphs**.

## Plan-gap guidance

If Textual wraps a long think line onto many rows, that is wrap, not one crumb per word — still coalesce. Do not fix wrap by splitting tokens into lines.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1 (proves-new): consecutive Grok `thought` events whose `data` is one word each become a single `think` feed line, not one line per word.
- AC-2 (guards-existing): the crumb feed is still bounded to `CRUMB_FEED_LINES` paragraphs; Claude snapshots still have an empty crumb feed.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_dashboard.py -q --test-timeout=30`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_dashboard.py -q --test-timeout=30`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_dashboard.py -q --test-timeout=30`
close_reason: Consecutive Grok thought tokens now share one think feed row

- `classify_crumb` records `ends_paragraph` when the token's raw data contains a newline so a later tick can append or start a new row
- `test_grok_token_stream_thoughts_share_one_think_row` drives a word-at-a-time thought stream; `test_grok_feed_is_bounded_to_newest_n` bounds on paragraph breaks

title: Add a who-only workflow_dispatch Action that runs ortus grind
description:
## Objective
Implement a manual-only GitHub Action workflow that executes `ortus grind` on the default branch, restricted to actor `who`, to claim and close ready beads via the bd tracker.

## Behavioral context
The workflow mirrors local `ortus grind .` behavior but runs hosted on ubuntu-latest. It hydrates the tracker from JSONL, installs required tools including CodeGraph and bubblewrap, selects a backend via input, invokes the grind CLI with worker parameters, and uploads logs. Non-`who` actors receive a no-op failure. Concurrency prevents overlapping runs on main.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
New `.github/workflows/grind.yml` with workflow_dispatch, who-allowlist, bd hydration, and `uv run ortus grind` invocation.

## Non-goals
No schedules, no push/PR triggers, no macOS runner, no --repair-unready, no changes to ingest workflow.

## Concrete locations
`.github/workflows/grind.yml` (new file) and `src/ortus/commands/grind.py:grind` (CLI entrypoint with --tasks/--backend/--worker-timeout).

## Resolved decisions
Use existing pins from test.yml and hydrate pattern from bead-from-issue.yml; fail-closed on missing backend secrets.

## Compatibility constraints
Linux ubuntu-latest only; Python 3.12; bd 1.2.1; CodeGraph 1.5.0.

## Ordered steps
1. Create grind.yml with allowlist if:, inputs, concurrency group grind-main (cancel-in-progress: false), and permissions contents:write.
2. Add checkout@v7 (ref:main), uv setup, python 3.12, bd 1.2.1, hydrate via bootstrap, Node+CodeGraph, bubblewrap.
3. Install selected backend CLI and fail if secret absent.
4. Configure git user, run grind command, upload logs artifact.

title: Reinstall PATH ortus from this tree (unsandboxed)
description:
## Objective

From a process that can write `~/.local`, force-install this tree so the `ortus` on PATH is post-`b966f92` and default `ortus tail` prints one `=== TAILING:` line.

## Behavioral context

Before. A landlock/seccomp worker on this host cannot `uv tool install --force .` (`Permission denied` under `~/.local/share/uv/tools`). PATH `ortus` stays `0.1.5.dev222+gb8acf08` and prints many `=== TAILING:` banners. `uv run ortus tail --verbose --lines 1` already prints one banner because `ortus-rjsp` is in `src/ortus/commands/tail.py` (`_selected_logs`).

After. An unsandboxed `uv tool install --force .` from the repo root replaces `~/.local/bin/ortus`. `ortus --version` is not `gb8acf08`. `ortus tail --verbose --lines 1` prints exactly one `=== TAILING:` line.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Run `uv tool install --force .` from an unsandboxed shell with write access to `~/.local/share/uv/tools` and `~/.local/bin`. Confirm PATH version and one-banner default tail. Do not edit `src/ortus/commands/tail.py` unless PATH and `uv run` both still multi-follow after that install.

## Non-goals

Do not reopen `ortus-rjsp`. Do not delete old logs. Do not change `--all`. Do not add a version-nag. Do not treat a sandboxed worker's Permission denied as a packaging pin.

## Concrete locations

- Installed entry: `~/.local/bin/ortus` → `~/.local/share/uv/tools/ortus/bin/ortus`
- Source already on tree: `src/ortus/commands/tail.py` function `_selected_logs`
- Proof already on tree: `tests/test_tail.py` function `test_default_follow_renders_only_newest_of_two_grind_logs`
- CodeGraph: `_selected_logs` → `_newest_log` → `_follow`

## Resolved decisions

This leftover exists because `ortus-rqnl` confirmed the tree is post-rjsp and the criterion-check suite passed, but the worker could not replace the PATH wheel. The remaining action is machine-local install, so this issue is labeled `human`.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux + macOS. `uv tool install` is how Ortus is distributed. hatch-vcs version comes from `git describe`; a dirty tree is acceptable if the commit is after `b966f92`.

## Ordered steps

1. From an unsandboxed terminal in the repo root, run `uv tool install --force .`
2. Run `ortus --version` and confirm it is not `gb8acf08`
3. Run `ortus tail --verbose --lines 1` and confirm exactly one `=== TAILING:` line
4. Only if step 3 still lists many files after a successful install: treat it as a `_selected_logs` regression (PLAN-GAP), not another install ticket

## Dependencies

Discovered from `ortus-rqnl`. No open code blocker. Callers are the operator's PATH. Consumers are `ortus tail` on PATH.

## Edge cases

A second checkout with an old install still reproduces until that machine reinstalls. `--all` must still show many banners. A worker that cannot write `~/.local` must not close this by rewriting tail.

## Plan-gap guidance

If `uv tool install --force .` exits 0 and `ortus --version` still prints `dev222+gb8acf08`, the packaging/version pin is the bug — stop and record PLAN-GAP rather than editing tail. If install still gets Permission denied from a sandboxed worker, leave this issue labeled `human` and do not claim it again in that sandbox.

title: GHA: labeled GitHub issues become readiness-v1 beads
description:
## Objective

When a GitHub issue in who/ortus is labeled `bead` **and filed by GitHub user `who`**, a GitHub Action turns it into a readiness-v1 bead (`bd create`), commits `.beads/issues.jsonl`, comments the new id, and closes the GitHub issue. Example intake: https://github.com/who/ortus/issues/14

## Behavioral context

Before. GitHub issues (e.g. #14) stay on GitHub. Beads live in local Dolt plus the git export `.beads/issues.jsonl`. There is no path from a remote GH ticket into the queue. #14 is open: “create a way to translate github issues into beads” / “match the spec” / “test pipeline.”

After. Label `bead` on an issue (create or later) runs `.github/workflows/bead-from-issue.yml`. The job **exits without creating a bead** unless `github.event.issue.user.login == 'who'`. If the author is `who`, it checks out `main`, installs `bd` the same way `test.yml` does, imports tracker state from the checkout, calls Grok (`XAI_API_KEY`) to write a readiness v1 packet from the issue title/body, runs `validate_issue`, then `bd create` with `external-ref: gh-<n>`. It exports JSONL, commits and pushes that export, attempts `bd dolt push` (failure is logged, job still succeeds if git push worked), comments `filed as ortus-xxxx` on the GH issue, and closes the GH issue. A second run on the same issue is a no-op (already has `gh-<n>` or the filed comment). Issues from any other GitHub user are ignored (no comment, no close, no bead).
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

One workflow plus a small Python helper Ortus can test: GH issue JSON → author gate → Grok → validate_issue → bd create → export → git commit/push → optional dolt push → GH comment+close. Trigger: `issues` types `labeled` and `opened` when label `bead` is present **and** the issue author is GitHub login `who`.

## Non-goals

No two-way sync. No PR-from-issue. No unlabeled issues. No issues authored by anyone other than `who`. No Claude/GitHub-Models path. Do not invent a second tracker. Do not change grind. Downstream project names stay out of packets.

## Concrete locations

- `.github/workflows/bead-from-issue.yml` — new. Author `if:` on `github.event.issue.user.login == 'who'` (job-level, before checkout/secrets). Checkout, install bd (copy pin/version from `.github/workflows/test.yml`, currently 1.2.1), run helper, commit JSONL, push, comment/close.
- New helper under `src/ortus/` or `scripts/` invoked by the workflow (prefer a tested module, e.g. `src/ortus/core/github_bead.py` + a thin CLI or `python -m`). Responsibilities: enforce author `who`, call Grok, `validate_issue`, `bd create --external-ref gh-<n>`, idempotency check.
- `src/ortus/core/readiness.py` — `validate_issue` is the gate; do not fork a second schema.
- `tests/test_github_bead.py` — mapping, idempotency, validate-fail does not create, **non-`who` author does not create**.
- CodeGraph: `validate_issue` `BdClient.create`. Operator interview 2026-08-15: GHA+bd+JSONL+dolt, full v1 via Grok, label `bead`, author must be `who`, comment+close GH, dolt fail is non-fatal, implement the workflow.

## Resolved decisions

Write path: checkout + `bd create` + commit JSONL + `bd dolt push` when possible. Packet: full readiness v1 from the GH body via Grok (`XAI_API_KEY`). Opt-in label: `bead`. **Author allowlist: only GitHub login `who`.** After success: comment the bead id and close the GH issue. If dolt push fails: still keep the JSONL commit and the GH close. Idempotent on `external-ref` `gh-<number>` or an existing bot comment. Grok output that fails `validate_issue` is PLAN-GAP for that run: comment the diagnostic on the GH issue, do not create, do not close.

Non-`who` author: skip. Do not comment, do not close, do not spend `XAI_API_KEY`. Enforce in the workflow `if:` **and** in the helper so a local/miswired invoke cannot bypass it.

Bot git identity: `github-actions[bot]`. Permissions: `contents: write`, `issues: write`. Branch: `main` only.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux GHA runner. bd 1.2.1 as in test.yml. Requires repo secret `XAI_API_KEY`. Requires `GITHUB_TOKEN` (default). Dolt remote credentials if dolt push is attempted — document the secret name if one exists, otherwise skip dolt when unset. Linux + macOS project; this workflow is Linux-only. The allowlist is the literal login `who`, not a display name.

## Ordered steps

1. Helper: reject unless author login is `who`; GH issue payload → prompt Grok for v1 fields → `validate_issue` → return packet or diagnostic.
2. Helper: `bd create` with external-ref; skip if `gh-<n>` already exists.
3. Workflow YAML: trigger on label `bead`, job `if:` author is `who`, install bd, import/export, commit JSONL, push, comment+close.
4. Tests for author reject, validate-fail, idempotency, and field mapping without a live Grok call (mock).
5. Document the `bead` label, `who` allowlist, and `XAI_API_KEY` in the workflow header comment only — no new README chapter unless one line under Development is needed.

## Dependencies

No blocking issue. Example ticket: GH #14 (author `who`). Callers: GitHub Actions. Consumers: `bd ready` / grind after the JSONL lands.

## Edge cases

Issue labeled `bead` then unlabeled then labeled again: second run must no-op if bead exists. Someone else files an issue and a collaborator adds `bead`: skip (author is not `who`). `who` files and someone else adds the label: proceed (author is `who`). Grok returns extra prose around JSON: parse defensively or fail validate. Empty body: Grok still must produce v1 or the job comments failure. Concurrent labels: one workflow concurrency group per issue number. JSONL commit conflicts: rebase-or-retry once. `bd create` succeeds, git push fails: leave GH open and report; do not close GH on a bead that never left the runner.

## Plan-gap guidance

If Grok cannot be called from GHA without a secret the operator has not created, stop and comment on this bead rather than shipping a workflow that always fails. If `bd create` on a fresh checkout cannot see Dolt and JSONL import is the only path, use import-then-create-then-export — do not hand-edit JSONL. If validate_issue cannot pass without a live model, tests stay mocked and the workflow is the live proof. Do not expand the allowlist without an operator decision.

title: Dashboard runs with no grind-transaction journal
description:
## Objective

`ortus dashboard` opens and stays useful with no `logs/grind-transaction.json`. Candidate/verdict regions do not require a journal. No dashboard code imports `CandidateJournal` after child 3.

## Behavioral context

Before. Dashboard reads the journal for header, candidate paths, verdict criteria, replay. Without a journal it already has idle strings, but many tests and some live paths construct `CandidateJournal`. After grind stops writing a journal (child 2), live dashboard would be idle-or-broken unless this leaf lands.

After. Live mode follows the newest grind log only (same as runstate `find_log`). Header/action/warnings come from the log. Candidate/verdict either idle with honest copy (no journal) or derive what they can from the log — they do not open a JournalStore. Tests do not require a journal fixture for idle/live-from-log.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Dashboard journal coupling: imports, idle/live frames, tests that save `CandidateJournal`. Align copy with lean grind (no "transaction in flight" if we are not writing one).

## Non-goals

Do not implement Grok NOC (ortus-dp36 is closed). Do not add a new persistence format. Do not change `ortus tail`.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/commands/dashboard.py` — `JournalStore`, candidate/verdict panels, `HEADER_IDLE` / `CANDIDATE_IDLE` / `VERDICT_IDLE`.
- `src/ortus/core/runstate.py` — `read_snapshot` journal fields.
- `tests/test_dashboard.py` — fixtures that `JournalStore.save(CandidateJournal(...))`.
- CodeGraph: `read_snapshot` `JournalStore` `candidate_panel` `verdict_panel`.

## Resolved decisions

Prefer idle/honest "no run record" over inventing candidate paths from git dirty. Action/warnings from the grind log stay. Region *keys* `candidate` and `verdict` may remain so tests that address keys keep working; titles/bodies must not teach journal words if rgs1 already stripped them.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux + macOS. Read-only / no-emoji / missing-textual contracts stay. `--replay` of a log with no sibling journal still renders from the log.

2. Idle and live-from-log frames without JournalStore.

title: tail defaults to the newest log, not every *.log
description:
## Objective

Default `ortus tail` follows only the newest orchestrator log. Today's "every grind-/goal-/ralph-/plan-*.log at once" becomes an opt-in `--all`.

## Behavioral context

Before. `_discover_logs` globs all `PREFIXES` (`grind-`, `goal-`, `ralph-`, `plan-`) and `_follow` attaches a stream to every file, printing `=== TAILING: <name> ===` for each. A repo with years of `logs/` (this one: 100+ files) dumps every historical run on attach. Reproduced 2026-08-14: `_follow(logs, lines=1, iterations=1)` emitted a TAILING banner per file, then a SKIPPED notice and last line for each. Operators watching a live grind cannot see the current worker. The dashboard already picks one file: `runstate.find_log` is newest `grind-*.log` by `(mtime, name)`.

After. Bare `ortus tail` attaches to the single newest matching log (same PREFIXES, same newest-key as `find_log`). If a newer matching log appears (new grind timestamp), it switches to that file and stops following the previous one. `ortus tail --all` restores today's multi-file follow. Empty `logs/` still idles and waits. `--lines` still applies per attach to the file actually followed.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Default log selection in `ortus tail` / `_follow` / `_discover_logs`. Add `--all`. Tests in `tests/test_tail.py` (including `test_multiple_logs_cap_independently`, which becomes `--all` behavior).

## Non-goals

Do not change decoders, `--verbose`/`--tools`/`--system`, or the `--lines` attach cap (ortus-haxd). Do not delete old log files. Do not change `find_log`'s grind-only glob unless sharing the newest-key helper. Do not add a `--replay` path flag in this leaf.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/commands/tail.py` — `PREFIXES`, `_discover_logs`, `_follow` (`for p in _discover_logs` attach-all loop), `tail` Typer options.
- `src/ortus/core/runstate.py` — `find_log` / `_mtime` (reuse newest-key `(mtime, name)`).
- `tests/test_tail.py` — `test_multiple_logs_cap_independently`; add default-newest and switch-on-newer tests.
- CodeGraph: `_discover_logs` `_follow` `find_log` (2026-08-14).

## Resolved decisions

Default follows one file: newest path among `_discover_logs` results, key `(mtime, name)` matching `find_log`. Not grind-only — the newest `plan-`/`goal-` file is correct when that is what last ran; a live grind's growing file wins on mtime.

When a newer matching file appears, switch: attach the new one, drop the old stream. Do not keep following yesterday's grind after today's starts.

`--all` is the escape hatch for today's attach-everything behavior. `test_multiple_logs_cap_independently` moves to `--all` / `follow_all=True`.

No logs: no banner, keep polling (same as today with an empty dir).

## Compatibility constraints

Linux + macOS. Help text must say the default is the newest log and name `--all`. Existing single-log tests stay valid. `--lines` / `--raw` / `--verbose` compose with both modes. Do not break `_follow(..., initial_files=)` if tests inject an explicit set — that path stays "exactly these files."

## Ordered steps

1. Add a failing test: two grind logs, default `_follow` renders only the newest; no TAILING banner for the older.
2. Add a failing test: after a newer grind log appears on iteration 2, follow switches; older file's later appends are not shown.
3. Default `_follow` to newest-only; `--all` / flag keeps the current discover-all loop.
4. Move the independent-cap test onto `--all`. Update help.

## Dependencies

No blocking issue. Related: ortus-haxd (`--lines` vs thinking) is a different slice. Callers: `tail()`. Consumers: `tests/test_tail.py`; operators.

## Edge cases

Two files, same mtime: `name` tie-break matches `find_log`. Newest file deleted mid-follow: rediscover, attach the new newest; do not crash. `--all` then a new file: attach it in addition (today's behavior). `initial_files` set: do not override with newest-only. A `ralph-` file newer than a live grind because something touched it — rare; mtime is still the rule, not a content heuristic.

## Plan-gap guidance

If defaulting to newest-among-PREFIXES vs newest-`grind-*.log` is contradicted by a live operator workflow (plan log stealing a grind tail), record PLAN-GAP with both paths rather than adding a third selector. Do not implement a TUI picker.

- AC-2 (proves-new): When a newer grind log appears while following, output switches to it and later appends to the old file are not shown.
- AC-3 (guards-existing): `--all` still tails every matching log with a per-file --lines cap; single-log and Grok decoder tests still pass.

## Criterion checks

- AC-2: uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py -q --test-timeout=30
- AC-3: uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py -q --test-timeout=30

title: tail --verbose --lines 1 drops current thinking (raw-line cap)
description:
## Objective

Make `ortus tail --verbose --lines 1` (and any small `--lines` attach cap) show the current thinking, not a dropped or one-token crumb.

## Behavioral context

Before. `--verbose` is documented as `--tools --system`, and `--system` is documented to include thinking. Claude `assistant.content[].type=thinking` only renders when `show_system` is true. Grok `type=thought` crumbs already render on the default path (coalesced as `  think  …`). `--lines N` trims *raw log lines* on the attach read in `_follow` (`chunk_lines[-lines:]`) before `_format_line`. A live Grok grind log is one JSON object per token (`{"type":"thought","data":"Now"}`). Reproduced 2026-08-14 on `logs/grind-20260814-163810.log`: last-50 types were thought/text/usage/tool_call; `--lines 1` keep only the last crumb (often `"."` or a `usage` line that the decoder drops). Operators running `ortus tail --verbose --lines 1` therefore see a SKIPPED banner and no useful thinking.

After. `--verbose` still means `--tools --system`. Attach with a small `--lines` still caps history, but the kept window includes the current Grok thought/text paragraph (the coalesce group) and Claude thinking when `--verbose`/`--system` is on. A last-line `usage` / `available_commands` does not hide the think that preceded it. `--lines 0` stays full history.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

`ortus tail` attach-time `--lines` cap and Grok/Claude thinking render under `--verbose`. Tests in `tests/test_tail.py`.

## Non-goals

Do not change default `--lines` (2000). Do not change `--raw`. Do not rewrite the dashboard. Do not change grind logging. Do not make `--lines` mean "last N seconds."

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/commands/tail.py` — `_follow` attach trim (`first_read` + `chunk_lines[-lines:]`); `_render_grok_object` (`type=thought`); `_render_assistant` (`ptype == "thinking" and show_system`); `_GrokCoalesce`.
- `tests/test_tail.py` — `test_attach_caps_history_at_default`, grok thought tests, `test_verbose_renders_every_real_stream_json_category`.
- CodeGraph: `_follow` `_format_line` `_render_grok_object` (2026-08-14). Live log: `logs/grind-20260814-163810.log` last crumbs are per-token `thought`/`text`.

## Resolved decisions

Yes, `--verbose` should output thinking. That is the `--system` contract (`thinking` in the help text) and the Claude `--verbose` tests.

`--lines 1` today means "last 1 raw line at attach," which is the wrong unit for Grok crumbs. The cap stays a line budget, but the attach slice must not start in the middle of a Grok thought/text coalesce group and must not keep only a dropped `usage`/`available_commands` line when a thought sits just above it. Walk back over the skipped prefix (or apply the cap after coalesce) so the current `  think  ` / `  (thinking) ` paragraph is in the attach window. Follow after attach is unchanged.

Claude thinking remains gated on `--verbose`/`--system`. Grok `thought` stays visible on the default path as today; verbose must not hide it.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux + macOS. `--lines 0` remains byte-identical full history for the existing Claude assistant-line fixture. `--raw --lines 1` still means last raw line (no decode). Existing skip-notice still names the trimmed count (may increase if we walk back extra crumbs — state the extra in the notice or keep the notice as raw-skipped; do not lie).

## Ordered steps

1. Add a failing test: a Grok log of many `thought` crumbs plus a trailing `usage` line, `_follow(..., lines=1, show_system=True)` must contain a `  think  ` line from the current paragraph, not only SKIPPED / empty.
2. Add a Claude fixture: last raw line is not thinking, previous assistant part is thinking, `--verbose --lines` small enough to drop it today — after the fix, `(thinking)` appears.
3. Change `_follow` attach trim (walk-back or post-coalesce cap) without changing follow.
4. Keep `--lines 0` and default-2000 tests green.

## Dependencies

No blocking issue. Builds on ortus-zt5n.7 (Grok crumb decoder) and ortus-fc2q (`--lines`). Callers: `ortus.commands.tail.tail`. Consumers: operators watching a grok grind; `tests/test_tail.py`.

## Edge cases

Last line is a complete `tool_call` — show the tool (verbose) plus any flushed think paragraph that immediately preceded it. Last line is plain grind `[YYYY-MM-DD …]` — still show that line; walk-back should not steal the whole file. Empty log: no crash. `--lines 1 --raw`: still last raw line only. Two logs: each has its own cap.

## Plan-gap guidance

If the only way to show "the thinking" is to ignore `--lines` and dump the whole log, PLAN-GAP. If Claude thinking lives only inside an assistant object that is not the last raw line and walking back one event is not enough, record the fixture and extend the walk-back rather than special-casing Claude in a third decoder.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1 (proves-new): A Grok log of many type=thought crumbs ending in usage, tailed with verbose and --lines 1, prints a coalesced think line from the current paragraph.
- AC-2 (proves-new): A Claude log whose last raw line is not thinking, with thinking in the previous assistant event, prints (thinking) under --verbose with a small --lines attach cap.
- AC-3 (guards-existing): Default --lines 2000 cap, --lines 0 full-history, and default Grok think/text/tool rendering still pass.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py -q --test-timeout=30
- AC-2: uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py -q --test-timeout=30
- AC-3: uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py -q --test-timeout=30

## Targeted tests

title: Cut glossary and operator strings to lean /goal vocabulary
description:
## Objective

Cut the README glossary to the six lean `/goal` words plus **session-close**, and strip the killed words from operator-facing Python (logs, dashboard titles, errors, prompts). Internal identifiers stay.

## Behavioral context

Before. README glossary has 19 terms, most from the journal/harness-finalization machine. `goal-prompt.md` only uses work spec, PLAN-GAP, leftover claims, and session-close. Audit (2026-08-14, this ticket): file hits under `src/`+`tests`+`README.md` excluding prd/experiments/.beads — candidate 44, phase 57, verdict 34, journal 30, finalization 23, harness 23, handoff 21, disown 11, seal 10, phase transition 9, degraded 6, tracker export 6, happy path 5. Dashboard still titles regions `candidate` and `verdict`. Grind logs still say `transaction handoff` and `disown`. Goal-prompt's "journal" means `bd events`, colliding with `CandidateJournal`.

After. Glossary TERMS are only: orphan, planning gap, readiness, session-close, task, work spec, worker. README regenerates from that. Operator-facing strings no longer teach candidate, degraded, disown, finalization, handoff, happy path, harness, journal (in the CandidateJournal sense), phase, phase transition, seal, tracker export, or verdict. `CandidateJournal`, `parse_verdict`, `handoff_paths`, dashboard region *keys*, and tests that address those keys stay. Claude/Codex/Grok `/goal` workers still session-close.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

1. Audit (already run; findings in this packet). 2. Delete the kill/maybe-kill rows from `src/ortus/core/glossary.py` `TERMS` and `tests/test_glossary_docs.py` `REQUIRED_TERMS`. 3. Add **session-close**. 4. Rewrite operator-facing strings in dashboard, grind logs/errors, and worker prompts. 5. Regenerate the README glossary block via the renderer.

## Non-goals

Do not delete or rename `CandidateJournal`, `parse_verdict`, `handoff_paths`, `disown`, `FINALIZATION_STEPS`, or dashboard region keys (`candidate`, `verdict`). Do not remove dashboard panels. Do not rewrite grind behavior, reap, or `/goal`. Do not edit PRDs or experiments. Identifier rename and journal-machine deletion are later work.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/core/glossary.py` — `TERMS`. Remove: candidate, degraded, disown, finalization, handoff, happy path, harness, journal, phase, phase transition, seal, tracker export, verdict. Keep: orphan, planning gap, readiness, task, work spec, worker. Add: session-close (home: `src/ortus/prompts/goal-prompt.md` step 4).
- `tests/test_glossary_docs.py` — `REQUIRED_TERMS` must match the new set.
- `README.md` — generated glossary markers only via `render_readme_block`; surrounding prose that names a killed word.
- `src/ortus/commands/dashboard.py` — `RegionSpec` *titles* (not keys), `CANDIDATE_IDLE`, `VERDICT_PENDING`, `header_line` / `verdict_panel` / `candidate_panel` user-visible text.
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` — `write_log` / `output.error` strings using handoff, disown, candidate, verdict, finalization, journal.
- `src/ortus/prompts/goal-prompt.md` — "journal" (bd events) and any killed words; say `bd events` / session-close.
- `src/ortus/prompts/grind-prompt.md` — "leave the candidate edits" and siblings if that prompt is still loaded.
- Audit method: `rg` counts above; CodeGraph on `TERMS render_readme_block RegionSpec header_line` (2026-08-14). Operator decision: strings + glossary only, not identifier rename or machine deletion.

## Resolved decisions

Kill list (kills + maybe-kills from the 2026-08-14 glossary audit): candidate, degraded, disown, finalization, handoff, happy path, harness, journal, phase, phase transition, seal, tracker export, verdict.

Keep: orphan, planning gap, readiness, task, work spec, worker. Add session-close: the worker's commit / `bd close` / `bd dolt push` / `git push` at the end of one issue, after which grind reaps.

Replacement wording (operator-facing only): grind not harness; session-close not finalization; owned/unrelated paths not candidate/disown; inherited dirty paths not handoff; acceptance checks / criterion results not verdict; `.beads/` files not tracker export; `bd events` not journal when meaning the tracker log. Do not say seal, phase, phase transition, degraded, or happy path to operators.

Dashboard region keys stay `candidate` and `verdict` so existing tests keep addressing them; only the border title and body copy change. Tests that assert those exact user-visible strings must be updated to the new copy. `tests/test_glossary_docs.py` one-sentence / home / REQUIRED_TERMS rules still apply.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux + macOS. Glossary renderer and `test_glossary_docs.py` / `test_state_graph_docs.py` must still pass. Do not change CLI verb names. Do not change grind's done-bar or `/goal` wrap. Downstream-forbidden names stay out.

## Ordered steps

1. Confirm the audit list against `TERMS` and the file-hit counts in this packet.
2. Edit `TERMS` and `REQUIRED_TERMS`; add session-close; regenerate README glossary.
3. Rewrite dashboard titles and idle/pending copy; keep region keys.
4. Rewrite grind `write_log` / `output.error` lines that teach killed words.
5. Rewrite goal-prompt (and grind-prompt if still shipped) so they do not say journal-in-the-CandidateJournal-sense or the other killed words.
6. Update tests that assert the old operator strings. Run glossary + dashboard + the touched prompt/grind tests.

## Dependencies

No blocking issue. Follows ortus-s1ki (README worker-close story). Do not mix with ortus-dp36 (Grok NOC). Callers: README renderer, dashboard, grind logs. Consumers: `tests/test_glossary_docs.py`, `tests/test_dashboard.py`.

## Edge cases

A test that greps the word `candidate` in source comments is implementer-facing — leave it. A test that asserts dashboard body `idle - no candidate captured` must change. Goal-prompt "The journal starts at enable" is beads events — reword to `bd events`, do not delete the step. `phase` in "CodeGraph phase contract" is a different sense — keep that phrase or say "CodeGraph contract"; do not invent a third name. Regenerating README must not hand-edit inside glossary markers.

## Plan-gap guidance

If cleaning a string requires changing grind control flow (who closes, what gets committed, whether disown still happens), stop and record PLAN-GAP — this leaf is vocabulary, not a pipeline rewrite. If a required test asserts a killed word as an operator contract and there is no agreed replacement in Resolved decisions, PLAN-GAP rather than invent a fourth synonym. Do not delete `CandidateJournal` or a dashboard region in this ticket.

title: Audit README.md terms and graphics; ask before kill or update
description:
## Objective

Audit every term and graphic in README.md. Inventory anything that may be stale, leftover, or no longer true, ask the operator kill / update / keep on each item, and apply only those recorded verdicts.

## Behavioral context

Before. README.md is the operator-facing map of Ortus. It mixes hand-written prose (install, eight verbs, backends, why, configuration, readiness, corrections, CodeGraph, session-close, development) with two generated, test-enforced blocks (state-graph mermaid + transition tables from `src/ortus/core/lifecycle.py`, glossary table from `src/ortus/core/glossary.py`). A CI badge and a CodeGraph log excerpt are the other graphics. Nothing currently forces the hand-written terms to match the product: `ortus dashboard` is a shipped verb and is absent from "The eight verbs"; `ortus tail` still advertises `logs/{grind,goal,ralph}-*.log`; bd is described as "backed by embedded Dolt"; workers are said to be forbidden to close, commit, or push. An earlier lean-pipeline docs audit (ortus-l2u9.5) rewrote surrounding prose against a pipeline that may or may not be what grind does today. Guessing which of those to delete would silently rewrite the product story.

After. Every suspect term and graphic has a numbered inventory item and an operator verdict (kill, update-to-X, or keep). README.md then matches those verdicts and nothing else. Generated marker interiors change only by editing the declaration and regenerating. Unmentioned terms and graphics stay.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

README.md only: headings, tables, lists, prose terms of art, the CI badge, mermaid state diagrams, the CodeGraph log excerpt, and the generated glossary table. The audit is two phases on this one issue: (1) inventory + ask, (2) apply recorded verdicts. Source changes in `src/ortus/core/lifecycle.py` or `src/ortus/core/glossary.py` are in scope only when the operator's verdict on a generated term or graph is update or kill.

## Non-goals

Do not audit AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, template READMEs, or PRDs. Do not add a new graphic, badge, or mermaid diagram. Do not rename vocabulary in runtime code just to tidy the README. Do not hand-edit inside `<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: state-graph -->` / `<!-- END GENERATED: state-graph -->` or `<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: glossary -->` / `<!-- END GENERATED: glossary -->`. Do not treat this packet's starter-suspect list as a kill list. Do not close the issue at the end of the inventory phase.

## Concrete locations

- `README.md` — the only document. Graphics today: the GitHub Actions badge (line 3), two mermaid `stateDiagram-v2` blocks plus their transition tables inside the state-graph markers, the CodeGraph probe log excerpt under CodeGraph lifecycle. Terms live in every hand-written section plus the generated glossary.
- `src/ortus/core/lifecycle.py` — `render_readme_block`, `BEGIN_MARKER` / `END_MARKER`. Hand-edits inside the markers fail `tests/test_state_graph_docs.py`.
- `src/ortus/core/glossary.py` — `render_glossary_table`. Hand-edits inside the glossary markers fail `tests/test_glossary_docs.py`.
- `src/ortus/cli.py` / `src/ortus/commands/` — the live verb set the "eight verbs" table must be checked against (dashboard is a shipped verb).
- CodeGraph: `codegraph_explore` on `render_readme_block render_glossary_table BEGIN GENERATED README` (2026-08-14).

## Resolved decisions

The operator decides every kill, update, or keep. The worker never deletes or rewrites a term or graphic because it "looks" stale. The ask is the work: a numbered inventory posted as a `bd comment` on this issue, then a stop.

Each inventory item is one row:

1. Item id (I-1, I-2, …)
2. Location (heading + a short verbatim quote)
3. Kind (term or graphic)
4. Why it may be stale or unused (code/CLI contradiction, leftover name, generated vs live behavior)
5. Recommended action (kill / update / keep) and, for update, the proposed replacement
6. If the text sits inside a generated marker, say so and name the source file — the ask is then about changing the declaration, not the README interior

Starter suspects the inventory must include (still asks, not decisions): "The eight verbs" vs the live CLI; `ortus tail` advertising `logs/{grind,goal,ralph}-*.log`; "issue tracking (backed by embedded Dolt)"; "No backend's worker may close an issue, commit, or push"; session-close `git add -A`; the Ralph Loop sentence; the leftover `(FR-025)` marker; whether the corrections/finalization/recovery prose and the two mermaid graphs still describe grind; any glossary row whose code home or sense is gone.

How to ask: post the inventory as a bd comment. If this is an interactive operator session, also print the same list and wait for per-item answers. If this is a grind worker, post the comment, leave the issue `in_progress`, and exit without editing README and without closing — that leftover claim is the ask. A later turn applies only items whose operator reply is on the issue (comment or notes) as kill / update / keep.

Apply rules: kill removes that term or graphic and any sentence that exists only to carry it. Update replaces with the operator's wording. Keep leaves the text. A generated-block verdict of update or kill is implemented in the declaration module, then the README block is regenerated the way those tests already print. An item with no verdict is not touched.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux + macOS docs only; do not reintroduce Windows as supported. Downstream project names and foreign bd ids stay out of README (existing project principle). The two generated marker pairs must remain, even if the operator kills a term inside a declaration — empty or smaller generated content is fine, missing markers are not. `tests/test_state_graph_docs.py` and `tests/test_glossary_docs.py` must pass after any apply. Session-close in README may differ from AGENTS.md; this task does not sync other files unless the operator's update text says to.

## Ordered steps

1. Read README.md end to end. Walk every heading, table, list, badge, mermaid block, log excerpt, and glossary row against the live CLI, grind/backend behavior, and the two declaration modules.
2. Write the numbered inventory, including every starter suspect plus anything else that may not matter. Post it as a bd comment on this issue. Ask the operator kill / update / keep per item.
3. Stop. Do not edit files. Do not close. If under grind, leave `in_progress`.
4. After recorded verdicts exist, apply only those items. Regenerate generated blocks from source when a verdict touches them. Leave unmarked text alone.
5. Run the two docs tests. Close only when every applied hunk traces to a verdict and the tests pass.

## Dependencies

No blocking issue. Related closed work: ortus-l2u9.5 (lean-pipeline docs audit — do not assume its after-state is still true), ortus-hhf0 (generated glossary), ortus-yu7w (generated state graphs), ortus-6oo8 (strip PRD/bd refs). Consumers: operators reading GitHub; `tests/test_state_graph_docs.py`, `tests/test_glossary_docs.py`.

## Edge cases

A term that is still in code but unused in operator-facing CLI is a keep-or-kill ask, not an automatic kill. A graphic that renders (mermaid valid, badge URL 200) can still be stale if it describes the wrong machine — ask. Two suspects in one sentence become two items if they can be decided separately. An operator "update" with no replacement wording is a PLAN-GAP, not a license to invent prose. Inventory-phase interruption: the comment may be partial; resume by appending, do not start applying. A grind that cannot post a bd comment still must not edit README — record PLAN-GAP.

## Plan-gap guidance

Applying any README, glossary.py, or lifecycle.py change without a recorded operator verdict (kill / update / keep) on that inventory id is a PLAN-GAP. Hand-editing inside generated markers is a PLAN-GAP. Expanding the edit set to AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md is a PLAN-GAP. Inventing a replacement graphic or a new verb table layout the operator did not approve is a PLAN-GAP. If live grind behavior and README contradict each other and the operator has not picked which is the story, stop — do not "fix" the README to match an unverified code path.

- AC-2: After apply, every README hunk traces to an operator verdict on an inventory id; items marked keep and anything not inventoried are unchanged; generated marker interiors differ from their renderers only if the operator's verdict changed the declaration and the block was regenerated. `uv run pytest tests/test_state_graph_docs.py tests/test_glossary_docs.py -q`

title: Dashboard Grok mode: animated crumb NOC / oversee view
description:
## Objective

When the dashboard is watching a Grok grind, turn it into a live NOC: animated crumbs, in-flight tool lights, and enough motion that a healthy Grok worker is interesting to watch and a stall is obvious by stillness. Claude and Codex keep the existing sparse instrument panel.

## Behavioral context

Before. `ortus dashboard` is one 1 Hz scanner pulse plus five static regions. Current action names the latest classified tool and its age. `runstate._describe` understands Claude stream-json and a few Codex item kinds; Grok `thought` / `text` / `tool_call` / `tool_call_update` crumbs are not actions, so a Grok think-heavy stretch looks like a silent blocked panel. Grok itself emits those crumbs at high frequency — `ortus tail` already coalesces them — but the dashboard never shows them. The result is a Grok run that is busy in the log and dead on the glass.

After. Detecting a Grok run (log event types, or the journal naming backend grok), the dashboard switches into a Grok oversee mode: a bounded rolling crumb feed, a pulse that reacts to crumb rate, and distinct in-flight / done / fail tool rows. Motion is driven by incoming crumbs and by the refresh tick, so a healthy stream flickers and a hung worker goes still. `--replay` of a Grok log plays the same mode. A Claude or Codex log is visually unchanged.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Grok-mode presentation inside the existing `ortus dashboard` Textual shell: backend detection, a crumb/activity surface, richer pulse animation tied to crumb arrivals, and tests that lock Claude/Codex frames and the read-only / no-emoji contracts.

## Non-goals

Not a rewrite of the dashboard layout for every backend. Not a replacement for `ortus tail` (no full transcript, no paging the whole log). Not a new verb, not a web UI, not fleet/multi-repo. No writes to the repository, bd, or git. Do not invent a third animation framework or pull a new TUI dependency. Do not change grind, the Grok runner, or the tail decoder's public flags.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/commands/dashboard.py` — `REGIONS`, `Frame`, `pulse` / `pulse_line`, `action_panel` / `frame`, `DashboardApp.refresh_run` / `paint`, `_CSS` / palette. Today the only moving element is a 24-cell scanner at `REFRESH_SECONDS = 1.0`.
- `src/ortus/core/runstate.py` — `LogEvent`, `_describe`. Grok top-level `type` values (`thought`, `text`, `tool_call`, `tool_call_update`) are unclassified here, so they never become `latest_action`.
- `src/ortus/commands/tail.py` — `_GROK_EVENT_TYPES`, `_is_grok_event`, `_summarize_grok_tool`, `_GrokCoalesce`. Reuse the detector and tool summary; do not fork a second Grok JSON vocabulary.
- `tests/test_dashboard.py` — visual contract, idle/live/ended frames, read-only `bd_argv`. Add Grok-mode frame tests from fixture crumbs.
- CodeGraph: `codegraph_explore` on `dashboard pulse REGIONS frame action_panel _describe _is_grok_event` (2026-08-14).

## Resolved decisions

Grok mode is detected from the run, not a CLI flag: a log that has emitted a Grok event type, or a journal that names backend grok. Absent that signal, keep today's panels even if `.ortusrc` says grok (an idle repo must not flip into an empty NOC).

The crumb surface is a bounded rolling feed (thought / text / tool), not the coalesced tail paragraph and not the one-line current-action text. Tail stays the place to read prose. The dashboard shows the last N crumbs (N small enough to fit the region, on the order of 8–12 lines) plus an in-flight tool row that lights on `tool_call` and settles on `tool_call_update` completed/failed.

Animation is load-bearing. In Grok mode: (1) refresh faster than 1 Hz (around 250 ms) so crumbs appear as they land rather than in one-second clumps; (2) the pulse reacts to recent crumb rate (wider or denser motion when crumbs are arriving, a slow scanner when they are not); (3) at least two independent moving elements so a single stuck widget cannot fake life. Stillness still means the dashboard or the worker stopped.

Keep the existing visual contract where it is safety, not austerity: dark ground, colour carries meaning (motion / attention / failure), no emoji, box-drawing and filled bars. Grok mode may use more of the motion accent and additional moving rules; it may not introduce pictographs or a light theme.

Reuse `_is_grok_event` / `_summarize_grok_tool` from tail rather than copying the type set. If those helpers are module-private, lift the shared bits to a small importable helper (or import the existing functions) — one vocabulary.

Claude and Codex frames must byte-compare equal to today's renderer for the same snapshot. Grok mode is an additive branch.

Read-only is unchanged: every bd call still goes through `bd_argv` (`--readonly --sandbox`); the crumb feed is parsed from the grind log the snapshot already tails.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux + macOS only, same as the rest of Ortus. Textual remains the only TUI dependency; a missing textual still fails only the dashboard verb with `MISSING_TEXTUAL`. `--replay` of a Grok log must enter Grok mode; `--replay` of a Claude log must not. Existing region keys stay so tests that address `header` / `current-action` / `candidate` / `verdict` / `warnings` keep working; a new region is allowed if it is added to `REGIONS` and `Frame` together. Refresh may be faster in Grok mode only. Markup stays off on regions that render log text (paths and crumbs contain brackets).

## Ordered steps

1. Detect Grok mode from the snapshot/log (and journal backend when present) and thread a boolean through `frame` / `DashboardApp` without changing Claude/Codex output.
2. Classify Grok crumbs in the incremental log tail: thought, text, tool_call, tool_call_update. Reuse tail's detector and tool summary.
3. Render a bounded crumb feed and in-flight tool row; drive pulse density from recent crumb rate; drop refresh interval in Grok mode.
4. Keep idle / ended / replay behaviour: idle repo stays the current idle view; a finished Grok replay freezes the last crumbs and marks tools ended; a mid-run hang (no new crumbs, pulse still ticks slowly) stays distinguishable from a dead dashboard (pulse frozen).
5. Add tests for detection, feed bounding, Claude-unchanged frames, faster grok refresh, and the existing no-emoji / read-only contracts.

## Dependencies

No open blocking issue. `ortus-zt5n.7` is the tail decoder this reuses; those helpers already live in `tail.py`. Parent epic `ortus-0udo` is closed — this is a new leaf, not a child of a closed epic. Callers: `ortus.commands.dashboard.dashboard` via `src/ortus/cli.py`. Consumers: operators watching a grok grind; `tests/test_dashboard.py`.

## Edge cases

A Claude log that happens to contain the substring `thought` must not trip Grok mode — detect on parsed JSON `type`, same as tail. A Grok log that has only grind scheduler lines so far stays on the sparse panel until the first Grok event. A think-only stretch with no tool_call still has to look alive (thought crumbs move the feed and the pulse). A 10k-crumb burst must drop the oldest, never grow the region without bound or re-parse the whole log each tick. `usage` and `available_commands` stay dropped. A tool_call with no later update stays in-flight. Replay of a truncated live log shows crumbs up to the current end. A repo that becomes unreadable mid-run keeps the last frame and still advances the pulse.

## Plan-gap guidance

If journal and log disagree about the backend, record PLAN-GAP with both values rather than picking one silently. If Textual cannot refresh faster than 1 Hz without pegging a CPU-bound grind (measure: dashboard tick vs grind worker on the same host), stop and record PLAN-GAP instead of shipping a 250 ms loop that steals the worker. If the only way to make it "vibrant" is emoji, animation libraries, or a second windowing toolkit, that is a PLAN-GAP — do not add a dependency to win the aesthetic.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1 (proves-new): A Grok crumb snapshot (thought, text, tool_call, tool_call_update) paints a crumb feed and a pulse that changes when more crumbs arrive; a Claude snapshot of the same header/action/candidate/verdict/warnings text paints the pre-change panel with no crumb feed.
- AC-2: The Grok crumb feed is bounded: feeding more crumbs than the region shows keeps only the newest N and does not grow Frame text without bound.
- AC-3: Claude and Codex dashboard frames stay on the existing 1 Hz sparse pulse; Grok mode is the only branch that shortens the refresh interval.
- AC-4 (guards-existing): Read-only and no-emoji contracts still hold: every dashboard bd vector carries --readonly --sandbox, and no Grok-mode string introduces emoji.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: uv run pytest tests/test_dashboard.py -q --test-timeout=30
- AC-2: uv run pytest tests/test_dashboard.py -q --test-timeout=30
- AC-3: uv run pytest tests/test_dashboard.py -q --test-timeout=30
- AC-4: uv run pytest tests/test_dashboard.py -q --test-timeout=30

## Targeted tests

uv run pytest tests/test_dashboard.py -q --test-timeout=30

title: tail: decode Grok streaming-json like pretty-grind-tail
description:
## Objective

Make `ortus tail` (default, not --raw) render Grok grind logs the way scripts/pretty-grind-tail.sh does: coalesced thought/text, one line per tool, grind scheduler lines intact, usage and available_commands dropped.

## Behavioral context

Before. Grok writes streaming-json crumbs (type=thought/text/tool_call/tool_call_update). ortus tail decodes Claude stream-json and Codex exec JSON. Grok lines fall through as raw JSON or get misread. Operators pipe --raw into the bash pretty-printer.

After. Default tail detects Grok events (type thought/text/tool_call) and formats them: think/text paragraphs, tool name plus command-or-path, done/fail on tool_call_update, yellow grind [YYYY-MM-DD …] lines. --raw stays verbatim. Claude and Codex renderers stay as they are.

## Why

Watching a grok grind without this is unreadable. The bash script proved the layout; the product surface is ortus tail.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Add a Grok branch in tail.py next to _render_object / _format_codex_line. Coalesce consecutive thought or text crumbs across lines (stateful decoder, or flush on type change). Tool line: toolName plus rawInput.command or target_file or file_path or query. Pass through non-JSON grind scheduler lines via existing _render_plain (or match pretty-grind-tail colours). Drop type=usage and available_commands. Keep --raw, --tools, --system flags meaningful: thoughts behind --system if that matches Claude thinking; tools behind --tools.

## Non-goals

Do not change GrokRunner --output-format. Do not require jq at runtime. Do not replace Claude/Codex decoders. Do not animate crumbs. scripts/pretty-grind-tail.sh may stay as a reference or be deleted once tail matches; do not invent extra docs.

## Concrete locations

- src/ortus/commands/tail.py — _format_line, _render_object, new _format_grok_line / coalesce state on _LogStream.
- scripts/pretty-grind-tail.sh — layout reference (think / text / tool / done / fail).
- tests for tail grok decode (tests/test_tail.py or sibling).

## Resolved decisions

1. Product decoder is Python in ortus tail, not a jq wrapper.
2. Layout matches the bash script: think, text, tool, done, grind timestamp lines.
3. Coalesce crumbs until type changes or a newline in data.
4. --raw unchanged.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux + macOS. Existing Claude/Codex tail tests stay green. NO_COLOR still disables ANSI.

## Ordered steps

1. Detect Grok event types in _format_line.
2. Implement coalesce + tool summary.
3. Wire --tools/--system.
4. Tests from a fixture slice of a real grind log.

## Dependencies

zt5n epic (grok backend). pretty-grind-tail.sh is the visual spec.

## Edge cases

Truncated JSON line: skip or raw, do not crash. Mixed grind scheduler + grok JSON in one file. tool_call without rawInput.

## Plan-gap guidance

Stop if Grok event shapes in current logs diverge from thought/text/tool_call/tool_call_update enough that one decoder cannot cover them.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1: Default ortus tail on a Grok grind log prints coalesced think/text and one tool line per tool_call, not raw crumb JSON.
- AC-2: --raw still emits the original JSON lines.
- AC-3: usage and available_commands lines are omitted in default mode.
- AC-4: Claude and Codex tail fixtures still render as today.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py -k grok -q --test-timeout=30
- AC-2: uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py -k grok -q --test-timeout=30
- AC-3: uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py -k grok -q --test-timeout=30
- AC-4: uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py -q --test-timeout=30

## Targeted tests

uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py -q --test-timeout=30
close_reason: Default tail coalesces Grok thought/text crumbs and prints one tool line per tool_call

title: grind: restore post-worker CodeGraph handshake after f2he.2 early exit
description:
## Objective

Make grind halt a silent implementation worker under CodeGraph policy required, after the f2he.2 early continue that judges bd status and returns.

## Behavioral context

Before f2he.2, grind parsed the implementation transcript and called require_handshake so a worker that never used CodeGraph MCP failed the iteration. After f2he.2 the loop continues or breaks on bd status first, so that assertion and the handshake-not-required resume log are unreachable. tests/test_grind_codegraph.py dropped the loop-level cases that proved that gate.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Either move require_handshake to a live point after the worker returns and before the bd-status continue, or document that the worker-owned prompt is the only handshake and delete the dead post-worker block.

## Non-goals

Do not restore issue-branch workspaces or Ortus-owned verification. Do not re-inline goal-prompt.md.

## Concrete locations

src/ortus/commands/grind.py around the judged_status continue and require_handshake. tests/test_grind_codegraph.py for any loop-level cases that come back.

## Resolved decisions

1. Product must choose: re-arm the post-worker gate, or accept worker-prompt-only handshake.
2. If re-armed, leftover in_progress resume still spawns a worker and must still handshake.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux + macOS. On-main worker-owns-close. Claude remains default.

## Ordered steps

1. Confirm require_handshake is unreachable after the bd-status continue.
2. Decide re-arm vs delete the dead block.
3. If re-arm, add a live test that a silent worker under required exits non-zero without restoring ScriptedRunner verify.
4. Run the targeted grind and codegraph tests.

## Dependencies

Discovered from ortus-wwfv. Callers are grind after a worker returns.

## Edge cases

A leftover in_progress resume must not be treated as candidate-captured skip. A worker that closed its issue still has to have shaken hands if the gate is re-armed.

## Plan-gap guidance

Stop and record PLAN-GAP if re-arming the gate contradicts f2he.2 (bd status is the only iteration result) and deleting the dead block is the intended product answer.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1: a silent fresh worker under required either halts with the no-CodeGraph-MCP error, or the dead require_handshake block is gone and the tests say so.
- AC-2: leftover in_progress resume still spawns a worker.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: uv run pytest tests/test_grind_codegraph.py tests/test_grind.py -k handshake -q --test-timeout=60
- AC-2: uv run pytest tests/test_grind_recovery.py::test_leftover_claim_with_dirty_work_is_resumed_not_replaced -q --test-timeout=60

## Targeted tests

uv run pytest tests/test_grind_codegraph.py tests/test_grind_recovery.py -q --test-timeout=60
close_reason: Retired the unreachable post-worker implementation handshake; worker prompt is the live gate
