title: grind: fixture dirt still inflates Claude /goal past 4000 chars
description:
## Objective

Keep Claude `/goal` composition under 4,000 characters when a recovery handoff is prepended and when grind tests start from a dirty `copy_bd_workspace` fixture.

## Behavioral context

Before. `copy_bd_workspace` templates hand ~7 uncommitted paths to the next worker. `_compose_work_prompt` used to inline `goal-prompt.md`, then prepend the RECOVERY HANDOFF, and raise at the Claude 4,000-character cap (observed 4051). `ortus-88ml` baselined some leftover-claim seeds; `tests/test_grind.py` worker-spawn cases (`test_leftover_claim_spawn_has_no_resume`, `test_grind_implement_argv_has_no_resume`, and siblings) still failed at compose time.

After `ortus-6rp6` (`5d091bc`) the `/goal` condition is `_GOAL_POINTER`, not the inlined prompt. That is necessary but not the whole leaf: a long `_HandoffState.instruction()` plus phase instruction, CodeGraph contract, and lessons can still trip the Claude cap, and dirty fixture trees still create those handoffs. After this leaf, compose stays under the cap with a recovery handoff present, and the worker-spawn grind tests pass.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Keep `_compose_work_prompt` under Claude's 4,000-character cap when `_HandoffState.instruction()` is prepended. Give worker-spawn grind fixtures a committed baseline (or otherwise stop handing seven uncommitted template paths into the handoff), so `test_leftover_claim_spawn_has_no_resume` and `test_grind_implement_argv_has_no_resume` no longer die at compose. `_GOAL_POINTER` already landed in `5d091bc`; this leaf owns the remaining handoff/fixture path.

## Non-goals

Do not re-inline `goal-prompt.md` into `/goal`. Do not raise or remove the Claude 4,000-character cap. Do not change Grok/Codex wrap. Do not re-enable grind readiness repair. Do not rewrite Orient.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` — `_compose_work_prompt()`, `_GOAL_POINTER`, `_HandoffState.instruction()`, `_HANDOFF_PROMPT_PATHS`.
- `tests/conftest.py` — `copy_bd_workspace()`.
- `tests/test_grind.py` — `_fixture_repo()`, `_baseline_commit()`, `test_leftover_claim_spawn_has_no_resume()`, `test_grind_implement_argv_has_no_resume()`.

## Resolved decisions

1. The `/goal` condition stays `_GOAL_POINTER`. If the cap still trips, shrink or bound the recovery handoff / fixture dirt — do not put the prompt body back into `/goal`.
2. Worker-spawn fixtures commit a baseline the way `ortus-88ml` did for leftover-claim seeds, unless a smaller handoff bound alone makes those tests pass.
3. The 4,000-character raise stays Claude-only (`backend == "claude"`).

## Compatibility constraints

Linux + macOS only. Claude `/goal` remains capped at 4,000 characters. Grok and Codex must not inherit that raise. Default grind still does not repair unready leaves.

## Ordered steps

1. Reproduce: compose a Claude prompt with a ~1500-character recovery handoff and confirm whether it still exceeds 4,000.
2. If it does, bound `_HandoffState.instruction()` or the inherited-path list so pointer + instruction + contract + lessons + handoff stay under the cap.
3. Give the worker-spawn grind fixtures a committed baseline (or equivalent) so they do not invent a dirty-tree handoff.
4. Run the targeted tests.

## Dependencies

None. `ortus-6rp6` already landed the pointer. No open leaf owns these files.

## Edge cases

A handoff that lists many paths must truncate (`_HANDOFF_PROMPT_PATHS`), not grow without bound. Lessons already drop when they would exceed the Claude cap; the handoff must not be the thing that still overflows after that drop. A fixture that is dirty only in `.beads/` export paths is still dirt for `git status` and still feeds the handoff.

## Plan-gap guidance

Stop and report PLAN-GAP rather than improvising if keeping the pointer and a useful handoff cannot both fit under 4,000 characters, or if the worker-spawn tests fail for a reason other than compose length. Never re-inline `goal-prompt.md` to "fix" a test.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1: Claude `_compose_work_prompt` stays at or under 4,000 characters when a 1,500-character recovery handoff is prepended.
- AC-2: The composed `/goal` condition contains `_GOAL_POINTER` and not the Orient standup body.
- AC-3: The leftover-claim and implement-argv worker-spawn grind tests pass.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `uv run python -c "from ortus.commands.grind import _compose_work_prompt; p=_compose_work_prompt('', {'id':'x','title':'t'}, 'claude', phase_instruction=' RECOVERY HANDOFF: '+'x'*1500); assert len(p.removeprefix('/goal '))<=4000"`
- AC-2: `uv run python -c "from ortus.commands.grind import _compose_work_prompt,_GOAL_POINTER; p=_compose_work_prompt('', {'id':'x','title':'t'}, 'claude'); assert _GOAL_POINTER in p and '**Orient.**' not in p"`
- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind.py::test_leftover_claim_spawn_has_no_resume tests/test_grind.py::test_grind_implement_argv_has_no_resume -q --test-timeout=60`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_grind.py::test_leftover_claim_spawn_has_no_resume tests/test_grind.py::test_grind_implement_argv_has_no_resume tests/test_grind.py::test_large_issue_uses_bounded_claude_goal_and_full_codex_packet tests/test_grind.py::test_goal_condition_limit_is_claude_only tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py -q --test-timeout=60`
close_reason: Claude /goal stays under 4000 with a recovery handoff; worker-spawn fixtures use a committed baseline

title: grok backend: document the third backend
description:
## Objective

Document `grok` as a third backend in the same places Claude and Codex
are documented, without implying it is the default.

## Behavioral context

Before. README, check help, and init help say `claude|codex`.

After. Those surfaces list `grok`, say Claude is the default, and
describe the headless launch (`grok -p`, not a TUI session) and the
Q1-determined prompt wrap in one short paragraph.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Update README backend section, `ortus init --help`, `ortus check --help`,
`ortus grind --help`, and the `.ortusrc` example. Mention Grok in the
prerequisites table. Do not rewrite the lean-pipeline PRD.

## Non-goals

Do not change runtime behaviour. Do not document a TUI-only `/goal`
workflow as if grind used it unless Q1 is EXPANDS. Do not add a new
verb.

## Concrete locations

- `README.md` — backend section and `.ortusrc` sample.
- `src/ortus/commands/init.py` — `--backend` help.
- `src/ortus/commands/check.py` — `--backend` help.
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` — `--backend` help.
- `tests/test_cli.py` / help-snapshot tests if any exist.

## Resolved decisions

1. Claude stays the documented default.
2. The launch line is `grok -p`, plus `/goal` only if Q1 is EXPANDS.
3. State-graph is untouched.

## Compatibility constraints

No generated README state-graph edit. Help text must stay valid for
`ortus <verb> --help`.

## Ordered steps

1. Read Q1 and the landed runner wrap.
2. Update README and Typer help strings.
3. Run help/docs tests.

## Dependencies

Depends on init/check (so documented files exist) and on grind wiring
(so the documented launch path is real).

## Edge cases

A docs-only change must not mention a `.grok/` file that the init leaf
decided not to emit.

## Plan-gap guidance

If Q1 or the init path is still open, wait; do not document both
futures.

title: grok backend: decode grok headless streams in tail
description:
## Objective

Make `ortus tail` render Grok headless JSON the same way it already
renders Claude stream-json and Codex `--json` events.

## Behavioral context

Before. Tail inspects the resolved backend and decodes Claude
stream-json or Codex JSONL. A Grok `streaming-json` / `streaming-messages-json`
log would print as raw lines or be misread as Claude events.

After. With `backend=grok`, tail shows assistant text, tool calls, and
session init from a Grok headless log without requiring `--raw`.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Add a Grok event decoder next to the Codex decoder. Teach backend
detection in `tail` a third branch. Add a fixture built from the
headless-mode documentation (and the Q1 artifact if it captured a real
stream).

## Non-goals

Do not change Claude or Codex decode tests. Do not implement the
runner. Do not pretty-print every Grok-only event type on day one —
assistant text, tool use, and `system/init` are the parity bar.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/commands/tail.py` — decoder dispatch, `codex=` flag or
  successor.
- `tests/test_tail.py`, `tests/test_tail_backend_detection.py`,
  `tests/test_codex_tail_decoder.py` as the shape to copy.
- `tests/fixtures/` — new grok stream fixture.
- `~/.grok/docs/user-guide/14-headless-mode.md` — event schema.

## Resolved decisions

1. Prefer `streaming-json` if the runner leaf pinned it; otherwise
   decode the format the runner actually writes.
2. Detection is by resolved backend first, then by event shape if the
   log is mixed (existing Codex detection pattern).
3. Fixture may be canned from docs if a live stream was not kept; if
   Q1 saved a stream, prefer that.

## Compatibility constraints

`ortus tail` stays read-only (NFR-006). Claude and Codex golden
outputs stay identical.

## Ordered steps

1. Read the runner leaf's chosen `--output-format`.
2. Add a fixture and a decoder function.
3. Branch tail's backend detection.
4. Assert assistant/tool/init lines against the fixture.
5. Run the targeted tests.

## Dependencies

Depends on the runner leaf for the format pin. No grind change.

## Edge cases

An empty log is a quiet follow, not a crash. A Claude log opened
under `--backend grok` must not raise. Unknown event types are
skipped or dim, matching current non-JSON behaviour.

## Plan-gap guidance

If Grok's stream schema cannot represent tool calls in the pinned
format, stop and record PLAN-GAP rather than parsing plaintext.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1 (proves-new): a canned Grok stream fixture renders an assistant
  banner without `--raw`.
- AC-2 (guards-existing): Claude stream fixtures still match their
  golden output.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py -k grok_stream_renders_assistant -q`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_tail_render_parity.py -q`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py tests/test_tail_backend_detection.py tests/test_tail_render_parity.py tests/test_codex_tail_decoder.py -q`

title: grind: the legacy shared-tree resume has no merge-forward, so a parked legacy journal whose fork point trails main rejects on every retry
description:
## Why

Run of 2026-08-13 13:28: a branch-scoped journal was misrouted down the legacy shared-tree path (an untracked bd lock file matched its candidate_paths — fixed separately), and the legacy path resumed the branch as-is: no rebase onto the integration head, base_head kept at the claim-time fork point. With main four commits ahead, the integration-moved guard rejected the candidate at the end of a 36-minute worker run, and every re-run repeats identically. The workspace path got merge-forward with the bz3c landing; the legacy path never did.

## What

Either give the legacy resume the same treatment — when the primary tree is clean enough to rebase (candidate fully committed on the branch), rebase the branch onto the integration head and refresh base_head — or retire the legacy path outright, which is already planned as part of the attribution/mutation-guard deletion. A truly dirty legacy tree cannot rebase safely; that case should at least warn that the fork point is stale instead of spending a full worker run on a guaranteed rejection.
acceptance_criteria:

- AC-1: A legacy shared-tree resume whose branch trails the integration head either rebases forward before the worker runs or warns up front that the stale fork point will fail the integration-moved guard; it never spends a full worker run on a guaranteed rejection.

title: worker workspaces: exclude HOME-skeleton artifacts from rescue and declarations; decide the clone trust story
description:
## Why

Clone workspaces accumulate untracked HOME-shaped files (.bash_profile, .bashrc, .gitconfig, .claude/agents, .claude/skills, ...) because the worker sandbox points HOME at the workspace. The unrelated-declaration filter currently ignores them at handoff, but they are not in the tool-state ignore set, so a rescue-commit or a future declaration change could sweep them onto an issue branch. Separately, every clone worker logs 'Ignoring 13 permissions.allow entries from .claude/settings.json: this workspace has not been trusted' — harmless under the current permission mode, but it means clone workers run without the repository's allowlist.

## What

Add the HOME-skeleton names to the workspace tool-state ignore set (the same mechanism that excludes .codegraph) so rescue commits and candidate captures can never include them, and either pre-trust workspace paths at materialization or document why the untrusted warning is acceptable.

title: prompts: bounded waits must bound TaskOutput blocking — a task reporting running with an empty file and an expired bound is failed
description:
## Objective

A worker waiting on its own background task gives up when the evidence says the work is gone — an empty output file past the bound — regardless of the task tracker still reporting `running`, so a wedged background check costs one bounded wait instead of the whole worker timeout.

## Behavioral context

Before. Observed 2026-08-12 08:00–08:16 (ortus-f26b's worker): a background pytest task reported `status: running` while its output file was empty and no test process existed on the machine. The worker followed its bounded-wait contract faithfully — blocked on `TaskOutput` (10-minute timeout), probed the file, found nothing, and blocked again — because each timeout's "still running" answer reads as progress and resets its judgment. The ortus-xjdf fix banned unbounded pipe waits; this is the same wedge one layer up, where the harness's task-status word defeats the attempt bound the contract prescribes. Cost: the worker rode ~40 minutes of dead waiting toward the 90-minute worker timeout.

After. The worker contract states the rule at the level of evidence, not plumbing: the bound applies to the *wait*, however implemented — polling loops, `TaskOutput` blocking, anything. When the bound expires with no output produced, the job is failed-to-report even if a status field says running; the worker names the command and either re-runs the checks in the foreground once or reports the blocker. Status words are not progress; bytes are.

## Reference

The ortus-xjdf packet and its landed "Background Jobs: Bounded Waits" prompt section, which this extends from pipes to task-tracker waits.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Extend the grind prompt's bounded-waits section and the work-issue condition to cover harness-tracked background tasks: the attempt bound governs `TaskOutput` blocking, a running status with an empty output file past the bound is a failure, and the prescribed recovery is one foreground re-run of the same command before reporting a blocker.

## Non-goals

Do not change the harness's task tracking (not ours), the worker timeout, or the xjdf section's existing pipe guidance. Do not forbid background tasks or TaskOutput.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/prompts/grind-prompt.md` — the "Background Jobs: Bounded Waits" section gains the task-tracker clause.
- `src/ortus/prompts/conditions/work-issue.txt` — if it references the waiting pattern, mirror the clause; otherwise no change.
- `tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py` — assertions per the section's existing test pattern.

## Resolved decisions

1. Evidence over status: the rule is phrased around produced bytes and the expired bound, explicitly stating that a `running` status does not extend the bound.
2. One foreground retry is prescribed before the blocker report — the observed wedge would have been resolved by exactly that (the suites run in ~1–7 minutes foreground).
3. The attempt bound is shared across wait mechanisms for the same job: blocking waits count as attempts.

## Compatibility constraints

Existing bounded-wait assertions keep passing; the new clause is additive to the same section.

## Ordered steps

1. Add the task-tracker clause to the bounded-waits section.
2. Add prompt-content assertions: status-not-progress, foreground-retry-once, blocking-counts-as-attempts.
3. Run `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py -m fast -n auto --test-timeout=30 -q`.

## Dependencies

None; prompt text and tests only.

## Edge cases

A task legitimately producing output slowly is protected by the existing still-producing rule — the new clause fires only on zero bytes past the bound. A foreground retry that also produces nothing is the blocker, reported once with the command named.

## Plan-gap guidance

Stop and report rather than improvising if the section's budget cannot absorb the clause, or if any existing assertion pins contrary wording. Never instruct workers to kill harness tasks they did not start.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1: The bounded-waits section states that a running status does not extend the bound; produced bytes do.
- AC-2: It prescribes one foreground re-run before a blocker report.
- AC-3: It states blocking waits count against the same attempt bound.
- AC-4: Existing bounded-wait assertions pass unchanged.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py -k status_is_not_progress -q`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py -k foreground_retry_before_blocker -q`
- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py -k blocking_waits_count_as_attempts -q`
- AC-4: `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py -m fast -q`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py -m fast -n auto --test-timeout=30 -q`

title: grind: pushes to origin announce themselves — ref, destination, and commit range
description:
## Objective

Every push grind performs is unmistakable on the console at the moment it happens: which ref, to which remote, carrying which commits — because a push is the one action that changes the world outside the machine, and today it hides inside a log line about synchronization.

## Behavioral context

Before. Finalization's sync step pushes the integration branch after every landing, and the only traces are the log's "finalization: main synchronized with origin" and the console's post-kawu landing line, neither of which names the act of pushing, the destination, or what left. The branch-guard's backstop push ("pushing so the closed work is deployable") is similarly quiet on the console. An operator watching a run — the operator's request, verbatim: "the output of ortus grind should be obvious when something is getting pushed to git" — cannot tell when commits leave the machine versus when they merely land on local main.

After. At each push the console states, in the narration register the landed ortus-kawu established: `pushing main → origin (2a37337..366b549, 2 commits)` followed by confirmation or the ipyq-style failure narrative. The pull-rebase-retry announces itself as a retry. Every push site routes through one announcing helper, so future push sites — the issue-branch push planned in ortus-6a0a.1 foremost — inherit the visibility instead of re-forgetting it.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

One announcing push helper used by every site that pushes: finalization's sync step, its pull-rebase retry, and the branch-guard's PUSH backstop. The announcement names ref, remote, and the commit range (old remote tip..new tip with a commit count); success confirms, failure keeps the ipyq narrative.

## Non-goals

Do not change push semantics, ordering, or retry behavior. Do not announce local-only operations (the fast-forward has its own kawu line). Do not add remote reads beyond what the push already knows — the range comes from refs already on hand (origin/<branch> before, HEAD after), never a network round trip.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` — the sync step's `git.push(integration_branch)` and retry, and `_enforce_branch_discipline`'s PUSH disposition.
- `src/ortus/core/git.py` — `push()` and `local_ahead_of_remote()`, whose ahead-count already computes the range's size; a `push_announced` wrapper (or a returned range record) lives beside them.
- `tests/test_grind_finalization.py`, `tests/test_grind.py` — console assertions.

## Resolved decisions

1. Announce before the attempt ("pushing main → origin (a1b2c3d..e4f5a6b, 2 commits)") and confirm after, so a push that hangs is visible as an in-flight push rather than silence.
2. The range reads old-remote-tip..local-tip from local refs; when origin/<branch> is unresolvable (first push, no tracking ref) the announcement says "all history" rather than inventing a range.
3. The retry path announces "push rejected; rebasing on origin and retrying" — it already logs this; the console joins.
4. One helper, all sites, so ortus-6a0a.1's future issue-branch push inherits announcement by construction; noted in that packet's consumers.

## Compatibility constraints

Log lines unchanged (dashboard/tail parse them). The no-stream-leak guard untouched. Console additions follow kawu's prefix-free, timestamped register.

## Ordered steps

1. Add the announcing helper beside `push()` with the range computation from local refs.
2. Route the three existing push sites through it.
3. Add console assertions per site, including the unresolvable-remote wording.
4. Run `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_finalization.py tests/test_grind.py tests/regression/test_grind_no_stream_leak.py -m "fast or integration" -n auto --test-timeout=180 -q`.

## Dependencies

None open on these lines; builds on landed ortus-kawu and ortus-ipyq conventions. ortus-6a0a.1 (open, human) is a future consumer, not a blocker.

## Edge cases

A no-remote repository announces nothing (the sync step already short-circuits). A push moving zero commits (guard backstop racing an already-synced remote) says "already up to date" rather than a zero-commit range. Range text uses short hashes through the existing console-safe path.

## Plan-gap guidance

Stop and report rather than improvising if any push site cannot know its range from local refs alone, or if announcing before the attempt would break a test that pins console ordering. Never add a network read to make an announcement prettier.

title: grind: readiness-skip warnings summarize, name the title, say the next step, and fire once per issue
description:
## Objective

A readiness skip reads like a colleague's aside — which issue (by title), what is wrong at summary altitude, and what to do about it — printed once per issue per run, while the full section-by-section diagnostic keeps serving the machine that actually consumes it.

## Behavioral context

Before. Observed 2026-08-11: `ortus-f26b`, an old bare issue with no packet, produced a fifteen-clause console warning enumerating every missing section ("description/objective: missing, empty, or placeholder section; description/behavioral context: missing, ..."), with no issue title and no suggested action — and the same wall re-prints on every subsequent selection pass of the run. The operator's verbatim reaction: "tell me how this is helpful." The enumeration exists because the readiness repair pass consumes it as a work order; the console inherited the machine's format.

After. The console prints, once per issue per run: `skipped "vocabulary accessibility" (ortus-f26b) — no readiness packet (15 of 15 sections missing); grind will draft one automatically when the queue has nothing ready, or run ortus plan / edit the packet yourself. It stays open and unclaimed.` A packet failing a few sections names just those sections. The full enumeration still goes to the log and to the repair prompt unchanged.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Add a summary rendering to the readiness report for console use — full-miss collapses to "no readiness packet (N of N sections missing)", partial-miss names only the failing sections — include the issue title, append the next-step sentence, and deduplicate the console warning per issue per run. Log and repair-prompt output keep the complete enumeration.

## Non-goals

Do not change validation itself, the repair pass's input, what selection skips, or the log's completeness. Do not suppress the warning entirely on later iterations — the log keeps every occurrence; only the console dedupes.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/core/readiness.py` — `ReadinessReport.diagnostic()`, which currently renders the machine enumeration; gains a `summary()` sibling (or a `verbose=` switch) that counts misses against the schema's section total and collapses accordingly.
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` — `report_unready()` inside the selection loop: console gets the summary via `output.warn`, the log keeps `diagnostic()`, and a per-run `set` of already-warned issue ids gates the console line. The queue-blocked exit path that re-prints diagnostics gets the same treatment.
- `tests/test_readiness.py`, `tests/test_grind.py` — rendering and dedupe coverage.

## Resolved decisions

1. Full miss (every required section failing) is one clause with a count, because an empty packet has one problem, not fifteen.
2. The title leads and the id follows in parentheses, matching the narration register ortus-kawu established for the console.
3. The next step names both paths: grind's own automatic repair (and when it triggers — only once nothing is ready), and the manual `ortus plan`/packet-edit route.
4. Dedupe is per run and console-only; a packet repaired and re-failing differently warns again because the summary text differs.

## Compatibility constraints

`diagnostic()`'s output is unchanged for its existing consumers (repair prompt, log, tests asserting it). Console dedupe must not suppress the final queue-blocked error listing, which is the run's exit explanation.

## Ordered steps

1. Add the summary rendering with section-count collapse.
2. Route console warnings through it in `report_unready`, with per-run dedupe; leave log/repair on `diagnostic()`.
3. Apply the same summary to the queue-blocked exit listing.
4. Add rendering and dedupe tests.
5. Run `uv run pytest tests/test_readiness.py tests/test_grind.py -m "fast or integration" -n auto --test-timeout=180 -q`.

## Dependencies

None. Presentation and one selection-loop guard; complements landed ortus-kawu.

## Edge cases

A packet failing exactly one section names it without the count clause. A run where the only remaining issues are unready still prints each issue's summary once before the repair pass or exit. Titles with markup-hostile characters go through `_console_safe`. The dedupe set must key on issue id plus summary text so changed failures re-warn.

## Plan-gap guidance

Stop and report rather than improvising if `diagnostic()` has consumers that would need the summary instead, or if the repair pass turns out to parse the console rather than the report object. Never trim the log's enumeration.
acceptance_criteria:

- AC-1: An all-sections-missing packet warns with a single collapsed clause, the issue title, and the next-step sentence.
- AC-2: A partially failing packet names only its failing sections.
- AC-3: The console warns once per issue per run; the log records every occurrence.
- AC-4: The repair prompt still receives the full enumeration.
- AC-5: The queue-blocked exit listing uses the summary form.

## Criterion checks

- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_readiness.py -k partial_miss_names_only_failures -q`

title: prompts: the worker contract omits the message rule the validation gate enforces
description:
## Objective

Workers' own commit messages survive finalization, because the contract that tells them what to write states every rule the validation gate enforces.

## Behavioral context

Before. The first two fully autonomous landings (ortus-u4zv.1 and ortus-l2u9.1, 2026-08-11 evening run) both had their worker-written commit messages rejected with the same reason — "the composed body names nothing from the diff" — and replaced by the weaker deterministic assembly. Root cause: the work-issue condition instructs "an imperative subject of at most 72 characters ... then a body of prose explaining the change," but `validate_message` additionally requires the message to name at least one function, class, or file that appears in the diff (and forbids restating the issue title, trailing periods, and ellipses). The gate enforces rules the writer was never told, so the rejection rate is currently 100% and every landed commit carries the fallback body instead of the worker's explanation.

After. The worker contract's message instruction states the same rules the gate checks — name something real from your diff, don't restate the title, imperative mood, no trailing period — and the correction-prompt footer's message guidance matches. Worker messages land verbatim in the common case; the gate returns to being the exception it was designed as.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Align the commit-message instructions in the worker-facing contracts with `validate_message`'s actual rule set, and assert the alignment so the two cannot drift again.

## Non-goals

Do not weaken `validate_message` — the rules are right; the telling was missing. Do not change finalization's amend/replace mechanics. Do not touch the deterministic assembly.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/prompts/conditions/work-issue.txt` — the step-2 message instruction.
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` — the correction-prompt footer's "commit the correction ... with a commit message describing the fix" line, and the implementation phase instruction.
- `src/ortus/core/compose.py` — `validate_message()`, the authoritative rule set; read, not modified. Its module already renders the same rules for the retired composer prompt (`compose_prompt`), which is the wording to borrow.
- `tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py` — the alignment assertion.

## Resolved decisions

1. State the gate's rules where the writer writes: name at least one function, class or file from your own diff; do not restate the issue title; imperative mood; no trailing period or ellipsis. Borrow the battle-tested phrasing from the retired composer prompt rather than inventing new wording.
2. Add a drift guard: a prompt-content test asserting the contract names each rule the validator enforces, so a future validation rule change fails loudly until the contract catches up.
3. Rejection stays graceful exactly as today — this leaf reduces its frequency, not its safety.

## Compatibility constraints

The message rules themselves are unchanged, so no finalization or compose test moves. Prompt-content tests asserting current step-2 wording are updated in the same change.

## Ordered steps

1. Rewrite the message instruction in the work-issue condition and the correction footer with the full rule set.
2. Add the drift-guard prompt-content test.
3. Run `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_prompt_content.py tests/test_core_compose.py -m fast -n auto --test-timeout=30 -q`.

## Dependencies

None. Prompt text and tests only; no open leaf touches these lines.

## Edge cases

A diff with no nameable symbol (pure deletion, pure config) must still be writable — the rule says name a file in that case, and the contract says so. Non-source candidates (prompt-only changes, like this leaf's own) name the prompt file. The 72-character subject rule keeps the id-prefix accounting the contract already states.

## Plan-gap guidance

Stop and report rather than improvising if any validator rule cannot be stated briefly enough for the contract's budget, or if the correction footer's length limit forces a trade — never trim a rule silently.

title: grind: console narrates milestones, not CodeGraph plumbing
description:
## Objective

`ortus grind`'s console tells the operator what they actually ask of it — which issue is claimed, which phase it is in, what the verdict was, what landed — instead of CodeGraph plumbing followed by twenty silent minutes.

## Behavioral context

Before. Observed across the 2026-08-11 runs: after startup, the console prints `implementation CodeGraph handshake requested` and then nothing for the whole implement-and-verify cycle (~21 minutes on the first autonomous landing). The claim line, the verifier's verdict, and per-issue progress are written only to `logs/grind-*.log`; of the milestones, only `finalized <id>` reaches the screen. An operator watching the terminal cannot answer "what is it working on and how is it going" without tailing the log — the exact question the console exists for. The imbalance is historical: progress lines grew around CodeGraph integration debugging, while milestone lines grew in the log.

After. The console narrates the run at executive altitude, one line per milestone: issue claimed (with title), implementation started, verification started, verdict (pass/fail with candidate short-hash), correction attempts, finalized/closed with a running tally, and every blocker or escalation verbatim. CodeGraph handshake and refresh lines demote to the log unless they fail. The deliberate quiet-terminal property is preserved: no worker transcript content, no stream leak — the regression guard's intent (`tests/regression/test_grind_no_stream_leak.py`) is narrowed to transcripts, not milestones.

The operator's own words, which are the acceptance bar for tone: "I want to know a more friendly human readable version of what is going on." Telemetry-flavored milestone lines fail that bar even when technically informative; the console should read like a colleague narrating the run.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Rebalance grind's two output channels: promote per-issue milestone lines (claim with title, phase starts, verdict, corrections, finalized, closed tally, blockers) to `output.progress`, demote healthy CodeGraph plumbing lines to log-only (failures stay on console), and update the quiet-terminal regression guard to assert its real invariant — no transcript content — while asserting milestones are present.

## Non-goals

Do not change what is written to the log — it remains the complete record and the dashboard/tail input. Do not print worker or verifier transcript content, prompts, or diffs to the console; the no-stream-leak property is load-bearing. Do not add timestamps-to-console formatting changes, spinners, or TUI elements — `ortus dashboard` owns rich presentation. Do not alter phase behavior; this is presentation only.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` — the `write_log`-only milestone sites (the claim line `harness selected+claimed`, the verdict line `verifier verdict=`, correction-attempt and closed-tally lines) gain paired `output.progress` calls; the CodeGraph `output.progress` sites (`handshake requested/succeeded`, `refreshing CodeGraph index`, `CodeGraph phase summary`) drop to log-only when healthy.
- `src/ortus/core/output.py` — the progress helper: the prefix lives here and is removed here, so the change is uniform across commands.
- `tests/regression/test_grind_no_stream_leak.py` — `test_grind_terminal_is_quiet_log_is_full` narrows to transcript-leak assertions and gains milestone-presence assertions.
- `tests/test_grind.py` — console-content assertions in flow tests, where present.

## Resolved decisions

1. The console is the executive channel, and it speaks operator, not telemetry: plain-English sentences leading with the issue *title*, the id in parentheses, elapsed durations on phase completions, and a running tally after every landing. The register to aim for, verbatim:

       [20:31:01] claimed "tail: attach at the last 2,000 lines by default" (ortus-fc2q) — implementing
       implementation done in 16m; fresh verifier reviewing the candidate
       verdict: PASS (candidate 1d990b11994e) after 4m
       landed on main and pushed — 2 done this run, 14 open
       escalated "pin the bd toolchain" (ortus-k46v.1) to a human: plan gap — see the issue's newest comment

   One line per event, no line for anything a healthy run repeats invisibly.
2. Plumbing failures still surface: a failed handshake, a stale index in required mode, or any blocker prints on console verbatim — quiet applies to health, never to trouble.
3. The verdict line carries decision and the candidate hash's first 12 characters, mirroring the log so the two channels correlate.
4. The quiet-terminal guard's invariant is restated, not deleted: transcripts, prompts and diffs never reach the console; milestone lines must. Both directions asserted.
5. Verbosity stays flag-free in this leaf: the log remains the verbose channel, and a `--quiet` flag is future work if anyone asks.
6. The `[ortus grind]` per-line prefix is dropped from the console: the operator invoked the program and every repeated tag is reading tax (operator request, 2026-08-11). Timestamps stay — they are what make "how long has this been going" answerable at a glance. The log keeps its current line format untouched.

## Compatibility constraints

Log content is byte-compatible — nothing that parses `logs/grind-*.log` (dashboard, tail, tests) sees any change. Console lines drop the `[ortus grind]` prefix (decision 6); `src/ortus/core/output.py`'s progress helper is the one place that changes, so every other command using it sheds its prefix consistently — sweep their tests in the same change. Tests that assert specific console strings are updated together.

## Ordered steps

1. Pair `output.progress` onto the milestone `write_log` sites; demote healthy CodeGraph progress lines to log-only.
2. Narrow and extend the no-stream-leak regression test per decision 4.
3. Sweep flow tests for console assertions broken by the rebalance.
4. Run `uv run pytest tests/regression/test_grind_no_stream_leak.py tests/test_grind.py -m "fast or integration" -n auto --test-timeout=180 -q`.

## Dependencies

None. Presentation-only; no open leaf touches the output sites.

## Edge cases

Titles with markup-hostile characters must survive the console (the `_console_safe` helper exists for exactly this). A run with `--tasks 0` draining many issues keeps one tally line per close, not a growing summary. Legacy `--condition` mode prints the same milestones it can know. Non-TTY stdout (piped) gets identical lines — no TTY detection in this leaf.

## Plan-gap guidance

Stop and report rather than improvising if any consumer parses console output programmatically (none is known), or if the no-stream-leak test's structure cannot express both directions. Never print transcript content, and never remove a log line to satisfy a console goal.

title: grind: run each worker in a disposable shared clone; the primary checkout never leaves the integration branch
description:
## Objective

Run each grind worker in a disposable shared clone of the repository, committing on its issue branch there, with finalization fetching the branch back into the primary repository — so the primary checkout never leaves the integration branch and concurrent operator intake becomes structurally safe rather than a matter of etiquette.

## Behavioral context

Before. Workers share the operator's working tree: the claim checks the shared checkout onto `ortus/<issue-id>`, the worker edits and commits there, and finalization fast-forwards and returns to the integration branch. Everything the operator (or an interactive intake session) does to that tree mid-run — a commit, a file edit — lands inside the worker's candidate range; on 2026-08-11 an intake session's tracker-churn commit landed on a live issue branch exactly this way, and only the export carve-out made it benign. The handoff/foreign-work machinery exists to manage this class after the fact.

After. The claim materializes a shared clone (`git clone --shared`, the mechanism the AC runner already uses — an ordinary directory, cheap because objects are shared, removable because it is not a worktree), checks out the issue branch inside it, and hands the worker that directory as its repo. The worker's commits accumulate in the clone. Finalization fetches `ortus/<issue-id>` from the clone into the primary repository and proceeds exactly as today (validate message, fast-forward the integration ref, push). The primary checkout stays on the integration branch for the entire run; operator intake — bd writes, even commits of export churn — can no longer collide with a candidate. The clone is removed after finalization; a blocked issue's branch survives in the primary repo via the fetch.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Materialize a per-issue shared clone at claim, run implementation/correction/verification phases with the clone as their repo, fetch the issue branch back to the primary repository before finalization's merge step, and remove the clone after the transaction completes or parks. The primary checkout stops switching branches.

## Non-goals

Do not containerize workers; this leaf is workspace isolation, not environment isolation — the container runtime is a separate later step. Do not run issues concurrently; one clone at a time, same serial loop. Do not change the candidate model, the verification pipeline, the journal's step vocabulary, or the finalization sequence beyond sourcing the branch from a fetch. Do not move `.beads/` — the tracker stays in the primary repository, and workers keep reaching it there (bd is excluded from sandbox command wrapping already).

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` — the claim-path branch cut (which becomes clone-then-checkout-in-clone), `_capture_codex_candidate()` and `_candidate_view()` (whose `git` client must point at the clone), `_finalize_candidate()`'s commit step (which gains a fetch-from-clone before the fast-forward), and the worker spawn (whose `repo=` becomes the clone path).
- `src/ortus/core/git.py` — `GitClient` (instantiated per clone as well as for the primary), `fast_forward()` (unchanged — it already updates refs without touching the worktree), and a `fetch_branch(remote_path, branch)` helper (`git fetch <clone> <branch>:<branch>`, fast-forward-only semantics like the existing helper).
- `src/ortus/core/transaction.py` — `CandidateJournal` gains the clone path so recovery can find or discard it; defaulted for legacy journals.
- `src/ortus/core/sandbox.py` / `src/ortus/core/claude.py` — the worker sandbox mounts, which must bind the clone directory rather than (or in addition to) the primary repo.
- `tests/test_grind_finalization.py`, `tests/test_grind.py`, `tests/test_grind_recovery.py` — the flow suites.

## Resolved decisions

1. `git clone --shared` into the runtime area (`logs/grind-workspaces/<issue-id>` or a tmp dir — resolved at implementation against sandbox mount rules), never a worktree: the sandbox makes worktree registrations unremovable, and a shared clone is an ordinary directory whose objects live in the primary repo. The AC-runner leaf (`ortus-l2u9.1`) standardizes the same mechanism; reuse its helper if it has landed, extract a shared one if not.
2. The primary checkout never switches branches during a run. The branch guard's `allowed_branch` tolerance and the finalization blocker's issue-branch allowance become dead paths to retire once this holds — noted for the machine-verification deletion leaf, not removed here.
3. Finalization fetches the branch from the clone (`fetch <clone-path> ortus/<id>:ortus/<id>`, ff-only) before its existing validate/fast-forward sequence, which then operates entirely in the primary repo exactly as today. A fetch that is not a fast-forward of an existing branch is a blocker, mirroring the existing never-reset rule.
4. The tracker stays primary-side: workers already run bd against the repository the harness names; the clone carries `.beads/` content as checked in, but worker bd commands target the primary workspace so intake and workers share one tracker. The export churn therefore lands in the primary tree — outside any candidate by the existing carve-out — and finalization sweeps it exactly as today.
5. Environment preparation in the clone reuses the dependency-sync convention the AC runner establishes (`uv sync --all-extras` default): a worker must be able to run the gate inside its clone. This is the same cost verification already pays for its own clone; measure before optimizing sharing.
6. Clone lifecycle: removed on successful finalization and on plan-gap/escalation park (the branch survives via fetch — the durable home is the primary repo's ref, never the clone). A crash leaves the clone for the startup sweep to fetch-then-remove, keyed by the journal's recorded path.

## Compatibility constraints

A repository with no remote behaves identically (clones are local). The verification pipeline consumes the same range diff — captured against the clone — with hashes unchanged in meaning. Legacy journals without a clone path recover by today's shared-tree rules. The `ortus tail`/dashboard log locations are unchanged (logs stay primary-side). Sandbox mount changes must keep the smoke test meaningful on hosts without bwrap changes.

## Ordered steps

1. Add the clone materialization + `fetch_branch` helper, with lifecycle (create at claim, record in journal, remove at completion/park, sweep at startup).
2. Point the worker spawn, capture, candidate view, and verifier at the clone's `GitClient`; keep bd primary-side.
3. Insert the fetch step at the head of finalization's commit step; everything after operates on the primary repo unchanged.
4. Update sandbox mounts for the clone directory.
5. Migrate the flow tests; add clone-lifecycle and intake-concurrency tests per Targeted tests.
6. Run the full gate with `codegraph` masked from `PATH`.

## Dependencies

Depends on `ortus-l2u9.3` (the machine-verification wiring): re-pointing capture and verification at a clone while the verifier contract is also being replaced would put two open leaves in the same functions. Benefits from `ortus-l2u9.1` landing first for the shared clone-and-sync helper. Human-landed: this modifies the claim, capture and finalization paths — the code that ships it.

## Edge cases

A clone whose creation fails is a claim-time blocker with the claim reverted, like an invalid branch name today. An operator commit on the primary integration branch mid-run no longer disturbs the worker, but moves the integration head — the existing isolation guard's integration-moved check now fires at capture with a clear reason instead of silently breaking the fast-forward. A worker that somehow escapes its clone and edits the primary tree is caught by the existing dirty-path machinery. `.codegraph/` is gitignored and absent in clones — the worker's CodeGraph contract must either build the index in-clone (cheap: ~0.2s on this repo) or degrade per policy; resolve against the CI job's precedent of `codegraph init` per fresh checkout. Disk: one clone plus one verification clone at peak, objects shared.

## Plan-gap guidance

Stop and report rather than improvising if bd cannot be kept primary-side without worker contract changes, if sandbox mounts cannot express the clone cleanly, or if the CodeGraph required-mode policy cannot be satisfied inside a clone. Never let the primary checkout switch branches in the new flow, and never make the clone the durable home of anything — the primary repo's refs are.

- AC-3: A commit made in the primary repository during implementation does not enter the candidate.
- AC-4: Tracker export churn written primary-side during a run is swept into the issue's finalization commit exactly as before.
- AC-5: The clone is removed after successful finalization; a parked issue's branch survives in the primary repository.
- AC-6: A crashed run's clone is swept (fetched then removed) at the next startup.

## Criterion checks

This structurally removes the intake-collision class and unblocks ortus-l2u9.4's deletion of the shared-tree machinery.

title: tail: attach at the last 2,000 lines by default, with --lines to widen or remove the cap
description:
## Objective

`ortus tail` starts each newly-attached log at its last 2,000 lines instead of replaying the whole file, with a `--lines/-n` option to widen or remove the cap, so attaching to a long-running grind shows the present in seconds rather than the entire past first.

## Behavioral context

Before. `_LogStream` initializes its position at the start of the file, so `_follow()`'s first poll reads from byte zero and renders every line the log has ever accumulated — a grind transcript reaches megabytes within an hour, and attaching mid-run floods the terminal with the full history (tens of thousands of rendered lines) before the first live line appears. There is no option to bound it; `--raw` changes formatting, not volume.

After. On first attach to each discovered log, tail renders only the last 2,000 input lines (default), preceded by a one-line notice naming how many earlier lines were skipped and how to see them (`--lines 0`). Follow behavior after attach is unchanged. `-n/--lines N` overrides the cap; `0` means unlimited — today's behavior, byte for byte. Logs shorter than the cap render identically to today.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Cap the first-attach rendering of each log stream at a line count, add the `--lines/-n` option with a 2,000-line default and `0` as unlimited, and print a skip notice when the cap trims history. Applies to every rendering mode (default, `--raw`, `--codex`).

## Non-goals

Do not change follow behavior after attach, the poll cadence, log discovery, or any renderer's per-line output. Do not bound file I/O — the cap governs what is rendered, not what is read; a memory-mapped or block-seek optimization is separate work if ever needed. Do not add persistence or config-file plumbing for the default; a CLI option suffices.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/commands/tail.py` — `_LogStream` at line 709 (initial position), `_follow()` at line 714 (the first-read path that renders the backlog), `tail()` at line 803 (the Typer options).
- `tests/test_tail.py` — the command's behavioral suite.
- `tests/test_tail_render_parity.py` — render parity coverage that must stay byte-identical for uncapped logs.

## Resolved decisions

1. The cap counts physical input lines per stream, applied once at first attach; every stream discovered later gets the same rule (a file created mid-follow is small, so the cap is a no-op there).
2. Default 2,000; `--lines 0` means unlimited and reproduces today's output byte-for-byte. Negative values are rejected by Typer validation.
3. The cap trims before rendering, not after: category filters (`--tools`, `--system`) apply to the kept tail, so `-n 2000` means "the last 2,000 log lines," not "2,000 rendered lines" — the count a reader can correlate with the file.
4. A single skip notice per trimmed stream, written where the stream banner already goes, naming the skipped count and `--lines 0`. Silent truncation reads as a complete history.
5. `--raw` obeys the cap too; raw means unformatted, not unbounded.

## Compatibility constraints

Uncapped output (`--lines 0`, or any log at or under the cap) is byte-identical to today, so the render-parity suite passes unchanged. The `iterations`-bounded mode used by tests keeps its semantics; position accounting stays byte-accurate so follow reads continue from end of file exactly as now. No other command or module reads `_LogStream`.

## Ordered steps

1. Add the `--lines/-n` option with default 2,000 and `min=0` validation.
2. In the first read of each stream, split the backlog, render only the last N lines, and emit the skip notice with the trimmed count.
3. Thread the cap through the raw and codex paths.
4. Add tests per Targeted tests.
5. Run `uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py tests/test_tail_render_parity.py -m fast -n auto --test-timeout=30 -q`.

## Dependencies

None. No open leaf touches `tail.py` or its test files.

## Edge cases

A log exactly at the cap renders fully with no notice. A log with a trailing partial line (still being written) must not count the partial as a rendered line twice across polls. CRLF line endings count once per line. Multiple logs attach with independent caps and independent notices. `--lines 0` with a megabyte log must still stream rather than buffer indefinitely — today's behavior, preserved. The skip notice must be plain enough for `--raw` consumers piping to files.

## Plan-gap guidance

Stop and report rather than improvising if the first-read path cannot distinguish attach from follow without restructuring `_follow()`'s polling loop, or if byte-accurate position accounting conflicts with line-based trimming in a way the tests expose. Never trim silently, and never change post-attach follow output.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1: Attaching to a log longer than the cap renders only its last 2,000 lines by default.
- AC-2: A skip notice names the number of trimmed lines and `--lines 0`.
- AC-3: `--lines 0` reproduces today's full-history output byte-for-byte.
- AC-4: A log at or under the cap renders identically to today, with no notice.
- AC-5: `--raw` obeys the cap.
- AC-6: Follow output after attach is unchanged.
- AC-7: Each discovered log gets an independent cap and notice.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py -k attach_caps_history_at_default -q`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py -k skip_notice_names_count_and_escape_hatch -q`
- AC-3: `uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py -k lines_zero_is_byte_identical_full_history -q`

`uv run pytest tests/test_tail.py tests/test_tail_render_parity.py -m fast -n auto --test-timeout=30 -q`

title: UX: replace insider vocabulary with standard software-engineering terms
description:
## Objective
Replace the surviving insider glossary vocabulary in Ortus with standard software-engineering terms, and record a naming bar in the glossary module so any future coinage must justify why no standard term fits.

## Behavioral context
Today README.md, worker prompts, CLI help, and log prose use private coinages (leaf, packet, plan-gap, main path, boundary) that a new engineer must be taught before any sentence about the system parses; the glossary (src/ortus/core/glossary.py, rendered into README.md, enforced by tests/test_glossary_docs.py) even carries team_role/analogy columns to make them teachable. After this change the same documents read with standard vocabulary (task, work spec, planning gap, happy path, phase transition), the glossary shrinks toward genuinely novel concepts, and serialized tokens (journal field names, the uppercase PLAN-GAP marker) are explicitly kept stable so no stored data or prompt contract breaks. Cautionary example (operator, 2026-08-11): Gastown — respected, but its polecats, mayors, governors, whizbangs and whatsits mean every document reads as lore before it reads as engineering; Ortus goes the other way and spends novelty only where the concept itself is genuinely novel.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Rename the surviving insider glossary terms to standard SE vocabulary mechanically everywhere at once: the TERMS declaration in src/ortus/core/glossary.py, the regenerated README glossary block, worker prompt prose under src/ortus/prompts/, CLI help text in src/ortus/cli.py and the command modules, and grind/dashboard operator-facing prose. Add the naming bar to the glossary module docstring.

## Non-goals
Do not rename what the lean pipeline deletes: disown, the seal apparatus, and the verdict/attribution machinery are removed by ortus-l2u9.4 per prd/PRD-lean-pipeline.md, and renaming a term scheduled for deletion is wasted churn. Do not change serialized journal field names, journal phase names, log event kinds, or the uppercase PLAN-GAP token that workers emit and grind parses — prose only. Do not touch prd/ history or git history. Terms that already are standard vocabulary stay: harness, worker, phase, readiness, journal.

## Concrete locations
src/ortus/core/glossary.py — `Term` dataclass, the `TERMS` list (~line 85), `sort_key()`, `render_glossary_table()`; README.md glossary block between the generated markers (tests/test_glossary_docs.py enforces declaration/render agreement — regenerate, never hand-edit); src/ortus/core/lifecycle.py `render_readme_block()` and the `main_path` machine attribute, with the state-graph block enforced by tests/test_state_graph_docs.py; src/ortus/commands/grind.py `_correction_task()` and `_plan_gap_task()` (packet and PLAN-GAP prose); src/ortus/commands/dashboard.py `packet_path()`; worker prompts under src/ortus/prompts/; CLI help strings in src/ortus/cli.py. CodeGraph evidence: `TERMS` has 2 callers inside glossary.py and `render_glossary_table` has 6, all covered by tests/test_glossary_docs.py.

## Resolved decisions
Renames: leaf becomes task (it is a grindable bd issue; the tree metaphor is load-bearing nowhere). packet becomes work spec (it is the structured issue document handed to a worker). plan-gap becomes planning gap in prose, while the serialized uppercase PLAN-GAP marker stays byte-identical because workers emit it and grind parses it. main path becomes happy path (lifecycle uses it for the nothing-goes-wrong walk through the state machine). boundary becomes phase transition. Scoping to surviving terms was chosen over sequencing after ortus-l2u9.4 so this issue stays independently executable. Journal schema field names are not renamed — a compat read path costs more than the prose win.

## Compatibility constraints
Serialized data stays stable: journal phases and field names, log event kinds, and the PLAN-GAP marker are unchanged, so existing run records and replay paths keep parsing. No candidate journal phase name changes hands in this leaf, so the lifecycle.py declaration and README state-graph block only change if their prose mentions a renamed term; if a phase name ever did change, both must move together per repository law. CLI verb names and flags are unchanged on all platforms.

## Ordered steps
1. Update the TERMS declaration in src/ortus/core/glossary.py with the renamed terms and adjusted definitions and homes.
2. Add the naming bar to the glossary module docstring under a heading named Naming bar: a new coinage must state why no standard term fits.
3. Regenerate the README glossary block inside the markers via the renderer; if it drifts, tests/test_glossary_docs.py prints the correct block.
4. Rename prose occurrences in src/ortus/prompts/, src/ortus/cli.py help strings, src/ortus/commands/grind.py worker-facing prose, and src/ortus/commands/dashboard.py labels, keeping serialized tokens byte-identical.
5. Audit with `rg -n -e "plan-gap" -e "packet" -e "main path" -e "\bleaf\b" src/ortus README.md` and fix stragglers, leaving prd/ and history untouched.
6. Run the targeted tests plus the prompt-composition tests.

## Dependencies
No blocking issue dependency: the rename is scoped to terms that survive ortus-l2u9.4 (open), so ordering with the lean-pipeline deletion is decoupled by construction. Code consumers: tests/test_glossary_docs.py and tests/test_state_graph_docs.py consume the generated README blocks; worker prompt files under src/ortus/prompts/ are consumed by compose_worker_prompt in src/ortus/commands/grind.py.

## Edge cases
sort_key() orders hyphenated terms by their words, so renamed multi-word terms must still land where an alphabetical lookup expects them. A case-insensitive rename sweep must not catch the uppercase PLAN-GAP marker. Generated README regions change only via regeneration, never hand-edits. Old spellings in prd/, .beads history, and commit history are expected and stay. Prompt-contract prose is worker-visible, so prompt tests must actually rerun, not be assumed green.

## Plan-gap guidance
If a surviving term turns out to be serialized in journals or parsed from logs rather than prose-only, or a chosen replacement collides with an existing distinct concept in the codebase, stop, record PLAN-GAP naming both the term and the colliding symbol, preserve candidate state, and route to planning rather than inventing a third name. Do the same if ortus-l2u9.4 lands mid-work and deletes a term this leaf is mid-rename on.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: The glossary declaration and the regenerated README glossary block agree, and leaf, packet, plan-gap, main path, and boundary are no longer declared terms.
- AC-2: The README state-graph block still matches the lifecycle declaration after the prose renames.
- AC-3: README.md's prose carries no old spelling of the renamed vocabulary (lowercase plan-gap, packet, or main path); the generated state-graph block is exempt, because it renders the journal's serialized phase names verbatim and those names are unchanged by this leaf's non-goals.
- AC-4: The glossary module docstring records the naming bar for future terms.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_glossary_docs.py -q`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_state_graph_docs.py -q`
- AC-3: `awk '/BEGIN GENERATED: state-graph/,/END GENERATED: state-graph/{next} {print}' README.md | rg -n -e "plan-gap" -e "packet" -e "main path"; test $? -eq 1`
- AC-4: `rg -n "Naming bar" src/ortus/core/glossary.py`

## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_glossary_docs.py tests/test_state_graph_docs.py -q` for the generated blocks, and `uv run pytest tests/test_core_compose.py -q` for the worker-prompt surface the renamed prose flows through.

title: Rebuild the dashboard for the lean pipeline: branch-and-commits model, pipeline stages, live activity
description:
Complete rebuild of `ortus dashboard`, for two reasons that compound.

**1. The model it renders no longer exists.** The dashboard (src/ortus/commands/dashboard.py) still speaks the pre-pivot vocabulary: a candidate as a dirty set minus a claim baseline, owned/inherited/disowned path groups, a verdict envelope, parsed verifier-report criterion matrices. Since the L0 keystone (ortus-rcdf.1) a candidate is a commit or range on `ortus/<issue-id>`; under prd/PRD-lean-pipeline.md verification becomes a deterministic harness — AC runner → red–green proof → claim diff → gate → optional agent reviewer (default off) — with corrections returning in-session and the attribution/disowning machinery deleted outright (ortus-l2u9.4). Every region built on that machinery must be replaced, not restyled.

**2. It should feel alive while doing it.** Vibrant, entertaining, informative to watch: a scrolling activity stream, motion, color — not five static text panes.

New region model (replacing header/current-action/candidate/verdict/warnings):

- **Run header** — issue id/priority/title, phase, iteration, elapsed, correction retries against the in-context bound, watchdog headroom. Largely survives; retire correction-*task* framing for in-session correction rounds.
- **Current action** — KEEP the region and its guarantees (operator-endorsed 2026-08-11): the age-based thinking/blocked call and the pytest-workspace evidence line survive unchanged. Two changes:
  1. *Lead with meaning, then mechanics.* The region shows a brief derived phrase of what is going on, then the raw action/command under it — e.g. "running the test suite" over `Bash: uv run pytest tests/test_dashboard.py -x`, "editing the dashboard renderer" over `Edit: src/ortus/commands/dashboard.py`. The phrase is derived deterministically from the tool kind and its argument (verb from the tool, object from the path/command — same derivation the activity stream uses), never invented: a tool call the deriver does not recognize gets a generic phrase, and the raw action line below stays the ground truth.
  2. *Relax the truncation.* ACTION_TEXT_CHARS is a hard 100-char clip today and there is plenty of dashboard space. Size the clip to the terminal width (or let the command wrap to two or three lines); same relaxation for the evidence lines. Keep a bound of some kind so an unbounded tool argument still cannot own the region.
- **Branch panel** (replaces candidate) — the issue branch name, merge base and head, commits in `merge-base..head` with subjects, files touched in the range, ahead-of-integration count, parked/active state. Owned/inherited/disowned dies with attribution.
- **Pipeline panel** (replaces verdict) — the lean stages as a visible pipeline: AC runner per-criterion rows (command, exit code, pass/fail, proves-new/guards-existing tag), red–green proof state (red-on-base proven? green-on-branch?), claim diff agreement, gate/CI status, merge decision. Stages not yet reached render as pending, preserving the outstanding-work-is-visible property the verdict region had. Until ortus-l2u9.3 lands, an interim source is the shim verifier's report; build the panel against the harness's recorded results (tracker comment / structured log events) and keep the shim path only as long as it exists.
- **Activity stream** (new) — scrolling feed of worker actions from the grind log, complementing the current-action region: current action answers "what is it doing right now and is it stuck", the stream answers "what has it been doing" — file paths being edited with a short derived summary ("editing src/ortus/core/agent.py", "running pytest tests/test_dashboard.py"), tool kind, timestamps; new entries highlight then fade to dim. The stream and the current-action phrase share one derivation, so the feed and the headline never disagree about the same event.
- **Status line** (new) — Claude-style rotating whimsical gerund ("Flummoxing…", "Percolating…", "Crafting…") decorating the truthful state (thinking / blocked-on-subprocess / verifying / merging / ended), with spinner and elapsed. Word rotates on tick so stillness still reads as a stall.
- **Warnings** — keep, with the ortus evidence line per warning; vocabulary re-derived from the lean pipeline's actual failure modes (AC command failed, red–green not proven, claim mismatch, parked at retry bound, gate red).

Vibrancy throughout: richer palette, sparkline/trend indicators (actions per minute, AC criteria passed over time), animated region state transitions.

Constraints that survive the rebuild:
- Read-only invariant: run state stays a pure function of log + journal + git plumbing reads; every bd call behind bd_argv's --readonly --sandbox pins; tests keep asserting both. Git reads must also be read-only (rev-list/diff-tree/log only, no index writes).
- Stillness means death: every animation tick-driven; a stalled dashboard visibly freezes.
- Truth over decoration: playful words decorate real states, never replace them; blocked is still blocked, evidence still labelled evidence, and the derived phrase never displaces the raw command it summarizes.
- Replay (--replay) renders finished runs through the same regions, scrolling the activity stream at replay pace.
- The module docstring's austere no-emoji posture is deliberately revised; update the design rationale, keep glyphs terminal-font-safe.

Sequencing: the branch panel, activity stream, status line, and both current-action changes can build against the L0 reality now. The pipeline panel's final form depends on how ortus-l2u9.1–.3 record results; file its leaf when the AC runner's output shape is settled, and rip out the verifier-report/verdict-envelope parsing in the same change that repoints the panel. tests/test_dashboard.py and tests/test_tail.py assert the old vocabulary (candidate/verdict rendering) and are rewritten alongside.

Suggested child issues (file when work starts):
- runstate: model branch/commits/pipeline-stage state from journal + log + read-only git; retire dirty-set candidate fields.
- Action phrasing: one deterministic tool-call → phrase derivation shared by the current-action headline and the activity stream.
- Current action: phrase-over-command layout; width-aware (or wrapping) clip replacing the fixed 100-char ACTION_TEXT_CHARS.
- Branch panel replacing the candidate region.
- Pipeline panel replacing the verdict region (after AC-runner output shape settles).
- Activity stream region with highlight-then-fade rendering.
- Whimsical status line mapped to truthful states.
- Vibrancy pass: palette, sparklines, transitions; docstring + test posture updates.

title: ci: bump the workflow's GitHub Actions to current majors, proven on a branch run
description:
## Objective

Move the workflow's GitHub Actions to their current major versions — `astral-sh/setup-uv@v3` and the `actions/*@v4` family are behind — and prove the bumped workflow on a real branch run before it reaches the integration branch.

## Behavioral context

Before. The test workflow uses `actions/checkout@v4`, `astral-sh/setup-uv@v3`, `actions/setup-node@v4` and `actions/upload-artifact@v4` across its jobs. Action majors deprecate on GitHub's schedule, not the repository's, and setup-uv in particular has moved several majors past v3.

After. Each action runs its current major, and the proof is a real run: the `ortus/**` branch trigger added by ortus-kdqt means a pushed branch runs the full matrix with the bumped workflow before any merge — the first upgrade in this repository able to use the branch gate for its own verification.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Bump every `uses:` reference in the test workflow to the action's current major, adjust any input renamed across the majors, and verify with a real branch-triggered run of the full matrix.

## Non-goals

Do not restructure jobs, the matrix, the gate invocation, the concurrency group, or the bd install steps. Do not pin to commit SHAs — the repository's convention is major tags, and changing that convention is its own decision. Do not touch the release workflow if one exists separately.

## Concrete locations

- `.github/workflows/test.yml` — every `uses:` line: `actions/checkout@v4`, `astral-sh/setup-uv@v3` (two jobs), `actions/setup-node@v4` (two jobs), `actions/upload-artifact@v4` (three sites).

## Resolved decisions

1. Current major per action, resolved at implementation time from each repository's releases — not the majors named here.
2. Inputs are re-checked against each new major's README; a renamed or removed input (setup-uv's cache flags have churned across majors) is adjusted as part of the bump, since the bump is meaningless if the step silently stops caching.
3. Verification is a real run: push `ortus/dep-gha-check` (the kdqt trigger fires the matrix), confirm all legs green, delete the branch. A workflow change proven only by YAML parsing is the environment-divergence lesson ignored.
4. All actions move in one leaf — one workflow file, one verifying run, and NFR-3 forbids splitting one file across open leaves anyway.

## Compatibility constraints

Job names, the matrix, the gate line, artifact names and the concurrency group are unchanged, so `ortus-kdqt`'s AC checks and any dashboard reading run names keep holding. The workflow must remain valid for the `release-smoke` job's conditional trigger.

## Ordered steps

1. Resolve each action's current major and any renamed inputs.
2. Update every `uses:` line and adjust inputs.
3. Validate the YAML loads and both jobs are intact.
4. Push `ortus/dep-gha-check`, confirm the full matrix passes with the bumped actions, delete the branch.
5. Record old → new per action in the completion comment.

## Dependencies

Depends on the bd-toolchain leaf: both edit `.github/workflows/test.yml`, and no two open leaves may modify one file (PRD NFR-3).

## Edge cases

An action whose new major changes a default (upload-artifact v4 changed overwrite semantics between others' majors) must be checked against how the workflow actually uses it, not assumed compatible. A branch run that fails only on one matrix leg is a real finding about the bump. The verification branch must be deleted even on failure — the run record persists. If the runner image lacks something a new major needs, that is a plan gap, not a reason to pin backward silently.

## Plan-gap guidance

Stop and report rather than improvising if any leg fails under the bumped actions or an input has no equivalent in the new major. Never merge a workflow bump whose only evidence is local YAML validation, and never leave the verification branch behind.

title: deps: refresh the Python lock with uv lock --upgrade under the full gate
description:
## Objective

Refresh the locked Python dependency set to current releases within the declared floors, with the full gate green against the new lock, so the pipeline runs on maintained versions instead of whatever was current at the last lock.

## Behavioral context

Before. `uv.lock` resolves 143 packages against floors in `pyproject.toml` (`typer>=0.12.0`, `rich>=13.7.0`, `textual>=1.0.0`, pytest tooling, and the rest), and the lock ages silently — nothing in the pipeline ever refreshes it, so drift accumulates until something forces the issue in an unrelated change.

After. `uv lock --upgrade` moves every locked version to the newest the floors admit, the full gate passes against the result, and any package that cannot move without a floor bump is named in the completion comment rather than silently pinned back.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Run `uv lock --upgrade`, sync, run the full gate against the new lock, and record what moved and what could not.

## Non-goals

Do not raise version floors or change `requires-python` — a floor bump is a compatibility decision that deserves its own leaf with the breaking-change evidence. Do not add or remove dependencies. Do not touch the bd toolchain or workflow files, which have their own leaves.

## Concrete locations

- `uv.lock` — the entire change surface.
- `pyproject.toml` — read for the floors; not modified.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` — read only, to mirror the gate invocation (`pytest -m "fast or integration"`).

## Resolved decisions

1. Floors stay; the lock moves. Within-floor upgrades are what a lock refresh is for, and anything needing a floor bump is a finding, not a fix.
2. The full gate decides, run as CI runs it plus `-n auto` per repository testing policy, with `codegraph` masked from `PATH` per the gating rule.
3. A test broken by an upgraded package is a plan gap carrying the package's name, the old and new versions, and the failing tests — never resolved by quietly re-pinning inside this leaf.
4. The completion comment lists the notable moves (direct dependencies old → new), because a lockfile diff is unreadable as a record.

## Compatibility constraints

`pyproject.toml` byte-identical. Supported Python range unchanged (3.10–3.12 per the CI matrix). The lock must resolve on the platforms uv already locks for; no platform markers change.

## Ordered steps

1. Run `uv lock --upgrade` and `uv sync --all-extras`.
2. Run the full gate per Targeted tests with `codegraph` masked from `PATH`.
3. Summarize direct-dependency moves in the completion comment.

## Dependencies

None. Disjoint files from the toolchain and Actions leaves.

## Edge cases

A resolver conflict that only appears with `--upgrade` is a real finding about the floors — report it. An upgrade that only fails on a Python version this machine lacks will surface on the CI matrix; the branch gate now runs on `ortus/**` pushes, so the failure arrives before merge in a grind flow. A lock that changes nothing is a legitimate completion ("already current").

## Plan-gap guidance

Stop and report rather than improvising if the gate fails against the new lock or the resolution needs a floor change. Never edit `pyproject.toml`, and never hand-pin a package inside the lock.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1: `uv.lock` is regenerated with `uv lock --upgrade` and the tree carries no other source change.
- AC-2: The full gate passes against the new lock.
- AC-3: `pyproject.toml` is byte-identical.
- AC-4: The completion comment lists direct-dependency moves, or states the lock was already current.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `git diff --name-only` contains `uv.lock` and tracker exports only
- AC-2: `uv run pytest -m "fast or integration" -n auto --test-timeout=180 -q` exits 0
- AC-3: `git diff --stat pyproject.toml` prints nothing
- AC-4: `bd comments <this-issue> --json` contains an "old → new" move list or the words "already current"

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest -m "fast or integration" -n auto --test-timeout=180 -q`
