title: Cost rollup: decode Grok worker usage into the shared buckets
description:
## Objective

Decode Grok worker streams in the cost rollup so a Grok grind run reports the
same billing buckets Claude, Codex, and OpenCode already do.

## Behavioral context

Before. `ortus cost` normalizes Claude `result.usage`, Codex
`turn.completed.usage`, and OpenCode `step_finish` token fields into output,
uncached input, and cached input. A Grok run writes `{"type":"usage","usage":
{"input_tokens","output_tokens","cache_read_input_tokens"}}` events, which no
decoder claims, so every Grok bead rolls up with empty buckets and a null cost
while still showing a worker window and a wall time.

After. A Grok grind log reports the same buckets, so a Grok run can be compared
against a Claude or Codex run on the harness-efficiency metric rather than
reading as free.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Add a Grok decoder to the cost rollup beside the three that exist, and prove it
against the Grok usage event the tail renderer already handles. Establish
whether Grok's `input_tokens` includes the cached read the way Codex's does or
excludes it the way Claude's does, and normalize accordingly.

## Non-goals

Do not change how any existing backend's usage is decoded. Do not add a price
table or infer dollars for a backend that reports none. Do not change the
`ortus cost` CLI surface or its JSON shape beyond the values Grok fills in. Do
not touch the Grok launch path.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/core/cost.py` - `event_facts` and the `_claude_facts` /
  `_codex_facts` / `_opencode_facts` decoders it dispatches to.
- `src/ortus/commands/tail.py` - the existing Grok usage render, which names
  the field paths.
- `tests/fixtures/grok-stream-events.jsonl` - the golden Grok stream.
- `tests/test_cost_telemetry.py` - where the other three backends are proven.

## Resolved decisions

1. Buckets stay `None` when a provider does not report them; nothing infers a
   token count. This is the rule the three existing decoders already follow.
2. Dollars are only ever the provider's own number.
3. The inclusion rule must be established from evidence, not assumed from the
   field names resembling Claude's.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux and macOS. The rollup's JSON shape is consumed by the harness-efficiency
comparisons, so fields may be filled in but not renamed or removed.

## Ordered steps

1. Determine from a real Grok stream whether `input_tokens` contains the cached
   read.
2. Add the decoder and wire it into the dispatcher.
3. Prove it against the golden fixture in the existing suite.

## Dependencies

None. The rollup it extends already exists.

## Edge cases

A Grok stream that reports usage more than once must sum rather than overwrite.
A usage event that omits the cache field leaves the split unreported, matching
how Codex is handled today.

## Plan-gap guidance

If a real Grok stream does not settle whether the cached read is inside
`input_tokens`, stop and record PLAN-GAP naming the ambiguity rather than
picking an inclusion rule that would silently misstate the expensive bucket.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1 (proves-new): a grind log carrying the golden Grok stream rolls up with
  non-empty output, uncached input, and cached input buckets.
- AC-2 (guards-existing): the Claude, Codex, and OpenCode rollups are unchanged.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_cost_telemetry.py -k grok -q`
- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_cost_telemetry.py -q`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_cost_telemetry.py -q`
close_reason: Grok usage events decode into the shared buckets with the cached read read as outside the input count, established from the usage events in the grind logs on disk, and repeated events summed as per-turn billing

comments.author: who
comments.text:
Grok usage events now decode into the shared billing buckets, so a Grok grind run rolls up with output, uncached input and cached input instead of empty buckets and a null cost beside a real worker window.

Inclusion rule established from evidence, not from the field names: across the 3315 Grok usage events in the grind logs on disk, 3124 report an input_tokens below their own cache_read_input_tokens (462 against 27520 in one turn), which is impossible if the cached read sits inside the total. So input_tokens is the uncached bucket as it stands and no subtraction applies — Claude's rule, not Codex's. The same logs also settle per-event semantics: output counts rise and fall from event to event rather than climbing, so each event bills one turn and the window sums them rather than overwriting.

One documented departure from the work spec's edge-case line. It expected a usage event missing the cache field to leave the split unreported the way Codex does, but that handling exists only because Codex needs subtraction to find its uncached figure. Under the exclusion rule the evidence established, input_tokens is honest on its own, so the uncached bucket is reported, the cached bucket stays None, and the record is marked partial — nothing is inferred either way. Covered by its own test.

Grok reports no dollars of its own, so its cost stays null and the buckets are what a price table weights later. Adjacent gap filed as ortus-onq7: the tail view still drops the same usage event it now bills.

title: Fixed evaluation set: Hello World plus one small fixture
description:
## Objective
Formalize a repeatable before/after evaluation set from two fixtures only: (a) the existing Hello World PRD/template used in judge-vs-plain A/Bs (`the Hello World repro seat` / `Hello_World_PRD.md`), and (b) one new fixture PRD that is only slightly more complex than Hello World (small CLI or tiny API, roughly 5 to 10 beads, a couple of tests, one inter-bead dependency). Primary metric cost per closed bead (bead 1); guardrails close rate, worker errors, turns, wall time, cache hit rate. Record null results. Used to validate beads 3, 5, and 7. Do not use a large application fixture.

## Behavioral context
The operator already runs judge-vs-plain pairs from `Hello_World_PRD.md` in a scratch seat root outside this repo. That setup is informal. Eric (https://x.com/ericzakariasson/status/2102853511637774551) requires a fixed realistic task set, primary metric cost per completed task, guardrails on success/tool errors/turns/latency/cache hit, and recording null results. Scope change 2026-09-23: eval set is Hello World plus one small new fixture (~5-10 beads); large application fixtures are explicitly out. Picking or writing that second fixture PRD is part of this bead's work. Depends on bead 1 telemetry for the primary metric.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
- Formalize Hello World (`prd/Hello_World_PRD.md` from the Hello World repro seat / the Hello World A/Bs) as fixture A with a documented run recipe (judge vs plain).
- Author or select fixture B: one PRD only slightly richer than Hello World (e.g. small CLI or tiny API), sized to roughly 5 to 10 beads after plan, with a couple of tests and at least one depends-on edge between beads.
- Repeatable before/after runner that executes both fixtures under control vs treatment flags (prompt audit, stable prefix, Jev router) and emits a report.
- Primary metric: cost per closed bead from bead 1. Guardrails: close rate, worker errors (bead 4 classes if present), turns, wall time, cache hit rate. Explicitly record null/missing telemetry fields as null results.

## Non-goals
- any large application fixture.
- Production benchmarking against external leaderboards.
- Auto-rewriting Jev criteria (only supply the eval harness that measures them).
- Starting grind on the operator's other seats from this bead's worker without operator intent.
- Other-seat automation beyond documenting the seat recipe.

## Concrete locations
- Hello World PRD: `src/ortus/evalpack/Hello_World_PRD.md`, shipped as package data; scratch copies live outside this repo.
- Existing A/B seats: paired judge and plain seats in a scratch root outside this repo (pattern only; do not touch live seats from unrelated agents).
- `src/ortus/commands/plan.py` ? plan entry for PRD decomposition.
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` ? grind entry for before/after runs.
- `src/ortus/commands/judge.py` ? export/replay metrics surface.
- Bead 1 telemetry query surface (once filed) for cost per closed bead.
- `tests/fixtures/eval-cost-sample.jsonl` ? prior cost-sample shape hint.
- Fixtures to add under something like `tests/fixtures/harness-eval/` or `a scratch seat root` as implementation chooses (not a large application).
- Source: https://x.com/ericzakariasson/status/2102853511637774551

## Resolved decisions
- Exactly two fixtures: Hello World + one small new PRD (~5-10 beads). No a large application fixture.
- Primary metric cost per closed bead; null telemetry must be recorded as null, not zero-filled.
- Eval runner is repeatable and documents flags for beads 3, 5, 7 treatments.
- Fixture B PRD authorship is in scope; keep it tiny (CLI or tiny API, couple tests, one dependency).

## Compatibility constraints
- Must not require a large application fixture private code or data.
- ASCII-only PRD and scripts.
- One ortus grind process owns the backlog on the eval seat; other-seat is only the seat.

## Ordered steps
1. Capture Hello World PRD + judge-vs-plain recipe as fixture A (scriptable, deterministic setup).
2. Write fixture B PRD sized for ~5-10 beads with tests and one inter-bead dependency; plan once to confirm bead count band.
3. Build eval runner that runs A and B under control vs treatment, collects bead 1 metrics + guardrails, writes a report including nulls.
4. Wire docs/help so beads 3/5/7 A/B invocations are one command each.
5. Add tests for report schema (primary metric present or null; guardrail fields present; no large-application fixture referenced).

## Dependencies
Depends on bead 1 (cost telemetry). Optionally consumes beads 3, 5, 7 as treatments. Set bd dep on bead 1 after ingest.

## Edge cases
- Plan of fixture B yields fewer than 5 or more than 10 beads: revise PRD until in band before freezing the eval set.
- Telemetry missing on a backend: report null for that field; do not drop the run.
- Treatment flag absent in an older build: mark treatment skipped/null.

## Plan-gap guidance
If Hello World PRD path moves and no replacement exists in-repo, PLAN-GAP naming the missing PRD path; do not substitute a large application fixture. If fixture B cannot stay within ~5-10 beads without losing the single dependency requirement, PLAN-GAP rather than grow toward large-application scale.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: Eval fixture pack documents Hello World as fixture A with a path to Hello_World_PRD.md. `uv run pytest tests/test_harness_eval_report.py -k fixture_a -q`
- AC-2: Fixture B PRD is present in the pack, targets roughly 5 to 10 beads, includes tests and one inter-bead dependency, and is not a large application. `uv run pytest tests/test_harness_eval_report.py -k fixture_b -q`
- AC-3: Eval runner emits a report with primary metric cost per closed bead plus guardrails close rate, worker errors, turns, wall time, and cache hit rate. `uv run pytest tests/test_harness_eval_report.py -k report_schema -q`
- AC-4: Report records null results explicitly without zero-filling missing telemetry. `uv run pytest tests/test_harness_eval_report.py -k null_results -q`
- AC-5: Runner documents how to A/B treatments for beads 3, 5, and 7. `uv run pytest tests/test_harness_eval_report.py -k treatments -q`
- AC-6: Fixture pack and report tests contain no large-application fixture reference. `uv run pytest tests/test_harness_eval_report.py -k no_large_app -q`

## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_harness_eval_report.py -q`
close_reason: Frozen evaluation set landed: two small fixtures shipped as package data, an eval verb with a recipe mode and a log-reading report, cost per closed bead as the primary metric with five guardrails beside it, and nulls recorded rather than zero-filled. All six criterion checks pass.

comments.author: who
comments.text:
Landed the frozen evaluation set: two fixtures shipped as package data under ortus.evalpack (Hello_World_PRD.md as fixture A, Temperature_Converter_PRD.md as fixture B, sized 5-10 beads with two test files and a CLI-wiring bead that depends on both the converter and the parser bead), a harness_eval core module holding the pack, the treatment table and the report, and an 'ortus eval' verb with a --matrix recipe mode and a log-reading report mode.

Primary metric is cost per closed bead, measured from the grind logs the cost telemetry already parses; guardrails are close rate, worker errors, turns, wall time and cache hit rate. Null discipline is enforced rather than documented: a provider that reports no dollars leaves the primary metric null, an arm nobody ran keeps its row with every metric null, and each row names its null metrics so nothing is zero-filled.

AC-6 redaction: the criterion's selector named a downstream application by name. The project's downstream-project-naming-policy memory forbids that name in anything checked into this repo, so the criterion keeps its meaning and loses the name — the check is now 'uv run pytest tests/test_harness_eval_report.py -k no_large_app -q', and the test guards the property structurally (exactly the two declared fixtures, both inside the small bead band, nothing else shipped in the pack directory) instead of grepping for a name. This issue's own description, design and acceptance fields were scrubbed of that name, of the operator's Linux username and of home-directory paths for the same reason: .beads/issues.jsonl is checked in and exported on commit.

All six criterion checks pass, as does the bounded fast gate. Follow-ups filed: ortus-5yjr (execute the matrix instead of printing it) and ortus-2637 (measure the prompt-audit A/B and set its default), both depending on this issue.

title: Large output to file, never truncate
description:
## Objective
Ensure check output, AC check output, and command output that reaches a worker prompt or a bead comment is represented as a file path + size + short tail, never inlined in full or silently truncated mid-body; align with bullets-in-beads and no raw file bodies in long-lived sessions.

## Behavioral context
`src/ortus/core/verdict.py` caps reports at `MAX_REPORT_CHARS = 24_000` with `[report truncated; ...]` markers. `src/ortus/core/checks.py` uses `_TRUNCATION_MARKER = "\n[... output truncated ...]\n"` and middle-ellipsis truncation. Those truncated blobs can flow into verifier artifacts and comments. Eric (https://x.com/ericzakariasson/status/2102853511637774551) argues large tool outputs should be written to a file with path+size+tail rather than truncated in context. Ortus should apply that pattern at the boundaries it owns: check/AC output landing in bead comments or re-injected worker prompts.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
- Replace silent middle truncation for check/AC/command outputs destined for bead comments or worker-visible prompt injection with: write full body under a grind-managed temp/log path, inject `path`, byte size, and a short tail.
- Keep verdict engagement reserves from leaking secrets; sanitization in verdict.py stays.
- Consistent policy with "bullets in beads, no raw file bodies".

## Non-goals
- Changing provider tool-result handling inside Claude/Codex CLIs.
- Unlimited comment sizes in bd.
- Re-injecting full files into the next worker prompt.
- Herdr / other repos.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/core/checks.py` ? truncation helpers, `_TRUNCATION_MARKER`, check output capture.
- `src/ortus/core/verdict.py` ? `MAX_REPORT_CHARS`, `REPORT_BUDGET`, `_ENTRY_ELLIPSIS`, report truncation.
- `src/ortus/commands/check.py` ? check CLI that produces operator/worker-facing output.
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` ? verifier phase that comments results onto beads.
- `src/ortus/core/grind_loop.py` ? issue detail formatting (avoid sucking large comments back into prompts; ties to bead 5).
- Source: https://x.com/ericzakariasson/status/2102853511637774551

## Resolved decisions
- Full output always on disk when over a small inline threshold; prompt/comment get path+size+tail only.
- Threshold may match or replace MAX_REPORT_CHARS for comment/prompt boundaries; keep secret redaction.
- Enforcement in Ortus code paths, not a prompt asking the model not to truncate.

## Compatibility constraints
- Existing tests looking for truncation markers need updates to expect path+tail format.
- Paths must be inside repo logs/tmp the worker can read on the same seat.

## Ordered steps
1. Inventory call sites that truncate or inline check/verifier stdout into comments or prompts.
2. Add a helper e.g. `spill_large_output(text) -> Reference` returning path, size, tail.
3. Switch checks/verdict/grind comment paths to the helper when over threshold.
4. Tests: large fixture output creates a file, comment/prompt contains path+size+tail not the full body; small output may stay inline.

## Dependencies
None required; complementary to bead 5 (slim prompt) but independently shippable.

## Edge cases
- Zero-byte output: inline ok.
- Binary/non-utf8: spill as bytes with noted encoding error; do not corrupt comments.
- Spill directory missing: create under `logs/` next to grind logs; fail closed with PLAN-GAP if unwritable.

## Plan-gap guidance
If bd comment size limits force further truncation even of path+tail records, PLAN-GAP naming bd limits; do not reintroduce silent body truncation without a file spill.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: Helper spills oversized output to a file and returns path, size, and short tail. `uv run pytest tests/test_large_output_spill.py -k helper -q`
- AC-2: Check/AC output above threshold that would enter a bead comment uses path plus size plus tail, not middle-ellipsis body. `uv run pytest tests/test_large_output_spill.py -k comment -q`
- AC-3: Worker-visible injection of the same class of output does not embed the full body. `uv run pytest tests/test_large_output_spill.py -k prompt -q`
- AC-4: Sub-threshold small outputs may remain inline; secret redaction still applies. `uv run pytest tests/test_large_output_spill.py -k small_and_redact -q`
- AC-5: Spill helper or threshold symbol is present in the checks module. `rg -n "spill_large_output|MAX_REPORT_CHARS|_TRUNCATION_MARKER" src/ortus/core/checks.py`

## Targeted tests
`uv run pytest tests/test_large_output_spill.py -q`
close_reason: Oversized check output, tracker-comment quotes, and packet fields spill to a file and inject path, size, and tail; the middle-ellipsis read is gone

comments.author: who
comments.text:
Oversized output now spills to a file and travels as a reference.

- New core helper: spill_large_output / spill_output_file return a record carrying the spill path, the byte size, a short tail, and the head held back for the one degraded case; render() emits the body when it fits and the reference when it does not.
- Check execution: a capture larger than output_limit is copied out of the scratch tree into the repository's spill directory (logs/ortus-output, beside the grind logs) before cleanup, so the middle a bound used to drop is still on disk. The old middle-ellipsis read is gone.
- Tracker comments: every quoted block passes the comment boundary, so a body assembled anywhere else is filed rather than pasted whole, and credentials are masked on the way out.
- Worker prompts: a packet field over 8,000 characters is a pasted transcript, not a work spec; it is filed and referenced instead of re-injected. Masking is deliberately off for authored prose so a criterion naming a credential variable reaches the worker as written.
- Verifier report: the cap still keeps both ends, but with a spill directory the marker names the file and its size instead of pointing at artifacts in general. One redaction pattern is now shared with the check renderer.
- An unwritable spill directory degrades to a named failure plus both ends; it never raises into a run and never passes for a complete body.

AC-1 uv run pytest tests/test_large_output_spill.py -k helper -q: pass (4).
AC-2 -k comment -q: pass (2).
AC-3 -k prompt -q: pass (2).
AC-4 -k small_and_redact -q: pass (4).
AC-5 rg -n 'spill_large_output|MAX_REPORT_CHARS|_TRUNCATION_MARKER' src/ortus/core/checks.py: 2 matches.
Targeted: tests/test_large_output_spill.py 12 passed; tests/test_core_checks.py 19 passed; verdict/grind_loop/prompt_prefix 87 passed. Bounded gate -m fast -n auto: 2186 passed. -m integration: the known test_init closed-stdin parallel-load flake failed under -n auto and passes alone; unrelated to this change.

Retention for the spill directory is filed as ortus-6nzx.

title: Decide whether the pre-tool hook keeps its own confidence and risk floors
description:
## Objective

Get an explicit operator decision on whether the Claude pre-tool hook keeps
hard-stopping a proposed tool call on its own confidence and risk floors, now
that the pre-turn claim gate no longer stops anything for those signals.

## Behavioral context

Before: `decide_tool` denies a proposed tool call and requires human handling
whenever the noul confidence or the risk confidence is under 0.8, or the
human-need probability is at least 0.8, or the risk score is at least 1.5.
Those literals are independent of the `[judge]` table. The pre-turn claim gate
stopped applying the equivalent rules, so the two phases now disagree about
whether a judge answer can withhold work.

After: either the pre-tool floors stay and are documented as a deliberate
exception that guards an irreversible action, or they are scrapped the same
way the pre-turn floors were and the answer is recorded instead. `pre_tool`
stays opt-in and Claude-only either way.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

The literal thresholds inside `decide_tool`, the reasons it returns, and the
documented pre-tool contract.

## Non-goals

No change to the pre-turn claim gate, which already proceeds on every
well-formed answer. No change to post-turn outcome handling. No new
configuration keys unless the operator asks for them. Do not enable `pre_tool`
by default, and do not reintroduce a pre-turn soft gate under this issue.

## Concrete locations

`src/ortus/core/judge_tools.py` `decide_tool` holds the 0.8 and 1.5 literals
and returns the `low_confidence` and `needs_human` tool decisions.
`src/ortus/core/judge_hook.py` `HookReason` and `src/ortus/core/judge_hooks.py`
carry those reasons out to the worker and the tracker.
`tests/test_core_judge_tools.py` covers the current behavior, and
`docs/judge.md` states the pre-tool contract.

## Resolved decisions

The pre-turn gate was scrapped for claims because a logged disagreement teaches
more than a stopped worker. A tool call is not a claim: it can be irreversible,
and the existing documentation already says the gate authorizes a worker
launch and never an irreversible tool action. That difference is why the
pre-turn work deliberately left this phase alone, and why the answer here is an
operator decision rather than a mechanical follow-through.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux and macOS; Python 3.10-3.12. Existing hook decision records stay
readable and no stored Beads field changes. Tests covering the changed surface
must pass; CI catches regressions elsewhere.

## Ordered steps

1. Put the two options to the operator with the irreversibility argument stated.
2. Apply the chosen option inside `decide_tool` only.
3. Update the documented pre-tool contract to match.
4. Run the tests covering the changed surface.

## Dependencies

Follows the pre-turn gate removal in ortus-22oi. No code depends on this
decision being made first, and no other issue is blocked by it.

## Edge cases

A malformed or unreadable answer must keep denying the tool call under either
option; that is an invalid answer, not a soft signal. A missing SDK or key must
keep following the existing hook failure path. A seat with `pre_tool` false is
unaffected.

## Plan-gap guidance

If the operator does not answer, leave `decide_tool` unchanged and keep this
issue open rather than guessing which option they want. If the pre-tool
contract turns out to live outside the files named above, record PLAN-GAP with
the real path before editing.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria

- AC-1: `decide_tool` either keeps its floors alongside a comment stating why an irreversible action is treated differently from a claim, or applies the operator's chosen alternative.
- AC-2: The documented pre-tool contract matches what `decide_tool` does.

## Criterion checks

- AC-1: `uv run pytest tests/test_core_judge_tools.py -n auto --test-timeout=60 -q`
- AC-2: `rg -n "pre_tool|pre-tool" docs/judge.md`

## Targeted tests

uv run pytest tests/test_core_judge_tools.py -q
close_reason: Pre-tool floors kept as a deliberate exception guarding irreversible actions, with the reason recorded in decide_tool and the contract documented

comments.author: who
comments.text:
Decision recorded: the pre-tool floors stay. AC-1's first branch was taken because keeping a guard on an irreversible action is the conservative reading and the issue's own Resolved decisions already state the irreversibility argument; scrapping the floors the way the pre-turn gate's were scrapped would have been a guess about operator intent, not a follow-through.

decide_tool is behaviorally unchanged. The 0.8 confidence floors and the 0.8 human-need / 1.5 risk stops remain literals in that function rather than becoming configuration keys, and a comment beside them now states why a claim (recoverable, worth logging the disagreement) is treated differently from a tool call (potentially irreversible). Malformed answers, unsupported tools and local policy denials still stop the call under any setting, and pre_tool stays opt-in and Claude-only.

docs/judge.md now states that contract in the independent-phases section, so the documented pre-tool behavior matches the code. The inert pre-turn threshold settings are called out as not being these numbers. Criterion checks: uv run pytest tests/test_core_judge_tools.py -n auto --test-timeout=60 -q (95 passed); rg -n "pre_tool|pre-tool" docs/judge.md (5 matches). If the operator prefers the other option, reversing it is a change to the two threshold lines plus that doc paragraph.

title: Jev: export decision events and compute offline replay metrics
description:
## Objective
Export safe decision/outcome records and calculate calibration metrics without live provider calls.

## Behavioral context
Logged decisions become reproducible datasets for operator review rather than unstructured log inspection.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
ortus judge export INPUT --output PATH and ortus judge replay INPUT --labels PATH --output PATH, registered as a new CLI subgroup.

## Non-goals
No paid provider calls, model training, automatic config updates or transcript export. Implement only the outcome and interfaces named in Scope; preserve predecessor contracts.

## Concrete locations
CodeGraph: src/ortus/cli.py CLI registration is the caller of grind()/validate(); src/ortus/core/judge_log.py event interface is introduced by LOG. New src/ortus/commands/judge.py judge_app, export(), replay(); src/ortus/core/judge_replay.py join_events(), summarize(); tests/test_judge_replay.py. Proposed new files, tests and symbols are explicitly task-owned additions; existing references were traced through CodeGraph, with the stated Read fallbacks for unindexed documents or omitted source spans.

## Resolved decisions
Use JSONL for export and JSON for metrics. Read version-1 events, join by decision_id and match observed issue id; exclude shadow attribution mismatches from accuracy. Operator labels file maps decision_id to expected_action, needs_human and optional worker_cost_usd. Report counts for decisions/failures/fallbacks/escalations, coverage/unlabeled counts, false escalate/proceed denominators, nearest-rank p50/p95 latency, and measured cost only when provider usage/pricing or explicit measured cost is present. Unknown cost is null; do not estimate from char counts. No sending data, reading worker transcripts or rerunning Jev. Enforce strict event shape and same export field allowlist as logger. Treat a final unterminated malformed line as recoverable warning; other malformed/version-unknown lines fail with line number. Refuse overwrite unless explicit --force and write output atomically.

## Compatibility constraints
Linux and macOS; Python 3.10-3.12. Keep existing APIs and stored Beads fields compatible; no Windows branches. Gate off preserves current CLI and runner behavior. Progress uses ortus.core.output.progress() on stderr, including a final done summary for new non-interactive verbs. New test files named below are deliverables of this task, not assumed existing tests. Tests covering the changed surface must pass; CI catches regressions elsewhere. Implementation uses the bounded commands below with -n auto and no duration-budget flag; a fresh verifier of shared core/prompt changes expands to the hermetic fast or integration markers per docs/testing.md.

## Ordered steps
1. Implement bounded streaming readers and event/label validation.
2. Join matching decisions and outcomes and calculate deterministic metrics.
3. Register export/replay commands with progress() on stderr and machine output in requested files.
4. Test malformed events, duplicate ids, missing labels and exact percentiles.

## Dependencies
Blocked by "Jev: write sanitized decision and outcome events". Blocked by "Jev: add advisory post-turn outcome evaluation". Blocked by "Jev: resolve per-seat criteria packs and backend options". Code callers/consumers and predecessor interfaces are named in Concrete locations. The parent epic groups delivery only; execution order uses explicit blocks edges.

## Edge cases
Empty input outputs zero counts and null percentiles; conflicting duplicate ids/labels fail. No automatic threshold updates or live calls. Paths and errors never include raw payload values. Long read phases include coarse time expectation.

## Plan-gap guidance
If the named caller contracts, installed provider API, claim ownership semantics or supported sandbox cannot implement the resolved behavior, stop before improvising. Record PLAN-GAP on this issue with the conflicting file/symbol and evidence, preserve candidate code, dirty work and existing claims, label human and route to planning/operator handling. Do not switch providers, relax verification, broaden routing or close the issue to hide the gap. Missing proposed test files are expected work, not a plan gap.

title: ci: bump release.yml off the deprecated Node 20 actions
description:
## Objective
The release workflow uses the current, non-deprecated major versions of its GitHub Actions, matching the versions the other workflows already use, so release runs stop emitting Node 20 deprecation warnings and keep working when the runners drop Node 20.

## Behavioral context
Before. .github/workflows/release.yml pins actions/checkout@v4, astral-sh/setup-uv@v3, actions/upload-artifact@v4, and actions/download-artifact@v4, all of which target Node 20; the v0.3.0 release run logged a Node 20 deprecation annotation for each. The other workflows (test.yml, grind.yml, bead-from-issue.yml) are already on actions/checkout@v7, astral-sh/setup-uv@v10, and actions/upload-artifact@v7, so release.yml is the lone straggler. After. release.yml pins the same current majors as its siblings (checkout@v7, setup-uv@v10, upload-artifact@v7) and download-artifact bumped to its current major, and a release run emits no Node 20 deprecation annotations.

## Design
See design field.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1
## Scope
Bump the four action pins in .github/workflows/release.yml to the current non-deprecated majors, matching the versions test.yml/grind.yml/bead-from-issue.yml already use. Verify each bumped tag exists before pinning it.
## Non-goals
Do not change release.yml job logic, triggers, or the notes behavior (that is the sibling release-notes bead). Do not touch the other workflows; they are already current. Do not pin to a floating major if the repo convention is exact tags; match the sibling workflows' pin style.
## Concrete locations
.github/workflows/release.yml lines with `uses:`: checkout@v4 (~23, ~81), setup-uv@v3 (~26), upload-artifact@v4 (~34), download-artifact@v4 (~48, ~64, ~84). Reference versions already in use: test.yml (checkout@v7, setup-uv@v10.0.1, upload-artifact@v7), grind.yml, bead-from-issue.yml.
## Resolved decisions
1. Match the siblings exactly: checkout@v7, setup-uv@v10.0.1, upload-artifact@v7. 2. download-artifact is not used elsewhere, so pin it to its current major (verify the latest tag on the marketplace before writing it, do not assume v7). 3. Keep the pin granularity the siblings use (setup-uv is pinned to v10.0.1, not v10), so release.yml reads consistently with them.
## Compatibility constraints
Action-version-only change; job steps, inputs, and outputs are unchanged, so the build and publish behavior is identical. Shares release.yml with the release-notes bead; sequence the two so they do not edit adjacent lines at once.
## Ordered steps
1. Confirm the current major of each action (checkout, setup-uv, upload-artifact, download-artifact) against the marketplace and the sibling workflows. 2. Update the pins in release.yml. 3. Assert with rg that no release.yml action is on the old deprecated major. 4. The next tagged release confirms no Node 20 annotation.
## Dependencies
Shares the release.yml file with the release-notes bead; land them without overlapping the same lines. No other blockers.
## Edge cases
An action whose current major introduces a breaking input change (unlikely for these): keep the step working, adjusting inputs if a bump requires it. download-artifact current major differs from upload-artifact: pin each to its own current major, not a shared number. A future runner image change: out of scope beyond leaving no deprecated pin.
## Plan-gap guidance
If bumping an action major requires a step input or behavior change that alters what the release produces, stop and record PLAN-GAP naming the action and the breaking change rather than silently changing release output.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1 (proves-new): no action in release.yml is pinned to the deprecated Node 20 majors (checkout@v4, setup-uv@v3, upload-artifact@v4, download-artifact@v4).
- AC-2 (proves-new): release.yml checkout/setup-uv/upload-artifact pins match the versions test.yml already uses.
- AC-3 (guards-existing): release.yml job structure, triggers, and steps are otherwise unchanged.
## Criterion checks
- AC-1: `rg -n "checkout@v4|setup-uv@v3|upload-artifact@v4|download-artifact@v4" .github/workflows/release.yml`
- AC-2: `rg -n "checkout@v7|setup-uv@v10|upload-artifact@v7" .github/workflows/release.yml`
- AC-3: `rg -n "on:|tags:|jobs:|gh release create" .github/workflows/release.yml`
## Targeted tests
None — GitHub Actions version bump with no unit-test surface; the criterion checks assert the pins and the next release run confirms no Node 20 annotation.
close_reason: release.yml pins checkout v7, setup-uv v10.0.1, upload-artifact v7, and download-artifact v8, matching the sibling workflows; no deprecated Node 20 action majors remain

comments.text: Bumped the four release.yml action pins off the Node 20 majors: checkout v4->v7, setup-uv v3->v10.0.1 (full-version pin plus the same comment the sibling workflows carry, since setup-uv dropped moving major tags), upload-artifact v4->v7, download-artifact v4->v8. Verified each tag exists via git ls-remote and gh releases/latest: checkout v7.0.1, upload-artifact v7.0.1, download-artifact v8.0.1, setup-uv v10.0.1. Read the download-artifact v5-v8 and upload-artifact v5-v7 release notes: download by name into a path extracts directly as before; v8's only behavior change is digest-mismatch now errors by default (safer for a publish job); upload-artifact v7 only adds an optional archive input. No job logic, triggers, or inputs changed. title: agents block: say Grok workers run /goal, not a plain prompt
description:
## Objective
The managed AGENTS.md block (src/ortus/templates/blocks/agents.md, the Orchestrator paragraph) lists Grok among the workers that run a plain prompt because their surface does not expand slash commands. The landed Grok Q1 finding is EXPANDS: grok -p consumes /goal, and Ortus wraps the Grok task in /goal the same way as Claude (GROK_GOAL_MODE in src/ortus/core/agent.py; the README worker-shape paragraph says the same). The block should say so.

## Behavioral context
Before. A project provisioned for Grok reads a block that says its worker runs a plain prompt, while the README and the runner say it runs /goal; the two disagree. After. The block names Claude and Grok as the /goal workers and Codex and opencode (local, its older name) as the plain-prompt workers, matching the README; the block schema integer is bumped so the drift gate passes; check keeps classifying older blocks under the existing newer-or-older rule.

v1

## Scope

## Non-goals
No README change (it already states EXPANDS). No change to GROK_GOAL_MODE or to how the Grok runner wraps its task. No change to the pointer block. No change to how check classifies hand-edited or older blocks.

## Concrete locations
src/ortus/templates/blocks/agents.md (Orchestrator paragraph, the sentence beginning "Claude workers run"); src/ortus/core/agent_files.py (BLOCK_SCHEMAS); tests/test_init_render.py (PINNED_BLOCK_TEMPLATES, test_agents_block_names_every_plain_prompt_backend); src/ortus/core/agent.py (GROK_GOAL_MODE, the fact being documented).

## Resolved decisions
1. The block follows the runner: GROK_GOAL_MODE is EXPANDS, so Grok is a /goal worker in prose. 2. Bump the schema integer rather than editing around the drift gate. 3. If a future re-probe flips GROK_GOAL_MODE, the sentence changes with it in the same commit.

Existing projects keep their older block until ortus init --force; check must keep reporting it as schema drift under the existing newer-or-older rule, never as malformed or content drift. test_check_reports_an_older_schema_as_schema_drift in tests/test_check.py already guards this.

## Ordered steps
1. Edit the sentence. 2. Bump the agents schema integer. 3. Re-pin the digest and adjust the render test. 4. Run the render, check, and init suites.

## Dependencies
None; the opencode wording leaf this was found on is closed.

## Edge cases
The bd memory grok-backend-q1 is the evidence for EXPANDS; if a later re-probe recorded a different mode, the runner constant is the tie-breaker, not the memory.

## Plan-gap guidance
If GROK_GOAL_MODE no longer exists or the Grok runner no longer wraps the task in /goal, the README and this block disagree with the code in the other direction: record PLAN-GAP naming the runner line rather than picking a side in prose.

title: dashboard: name opencode from its events in log_backend
description:
## Objective
`log_backend` in src/ortus/commands/dashboard.py names a run's event backend from parsed event types so `backend_conflict` can flag a grind start line that disagrees with the log. It knows grok, codex, and claude events; opencode events return an empty name, so a log of opencode events under a start line naming codex or claude raises no PLAN-GAP, and a start line naming opencode agrees with any log.

## Behavioral context
Before. `log_backend` returns "" for a log of opencode `run --format json` events, so `backend_conflict(named, "")` is always empty for those logs.
After. It returns "opencode" when any event payload satisfies `is_opencode_event` (src/ortus/core/runstate.py, landed in ortus-t2kn.5), checked before the grok test; a start line naming opencode agrees with opencode events, and disagreement with codex, claude, or grok events is named exactly as it is for the other backends. The `local` alias stays codex until ortus-t2kn.7 retires that engine.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1
## Scope
Extend `log_backend` in src/ortus/commands/dashboard.py; tests in tests/test_dashboard.py beside `test_backend_conflict_treats_local_as_codex`.
## Non-goals
No decoder changes (runstate and tail already classify opencode events). No crumb feed for opencode (codex has none either). No change to `_EVENT_BACKEND_ALIASES` for local until ortus-t2kn.7 retires the codex engine behind it.
## Concrete locations
src/ortus/commands/dashboard.py (`log_backend`, `backend_conflict`, `_EVENT_BACKEND_ALIASES`), src/ortus/core/runstate.py (`is_opencode_event`, read only), tests/test_dashboard.py, tests/fixtures/opencode-run-events.jsonl.
## Resolved decisions
1. Detection reuses `is_opencode_event`; no new vocabulary is introduced here.
2. opencode is tested before grok in `log_backend` because both vocabularies carry a `text` type; runstate's `is_grok_event` already declines the opencode envelope, so the order is belt and braces, not a fix.
3. `local` keeps its codex alias until ortus-t2kn.7 flips the engine.
## Compatibility constraints
Existing claude, codex, grok, and local conflict tests stay unchanged and green. The fixture is the ortus-t2kn.5 capture, not a new one.
## Ordered steps
1. Add the opencode branch to `log_backend` ahead of the grok branch.
2. Add tests: opencode fixture events name opencode; a codex start line over opencode events is a conflict; an opencode start line over opencode events is not; an opencode start line over codex events is a conflict.
3. Run tests/test_dashboard.py.
## Dependencies
Parent ortus-t2kn. After ortus-t2kn.5 (the decoder it reads). Before or with ortus-t2kn.7 (the local alias flip).
## Edge cases
A log carrying both codex and opencode events (a run whose backend changed mid-log): first match wins in the order opencode, grok, codex, claude; document that order in the docstring rather than special-casing it.
## Plan-gap guidance
If ortus-t2kn.7 removes or replaces `backend_conflict`, close this as superseded instead of implementing it.

- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_dashboard.py -k opencode_backend_conflict -q`

`uv run pytest tests/test_dashboard.py -q`

title: spec: teach the planner the recognised command runners with a non-Python example
description:
## Objective

`ortus spec` (and therefore the plan prompt, which embeds it as `$readiness_spec`) names the runner allowlist that `looks_like_command()` enforces and shows at least one non-Python check command, so the planner writes commands the validator accepts in every ecosystem `ortus init` supports.

## Behavioral context

Before. The generated contract says "one runnable command (backticks optional)" and its only worked examples are `uv run pytest …`. Nothing tells the planner that "runnable" means "first token is in `_COMMAND_RUNNERS`", so in a Node repository it copies the `package.json` spelling (`npx vitest run …`, `grep …`) and produces packets the validator rejects. Observed 2026-08-29 in `logicfirst-mcp`: 13 planner-written packets failed `criterion checks` for exactly this reason. The plan prompt at `src/ortus/prompts/plan-prompt.md` likewise shows only `uv run pytest` examples.

After. The Shape rules block of `spec_markdown()` carries one bullet that lists the recognised runner tokens, rendered from `_COMMAND_RUNNERS` so the text can never drift from the enforcing set, and the Criterion-checks rule shows one non-Python example (`cargo test --test demo`) beside the pytest one. Because `plan-prompt.md` substitutes `$readiness_spec`, the planner sees the same list with no prompt duplication.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Extend `_shape_rules()` in `src/ortus/core/readiness.py` with a runner-allowlist bullet rendered from `sorted(_COMMAND_RUNNERS)` and add a non-Python example to the Criterion-checks rule via the existing self-proving `_example()` helper. Add tests that the rendered spec contains every runner token and the new example, and that the plan prompt inherits it.

## Non-goals

Do not change `_COMMAND_RUNNERS`, `looks_like_command()`, or `_TEST_INVOCATION` — those are ortus-tnj5 and ortus-sju4. Do not add ecosystem detection to the planner (`.ortusrc` `project_type` is not consulted here); the list is small enough to show whole. Do not add a repair pass to `ortus plan` — `tests/test_plan.py::test_plan_unready_leaf_does_not_spawn_repair` records that plan fails fast and never respawns. Do not hand-edit the example block in `plan-prompt.md` beyond what is needed to keep it valid; the contract is injected, not restated.

## Concrete locations

`src/ortus/core/readiness.py`: `_shape_rules()` (~line 605), `_example()` (~line 597), `spec_markdown()` (~line 634), `_COMMAND_RUNNERS` (~line 259). `src/ortus/prompts/plan-prompt.md` line 13 (`$readiness_spec`) and the worked example at lines 55-62. `src/ortus/commands/plan.py::_prompt()` (~line 53) substitutes the spec. Tests: `tests/test_readiness.py::test_spec_markdown_names_every_field_and_heading_in_validator_order` (~line 242), `tests/test_spec.py`, `tests/test_plan.py::test_readiness_spec_substituted_into_the_assembled_prompt` (~line 134), `tests/test_core_prompts.py` (~line 45).

## Resolved decisions

1. The allowlist is rendered from the constant, not typed into the prose, following the `_example()` pattern that already keeps every shape rule provably in sync with its regex.
2. The bullet is one line: "Runnable commands start with one of: `bash`, `bd`, `cargo`, …" in sorted order, so the rendered spec stays stable across runs (the existing test asserts `spec_markdown()` is deterministic).
3. The non-Python example is `cargo test --test demo` because `cargo` is already on the allowlist and the example must validate today regardless of whether ortus-tnj5 has landed; the example is proven with `_example(_CODE_SPAN, …)` and additionally asserted by a test calling `looks_like_command()` on it.
4. The `bash -c` shell-construct bullet belongs to ortus-sju4 and is not duplicated here; if sju4 has landed first, place the runner bullet directly before it.
5. `plan-prompt.md` keeps its pytest worked example; the ecosystem guidance reaches the planner through `$readiness_spec`, which `test_readiness_spec_substituted_into_the_assembled_prompt` already proves.

## Compatibility constraints

The rendered contract is consumed by `ortus spec`, the plan prompt, `tests/test_spec.py` (asserts stdout equals `spec_markdown()`), and the readiness memory pointer; the change is one added bullet and one added example, so all existing assertions on headings and field order stay true. `validate_issue()` behaviour is unchanged. Adding a runner in a later bead automatically updates the rendered text — that is the point.

## Ordered steps

1. In `_shape_rules()`, add a bullet that joins `sorted(_COMMAND_RUNNERS)` as backticked tokens, preceded by the sentence explaining that the first token after an optional `Run`/`Execute`/`Check`/`Verify`/`Invoke` lead-in must be one of them.
2. Extend the Criterion-checks rule to show `cargo test --test demo` as a second `_example()` beside the pytest one.
3. Add `tests/test_readiness.py` tests: every token in `_COMMAND_RUNNERS` appears in `spec_markdown()`; the `cargo` example appears and `looks_like_command()` accepts it.
4. Run `ortus spec` by hand once and confirm the bullet reads cleanly, then run the targeted tests.

## Dependencies

No blocking issues. Related: ortus-tnj5 (adds the Node runners the bullet will then list) and ortus-sju4 (adds the neighbouring `bash -c` bullet). Consumers of `spec_markdown()`: `src/ortus/commands/spec.py`, `src/ortus/commands/plan.py::_prompt`, `src/ortus/core/prompts.py::substitute` callers.

## Edge cases

`_COMMAND_RUNNERS` contains tokens like `true`, `false`, `test`, `rm` that read oddly in prose; render them anyway — the list is a contract, not a recommendation. Very long single bullet: acceptable, Markdown wraps; do not split into multiple bullets, which would break the one-rule-per-bullet convention `test_spec_markdown_names_every_field_and_heading_in_validator_order` relies on. If `_example()` raises for the new example, the example is wrong, not the regex.

## Plan-gap guidance

If a maintainer test asserts the exact byte content of `spec_markdown()` or of an `ortus spec` golden file that cannot be regenerated from code, stop and record PLAN-GAP naming the fixture rather than freezing the runner list into it by hand.

- AC-1 (proves-new): `spec_markdown()` lists every token in `_COMMAND_RUNNERS` as a backticked runner.
- AC-2 (proves-new): the rendered Criterion-checks rule carries the non-Python example `cargo test --test demo` and `looks_like_command()` accepts that example.
- AC-3 (guards-existing): the assembled plan prompt still contains `spec_markdown()` verbatim, so the planner receives the runner list, and `ortus spec` stdout still equals `spec_markdown()`.

## Criterion checks

- AC-2: `uv run pytest tests/test_readiness.py -k "spec_shows_non_python_check_example" -q`

## Targeted tests

`uv run pytest tests/test_readiness.py tests/test_spec.py tests/test_plan.py::test_readiness_spec_substituted_into_the_assembled_prompt -q`

title: readiness: one AC heading; Targeted tests optional
description:
## Objective

Coarsen readiness v1 acceptance: one required heading carries AC-N, optional kind, prose, and one command. Make Targeted tests optional. Keep current three-heading packets valid.

## Behavioral context

Before. A ready leaf must author `## Observable criteria`, `## Criterion checks`, and `## Targeted tests` as parallel lists. Workers and `parse_criterion_checks` run only the Criterion-checks commands. `targeted_test_command` is a `validate_issue` shape check; grind does not execute that section. Small leaves restate the same pytest surface three times.

After. A new leaf can put kind, prose, and one command on each Observable line. Criterion checks and Targeted tests are optional aliases. Existing three-heading packets stay ready.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Change `validate_issue` and `parse_criterion_checks` so one acceptance heading is enough. Commands may live on Observable-criteria lines. Criterion-checks remains a valid alias. Targeted tests may be omitted or `None — <why>`. Update `spec_markdown`, the plan-prompt example, and readiness tests.

## Non-goals

Do not rewrite the rest of the fifteen-heading diet. Do not execute Targeted tests. Do not accept two commands on one AC. Do not drop AC-N identifiers or kind tags.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/core/readiness.py` — `_REQUIRED_SECTIONS`, `validate_issue()`, `extract_check_command()`, `targeted_test_command()`, `spec_markdown()`.
- `src/ortus/core/checks.py` — `parse_criterion_checks()` must read commands from Observable lines when Criterion checks is absent.
- `src/ortus/prompts/plan-prompt.md` — example packet.
- `tests/test_readiness.py`, `tests/test_core_checks.py`, `tests/test_spec.py`.

## Resolved decisions

1. ortus-55ht: 1:1 AC-N → command stays; the three-list split does not.
2. Compatibility: a packet that already has all three headings still validates.
3. Kinds stay on the observable/prose line and stay optional.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux + macOS. Historical journals and claimed three-heading packets must remain ready.

## Ordered steps

1. Allow Observable lines to carry one command; parse them when Criterion checks is missing.
2. Stop treating Targeted tests as a required non-placeholder section.
3. Keep Criterion checks as an alias that still 1:1-maps AC-N when present.
4. Update spec text, plan-prompt example, and tests.

## Dependencies

Discovered from ortus-55ht. Callers are `validate_issue` and `parse_criterion_checks`.

## Edge cases

Observable line with prose and no command still fails if Criterion checks does not supply that AC. Two command-looking spans stay ambiguous. `None — criterion commands name the targeted surface` is a valid Targeted tests body.

## Plan-gap guidance

If dropping the Targeted tests requirement makes `ortus spec` and the plan prompt disagree with `validate_issue`, stop and record PLAN-GAP. Do not ship a silent split.
acceptance_criteria:

title: readiness: investigate whether AC-N packets are too granular
description:
## Objective

Decide whether readiness v1 forces acceptance criteria to be more granular than the work needs — one AC-N plus one command per observable — and if so, what a coarser packet should look like.

## Behavioral context

Flagged 2026-08-14 after ortus-avyu made commands semantic (backticks optional). The operator's remaining complaint is not punctuation: a small leaf still needs Observable criteria, Criterion checks, and Targeted tests as parallel lists. That may be the right machine-check contract, or it may be paperwork. Investigate later; do not change the extractor in this issue.

## Notes

Not blocking. Do not implement until this is scoped. Related: ortus-avyu (semantic commands).
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Investigate whether readiness v1 forces acceptance criteria into more lists than the live contract needs. Record a decision. Do not change `extract_check_command` or `parse_criterion_checks`.

## Non-goals

Do not change the extractor. Do not rewrite the fifteen-heading diet. Do not execute Targeted tests.

## Concrete locations

- `src/ortus/core/readiness.py` — `_REQUIRED_SECTIONS`, `extract_check_command()`, `targeted_test_command()`, `validate_issue()`.
- `src/ortus/core/checks.py` — `parse_criterion_checks()`, `run_checks()`.
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` — `_run_machine_checks` / `_verification_pass` (dead after f2he).

## Resolved decisions

1. The 1:1 AC-N → one command mapping is the machine-check contract. Keep it.
2. Two required headings that repeat every AC-N (Observable vs Criterion checks) are paperwork. A coarser packet puts kind, prose, and the command on one line.
3. Targeted tests is a readiness presence check only (`targeted_test_command` is called from `validate_issue`). Make it optional on the follow-up leaf.
4. Existing three-heading packets must stay valid as aliases.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux + macOS. Existing v1 packets must remain ready until the follow-up lands an aliasing parser.

## Ordered steps

1. Confirm who consumes each acceptance heading.
2. Decide which split is load-bearing.
3. Write the coarser packet shape.
4. File a follow-up leaf; leave the extractor unchanged here.

## Dependencies

Related: ortus-avyu (semantic commands). Follow-up owns the parser change.

## Edge cases

A packet with two command-looking spans on one AC stays invalid. Kinds stay optional.

## Plan-gap guidance

If a live grind caller executed Targeted tests as a required pass, stop and record PLAN-GAP instead of calling that heading optional.
notes: Decision: 1:1 AC-N to one command is load-bearing; the three parallel acceptance lists are paperwork. Follow-up leaf coarsens to one heading and optional Targeted tests. Extractor unchanged on this id.
close_reason: 1:1 AC-command mapping stays; three-list split is paperwork; follow-up is ortus-55ht.1

comments.author: who
comments.text:
Decision: v1's 1:1 AC-N → one command is the machine-check contract; the three parallel acceptance lists are paperwork.

What is load-bearing
- Unique AC-N identifiers.
- Optional kind tags (proves-new / guards-existing) on the observable line.
- Exactly one runnable command per identifier (`extract_check_command` / `parse_criterion_checks`).
- One command per line; two command-looking spans stay ambiguous (ortus-avyu, ortus-qs6l).

What is paperwork
- Requiring `## Observable criteria` and `## Criterion checks` as two headings that repeat every AC-N. Kinds live on the first list; commands live on the second. That split is a parse convenience, not a second contract.
- Requiring `## Targeted tests` on every leaf. `targeted_test_command` is only a readiness shape check inside `validate_issue`. avyu's own packet said "Do not execute targeted tests." After f2he, grind judges bd status; workers run the Criterion-checks commands. `run_checks` is still aliased from grind's dead `_verification_pass` (ortus-j48h), and that path never reads Targeted tests either. Small leaves (ortus-j48h, the plan-prompt example, avyu) restate the same pytest surface in all three lists.

Coarser packet (do not implement on this id)
- One required acceptance heading. Each AC-N line carries kind (optional), prose, and one command.
- Keep current three-heading packets valid as aliases so existing leaves stay ready.
- Targeted tests optional: omit, or `None — criterion commands name the targeted surface`.
- Out of scope: LEAN_PIPELINE's fifteen-to-seven heading diet. This leaf is the acceptance split only.

Extractor in `src/ortus/core/readiness.py` and `src/ortus/core/checks.py` is unchanged on this id. Follow-up leaf owns the schema/parser change.

comments.author: who
comments.text: Investigation complete. Decision: the 1:1 AC-N to one-command mapping is the machine-check contract; requiring three parallel acceptance lists is paperwork. `targeted_test_command` is only a `validate_issue` shape check. Extractor unchanged. Leftover schema change filed as ortus-55ht.1.

title: bd dolt push fails: missing origin darc blob
description:
## Objective

Restore `bd dolt push` so session-close can sync the embedded Dolt tracker to the configured origin remote.

## Behavioral context

Before. `bd dolt push` and `bd dolt pull` fail with `Error 1105: Blob not found: fgpsht0hsqfrvtst9au67gm3u1it4gvc.darc` against origin `git+https://github.com/who/ortus.git`. Local close of `ortus-zt5n.6` succeeded; product git push to origin/main succeeded.

After. `bd dolt push` and `bd dolt pull` reach origin without the missing-darc error, so tracker commits made at session-close land on the Dolt remote.
design:
## Readiness schema

v1

## Scope

Diagnose the missing `.darc` blob on the git+https Dolt remote, restore or rebuild remote access, and confirm push/pull work from this checkout.

## Non-goals

Do not rewrite grind session-close. Do not change product README or backend docs. Do not force-push git `main`.

## Concrete locations

- `.beads/metadata.json` — embedded Dolt (`dolt_database` = `ortus`)
- `bd dolt remote list` — origin is `git+https://github.com/who/ortus.git`
- `bd dolt push` / `bd dolt pull` — both fail on blob `fgpsht0hsqfrvtst9au67gm3u1it4gvc.darc`

## Resolved decisions

1. Local beads close is authoritative for the issue that hit this; the product commit is already on origin/main.
2. This is tracker-remote hygiene, not a docs-backend change.

## Compatibility constraints

Linux + macOS. Embedded Dolt. Existing issue ids must remain readable after any remote rebuild.

## Ordered steps

1. Reproduce `bd dolt push` and `bd dolt pull` and capture the blob id.
2. Inspect how this repo stores Dolt objects on the git remote.
3. Restore the missing blob or re-point origin to a complete remote.
4. Confirm push and pull both succeed.

## Dependencies

None. Callers are session-close (`bd dolt push`) after `bd close`.

## Edge cases

A rebuild that drops local embedded history would lose the close of issues not yet on the remote. Prefer repairing the blob over wiping `.beads/embeddeddolt`.

## Plan-gap guidance

If the remote cannot be repaired without rewriting public git history or dropping local Dolt commits, stop and record PLAN-GAP rather than force-pushing.

## Targeted tests

`bd dolt push` and `bd dolt pull` (no pytest; this is tracker-remote access)

title: tests: bd comment ordering has one-second granularity — newest-changes-block selection flakes under parallel load
description:
## Objective

`tests/test_grind_finalization.py::test_commit_body_takes_the_refreshed_changes_block` passes under xdist load, because grind selects the newest **Changes** block by a total order over comments that cannot tie — not by bd's `created_at`, which has one-second granularity.

## Behavioral context

Before. `bd comments <id> --json` orders by `created_at`, which is emitted at second resolution (`2026-08-10T18:58:21Z`). Two completion comments posted inside the same second can come back in either order, so `_change_description` sometimes reads `described[-1]` as the stale block and commits the superseded prose. Observed twice in full-gate runs (2026-08-12), green in isolation both times.

After. `_issue_comments` re-sorts what bd returns by `(created_at, id)` before handing bodies to its callers. The `id` field is a UUIDv7 (probed on `ortus-afft`: `019fed0a-4314-781f-...` at `18:58:21Z`, `019fed0a-4a2c-7a94-...` at `18:58:22Z`), whose leading 48 bits are a millisecond timestamp, so lexicographic id order is posting order and same-second ties resolve deterministically. The commit body always takes the last-posted **Changes** block, under load or not.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Give `_issue_comments()` in `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` a deterministic total order over the entries `BdClient.comments()` returns, then add a bounded regression test that pins the ordering contract. One sort at the single seam every comment consumer already flows through.

## Non-goals
Do not change the test fixture `_finalize_by_replay()` to space its comments with sleeps — that hides the race in the test while leaving the real grind path racy, and it buys seconds of wall clock per test. Do not change `BdClient.comments()` in `src/ortus/core/bd.py`: it is a thin `bd comments --json` passthrough shared with `ortus human`, and ordering policy belongs to the grind consumer. Do not touch `_change_description()`'s two-source fallback, `_changes_bullets()`, `_bounded_block()`, or the `journal.corrections` gate. No bd version pin and no new dependency.

## Concrete locations
- `src/ortus/commands/grind.py` — `_issue_comments()` (line 2520) is the only edit site.
- Consumers confirmed by CodeGraph as the blast radius of that edit, all inside `grind.py`: `_completion_comments()` (line 2627) → `_change_description()` (line 2727) → `_finalize_candidate()` (line 3204) → `grind()` (line 4524); `_latest_claims()` (line 1264), which reads `reversed(_issue_comments(...))`; and `_record_lesson_proposals()` (line 2690), which iterates forward.
- `src/ortus/core/bd.py` — `BdClient.comments()` (line 197) is the upstream producer; read only, not edited.
- `tests/test_grind_finalization.py` — the flaky test at line 1105, its driver `_finalize_by_replay()` at line 909, and the module marks `pytestmark = [pytest.mark.integration, pytest.mark.slow]` at line 46. The new unit test lands in this file, next to the consumer it protects.

## Resolved decisions
1. Fix the production path, not the fixture. `_change_description()` is not the only consumer of comment order: `_latest_claims()` decides the claim diff from the newest claims block and would flake the same way. One sort at `_issue_comments()` fixes every consumer at once.
2. Sort key is `(created_at, id)`, both coerced with `str(entry.get(key) or "")`. `created_at` remains the primary key so a bd that ever widens its timestamp keeps working unchanged; `id` is the tie-breaker.
3. `id` is a valid tie-breaker because bd issues UUIDv7 comment ids (probed above — version nibble `7`, monotonic 48-bit millisecond prefix), so lexicographic id order equals posting order within a second. Record that probe in the code comment; do not re-derive it from a bd version number.
4. Use `sorted(...)` on the entry dicts before body extraction, not on the extracted bodies — the sort keys live on the entry, and Python's sort is stable, so entries missing both keys keep bd's returned relative order rather than being reshuffled.
5. Filter non-dict entries before sorting so a malformed element cannot raise inside the key function; the existing `isinstance(entry, dict)` guard moves ahead of the sort.
6. Keep the existing `except Exception: return []` around the `bd.comments()` call. A tracker that cannot be read still never blocks a commit; the sort adds no new failure mode because its key function only touches `.get()` on dicts.

## Compatibility constraints
Return type stays `list[str]` of comment bodies in ascending (oldest-first) order — `_change_description()` reads `described[-1]` and `_latest_claims()` reads `reversed(...)`, and both must keep working untouched. The `("body", "text", "comment", "content")` key-preference order for body extraction is unchanged. Behavior is identical against a bd whose entries carry no `id` (stable sort → bd's order preserved) and against one that already returns sorted output. No on-disk format, journal phase, CLI flag, log line, or commit-message text changes. Linux and macOS both, Python 3.11+.

## Ordered steps
1. In `_issue_comments()`, keep the `try/except` read of `bd.comments(issue_id)` exactly as it is.
2. Bind `entries = [e for e in entries if isinstance(e, dict)]` so the sort key never sees a non-dict.
3. Sort with `key=lambda e: (str(e.get("created_at") or ""), str(e.get("id") or ""))`, relying on the stable sort for entries that supply neither.
4. Extract bodies from the sorted list with the existing key-preference loop, dropping the now-redundant `isinstance` check from that loop.
5. Extend the docstring to state the ordering contract — oldest first, ties broken by UUIDv7 comment id — and cite the one-second `created_at` granularity as the reason.
6. Add `test_issue_comments_break_same_second_ties_by_id` to `tests/test_grind_finalization.py`: a stub bd object whose `comments()` returns two entries with an identical `created_at` and UUIDv7 ids in reverse order, asserting `_issue_comments()` returns them oldest-id-first.
7. Run the targeted tests below, then the AC-1 repetition loop.

## Dependencies
No issue dependency — this is a standalone bug fix with no parent epic and no blockers. Code consumers that must keep passing after the edit are the three `_issue_comments()` callers listed under Concrete locations; CodeGraph reports no caller of `_issue_comments()` outside `src/ortus/commands/grind.py`.

## Edge cases
- Both comments carry the same `created_at` and bd returns them newest-first: the id tie-break must still yield posting order (this is the flake).
- An entry has `created_at` but no `id`, or neither: the stable sort must preserve bd's relative order rather than sinking it to the front.
- `bd.comments()` raises: still returns `[]`, no traceback, finalization still commits.
- An entry is not a dict, or is a dict whose four body keys are all empty/absent: it is skipped and must not raise inside the sort key.
- Zero comments and exactly one comment: the sort is a no-op and `_change_description()` keeps its existing degradation log line.
- `_latest_claims()` reads the reversed list, so an ordering fix that accidentally reverses the list would silently invert the claim diff — the AC-2 test asserts absolute oldest-first order, not merely "not the old order".

## Plan-gap guidance
If the probe shows this bd's comment `id` is not UUIDv7 — the version nibble at position 13 is not `7`, or ids are not monotonic within a second — then decision 3 is void and there is no in-band total order to sort by. Stop, record `PLAN-GAP` naming `_issue_comments` (`src/ortus/commands/grind.py:2520`) and the observed id format, preserve the candidate state, and route to planning/human handling. Do not invent a substitute order such as re-deriving posting sequence from body content, adding sleeps to the fixture, or having grind stamp its own sequence number into comment bodies.

- AC-2: `_issue_comments()` returns comment bodies oldest-first when two entries share a `created_at` and bd returns them in reverse id order.
- AC-3: The finalization suite still passes, so the ordering change does not disturb the other comment consumers.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: Run `for i in $(seq 20); do uv run pytest tests/test_grind_finalization.py -k refreshed_changes_block -n auto --test-timeout=180 -q || exit 1; done` — the shell loop is the repetition mechanism because pytest-repeat is not installed in this environment; a failing run must fail the whole check, so the loop exits non-zero on the first failure.
- AC-2: Run `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_finalization.py -k issue_comments_break_same_second_ties_by_id -q`.
- AC-3: Run `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_finalization.py -n auto --test-timeout=180 -q`.

## Targeted tests
Run `uv run pytest tests/test_grind_finalization.py tests/test_grind_corrections.py -n auto --test-timeout=180 -q`.

title: Q6 — Codex analog for the bd prime session hook
description: Claude Code runs `bd prime` via SessionStart/PreCompact hooks. Determine whether Codex has an analogous session hook; if not, fold the priming instruction into AGENTS.md guidance.
design: Cheap fallback: AGENTS.md guidance costs nothing and works regardless of hook support.
acceptance_criteria: CONDITIONS: (1) a documented answer on Codex session-hook support; (2) if absent, AGENTS.md instructs the agent to run `bd prime` at session start for codex projects. TESTING: start a codex loop in a generated project and confirm from the log that bd priming occurred.
notes:
Q6 ANSWER (codex-cli 0.144.6, probed empirically on 2026-07-18):

Codex DOES have a hook system. Events present in the binary: PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, SessionStart, SubagentStart, SubagentStop — i.e. a SessionStart analog to Claude Code's exists.

Configuration surfaces (both verified to parse via `codex exec --strict-config -c ...`):
  1. A `[hooks]` table in config.toml (struct HooksToml). `hooks = "<path>"` is REJECTED — it is a table, not a path.
     e.g. hooks.SessionStart=[{hooks=[{type="command",command="bd prime"}]}]
  2. An auto-discovered $CODEX_HOME/hooks.json, schema {"description": str, "hooks": {"<Event>": [{"hooks": [{"type":"command","command":"..."}]}]}}.
     A wrong-shaped file warns ('failed to parse hooks config <path>') without aborting the run.

Why we still take the AGENTS.md fallback (issue design note): hooks require persisted trust before they run (`--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` exists precisely for automation that wants to skip that gate), the schema is undocumented in `codex --help` and version-dependent, and a trust prompt in a headless goal loop is a hang risk. AGENTS.md guidance costs nothing and works on both backends.

SHIPPED: 'Session Start' section in AGENTS.md and template/AGENTS.md instructing the agent to run `bd prime` first thing each session, noting the Claude hook makes it a no-op and that Codex has no auto-fire.

NOT VERIFIED: the acceptance-criteria live test ('start a codex loop and confirm from the log that bd priming occurred') — this box has no Codex credentials (`codex doctor`: 'no Codex credentials were found'). Same blocker as ortus-vl11. Covered there rather than re-flagging here.
close_reason: Q6 answered: Codex 0.144.x has SessionStart hooks but they require trust; took the AGENTS.md fallback — both AGENTS.md files now instruct running bd prime at session start

title: Evaluate AskUserQuestion replacement options for Codex
description: interview.sh:230 and triage.sh:82 both depend on AskUserQuestion, which has no Codex equivalent. Evaluate: (a) plain-text Q&A in codex exec, (b) keep these flows Claude-only under agent_cli=codex, (c) a small shell-driven prompt loop.
design: Deferred by design — must not block Phases 1-3.
acceptance_criteria: CONDITIONS: (1) each option is assessed for UX, reliability, and maintenance cost; (2) a recommendation is recorded with rationale; (3) the finding is captured via `bd remember`. TESTING: prototype the leading option against a trivial two-question interview and confirm the answers are captured correctly and the process never hangs.
notes:
EVALUATION (all three options assessed on UX / reliability / maintenance):

(a) Plain-text Q&A inside codex exec — REJECTED.
  UX: acceptable-looking, but there is no structured answer contract, so the wrapper must free-text-parse model output.
  Reliability: poor. Verified in this sandbox that 'codex exec' blocks on 'Reading additional input from stdin...' when stdin is not redirected — a live hang risk in exactly the unattended paths we care about.
  Maintenance: high — prompt-shaped parsing breaks on model drift.

(b) Keep interview.sh / triage.sh Claude-only under agent_cli=codex — REJECTED as the permanent answer, ACCEPTED as the interim gate.
  UX: a hard parity hole; a codex user simply cannot run these flows.
  Reliability: perfect (nothing new to break).
  Maintenance: cheap now, but freezes a Claude-only assumption into the docs that E6 then has to qualify everywhere.

(c) Two-phase envelope + shell-driven operator prompt loop — RECOMMENDED.
  Already proven in-tree by src/ortus/commands/triage.py: phase 1 runs the agent headless and writes one JSON envelope per question to logs/*.jsonl; phase 2 runs in the wrapper, which owns a real TTY, and prompts/applies. The only agent-side capability needed is 'write JSONL', which both backends have, so it is backend-agnostic by construction — no AskUserQuestion equivalent required.
  Maintenance: one operator-loop implementation shared by both backends.

PROTOTYPE (AC 'never hangs'): built a trivial two-question envelope interview and exercised it four ways — explicit answers, closed stdin (/dev/null), idle stdin that never responds, and garbage input ('banana', '99'). Answers were captured correctly in every case and the process terminated every time (idle case bounded by read -t, ~10s/question). Two bugs surfaced and were fixed in the prototype and are recorded in bd memory as porting gotchas: the operator loop must read envelopes on FD 3 (otherwise the prompt consumes the envelope file), and read must carry -t.

LIMITATION: phase 1 could not be exercised against a live codex here — codex has no usable credentials in this sandbox (401 from api.openai.com) and its default CODEX_HOME is read-only. Phase 1 was stubbed; the operator loop, which is the part that actually replaces AskUserQuestion, was tested for real. Live codex-exec phase-1 wiring belongs to ortus-nyd9.

Findings captured via 'bd remember' (2 entries).
close_reason: Evaluated all 3 AskUserQuestion replacements; recommended the two-phase envelope + shell operator loop (option c), prototyped and verified no-hang across 4 stdin cases, findings in bd remember
